Release 30 November 2026. Epic 1 status: confirmed. The technical enabler stories for Epic 1 are in their own file and in the Epic 1 story files.

Each story is written for build: the business rationale, preconditions, the main flow and its exception paths, acceptance criteria in Gherkin, business rules, state transitions, authority, the fields it reads and writes with their BR Field IDs, the contract, the solution plan, messages, screens, test cases and traceability to the business requirements. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary, endpoints those in the API Specification, messages those in the Error and Message Standard and requirement IDs those in the Business Requirements. The same stories are also supplied one file per story, to hand to a coding agent with the module specifications.

## RWB-E1-001 Recovery tables for the 14 data products

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-001 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-01 Create the recovery tables in the ACE database; FEAT-RDF-02 Define the 14 data products and their systems of record |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-001 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-044, RWB-E1-043 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **the recovery tables for the 14 data products created in the ACE database, with a data dictionary and one system of record and one owner per data product**, so that **every later load has one target table and one accountable owner**.

### 2. Business rationale

Recovery data is held today in the core bank, EFS, LIT, CCMS, SVAF, AMIS and team spreadsheets, with no single checked copy. This story creates the 43 recovery tables from the physical schema, the metadata registry that holds the data dictionary as data, and the catalog of the 14 data products DP01 to DP14. Each data product then has exactly one system of record and one named owner, as REQ-RDF-001 requires. The measure it serves is "loads on time and complete on 99 percent of days" (FSD P1 A2.1), because no load can start until its target table and owner exist.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-044 is done: Flyway runs in the ACE pipeline and takes the schema name from the parameter `recoverySchema`.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: the reference data service accepts a validated load for a table code and calls the handler that the owning module provides.
- The DEV and SIT databases of the ACE service exist and the pipeline service identity may run migrations in the recovery schema.
- The reference data administrator (RW-REFADM) holds Reference data C. The person who queries the dictionary view has read access to the recovery schema in DEV or SIT.
- The catalog load file for the 14 data products is prepared from the seed values in section 13, with an owner user ID for each product in that environment (synthetic test users in DEV and SIT).

### 4. Flow

1. Pipeline: runs migration `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` in DEV with `recoverySchema = recovery`.
2. Migration: creates the 43 tables, the 68 foreign keys, the 76 indexes and the append-only triggers on decision_log_entry and interaction, and the new table data_product, in one transaction.
3. Migration: inserts the 108 sys_objects rows, the 1,256 sys_fields rows and the 14 data_product seed rows (section 13), and creates the view `v_data_dictionary`.
4. Pipeline: runs the dictionary conformance test, which compares every column in the recovery schema with sys_fields.
5. Pipeline: repeats steps 1 to 4 in SIT.
6. Reference data administrator: loads the data product catalog file with table code `data_product` through `POST /admin/reference-loads`, naming the owner user ID of each product for the environment.
7. System: `DataProductCatalogHandler.validate` checks the file: 14 products DP01 to DP14, each with one system of record, one owner role from LOV-ROLE, one owner user ID and one refresh cycle.
8. Data steward: confirms the load as owner of the catalog through the reference data change process (RWB-E1-043).
9. System: `DataProductCatalogHandler.apply` writes the 14 rows in one transaction with the valid from date.
10. Developer or data steward: queries `v_data_dictionary` for entity loan_account and field days_past_due.
11. System: returns field ID DF-ACC-014, the types, the source system and source field, the data product, its refresh cycle and its owner.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X4 | A catalog row names no system of record, two systems of record, or no owner user ID | The whole load is refused; no row is written | MSG-P1-003 | AC7 |
| X5 | The catalog file does not hold exactly the 14 products DP01 to DP14 | The whole load is refused | MSG-P1-004 | AC8 |
| X6 | A catalog row names an owner role or refresh cycle outside its list | The whole load is refused | MSG-P1-007 | AC9 |
| X7 | The same catalog file is loaded again | Nothing is written; the load is reported as already done | MSG-P1-011 | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Reference data C loads the catalog | 403 Problem response; the refusal is in the access log | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-001-11 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the migration tooling (RWB-E1-044) and the reference load service (RWB-E1-043); every load story and the data dictionary story (RWB-E1-064) build on this one |
| Negotiable | The catalog values (names, owners, refresh cycles) are data in a load file; the story fixes the tables and the checks |
| Valuable | Gives every later load one target and every data product one accountable owner |
| Estimable | One migration, one view, one conformance test, one reference table handler |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Recovery tables for the 14 data products

  Scenario: AC2 Dictionary published
    Given the data dictionary and the data product seed loaded by the migration, and the catalog loaded for DP01
    When a developer queries v_data_dictionary for entity "loan_account" and field "days_past_due"
    Then the row holds field ID "DF-ACC-014", data type "NUMBER", physical type "integer"
    Then source system "Core bank (ALS) via COLLINS", source field "DELAY_DAYS"
    Then data product "DP01", refresh cycle "DAILY", owner role "RW-DATASTEW" and the owner user ID of DP01

  Scenario: AC3 One system of record
    Given a catalog load file with the 14 rows DP01 to DP14, each with one system of record and one owner user ID
    When the reference data administrator loads it with valid from 2026-11-20
    Then data_product holds 14 rows
    Then each row has exactly one system of record and one owner user ID
    Then the catalog for DP06 names system of record "CCMS" and refresh cycle "WEEKLY"

  Scenario: AC7 Catalog row with two systems of record is refused
    Given a catalog load file in which DP06 names system of record "CCMS; SVAF"
    Given DP11 has no owner user ID
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-003 for DP06 and for DP11
    Then data_product keeps the rows of the version in force

  Scenario: AC8 Catalog with a missing product is refused
    Given a catalog load file with 13 rows and no row for DP09
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-004 naming "DP09"
    Then the system writes no row

  Scenario: AC9 Value outside its list
    Given a catalog load file in which row 4 (DP04) names owner role "DP_OWNER" and row 5 (DP05) names refresh cycle "HOURLY"
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-007 "Row 4: owner_role must be one of the role codes in LOV-ROLE." and "Row 5: refresh_cycle must be one of DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, ON_CHANGE."

  Scenario: AC10 Same catalog file loaded again
    Given the catalog version loaded on 2026-11-20 is in force
    When the reference data administrator loads the same file again
    Then the system writes nothing
    Then the response carries MSG-P1-011 "The data product catalog load for 2026-11-20 is already complete or running. It was not run again."
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every table and column in the recovery schema has exactly one row in the data dictionary, with its BR Field ID, types, source system and meaning | Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary; sys_fields |
| BR2 | Recovery data is held in the 14 data products DP01 to DP14 | REQ-RDF-001; sys_objects.data_product |
| BR3 | Each data product has exactly one system of record and one named owner | REQ-RDF-001 |
| BR4 | The catalog values are a versioned data load, changed without a code release; a load with an exception is refused in full | Principle 1; DT02; CTL-08 |
| BR5 | Where the entities of one product name more than one source (DP06, DP07, DP13), the catalog names one accountable system of record; the seed values in section 13 are assumed until the data steward confirms them | DL12 |
| BR6 | Schema names come from parameters; one migration per story; forward only in PROD | RWB-E1-044 |
| BR7 | Personal fields carry is_personal = true in the dictionary so masking (RWB-E1-016) can read them | sys_fields.is_personal; CTL-11 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the Flyway version of the recovery schema (none to 1.001) and the version of the data product catalog (none to the first loaded version).

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Pipeline service identity (ACE pipeline) | Runs the migration and the conformance test in DEV and SIT |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the catalog file (Reference data C) |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Confirms the catalog version as its owner (Reference data U); cannot load it (no Reference data C) |
| Developers and the data steward in DEV and SIT | Query v_data_dictionary with read access to the recovery schema |
| Any role without Reference data C | Refused with MSG-P4-002 on the catalog load |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies.

Ruled 2026-11-06 as D-RCV-29: the baseline migration seeds the full recovery dictionary with 108 `sys_objects` rows and 1,256 `sys_fields` rows as held in Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql, so the dictionary is complete before the tables exist and the conformance test can run; RWB-E1-016 and RWB-E1-064 read the full dictionary and later dictionary changes are reference loads through RWB-E1-043 (D-RCV-28).

### 12. Contract

**Dictionary view** `v_data_dictionary` (read model created by the migration; RWB-E1-064 builds the dictionary endpoint on it)

| Column | From |
|---|---|
| field_id, entity, field, data_type, physical_type, mandatory, lov_code, source_system, source_field, personal | sys_fields |
| data_product, entity_system_of_record | sys_objects |
| product_system_of_record, refresh_cycle, owner_role, owner_user_id | data_product |

**Reference load handler** (published interface of P4 that P1 implements, from RWB-E1-043)

```java
public interface ReferenceTableHandler {
    String tableCode();                                              // returns "data_product"
    ValidationReport validate(ReferenceLoadFile file);               // checks every row, writes nothing
    int apply(UUID loadId, ReferenceLoadFile file, LocalDate validFrom); // writes all rows in one transaction, returns the row count
}
```

The load itself is `POST /admin/reference-loads` (P4, Reference data C) with `table = data_product`, and its response is `ReferenceLoad`. A refused load returns 422 with MSG-P1-003, MSG-P1-004 or MSG-P1-007 in the Problem response; a caller without Reference data C gets 403 with MSG-P4-002. Idempotency: a file whose content hash matches the version in force is reported with MSG-P1-011 and writes nothing.

**Migration**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | The ACE pipeline, on each deployment to DEV and SIT |
| Name | `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` with placeholder `${recoverySchema}` |
| Idempotency | The Flyway version 1.001; a changed checksum on an applied version fails the pipeline |
| Restart | A failed run rolls back; the next run applies the full version again |

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dataengine/catalog`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.catalog`; migration in `src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql | Flyway migration | Creates the 43 tables of the physical schema, data_product, the references, indexes, triggers and v_data_dictionary; inserts sys_objects, sys_fields and the 14 data_product seed rows |
| DataDictionaryConformanceTest | Test (pipeline) | Compares information_schema.columns with sys_fields in both directions, ignoring the 7 standard columns |
| DataProduct | Entity | Maps data_product |
| DataProductRepository | Repository | Reads and writes data_product |
| DataProductCatalogHandler | Published interface implementation | Implements ReferenceTableHandler for table code `data_product` |

**Database.** Creates every table in the physical schema. Creates data_product with the columns RWB-E1-064 also uses: product_code varchar(4) primary key, product_name varchar(80) not null, definition varchar(400), owner_role varchar(20) not null, system_of_record varchar(120) not null, refresh_cycle varchar(10) not null check in ('DAILY','WEEKLY','MONTHLY','ON_CHANGE'), expected_by varchar(20), plus owner_user_id uuid (null in the seed, required by the catalog load) and valid_from date, and the 7 standard columns. Creates v_data_dictionary. Adds a foreign key from sys_objects.data_product to data_product.product_code; the migration inserts the data_product seed rows before the sys_objects rows.

**Configuration and reference data.** Parameter `recoverySchema` per environment (platform administrator). Seed values inserted by the migration and repeated in the first catalog load file, with the owner user IDs, prepared by the reference data administrator and confirmed by the data steward:

| Product | Name | System of record | Refresh cycle |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP01 | Account and arrears | Core bank (ALS) via COLLINS | DAILY |
| DP02 | Customer and party | SCBPDM via COLLINS | DAILY |
| DP03 | Case and work management | Workbench | DAILY |
| DP04 | Treatment | Workbench | DAILY |
| DP05 | Interaction | Workbench | DAILY |
| DP06 | Collateral and asset | CCMS (assumed, DL12) | WEEKLY |
| DP07 | Legal | LIT via COLLINS (assumed, DL12) | DAILY |
| DP08 | Partner | Workbench | DAILY |
| DP09 | Debt sale | Workbench | DAILY |
| DP10 | Document | Workbench document hub | DAILY |
| DP11 | Score | COLLINS | DAILY |
| DP12 | Decision log | Workbench | DAILY |
| DP13 | Money and closure | Workbench (assumed, DL12) | DAILY |
| DP14 | Reference and access | Workbench | DAILY |

Owner role RW-DATASTEW for every product; owner user IDs per environment.

**Build steps**

Ruled 2026-11-05 as D-RCV-28: recovery Flyway files are named `V<seq>__<story>_<name>.sql` with a four-digit sequence taken in merge order; line 1 is `-- Story: <story key>`; the schema is referenced only as `${recoverySchema}` and is `recovery` in every environment. The RWB-E1-001 baseline is `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql`; RWB-E1-044 ships no production migration file. Former open point: This story names the migration file V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql with the placeholder ${recoverySchema}. RWB-E1-044, which sets the migration rule for the module, names the baseline V1__rwb_e1_001_baseline.sql with the placeholder ${schema} fed by the environment value RWB_SCHEMA. The stories were reissued to the ruled baseline on 6 November 2026.

1. Write `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` from the physical schema, with `${recoverySchema}` in place of the fixed schema name, plus data_product with its 14 seed rows and v_data_dictionary; run it on an empty PostgreSQL container.
2. Write DataDictionaryConformanceTest and add it to the pipeline after the migration stage; prove it fails on an extra column and on a changed type.
3. Write DataProduct, DataProductRepository and DataProductCatalogHandler with the checks for BR2, BR3 and the list values; unit test the checks for X4, X5 and X6.
4. Connect the handler to the reference data service of RWB-E1-043 and test a full load, a refused load and a repeated file against a container database.
5. Write a test that reads v_data_dictionary for loan_account.days_past_due after a catalog load.
6. Add messages MSG-P1-003, MSG-P1-004, MSG-P1-007 and MSG-P1-011 to the message table with English and Thai text.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.data-catalog`. The flag covers the catalog handler; the migration is not behind a flag.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the migration runs clean in DEV and SIT, and the catalog version for SIT holds 14 rows.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-003 | Catalog row with no system of record, more than one, or no owner | {product} must have exactly one system of record and one named owner. |
| MSG-P1-004 | Catalog file without exactly DP01 to DP14 | The catalog must hold the 14 data products DP01 to DP14. Missing: {products}. |
| MSG-P1-007 | Catalog value outside its list | Row {row}: {field} must be one of {values}. |
| MSG-P1-011 | Same catalog file loaded again | The {source} load for {date} is already complete or running. It was not run again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without Reference data C | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

Thai text for each new message follows DL10 and is in the additions file.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The pipeline log shows the migration and conformance results. Developers read the dictionary through v_data_dictionary; the dictionary endpoint comes with RWB-E1-064, the catalog entries with RWB-E1-016, and SCR-40 Reference data in E8.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: product names, systems of record, owners and refresh cycles come from the catalog load.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. Owner user IDs in DEV and SIT are synthetic test users.
- No read of another module's tables. The dictionary reads only sys_objects, sys_fields and data_product.
- The migration changes no data outside the recovery schema and never drops a table in PROD.

## RWB-E1-002 Case list v1 with case ID, owner and queue

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-002 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-18 Show the case list with case ID, owner and queue |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-007 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | 06 Take over and own the case |
| Decision | D6 entry |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-003, RWB-E1-007, RWB-E1-020 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **one case list with case number, account, product, stage, status, owner, queue, route, total balance and days past due for every account at 90 days past due or more, refreshed each working day and available in Power BI**, so that **every recovery team works from one list**.

### 2. Business rationale

Each recovery team keeps its own list of accounts today, and the lists do not agree with each other or with ALS. This story builds one case list each working day from the open cases and the account and arrears data product, checks its count against the ALS count of accounts at 90 days past due or more, and publishes it to Power BI. It meets REQ-RDF-007 (the case list reconciles daily to the ALS count, DL25) and serves the measure "loads on time and complete on 99 percent of days".

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-018 is done: open cases exist with their linked accounts, and P3 publishes `CaseQueryApi`.
- RWB-E1-020 is done: JOB-03 morning allocation sets the owner and the queue.
- RWB-E1-003 is done: the INT-01 load for the business date is COMPLETED, as `LoadRunQuery` reports.
- RWB-E1-007 is done: the outbound file adapter writes files to the data lake (INT-19).
- Parameters are loaded: `case.entry.dpd` 90 (DL16), `recon.caselist.tolerance.pct` 0.00 (assumed, DL25), `caselist.allocation.wait.until` 07:15.
- The reporting and BI analyst (RW-BIANAL) has built the Power BI data set "Case list v1" on the lake file and scheduled its refresh at 07:30.
- JOB-04 runs as service identity SY-DATALOAD.

### 4. Flow

1. Quartz: JOB-04 Daily reconciliation reaches its case list step after JOB-03 completes for the business date.
2. System: checks through `LoadRunQuery.completedLoad("INT-01", businessDate)` that the account load for the business date is COMPLETED.
3. System: opens a load_run row with job code JOB-04 and product DP03.
4. System: reads the open case accounts from `CaseQueryApi.openCaseAccounts(businessDate)`.
5. System: joins each account to loan_account for account number, total balance and days past due.
6. System: replaces the case_list_row rows for the business date in one transaction, each with the refresh time.
7. System: counts the case list rows at or above 90 days past due and compares the count with the ALS count of accounts at or above 90 days past due, less the accounts P3 excluded at entry.
8. System: writes the count check result to the load_run and alerts the data steward and the team managers if the difference is above the tolerance.
9. System: writes the extract file for the business date to the data lake through the outbound file adapter.
10. Power BI: refreshes the data set at 07:30; the report shows the ten columns, the filters and the refresh time.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The count of rows differs from the ALS count by more than the tolerance | The list is built and published; the load_run check COUNT is FAIL; the data steward and team managers are alerted | MSG-P1-012 | AC4 |
| X2 | The INT-01 load for the business date is not COMPLETED | The step does not run; the previous list stays in the lake | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |
| X3 | JOB-03 has not completed by 07:15 | The list is built with the owner and queue as they are; the check ALLOCATION_COMPLETE is NO on the run | None (shown on the report) | AC6 |
| X4 | The step runs again for the same business date | The rows for that date are replaced; no duplicate rows | None | AC7 |
| X5 | `CaseQueryApi` raises an error | The transaction rolls back; status FAILED; the previous rows stay; the platform administrator reruns | None (alert to the platform administrator) | AC8 |
| X6 | The file transfer to the lake fails after the adapter retries | The run is COMPLETED in the Workbench; the transfer goes to the exception queue with a task for the platform administrator | None (R-UNI-34) | AC9 |
| X7 | A case account has no loan_account row | The row is written with empty balance and days past due and counted as an exception | None (dq_exception, check CL-01) | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Platform administration R lists the case list runs | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-002-11 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads cases only through the P3 published interface and accounts from its own table; the Power BI report is built by the BI analyst |
| Negotiable | The entry threshold, the tolerance and the wait time are parameters |
| Valuable | One list for every team, with owner and queue, replacing the team files |
| Estimable | One batch step, one table, one extract file, one count check |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic cases |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case list v1 with case ID, owner and queue

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-11-30 and DP01 is loaded for 2026-11-30
    Given the parameters case.entry.dpd = 90 and recon.caselist.tolerance.pct = 0.00 are in force

  Scenario: AC1 List reconciles
    Given loan_account holds 28,140 accounts at 90 days past due or more for 2026-11-30
    Given P3 excluded 21 of them at entry, so the ALS count to match is 28,119
    Given the open cases link 28,119 accounts at 90 days past due or more and 37 accounts below 90 days past due
    When the case list step of JOB-04 runs
    Then case_list_row holds 28,156 rows for 2026-11-30
    Then the count check compares 28,119 with 28,119 and the load_run check COUNT is PASS
    Then the check results show 37 rows below 90 days past due

  Scenario: AC2 Columns present
    Given the case list for 2026-11-30 is built
    When the extract file for 2026-11-30 is written
    Then each row holds case number, account number, product, stage, status, owner, queue, route, total balance and days past due, in that order
    Then each row also holds team, business date and refresh time
    Then the Power BI data set "Case list v1" offers filters on team, queue and product
    Then the row for case "RW-2026-000123" shows account "ACC0000123", product "MORTGAGE", status "ASSIGNED", queue "MTG-BKK-CO", total balance 1,250,000.00 and days past due 96

  Scenario: AC3 Daily refresh
    Given the 07:00 loads are complete and JOB-03 completed at 06:52
    When the case list step runs and completes at 07:12
    Then every row for 2026-11-30 carries refresh time 2026-12-01 07:12
    Then the report after the 07:30 data set refresh shows "Refreshed 1 Dec 2026 07:12, data as of 30 Nov 2026"

  Scenario: AC4 Count outside the tolerance
    Given the ALS count to match is 28,119 and the open cases link 28,094 accounts at 90 days past due or more
    When the case list step runs
    Then the system builds the list and published with 28,094 rows at or above 90 days past due
    Then the load_run check COUNT is FAIL with a difference of 25 accounts, 0.09 percent
    Then the data steward and team manager groups receive MSG-P1-012 "The case list for 2026-11-30 does not reconcile to ALS for all products: a difference of 25 accounts, 0.09 percent."

  Scenario: AC5 Account data not loaded
    Given the INT-01 load for 2026-11-30 was refused and is not COMPLETED
    When JOB-04 reaches the case list step
    Then the step does not run and no case_list_row for 2026-11-30 is written
    Then the lake keeps the extract file for 2026-11-27
    Then the load_run for the step shows status REFUSED with failed check "INT-01 not complete"
    Then the team manager group receives MSG-P1-001 "DP01 Account and arrears is from 2026-11-27. Today's load has not arrived."

  Scenario: AC6 Allocation not finished
    Given JOB-03 for 2026-11-30 has not completed at 07:15
    When the case list step starts at 07:15
    Then the system builds the list with the owner and queue as they are at 07:15
    Then the load_run check ALLOCATION_COMPLETE is NO
    Then the report shows "Owners and queues may be incomplete for 30 Nov 2026"

  Scenario: AC7 Run repeated for the same date
    Given the case list for 2026-11-30 holds 28,156 rows
    When the platform administrator reruns the step for 2026-11-30
    Then case_list_row still holds 28,156 rows for 2026-11-30 and no case account appears twice
    Then the refresh time is the time of the rerun

  Scenario: AC8 Case interface error
    Given CaseQueryApi raises an error after 12,000 accounts are read
    When the case list step runs
    Then the system writes no case_list_row for 2026-11-30
    Then the load_run status is FAILED
    Then the rows for 2026-11-27 are unchanged

  Scenario: AC9 Transfer to the lake fails
    Given the outbound file adapter fails all its retries for the 2026-11-30 extract file
    When the case list step completes
    Then the system completes the load_run status with check PUBLISHED = NO
    Then the transfer is in the exception queue with a task for the platform administrator

  Scenario: AC10 Case account without account data
    Given case "RW-2026-000456" links account "ACC0000456", which has no loan_account row
    When the case list step runs
    Then the row for "ACC0000456" has an empty total balance and days past due
    Then the system writes one dq_exception row with check code "CL-01" and record key "ACC0000456"
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The case list holds one row per open case and linked account for the business date | REQ-RDF-007; DL17 (one case per customer per product, accounts linked) |
| BR2 | The ALS count to match is the accounts at or above the entry threshold in loan_account, less the accounts excluded at entry | CTL-01; REC-01; parameter case.entry.dpd (DL16) |
| BR3 | The count check passes when the difference is within the tolerance | Parameter recon.caselist.tolerance.pct, 0.00 assumed (DL25) |
| BR4 | The list is built only when the INT-01 load for the business date is COMPLETED | BR1 of RWB-E1-003; MSG-P1-001 |
| BR5 | The list carries the business date and the refresh time on every row | REQ-RDF-009 (freshness); FEAT-RDF-18 |
| BR6 | A repeated step for the same business date replaces that date's rows | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | A file that fails after the retry limit goes to the exception queue with a task for the owner | R-UNI-34; REQ-DRI-007 |
| BR8 | Case data is read only through the P3 published interface | ADR-002; DT08 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It writes the load_run status for the case list step (RUNNING to COMPLETED, REFUSED or FAILED) and the case_list_row rows of the business date.

| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Lists the runs (Platform administration R) and reruns the step (Platform administration U) |
| RW-DATASTEW, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-SECADM | List the runs (Platform administration R) |
| RW-BIANAL, reporting and BI analyst | Builds and schedules the Power BI data set (Reporting CRUD) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CASEOWN, RW-PHONECOL | Read the case list report in Power BI (Reporting R); row-level security by team follows RWB-E1-016 |

| DF-OPS-022 | load_run | interface_id | Read through LoadRunQuery (INT-01) |
| DF-OPS-025 | load_run | business_date | Read through LoadRunQuery (INT-01) |
| DF-OPS-026 | load_run | status | Read through LoadRunQuery (INT-01) |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**Job step**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | JOB-04 Daily reconciliation, case list step; chained after JOB-03 completes, or at 07:15 if JOB-03 has not completed |
| Job name | JOB-04 Daily reconciliation |
| Input | `CaseQueryApi.openCaseAccounts(businessDate)`, `CaseQueryApi.excludedAccountCount(businessDate)`, loan_account, `LoadRunQuery` (INT-01) |
| Output | case_list_row for the business date; load_run with checks COUNT, BELOW_ENTRY, ALLOCATION_COMPLETE, PUBLISHED; extract file `case-list/<businessDate>.csv` to the data lake through the outbound adapter (INT-19) |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | business_date; the step deletes and inserts the rows of that date in one transaction |
| Restart | A FAILED step is rerun by POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun; it runs in full again |

**Published interface used** (P3, from RWB-E1-018)

```java
public interface CaseQueryApi {
    Stream<OpenCaseAccountView> openCaseAccounts(LocalDate businessDate);
    long excludedAccountCount(LocalDate businessDate);
}

public record OpenCaseAccountView(UUID caseId, String caseNo, UUID accountId, String productGroup,
        String stageCode, String status, UUID ownerUserId, String queueCode, String teamCode, String routeCode) {}
```

**GET /admin/jobs** (API-P1-001), with `type=JOB-04`

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Response 200 | `Job[]` with checks COUNT (PASS or FAIL with the difference), BELOW_ENTRY (count), ALLOCATION_COMPLETE (YES or NO), PUBLISHED (YES or NO) |
| 401, 403, 503 | MSG-P4-001; MSG-P4-002; database unavailable |
| Authorization | Platform administration R |
| Idempotency | Read only |

**POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun** (API-P1-002) reruns the step for the run's business date; Platform administration U; Idempotency-Key header; 409 with MSG-P1-011 while a run for that date is RUNNING.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dataengine/caselist`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.caselist`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseListStepConfig | Job (Spring Batch step in JOB-04) | Reads open case accounts, joins accounts, writes rows, runs the count check |
| CaseListChainListener | Listener (Quartz job listener) | Starts the step when JOB-03 completes for the business date, or at the wait time |
| CaseListRow | Entity | Maps case_list_row |
| CaseListRowRepository | Repository | Deletes and inserts the rows of one business date |
| CaseListCountCheck | Service | Computes the ALS count to match and compares it within the tolerance |
| CaseListExtractWriter | Service | Writes the CSV extract and hands it to the outbound file adapter |
| LoadAlertNotifier | Service (from RWB-E1-003) | Sends MSG-P1-012 |
| RecoveryDataEngineController | Controller (from RWB-E1-003) | Lists and reruns the step through the job endpoints |

**Database.** Migration `V1_002__case_list_row.sql` creates case_list_row with the columns in section 11 (case_no varchar(18), account_no varchar(20), product_group varchar(15), stage_code varchar(20), status varchar(20), queue_code varchar(30), team_code varchar(20), route_code varchar(4), total_balance numeric(18,2), days_past_due integer, refreshed_at timestamptz) and the standard columns, with `uk_case_list_row UNIQUE (business_date, case_id, account_id)` and an index on (business_date, team_code, queue_code). Reads loan_account by id.

**Configuration and reference data.** Parameters `case.entry.dpd`, `recon.caselist.tolerance.pct` and `caselist.allocation.wait.until` from the parameter catalog, loaded by the center of excellence analyst. Lake path and alert recipient groups as configuration, set by the platform administrator. The Power BI data set and its 07:30 schedule are owned by the reporting and BI analyst.

**Build steps**

1. Write migration V1_002, CaseListRow and CaseListRowRepository; test the replace of one date's rows.
2. Write a contract test against `CaseQueryApi` with a stub of synthetic cases.
3. Write CaseListStepConfig: read, join to loan_account, write in one transaction; write CL-01 exceptions for accounts with no loan_account row.
4. Write CaseListCountCheck with the exclusion count and the tolerance; unit test the boundary at the tolerance.
5. Write the INT-01 completion check and the REFUSED run record.
6. Write CaseListChainListener with the wait time and the ALLOCATION_COMPLETE check.
7. Write CaseListExtractWriter with the column order and the adapter hand-off; test the PUBLISHED check when the adapter fails.
8. Add the JOB-04 step to the job listing and the rerun endpoint.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.case-list`. Off: JOB-04 skips the case list step.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and the Power BI data set "Case list v1" refreshes in SIT from the extract file.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-012 | Count difference above the tolerance | The case list for {date} does not reconcile to ALS for {product}: a difference of {variance} accounts, {pct} percent. |
| MSG-P1-001 | INT-01 not complete, list not refreshed | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P1-011 | Rerun while a run for the date is running | The {source} load for {date} is already complete or running. It was not run again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

## RWB-E1-003 ALS daily extract load

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-003 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-03 Load account and arrears daily from ALS |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-002 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | 06 Take over and own the case |
| Decision | D6 entry |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **ALS balances, arrears, payments and classification loaded every working day from the COLLINS daily batch for accounts at 90 days past due or more**, so that **account and arrears data is current to the previous working day**.

### 2. Business rationale

Case owners today read balances and days past due from ALS screens and team files, so two people can see two different numbers for one account. This story loads INT-01 (accounts) and INT-02 (payments) from the COLLINS daily batch into the account and arrears data product DP01, after the seven load checks, so every case reads one checked balance with its business date. It meets REQ-RDF-002 and serves the measure "loads on time and complete on 99 percent of days" and the load target "job runs by 07:00" (NFR-013).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: loan_account, account_payment and data_product exist, and the catalog holds DP01.
- COLLINS writes the INT-01 and INT-02 records for the business date and a trailer row (record count, balance total, business date) into its staging tables in the ACE database. The table names are configuration values, owned by the ACE team.
- The mapping version for INT-01 and INT-02 (source_field_map) and the code map (source_code_map) are loaded and approved.
- The working day calendar is loaded in the reference data service (RWB-E1-043).
- Parameters are loaded: `load.window.end` 09:00, `load.retry.interval` 60 minutes, `load.hold.tolerance.pct` 0.50, `load.movement.tolerance.pct` 10.00, `load.sample.size` 50 (tolerances assumed, DL25).
- JOB-01 runs as service identity SY-DATALOAD.

### 4. Flow

1. Quartz: starts JOB-01 COLLINS load check and intake at 05:00 for the expected business date, the previous working day.
2. System: opens a load_run row for INT-01 with status RUNNING; the unique key (interface, business date) stops a second run.
3. System: runs DQ-001 business date, DQ-002 structure, DQ-003 control total and DQ-004 keys on the staging records; any failure refuses the load.
4. System: runs DQ-005 references and DQ-006 lists of values; records that fail are counted, and the load is refused if the count is above 0.50 percent.
5. System: maps each record through the mapping version in force and the code map, and writes loan_account in one transaction, with data_as_of set to the business date.
6. System: writes the held records to dq_exception with the check code and the account number.
7. System: runs DQ-007 movement against the previous load and alerts the data steward if it is outside 10 percent.
8. System: repeats steps 2 to 7 for INT-02 into account_payment, after INT-01 completes.
9. System: runs the sample check on 50 random accounts and writes the result to the load_run check results.
10. System: sets the load_run status to COMPLETED and publishes LoadCompleted through the outbox in the same transaction; RWB-E1-015 adds the freshness stamp to this transaction.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A blocking check fails (DQ-002, DQ-003 or DQ-008 to DQ-011) | Load refused in full; nothing written; LoadRefused published (RWB-E1-015 marks DP01 stale on it); alert sent | MSG-P1-002 | AC2 |
| X2 | Staging holds a business date other than the expected one (DQ-001) | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | One account key appears twice (DQ-004) | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC5 |
| X4 | Unmatched references at or below 0.50 percent (DQ-012) | Those records held in dq_exception; the rest loaded | None (count on the load_run) | AC6 |
| X5 | Unmatched references above 0.50 percent | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A source code missing from the code map (DQ-006) | Record held; the rest loaded | None (count on the load_run) | AC8 |
| X7 | Count or balance moves more than 10 percent from the previous load (DQ-007) | Loaded; data steward alerted | MSG-P1-006 | AC9 |
| X8 | No complete delivery by 09:00 | load_run status LATE; LoadRefused published with failed check LATE; previous data stays in use | MSG-P1-002 | AC10 |
| X9 | Rerun asked for a business date already COMPLETED | 409; nothing changes | MSG-P1-011 | AC11 |
| X10 | Two nodes start JOB-01 at the same time | One run proceeds; the other stops at the unique key; no duplicate rows | None | AC12 |
| X11 | The database fails during the write | The transaction rolls back; status FAILED; the next hourly attempt loads again | None (alert to the platform administrator) | AC13 |
| X12 | The data steward or another role without Platform administration U asks for a rerun | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-003-15 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the tables and catalog of RWB-E1-001; case creation and allocation read the result later |
| Negotiable | Tolerances, the window end and the sample size are parameters; the mapping is data |
| Valuable | Every case reads one checked balance and days past due, current to the previous working day |
| Estimable | One Quartz job, two Spring Batch steps, one check runner, two endpoints |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic staging data |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: ALS daily extract load

  Background:
    Given the expected business date is 2026-11-30 and the previous completed load is for 2026-11-27
    Given the mapping version "ALS-MAP-1" for INT-01 and INT-02 is approved
    Given the parameters load.hold.tolerance.pct = 0.50 and load.movement.tolerance.pct = 10.00 are in force

  Scenario: AC1 Daily load
    Given COLLINS completed the staging records for 2026-11-30 at 04:40 with 184,500 INT-01 accounts and 2,310 INT-02 payments, each with a matching trailer
    When JOB-01 runs at 05:00
    Then loan_account holds 184,500 rows with data_as_of 2026-11-30 before 07:00
    Then the load_run for INT-01 shows 184,500 read, 184,500 loaded and 0 held, with status COMPLETED
    Then the load_run for INT-02 shows 2,310 read, 2,310 loaded and 0 held
    Then one LoadCompleted event is in the outbox for each interface with business date 2026-11-30

  Scenario: AC2 Failure alerts
    Given the INT-01 trailer states 184,500 records and the staging holds 184,498
    When JOB-01 runs
    Then the system refuses the INT-01 load at DQ-003 and no loan_account row changes
    Then loan_account keeps data_as_of 2026-11-27
    Then the data steward and platform administrator groups receive MSG-P1-002 "The INT-01 load for 2026-11-30 was refused: control total. The previous load is still in use."
    Then one LoadRefused event is in the outbox with failedCheck "DQ-003"

  Scenario: AC3 Sample matches
    Given the INT-01 load for 2026-11-30 is complete
    When the sample check picks 50 accounts at random
    Then for all 50 the total_balance, days_past_due and classification equal the INT-01 staging values after mapping
    Then the load_run check results show "SAMPLE" = "50 of 50"

  Scenario: AC4 Wrong business date
    Given the INT-01 staging records and trailer carry business date 2026-11-27
    When JOB-01 runs for 2026-11-30
    Then the system refuses the load at DQ-001 with MSG-P1-002 naming "business date"
    Then no loan_account row changes

  Scenario: AC5 Duplicate account key
    Given account key "ACC0000017" appears twice in the INT-01 staging records
    When JOB-01 runs
    Then the system refuses the load at DQ-004 with MSG-P1-002 naming "keys"
    Then no loan_account row changes

  Scenario: AC6 Unmatched payments within the tolerance are held
    Given 11 of the 2,310 INT-02 payments name an account key not in loan_account, which is 0.48 percent
    When JOB-01 runs
    Then the system writes 2,299 payments to account_payment
    Then the system writes 11 dq_exception rows with check code "DQ-012", the account key and raised_on 2026-11-30
    Then the INT-02 load_run shows 11 held and status COMPLETED

  Scenario: AC7 Unmatched payments above the tolerance refuse the load
    Given 13 of the 2,310 INT-02 payments name an account key not in loan_account, which is 0.56 percent
    When JOB-01 runs
    Then the system refuses the INT-02 load at DQ-012 with MSG-P1-002
    Then the system writes no account_payment row for 2026-11-30

  Scenario: AC8 Code missing from the code map is held
    Given 3 INT-01 records carry bucket code "Z9", which is not in the code map for LOV-BUCKET
    When JOB-01 runs
    Then the system holds the 3 records in dq_exception with check code "DQ-006"
    Then the system loads 184,497 accounts

  Scenario: AC9 Movement outside the expected range
    Given the previous load for 2026-11-27 held 165,000 accounts and the load for 2026-11-30 holds 184,500, a change of 11.82 percent
    When JOB-01 runs
    Then the system loads the accounts
    Then the data steward group receives MSG-P1-006 "The INT-01 load for 2026-11-30 changed by 11.82 percent against the previous load, outside the expected 10.00 percent. Check it before use."
    Then a change of exactly 10.00 percent sends no alert

  Scenario: AC10 Late delivery
    Given COLLINS has not completed the INT-01 staging records for 2026-11-30 by 09:00
    When the last JOB-01 attempt runs at 09:00
    Then the INT-01 load_run status is LATE and loan_account keeps data_as_of 2026-11-27
    Then one LoadRefused event is in the outbox with failedCheck "LATE"
    Then the data steward group receives MSG-P1-002 "The INT-01 load for 2026-11-30 was refused: no delivery by 09:00. The previous load is still in use."

  Scenario: AC11 Rerun of a completed load
    Given the INT-01 load for 2026-11-30 is COMPLETED
    When the platform administrator calls POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun for that load
    Then the response is 409 with MSG-P1-011 "The INT-01 load for 2026-11-30 is already complete or running. It was not run again."
    Then no loan_account or load_run row changes

  Scenario: AC12 Two runs at the same time
    Given two ACE nodes fire JOB-01 for 2026-11-30 at 05:00
    When both start
    Then one load_run row exists for INT-01 and 2026-11-30
    Then loan_account holds 184,500 rows with no duplicate account_no

  Scenario: AC13 Database failure during the write
    Given the database connection is cut after 90,000 of 184,500 accounts are written in the transaction
    When the write step fails
    Then no loan_account row carries data_as_of 2026-11-30
    Then the load_run status is FAILED
    Then the attempt at 06:00 loads 184,500 accounts and sets the status to COMPLETED

  Scenario: AC14 Rerun after a refused load
    Given the INT-01 load for 2026-11-30 was refused at DQ-003
    Given COLLINS has delivered corrected staging records with a matching trailer
    When the platform administrator calls POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun for that load
    Then the response is 200 with a Job of status RUNNING
    Then the load completes with 184,500 accounts and one LoadCompleted event is in the outbox
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A load is refused in full if the business date, structure, control totals or keys fail; the previous load stays in use and LoadRefused is published | DQ-001 to DQ-004, DQ-008 to DQ-011; INT-01 and INT-02 error handling; CTL-02 |
| BR2 | A record whose reference or code does not match is held in the exception list; above 0.50 percent the load is refused | DQ-005, DQ-006, DQ-012, DQ-013; parameter load.hold.tolerance.pct (assumed, DL25) |
| BR3 | A count or balance change above 10 percent against the previous load is loaded and alerted | DQ-007, DQ-014; parameter load.movement.tolerance.pct (assumed, DL25) |
| BR4 | JOB-01 starts at 05:00 and retries every hour until 09:00 | JOB-01; INT-01 retry |
| BR5 | Every loaded row carries the business date of its load in data_as_of | Mapping rule "Business date"; DF-ACC-021, DF-ACC-028 |
| BR6 | Buddhist Era years become Gregorian dates; amounts are THB numeric with two decimals; source codes map through the versioned code map | Mapping rules "Dates", "Amounts", "Codes" |
| BR7 | Source fields map to Workbench fields through the approved mapping version in force; an unapproved mapping refuses the load | Principle 1; source_field_map |
| BR8 | A repeated run for a completed business date changes nothing | R-UNI-40 |
| BR9 | Load results are recorded on the load_run, not in the decision log, because a decision log entry needs a case (DF-DEC-002); case decisions taken from this data write their own entries | Principle 5; ADR-009 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the load_run status (RUNNING to COMPLETED, REFUSED, LATE or FAILED). The stale flag of DP01 is set by RWB-E1-015 from the LoadRefused event.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | JOB-01 trigger | No run for the interface and date | RUNNING |
| RUNNING | Checks and write done | All blocking checks pass | COMPLETED |
| RUNNING | Check failed | A blocking check fails or held records above 0.50 percent | REFUSED |
| RUNNING | No delivery | Window end 09:00 passed | LATE |
| RUNNING | Write error | Database or step error | FAILED |
| REFUSED, LATE, FAILED | Rerun or next attempt | Delivery present | RUNNING |

| RW-DATASTEW, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY | List jobs and their checks (Platform administration R); no rerun |
| Data steward group, platform administrator group | Receive the load alerts |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies.

### 12. Contract

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz cron 05:00 Asia/Bangkok on working days, then every 60 minutes until 09:00, until INT-01 and INT-02 are COMPLETED or REFUSED |
| Job name | JOB-01 COLLINS load check and intake (this story builds the INT-01 and INT-02 steps) |
| Input | COLLINS staging records and trailer for INT-01 and INT-02 in the ACE database; table names from `rwb.p1.collins.int01.table`, `rwb.p1.collins.int02.table`, `rwb.p1.collins.trailer.table` |
| Output | loan_account, account_payment, load_run, dq_exception |
| Events published | LoadCompleted (EV-26: source, businessDate, rows, checks) on completion; LoadRefused (EV-27: source, businessDate, failedCheck) on refusal; both through the outbox in the same transaction as the load_run status |
| Idempotency key | interface_id and business_date; unique index on load_run where status in ('RUNNING','COMPLETED') |
| Restart | A FAILED or LATE run is attempted again at the next hourly trigger or by rerun; the write step runs again from its start, because it writes in one transaction |

**GET /admin/jobs** (API-P1-001)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query `type` (interface or job code, for example INT-01), `status`, `from`, `to` (business dates) |
| Response 200 | `Job[]`: id (load_run.id), type (interface_id), businessDate, status, startedAt, endedAt, checks (object: check code to PASS, FAIL, HELD n or NOT_APPLICABLE, plus SAMPLE) |
| 401, 403, 503 | No session (MSG-P4-001); role lacks the right (MSG-P4-002); database unavailable |
| Authorization | Platform administration R, scope All |
| Idempotency | Read only |

**POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun** (API-P1-002)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path `jobId` (load_run.id); header `Idempotency-Key` |
| Response 200 | `Job` of the new attempt, status RUNNING |
| 404 | No load_run with that id (MSG-P4-003, as the E404 response defines) |
| 409 | The load for that interface and date is COMPLETED or RUNNING (MSG-P1-011) |
| 401, 403, 503 | As above; 403 uses MSG-P4-002 |
| Authorization | Platform administration U |
| Idempotency | A second call with the same Idempotency-Key returns the first response |

**Published interface** (other P1 packages and P3 read the load result)

```java
public interface LoadRunQuery {
    Optional<LoadRunView> completedLoad(String interfaceId, LocalDate businessDate); // empty when not COMPLETED
}

public record LoadRunView(UUID loadRunId, String interfaceId, LocalDate businessDate, String status,
        int rowsLoaded, int rowsHeld, OffsetDateTime endedAt) {}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dataengine/load` for the load framework and `recovery/dataengine/load/als` for the ALS steps; Java packages `recovery.dataengine.load` and `recovery.dataengine.load.als`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CollinsLoadJob | Job (Quartz) | JOB-01 trigger; computes the expected business date from the working day calendar; launches the Spring Batch job per interface in order |
| AlsLoadJobConfig | Job (Spring Batch) | Steps: open run, blocking checks, tolerance checks, map and write, movement check, sample check, close run |
| LoadCheckRunner | Service | Runs DQ checks by SQL over the staging records and returns a CheckResult per check code |
| SourceMappingService | Service | Reads the approved mapping version and code map in force; maps one staging record to a loan_account or account_payment value |
| LoanAccountWriter, AccountPaymentWriter | Repository | Upsert by account_no; insert by (account_id, payment_code) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING |
| LoadRun, DqException | Entity | Map load_run and dq_exception |
| LoadRunRepository, DqExceptionRepository | Repository | Read and write the module's load tables |
| LoadRunQueryService | Service and Published interface | Implements LoadRunQuery over load_run |
| LoadEventPublisher | Service | Writes LoadCompleted and LoadRefused to the outbox |
| LoadAlertNotifier | Service | Sends MSG-P1-002 and MSG-P1-006 through the ACE notification path to the recipient groups in reference data |
| RecoveryDataEngineController | Controller | GET /admin/jobs and POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun |

**Database.** Writes loan_account (all columns) and account_payment (all columns). Adds `uk_loan_account_no UNIQUE (account_no)` if not present and `uk_account_payment UNIQUE (account_id, payment_code)`. Migration `V1_003__load_run.sql` creates load_run, dq_exception, source_field_map and source_code_map, and creates `uk_load_run_active UNIQUE (interface_id, business_date) WHERE status IN ('RUNNING','COMPLETED')` and an index on dq_exception (product_code, raised_on).

**Configuration and reference data.** Parameters `load.window.end`, `load.retry.interval`, `load.hold.tolerance.pct`, `load.movement.tolerance.pct`, `load.sample.size` from the parameter catalog (RWB-E1-042), loaded by the center of excellence analyst. Mapping version and code map for INT-01 and INT-02, loaded by the reference data administrator and approved by the data steward. Staging table names and alert recipient groups as configuration, set by the platform administrator. Working day calendar from the reference data service (RWB-E1-043).

**Build steps**

1. Write migration V1_003 and the LoadRun, DqException, SourceFieldMap and SourceCodeMap entities with repositories; test the unique run key.
2. Write LoadCheckRunner with the seven checks for INT-01 and INT-02 as SQL over staging; unit test each check with a pass and a fail fixture, and the 0.50 and 10.00 percent boundaries.
3. Write SourceMappingService with the transformations COPY_TRIM, SUM, TO_DATE_BE, TO_NUMERIC_2, BOOLEAN_YN, CODE_MAP and BUSINESS_DATE; refuse when the mapping version has no approval.
4. Write the INT-01 step: map and upsert loan_account in one transaction; write held records to dq_exception.
5. Write the INT-02 step in the same way into account_payment, run after INT-01 completes.
6. Write the movement and sample checks and store their results in load_run.check_results.
7. Write LoadRunQueryService, LoadEventPublisher and LoadAlertNotifier; test that a refusal writes the LoadRefused event in the same transaction as the REFUSED status.
8. Write CollinsLoadJob with the cron, the hourly retry to the window end, @DisallowConcurrentExecution and the clustered job store.
9. Write the two endpoints with capability checks, the Job mapping and the Idempotency-Key handling.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.als-load`. Off: JOB-01 skips the INT-01 and INT-02 steps and records nothing.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and a full synthetic run of 184,500 accounts completes in under 30 minutes in SIT.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-002 | Load refused at a check | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-P1-006 | Movement outside the expected range | The {source} load for {date} changed by {pct} percent against the previous load, outside the expected {limit} percent. Check it before use. |
| MSG-P1-011 | Rerun of a completed or running load | The {source} load for {date} is already complete or running. It was not run again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

No screen in this story. The data steward and the platform administrator receive the alerts and read the run through GET /admin/jobs. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor shows the same runs with the states Running, Failed and Complete from E2.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: tolerances, window times, sample size, mappings and code maps are data.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. dq_exception.record_key holds the account key only; test data is synthetic in DEV and masked in SIT.
- No read of another module's tables. Reference values come through the P4 published interface; case data is not read.
- No call to ALS or any system of record; the only input is the COLLINS staging records (ADR-005).
- No partial load is ever visible: the write is one transaction per interface.

## RWB-E1-004 EFS extract load

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-004 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-04 Load collections status and contact history from EFS |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-003 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | 06 Take over and own the case |
| Decision | D6 entry, X6 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-003, RWB-E1-015, RWB-E1-002 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **the EFS contacts and promises for accounts at 90 days past due loaded each working day from the COLLINS daily batch**, so that **the contact history is on the case from its first day**.

### 2. Business rationale

When an account moves from collections to recovery today, the case owner does not see what the phone team agreed with the customer, and the customer can be called twice or asked again for a promise already made. This story loads the EFS contact and promise records (INT-07) into the collections history held by the Workbench, checked like every other load, and puts the latest contact on the case list. It meets REQ-RDF-003 and serves NFR-014 (collections data ingested at start of day).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-003 is done: the load framework, load_run, dq_exception, source_field_map and source_code_map exist, and DP01 is loaded.
- RWB-E1-002 is done: the case list step and case_list_row exist.
- RWB-E1-015 is done: FreshnessStampService records each load and its freshness check marks a product stale at its expected-by time (08:00 for DP05).
- COLLINS writes the INT-07 records and their trailer for the business date into its staging tables in the ACE database.
- The mapping version for INT-07 and the code maps for LOV-ACTION-CODE and LOV-CONTACT-RESULT are loaded; the mapping version is approved with the EFS system owner's sign-off reference.
- Parameters are loaded: `load.window.end.INT-07` 08:00 (assumed, NFR-014 and DL11), `efs.history.action.codes` (the named list of action codes; assumed every code in LOV-ACTION-CODE until the business lead names the list, DL29).
- JOB-01 runs as service identity SY-DATALOAD.

### 4. Flow

1. Quartz: JOB-01 attempt reaches the INT-07 step after the INT-01 step has completed for the business date.
2. System: opens a load_run for INT-07 and checks that the mapping version in force is approved.
3. System: runs DQ-036 business date, DQ-037 structure, DQ-038 control total and DQ-039 keys; any failure refuses the load.
4. System: runs DQ-040 references (the account key matches loan_account) and DQ-041 lists of values; above 0.50 percent the load is refused.
5. System: skips records whose action code is not in the named list and counts them.
6. System: maps the remaining records and inserts collections_history rows by their EFS record key in one transaction; a key already held is not inserted again.
7. System: writes held records to dq_exception, runs DQ-042 movement, calls `FreshnessStampService.recordLoad` for DP05 in the same transaction, sets the status COMPLETED and publishes LoadCompleted.
8. System: the case list step of JOB-04 reads the latest contact per case from collections_history and writes it to case_list_row.
9. System: at 08:00, if INT-07 is not COMPLETED, marks the load LATE and publishes LoadRefused with failed check LATE; the freshness check of RWB-E1-015 marks DP05 stale and alerts the data steward.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No complete INT-07 delivery by 08:00 | Status LATE; LoadRefused published; DP05 stale through RWB-E1-015; the previous history stays with its freshness stamp | MSG-P1-001 | AC3 |
| X2 | The mapping version in force has no approval | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | Unknown account keys at or below 0.50 percent (DQ-040) | Records held; the rest loaded | None (count on the load_run) | AC5 |
| X4 | Action code or call result missing from the code map (DQ-041) | Record held; the rest loaded | None (count on the load_run) | AC6 |
| X5 | Action code not in the named list (DL29) | Record skipped and counted; not held | None | AC7 |
| X6 | A record already held is delivered again | Not inserted again; counted as repeated | None | AC8 |
| X7 | Structure, control total or key check fails | Load refused in full; nothing written; LoadRefused published | MSG-P1-002 | AC9 |
| X8 | Rerun asked for a completed load | 409; nothing changes | MSG-P1-011 | AC10 |
| X9 | A role without Platform administration U asks for a rerun | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-004-11 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the load framework of RWB-E1-003; P3 copies the history into the interaction ledger at case entry in its own story |
| Negotiable | The window end and the named list of action codes are parameters |
| Valuable | The case owner sees the last contact and promise before calling the customer |
| Estimable | One batch step, one table, two code maps, two case list columns |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic EFS records |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: EFS extract load

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-11-30 and INT-01 is COMPLETED for 2026-11-30
    Given the INT-07 mapping version "EFS-MAP-1" is approved with sign-off reference "EFS-SIGN-2026-11-18" on 2026-11-18

  Scenario: AC1 Start-of-day file
    Given COLLINS completes the INT-07 staging records at 06:30 with 9,450 contact records for 2026-11-30 and a matching trailer
    When the JOB-01 attempt at 07:00 runs the INT-07 step
    Then collections_history holds 9,450 new rows with business date 2026-11-30, of which 1,320 carry a promise amount and date
    Then the INT-07 load_run shows 9,450 read, 9,450 loaded, status COMPLETED
    Then after the case list step, the row of case "RW-2026-000123" shows last contact 2026-11-30 15:42 and action code "PTP"

  Scenario: AC2 Mapping signed
    Given the INT-07 load for 2026-11-30 is COMPLETED
    When the data steward calls GET /admin/jobs with type "INT-07" and from 2026-11-30
    Then the Job shows mapping version "EFS-MAP-1"
    Then the mapping version in source_field_map carries approved_on 2026-11-18 and approval reference "EFS-SIGN-2026-11-18"

  Scenario: AC3 Late file
    Given COLLINS has not completed the INT-07 staging records for 2026-11-30 by 08:00
    When the INT-07 window check runs at 08:00
    Then the INT-07 load_run status is LATE
    Then one LoadRefused event is in the outbox with failedCheck "LATE"
    Then FreshnessQuery returns DP05 with business date 2026-11-27 and status STALE
    Then the data steward group receives MSG-P1-001 "DP05 Interaction is from 2026-11-27. Today's load has not arrived."
    Then collections_history keeps every row for 2026-11-27 unchanged

  Scenario: AC4 Mapping not approved
    Given the INT-07 mapping version in force is "EFS-MAP-2" with no approval
    When the INT-07 step runs
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P1-002 "The INT-07 load for 2026-11-30 was refused: mapping version EFS-MAP-2 not approved. The previous load is still in use."
    Then the system writes no collections_history row

  Scenario: AC5 Unknown account keys within the tolerance
    Given 40 of the 9,450 records name an account key not in loan_account, which is 0.42 percent
    When the INT-07 step runs
    Then the system writes 9,410 rows
    Then the system writes 40 dq_exception rows with check code "DQ-040"

  Scenario: AC6 Code missing from the code map
    Given 6 records carry call result "R99", which is not in the code map for LOV-CONTACT-RESULT
    When the INT-07 step runs
    Then the system holds the 6 records in dq_exception with check code "DQ-041"
    Then the system writes 9,444 rows

  Scenario: AC7 Action code outside the named list
    Given the named list efs.history.action.codes does not hold action code "SYS01"
    Given 120 records carry action code "SYS01"
    When the INT-07 step runs
    Then the system does not writ the 120 records and not held
    Then the load_run check results show "SKIPPED_ACTION_CODE" = 120

  Scenario: AC8 Same contact delivered again
    Given collections_history already holds EFS record key "EFS-77001234" from the load of 2026-11-27
    Given the 2026-11-30 delivery holds "EFS-77001234" again
    When the INT-07 step runs
    Then collections_history holds one row for "EFS-77001234"
    Then the load_run check results show "REPEATED" = 1

  Scenario: AC9 Blocking check fails
    Given the INT-07 staging records have no column "Call Result"
    When the INT-07 step runs
    Then the system refuses the load at DQ-037 with MSG-P1-002 naming "structure"
    Then one LoadRefused event is in the outbox with failedCheck "DQ-037"

  Scenario: AC10 Rerun of a completed load
    Given the INT-07 load for 2026-11-30 is COMPLETED
    When the platform administrator calls POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun for it
    Then the response is 409 with MSG-P1-011
    Then collections_history is unchanged
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Contact history before day 90 comes from EFS through COLLINS | Mapping rule "Contact history"; DL29; ADR-005 |
| BR2 | A load is refused in full on a failed business date, structure, control total or key check, or an unapproved mapping | DQ-036 to DQ-039; CTL-02; Principle 1 |
| BR3 | Records with unknown references or codes are held; above 0.50 percent the load is refused | DQ-040, DQ-041; parameter load.hold.tolerance.pct (assumed, DL25) |
| BR4 | Only action codes in the named list are kept | DL29 (assumed: every code until the list is named) |
| BR5 | INT-07 must be complete by 08:00, or the load is LATE and the product is stale | Parameter load.window.end.INT-07 and data_product.expected_by (assumed, NFR-014, DL11); MSG-P1-001 |
| BR6 | A record already held is not written twice | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | The latest contact per case is the latest contact_at across the case's accounts | FEAT-RDF-04 |
| BR8 | Free-text notes are not loaded; only codes, dates and amounts | Mapping rule "Personal data"; CTL-11 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the INT-07 load_run status (RUNNING to COMPLETED, REFUSED or LATE). The freshness status of DP05 is changed by RWB-E1-015.

| RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-SECADM | List runs (Platform administration R) |

### 12. Contract

**Job step**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | JOB-01 COLLINS load check and intake, INT-07 step, at each hourly attempt after INT-01 completes; window check at 08:00 |
| Job name | JOB-01 COLLINS load check and intake |
| Input | COLLINS staging records and trailer for INT-07 (table name `rwb.p1.collins.int07.table`) |
| Output | collections_history; load_run; dq_exception; the DP05 freshness stamp through FreshnessStampService |
| Events published | LoadCompleted (EV-26) with source INT-07; LoadRefused (EV-27) with the failed check |
| Idempotency key | interface_id and business_date for the run; efs_record_key for each row (unique) |
| Restart | A refused or late load is rerun by the next attempt or by POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun; the write is one transaction |

**Published interface** (P3 reads the history at case entry)

```java
public interface CollectionsHistoryApi {
    List<CollectionsContact> contactsForAccount(String accountNo, LocalDate fromDate, LocalDate toDate);
}

public record CollectionsContact(String efsRecordKey, OffsetDateTime contactAt, String actionCode,
        String actionContactStatus, String contactResult, BigDecimal promiseAmount, LocalDate promiseDate) {}
```

**GET /admin/jobs** and **POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun** as in RWB-E1-003; the Job for INT-07 adds `mappingVersion` and the checks SKIPPED_ACTION_CODE and REPEATED inside `checks`.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dataengine/load/efs`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.load.efs`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| EfsLoadStepConfig | Job (Spring Batch step in JOB-01) | Checks, maps and writes INT-07 |
| EfsWindowCheck | Job (Quartz trigger at 08:00) | Marks INT-07 LATE and publishes LoadRefused when the step has not completed |
| CollectionsHistory | Entity | Maps collections_history |
| CollectionsHistoryRepository | Repository | Inserts with ON CONFLICT (efs_record_key) DO NOTHING; returns the inserted count |
| CollectionsHistoryService | Service and Published interface | Implements CollectionsHistoryApi |
| LoadCheckRunner, SourceMappingService | Service (from RWB-E1-003) | Run DQ-036 to DQ-042; map through EFS-MAP-1 and the code maps |
| CaseListLastContactEnricher | Service | Called by the case list step; writes last_contact_at and last_action_code per case |

**Database.** Migration `V1_004__collections_history.sql` creates collections_history (account_no varchar(20), efs_record_key varchar(40) unique, contact_at timestamptz, action_code varchar(10), action_contact_status varchar(20), contact_result varchar(20), promise_amount numeric(18,2), promise_date date, business_date date, standard columns) with an index on (account_no, contact_at desc); adds approval_ref varchar(200) to source_field_map; adds last_contact_at timestamptz and last_action_code varchar(10) to case_list_row.

**Configuration and reference data.** Parameters `load.window.end.INT-07` and `efs.history.action.codes` from the parameter catalog, loaded by the center of excellence analyst; the named list is set by the business lead (DL29). Mapping version EFS-MAP-1 and the code maps loaded by the reference data administrator; the data steward records the EFS owner's sign-off reference. Staging table name set by the platform administrator.

**Build steps**

1. Write migration V1_004, the entity and the repository; test the unique record key.
2. Configure the INT-07 checks in LoadCheckRunner and the mapping approval check; test refusal on an unapproved mapping.
3. Write EfsLoadStepConfig with the named list filter, the held records and the repeated count.
4. Write EfsWindowCheck at the INT-07 window end with the LATE status and LoadRefused; test with RWB-E1-015 that DP05 turns STALE and MSG-P1-001 is sent.
5. Write CollectionsHistoryService and a contract test for CollectionsHistoryApi.
6. Write CaseListLastContactEnricher and add it to the case list step; test the latest contact across two accounts of one case.
7. Add the mapping version and the new checks to the Job mapping of GET /admin/jobs.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.efs-load`. Off: JOB-01 skips the INT-07 step and the window check.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass.
