## RWB-E1-005 Excel and SharePoint inventory

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-005 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-07 Inventory the Excel and SharePoint trackers |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-005 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-043 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **every recovery team's Excel files, SharePoint lists and local files listed with owner, fields, update cycle and a load, retire or keep decision**, so that **each file can be loaded into its data product and then retired**.

### 2. Business rationale

The TDR, deed in lieu, litigation, NPA, debt sale and write-off teams each keep their own trackers, and no list says which trackers exist, who owns them or what replaces them. This story holds the tracker inventory as a versioned table in the Workbench, refuses an inventory that leaves out a team or a decision, and gives every tracker the status that the load (RWB-E1-010) and the retirement (RWB-E1-012) move forward. It meets REQ-RDF-005 and is the first step of REQ-RDF-006.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the data product catalog holds DP01 to DP14.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: the reference data service loads a table through the handler the owning module provides.
- Parameter `tracker.inventory.teams` holds the six team codes TDR, DIL, LIT, NPA, DEBT_SALE and WRITE_OFF (assumed codes; the values come from LOV-TEAM, loaded from the organization structure).
- The data steward has collected the inventory from the six team managers in the inventory template (one row per tracker).
- The reference data administrator (RW-REFADM) holds Reference data C; the data steward holds Reference data R and U.

### 4. Flow

1. Data steward: fills the inventory template, one row per tracker, with the decision and reason for each.
2. Reference data administrator: loads the file through `POST /admin/reference-loads` with table code `tracker_inventory`, version "TRK-2026.11" and valid from 2026-11-16.
3. System: `TrackerInventoryHandler.validate` checks every row: required fields, list values, a unique tracker code, a target data product for each LOAD decision, and at least one row for each of the six teams.
4. System: refuses the whole file and returns the row errors if any check fails.
5. Data steward: confirms the version as its owner through the reference data change process.
6. System: `TrackerInventoryHandler.apply` writes the rows in one transaction; a tracker already in the previous version keeps its status; a new tracker gets status LISTED, or KEPT for a KEEP decision.
7. Data steward or team manager: calls `GET /admin/trackers?team=LIT` and reads the trackers of the team with owner, fields, update cycle, decision and status.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The file has no row for one of the six teams | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-016 | AC3 |
| X2 | A row has no decision or no decision reason | Load refused in full; the row and field are named | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X3 | A row has a value outside its list (for example decision "MAYBE") | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-007 | AC5 |
| X4 | A LOAD row has no target data product | Load refused in full | MSG-GEN-001 | AC6 |
| X5 | A tracker code appears twice in the file | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-017 | AC7 |
| X6 | The same file is loaded again | Nothing is written; the load is reported as already done | MSG-P1-011 | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without Reference data R lists the trackers | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-005-09 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the catalog of RWB-E1-001 and the reference load service; the load and retire stories build on it |
| Negotiable | The team list is a parameter and the decisions are data; the story fixes the checks |
| Valuable | One list of every tracker with a decision, owned by one person |
| Estimable | One table, one handler, one read endpoint |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic inventory files |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Excel and SharePoint inventory

  Background:
    Given the parameter tracker.inventory.teams holds TDR, DIL, LIT, NPA, DEBT_SALE and WRITE_OFF

  Scenario: AC1 Inventory covers six teams
    Given an inventory file "TRK-2026.11" with 23 rows: 5 for TDR, 3 for DIL, 6 for LIT, 4 for NPA, 2 for DEBT_SALE and 3 for WRITE_OFF
    Given each row has tracker code, tracker name, location type, location, owner user ID, field list, update cycle, decision and reason
    When the reference data administrator loads it and the data steward confirms it
    Then tracker_inventory holds 23 rows for version "TRK-2026.11"
    Then GET /admin/trackers with team "LIT" returns 6 trackers, among them "LIT-07 Litigation case tracker" on SharePoint, update cycle WEEKLY, with its owner and 18 fields

  Scenario: AC2 Decision per file
    Given the loaded version "TRK-2026.11"
    When the data steward calls GET /admin/trackers
    Then every one of the 23 trackers has a decision LOAD, RETIRE or KEEP and a reason
    Then the 14 LOAD trackers each name a target data product, for example "LIT-07" names DP07
    Then the 14 LOAD and 6 RETIRE trackers have status LISTED and the 3 KEEP trackers have status KEPT

  Scenario: AC3 A team is missing
    Given an inventory file with no row for team DEBT_SALE
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-016 "The inventory has no row for team DEBT_SALE. List its trackers, or add one row with location type NONE."
    Then the system writes no tracker_inventory row

  Scenario: AC4 A row without a decision
    Given an inventory file whose row 7 has no decision
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-GEN-001 "Enter decision." for row 7

  Scenario: AC5 A value outside its list
    Given an inventory file whose row 9 has decision "MAYBE"
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-007 "Row 9: decision must be one of LOAD, RETIRE, KEEP."

  Scenario: AC6 A load decision without a target data product
    Given an inventory file whose row 12 has decision LOAD and no target data product
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-GEN-001 "Enter target data product." for row 12

  Scenario: AC7 A tracker code twice
    Given an inventory file in which tracker code "NPA-02" is on rows 15 and 16
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-017 "Row 16: tracker code NPA-02 appears more than once."

  Scenario: AC8 The same file loaded again
    Given version "TRK-2026.11" is in force
    When the reference data administrator loads the same file again
    Then the system writes nothing
    Then the response carries MSG-P1-011 "The tracker inventory load for 2026-11-16 is already complete or running. It was not run again."
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every recovery team's Excel files, SharePoint lists and local files are listed with owner, fields and update cycle | REQ-RDF-005 |
| BR2 | Each tracker has a decision: LOAD into a named data product, RETIRE without a load, or KEEP as out of scope, with a reason | REQ-RDF-005 |
| BR3 | The inventory covers the six teams named in the parameter | Parameter tracker.inventory.teams (assumed codes, LOV-TEAM) |
| BR4 | The inventory is a versioned load; a file with an exception is refused in full | Principle 1; reference data change process, step 3; CTL-08 |
| BR5 | A tracker already in the previous version keeps its status in the new version | Reference data change process, step 6 |
| BR6 | Field names in the field list carry a personal data tag; personal fields are not loaded later | CTL-11; PDPA minimization (FEAT-RDF-15) |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It sets the first status of each tracker: LISTED for a LOAD or RETIRE decision and KEPT for a KEEP decision. RWB-E1-010 and RWB-E1-012 move LISTED to LOADED, SIGNED_OFF and RETIRED.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the inventory file (Reference data C) |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Prepares the file; confirms the version as owner; lists trackers (Reference data R) |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Lists trackers (Reference data R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Supplies the team's rows; lists trackers (Reference data R) |
| Partner users | Refused with MSG-P4-002 |

Separation of duty: the reference data administrator who loads the version cannot confirm it.

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**Inventory load.** `POST /admin/reference-loads` (P4, Reference data C) with `file`, `table = tracker_inventory`, `validFrom`; response `ReferenceLoad` (id, table, validFrom, status, rows). P1 implements `ReferenceTableHandler` (signature in RWB-E1-001) as `TrackerInventoryHandler`. Errors: 422 with MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P1-007, MSG-P1-016 or MSG-P1-017 and the row number in `detail`; 409 when the file hash equals the version in force (MSG-P1-011). Idempotency: the file hash.

**GET /admin/trackers** (new endpoint, recorded in the additions file)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query `team`, `decision`, `status` (all optional) |
| Response 200 | `Tracker[]`: id, trackerCode, team, name, locationType, locationRef, ownerUserId, fields (name and personal tag), updateCycle, targetProduct, decision, decisionReason, status, inventoryVersion |
| 401, 403, 503 | MSG-P4-001; MSG-P4-002; database unavailable |
| Authorization | Reference data R |
| Idempotency | Read only |

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dataengine/tracker`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.tracker`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TrackerInventory | Entity | Maps tracker_inventory |
| TrackerInventoryRepository | Repository | Reads by team, decision and status; writes a version with carried-over status |
| TrackerInventoryHandler | Published interface implementation | ReferenceTableHandler for `tracker_inventory`: row checks, team coverage, apply |
| TrackerService | Service | Lists trackers with filters |
| RecoveryDataEngineController | Controller | GET /admin/trackers |

**Database.** Migration `V1_005__tracker_inventory.sql` creates tracker_inventory: tracker_code varchar(20), inventory_version varchar(20), team_code varchar(20), tracker_name varchar(120), location_type varchar(12) check in ('EXCEL','SHAREPOINT','LOCAL_FILE','NONE'), location_ref varchar(400), owner_user_id uuid, field_list jsonb, update_cycle varchar(10) check in ('DAILY','WEEKLY','MONTHLY','AD_HOC'), target_product varchar(4) references data_product, decision varchar(8) check in ('LOAD','RETIRE','KEEP'), decision_reason varchar(400), status varchar(12) check in ('LISTED','LOADED','SIGNED_OFF','RETIRED','KEPT'), valid_from date, standard columns; unique (tracker_code, inventory_version); index on (team_code, status).

**Configuration and reference data.** Parameter `tracker.inventory.teams` from the parameter catalog, loaded by the center of excellence analyst. Inventory template columns: tracker_code, team_code, tracker_name, location_type, location_ref, owner_user_id, field_list, update_cycle, target_product, decision, decision_reason. The list values for location_type, update_cycle, decision and status are proposed as new lists LOV-TRACKER-LOCATION, LOV-UPDATE-CYCLE, LOV-TRACKER-DECISION and LOV-TRACKER-STATUS (recorded in the additions file).

**Build steps**

1. Write migration V1_005, TrackerInventory and its repository.
2. Write the row checks of TrackerInventoryHandler.validate: required fields, list values, unique code, target product for LOAD, LOV-TEAM membership; unit test each with a failing row.
3. Write the team coverage check against the parameter.
4. Write TrackerInventoryHandler.apply with the status carry-over from the previous version and the first status for new trackers.
5. Connect the handler to the reference data service and test a full load, a refused load and a repeated file.
6. Write TrackerService and the GET /admin/trackers method with the capability check.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.tracker-inventory`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and the SIT inventory version holds at least one row for each of the six teams.

| MSG-P1-011 | The same file loaded again | The {source} load for {date} is already complete or running. It was not run again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

## RWB-E1-006 Data quality rules v1

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-006 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-10 Run data quality rules on every load |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-008 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-002, RWB-E1-003, RWB-E1-043 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **ten data quality rules (missing owner, duplicate account, days past due mismatch, stale balance, missing collateral link and five more) run on every load, with a reason code on every failed row**, so that **the case list can be trusted**.

### 2. Business rationale

Today a wrong owner, an account on two cases or a balance that does not add up is found only when a case owner works the case. This story runs ten row-level rules, held as versioned data rows, after every load and after the daily case list build, and writes each failed row with its rule code to the exception list that the data steward and Power BI read. It meets REQ-RDF-008 and serves the data quality measures completeness 99.9 percent, validity 99.5 percent and uniqueness 100 percent.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-003 is done: loads write load_run and dq_exception and raise an internal completion call for each data product.
- RWB-E1-002 is done: case_list_row is built by the case list step of JOB-04.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: the reference data service loads a table through the handler the owning module provides.
- The rule version "DQR-2026.11" with the ten rules in section 13 is loaded and approved by the data steward.
- Parameter `case.entry.dpd` 90 (DL16) is loaded.
- The rules run as service identity SY-DATALOAD.

### 4. Flow

1. System: a load completes for a data product (for example INT-01 for DP01), or the case list step of JOB-04 completes for DP03.
2. System: reads the dq_rule rows in force for that data product on the business date.
3. System: builds the SQL for each rule from its rule type template and its parameters, using only table and column names that sys_fields holds for P1-owned tables.
4. System: runs each rule and collects the failing records.
5. System: writes one dq_exception row per failing record with the rule code as check and reason code, the rule version, the record key and the business date.
6. System: sets CLEARED on any OPEN exception of the same rule and record that no longer fails.
7. System: writes the count per rule to the load_run check results.
8. System: the JOB-04 publish step writes the open and new exceptions for the business date to the data lake extract for Power BI.
9. Data steward: reads the exceptions through GET /admin/data-quality/exceptions or the Power BI data quality report.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A rule version names a field not in the data dictionary | The rule load is refused in full | MSG-P1-005 | AC4 |
| X2 | A rule row names a rule type or a table outside the allowed set | The rule load is refused in full | MSG-P1-007 | AC5 |
| X3 | One rule fails at run time (for example a statement timeout) | That rule is ERROR on the load_run; the other rules run; the data steward is alerted | MSG-P1-015 | AC6 |
| X4 | The rules run again for the same load | No second exception row for the same rule, record and load | None | AC7 |
| X5 | A rule's valid to date has passed or its valid from date is in the future | The rule does not run | None | AC8 |
| X6 | A record that failed before now passes | Its open exception is set CLEARED with the date | None | AC9 |
| X7 | A role without Platform administration R lists exceptions | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-006-10 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs on the outputs of the load stories and the case list; no case is changed |
| Negotiable | The rules, their parameters and their versions are data; the story fixes the rule types and the run points |
| Valuable | Every failed row is visible with a reason before a case owner meets it |
| Estimable | Seven rule type templates, one runner, one handler, one read endpoint |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic data |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Data quality rules v1

  Background:
    Given the rule version "DQR-2026.11" with rules DQ01 to DQ10 is in force from 2026-11-20
    Given the business date is 2026-11-30

  Scenario: AC1 Rules run daily
    Given the case list for 2026-11-30 holds three accounts "ACC0000301", "ACC0000302" and "ACC0000303", each linked to two open cases
    When the case list step of JOB-04 completes and the rules for DP03 run
    Then the system writes three dq_exception rows with check code and reason code "DQ02", rule version "DQR-2026.11" and raised_on 2026-11-30
    Then GET /admin/data-quality/exceptions with product "DP03" and from 2026-11-30 returns the three rows
    Then the load_run check results show "DQ02" = 3

  Scenario: AC2 Report in Power BI
    Given the rules for 2026-11-30 wrote 3 DQ02, 14 DQ05 and 2 DQ06 exceptions
    When the JOB-04 publish step writes the data quality extract for 2026-11-30
    Then the extract holds 19 rows with rule code, rule name, data product, business date and record key
    Then the Power BI data quality report shows failures by rule, by data product and by day for 2026-11-30

  Scenario: AC3 Rule as data
    Given the reference data administrator loads rule version "DQR-2026.12" adding rule DQ11 of type RANGE on loan_account.interest_rate with maximum 30.0000, valid from 2026-12-01
    Given the data steward approves the version
    When the INT-01 load for 2026-12-01 completes
    Then DQ11 runs with no deployment and writes 2 exceptions for the 2 accounts with interest rate 32.5000
    Then DQ01 to DQ10 run unchanged

  Scenario: AC4 Rule naming an unknown field
    Given a rule version in which DQ12 names loan_account.balance_total
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-005 "loan_account.balance_total is not in the data dictionary."
    Then the rule version in force stays "DQR-2026.11"

  Scenario: AC5 Rule on a table outside P1
    Given a rule version in which DQ12 is of type NOT_NULL on recovery_case.owner_user_id
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-007 "Row 12: target_entity must be one of loan_account, account_payment, party, contact_point, collateral, account_collateral, collections_history, case_list_row."

  Scenario: AC6 One rule fails at run time
    Given the statement for DQ05 times out after the 60 second limit
    When the rules for DP03 run
    Then the system shows DQ05 as ERROR on the load_run and the other rules for DP03 write their exceptions
    Then the data steward group receives MSG-P1-015 "Rule DQ05 did not run for 2026-11-30: statement timeout. The other rules ran."

  Scenario: AC7 Rules run twice for one load
    Given the rules for the INT-01 load of 2026-11-30 have written 2 DQ06 exceptions
    When the rules run again for the same load
    Then dq_exception still holds 2 DQ06 rows for that load

  Scenario: AC8 Rule outside its valid dates
    Given DQ07 has valid to 2026-11-30
    When the INT-01 load for 2026-11-30 completes
    Then DQ07 does not run and the load_run check results do not list DQ07

  Scenario: AC9 Exception cleared when the record passes
    Given an OPEN DQ01 exception for case account "ACC0000777" raised on 2026-11-27
    Given the case of "ACC0000777" now has an owner
    When the rules for DP03 run for 2026-11-30
    Then the system sets the exception CLEARED with cleared_on 2026-11-30
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Data quality rules run on every load and every failed row carries a reason code | REQ-RDF-008; FEAT-RDF-10 |
| BR2 | Each rule is a versioned data row with valid from, valid to, approver and test case; a change needs no code release | Principle 1; DT02; CTL-08 |
| BR3 | A rule version takes effect on its valid from date | R-UNI-38 |
| BR4 | A rule version with an exception is refused in full | Reference data change process, step 3 |
| BR5 | Rules read only P1-owned tables and columns that the data dictionary holds | ADR-002; sys_fields |
| BR6 | Row rule codes DQ01 to DQ10 are separate from the load checks DQ-001 to DQ-098, which refuse or hold a whole load | Data quality and reconciliation rules, load checks |
| BR7 | DQ03 uses the entry threshold of 90 days past due | Parameter case.entry.dpd (DL16) |
| BR8 | A duplicate case found by DQ02 is merged by P3 under its own rule | R-UNI-17 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the status of dq_exception rows (OPEN to CLEARED) and adds rule results to the load_run check results.

| RW-BIANAL, reporting and BI analyst | Builds the Power BI data quality report (Reporting CRUD) |

Separation of duty: the reference data administrator who loads a version cannot approve it.

### 12. Contract

**Rule run**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | The completion of each load step in JOB-01 and JOB-09 (internal call `DataQualityRuleRunner.runFor(productCode, loadRunId)`); the case list step of JOB-04 for DP03 |
| Job name | JOB-01 COLLINS load check and intake; JOB-09 File loads; JOB-04 Daily reconciliation |
| Input | dq_rule rows in force; the P1 tables named by the rules |
| Output | dq_exception; load_run check results; the data quality extract in the JOB-04 publish step |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | load_run_id, check_code and record_key (unique) |
| Restart | Rules run again in full on rerun of the load; existing rows are not duplicated |

**GET /admin/data-quality/exceptions** (API-P1-003)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query `product` (data product code, for example DP03), `from`, `to` (raised_on dates) |
| Response 200 | `DataQualityException[]`: id, product, check (rule or check code), record (record key), raisedOn |
| 401, 403, 503 | MSG-P4-001; MSG-P4-002; database unavailable |
| Authorization | Platform administration R, scope All |
| Idempotency | Read only |

**Rule load.** `POST /admin/reference-loads` (P4, Reference data C) with `table = dq_rule`; P1 implements `ReferenceTableHandler` (signature in RWB-E1-001) as `DqRuleHandler`. Refusals return 422 with MSG-P1-005 or MSG-P1-007.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dataengine/quality`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.quality`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DqRule | Entity | Maps dq_rule |
| DqRuleRepository | Repository | Reads the rules in force by product and date |
| DqRuleHandler | Published interface implementation | ReferenceTableHandler for `dq_rule`: validates entity, field, rule type and parameters against sys_fields and the allowed set |
| RuleTypeTemplates | Service | One SQL template per rule type: NOT_NULL, UNIQUE_ACROSS, RANGE, SUM_EQUALS, EXISTS_LINK, MAX_AGE_DAYS, FIELD_BEFORE |
| DataQualityRuleRunner | Service | Runs the rules of one product for one load with a 60 second limit per rule; writes and clears exceptions |
| DqExceptionRepository | Repository (from RWB-E1-003) | Insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; clear by rule and record |
| DataQualityExtractWriter | Service | Writes the day's exceptions to the lake extract in the JOB-04 publish step |
| RecoveryDataEngineController | Controller | GET /admin/data-quality/exceptions |

**Database.** Migration `V1_006__dq_rule.sql` creates dq_rule (rule_code varchar(8), rule_version varchar(20), rule_name varchar(120), product_code varchar(4), target_entity varchar(60), rule_type varchar(15), rule_params jsonb, valid_from date, valid_to date, approved_by uuid, test_case_id varchar(20), standard columns, unique (rule_code, rule_version)); adds rule_version varchar(20) and cleared_on date to dq_exception and `uk_dq_exception UNIQUE (load_run_id, check_code, record_key)`.

**Configuration and reference data.** Rule version "DQR-2026.11", loaded by the reference data administrator and approved by the data steward:

| Rule | Name | Product | Table | Type and parameters |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DQ01 | Missing owner | DP03 | case_list_row | NOT_NULL owner_user_id where status is not NEW |
| DQ02 | Duplicate account | DP03 | case_list_row | UNIQUE_ACROSS account_id over case_id |
| DQ03 | Days past due mismatch | DP03 | case_list_row | RANGE days_past_due minimum case.entry.dpd |
| DQ04 | Stale balance | DP01 | loan_account | MAX_AGE_DAYS data_as_of 0 days behind the load business date, for accounts on the case list |
| DQ05 | Missing collateral link | DP03 | case_list_row | EXISTS_LINK account_collateral.account_id where product_group in MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE |
| DQ06 | Balance parts do not add up | DP01 | loan_account | SUM_EQUALS total_balance = principal_outstanding + interest_outstanding + fees_outstanding, tolerance 0.00 |
| DQ07 | Negative principal | DP01 | loan_account | RANGE principal_outstanding minimum 0.00 |
| DQ08 | Missing classification | DP01 | loan_account | NOT_NULL classification where days_past_due at or above case.entry.dpd |
| DQ09 | Party without a contact point | DP02 | party | EXISTS_LINK contact_point.party_id |
| DQ10 | Payment after the last payment date | DP01 | account_payment | FIELD_BEFORE payment_date not after loan_account.last_payment_date |

**Build steps**

1. Write migration V1_006, DqRule and DqRuleRepository; test the in-force query by date.
2. Write RuleTypeTemplates with bound parameters and identifiers taken only from sys_fields; unit test each template with a pass and a fail fixture.
3. Write DqRuleHandler with the checks for X1 and X2; connect it to the reference data service.
4. Write DataQualityRuleRunner with the per-rule limit, the ERROR result and the clear step.
5. Call the runner from the completion of each load step and from the case list step.
6. Write DataQualityExtractWriter and add it to the JOB-04 publish step.
7. Write the controller method with the capability check.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.dq-rules`. Off: no rule runs; loads complete as before.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and the ten rules of "DQR-2026.11" each have a passing and a failing test case named in test_case_id.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: rules, thresholds and product lists are rule rows and parameters; only the seven rule type templates are code.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. record_key holds account keys or record IDs, never names or contact values.
- No read of another module's tables. Rules on case data read case_list_row, which P1 builds from the P3 published interface.
- No rule text is executed as SQL: identifiers come from sys_fields and values are bound parameters.

## RWB-E1-007 Integration adapters for file loads and outbound files

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-007 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P2 Integration |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-21 Run the integration adapters for file loads and outbound files; FEAT-RDF-23 Queue and retry a failed interface call; FEAT-RDF-24 Raise an interface failure to the exception queue; FEAT-DRI-09 Run the file adapters for sources outside COLLINS; FEAT-DRI-10 Run file and SFTP adapters; FEAT-DRI-11 Route every outbound file through the integration adapters; FEAT-DRI-13 Detect and ignore a duplicate event |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-006, REQ-DRI-007, REQ-DRI-008 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.2; Business Requirements Program, section 5.2 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **one adapter pattern for every file load and outbound file, with file checks, a run log, retry and an exception queue**, so that **every later interface follows one pattern and a failed file is found on the day it fails**.

### 2. Business rationale

Each source outside COLLINS is reached today by hand or by a one-off file, and failures are found late. This story builds the one path every file takes in and out: checked, logged, retried on a schedule held as data, and moved to the exception queue with a task for a named owner after the retry limit. It meets REQ-DRI-006, REQ-DRI-007 and REQ-DRI-008 and serves the FSD P2 measure "outbound items in the exception queue over one day: zero".

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 (recovery schema) is done.
- The interface configuration rows for INT-10, INT-11, INT-14 and INT-15 are loaded by the reference data administrator (RW-REFADM), version "IF-2026.11".
- The load check rows DQ-057 to DQ-063 (INT-10 CCMS) and DQ-085 to DQ-091 (INT-15 WIN) are in force.
- The SFTP inbound and outbound folders exist in DEV and SIT, with credentials in the key store (NFR-052).
- The service identity SY-DATALOAD holds its Entra ID managed identity in each environment.
- The Quartz scheduler of the ACE service runs JOB-09 (file loads), JOB-10 (WIN outbound notices) and JOB-11 (outbox sender).

### 4. Flow

1. Scheduler: JOB-09 starts the file load for an inbound interface, for example INT-10 CCMS, at its time.
2. SY-DATALOAD: the FileLoadAdapter reads the interface configuration row in force and lists the inbound folder for the file pattern and business date.
3. SY-DATALOAD: the adapter writes an interface_run row with status RECEIVED, the file name, the file hash and the business date.
4. SY-DATALOAD: the adapter runs the file checks held as data (business date, structure, control total, keys) against the header and trailer.
5. SY-DATALOAD: when every file check passes, the adapter hands the records to the owning module's loader through its published interface and sets the run to LOADED with the record count.
6. Owning module: writes an outbound file request through OutboundFiles.enqueue, for example JOB-10 for the daily WIN notice file (INT-14).
7. SY-DATALOAD: the adapter writes one outbound_item with an idempotency key, in the same transaction as the request.
8. Scheduler: JOB-11 runs every minute; the OutboundSender sends each due item over SFTP and marks it SENT, then ACKNOWLEDGED when the acknowledgment file arrives.
9. SY-DATALOAD: on a transfer failure, the sender raises SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE for each case in the file and schedules the next attempt from the retry intervals.
10. SY-DATALOAD: after the last allowed attempt fails, the sender sets the item to EXCEPTION, raises OUTBOUND_FAILED for each case and a task for the owner role, and logs MSG-P2-001.
11. SY-DATALOAD: every consumer of an application event checks the idempotency key through IdempotencyGuard before it acts.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A file check fails (control total, business date, structure or keys) | The file is refused in full; no record is passed on; the previous load stays in use; the data product is marked stale; the data steward is alerted | MSG-P1-002 | AC2, AC4 |
| X2 | The outbound transfer fails | The item waits for the next attempt; the cases move to RETRY_QUEUE | MSG-GEN-006 | AC3 |
| X3 | The retry limit is reached | The item moves to the exception queue; a task goes to the owner role; the cases move to EXCEPTION_QUEUE | MSG-P2-001 | AC3 |
| X4 | No file is in the inbound folder by the cut-off | The run is written as MISSING; the data product is marked stale one business day after the file was due | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |
| X5 | The same file (same hash and business date) arrives again | The repeat is logged as DUPLICATE; nothing is loaded | None | AC6 |
| X6 | The same application event arrives twice with the same key | The second event is ignored and the hit is counted (R-UNI-40) | None | AC7 |
| X7 | Two sender instances pick the same item | Only one holds the row lock; the other skips it | None | AC8 |
| X8 | A platform administrator resends an item from the exception queue | The item returns to PENDING with attempt count 0 | MSG-GEN-005 | AC9 |
| X9 | A role without the right lists or resends exception items | Refused; nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-007-10 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the schema (RWB-E1-001); the EFS load (RWB-E1-004) and later file loads and outbound files reuse it |
| Negotiable | Retry counts, intervals, folders and owners are interface configuration rows; the story fixes the behavior |
| Valuable | Every file in and out is logged, retried and raised to a named owner from Epic 1 |
| Estimable | Four tables, two adapters, one sender job, one guard, two endpoints |
| Small | One squad, within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Integration adapters for file loads and outbound files

  Background:
    Given the interface configuration version "IF-2026.11" is in force
    Given interface "INT-14" WIN outbound has max attempts 3 and retry intervals 5, 15 and 45 minutes
    Given interface "INT-14" has owner role "RW-PLATADM"

  Scenario: AC2 File load checked
    Given a CCMS file "CCMS_COLL_20261109.txt" in SIT with 4,200 records and a trailer control total of 4,201
    When the adapter loads it
    Then the system refuses the file in full with failed check "DQ-059 Control total"
    Then the system passes no collateral record to the loader
    Then the CCMS data product keeps the load of business date 2026-11-02 in use and is marked stale
    Then the system alerts the data steward with message MSG-P1-002

  Scenario: AC3 Retry and exception queue
    Given the outbound WIN file "WIN_NOTICE_20261110.txt" for 85 notices on 85 cases
    Given the SFTP transfer fails on attempts 1, 2 and 3
    When the outbox sender runs
    Then attempt 2 starts 5 minutes after attempt 1 and attempt 3 starts 15 minutes after attempt 2
    Then each case in the file moves to route state "RETRY_QUEUE" after attempt 1 (R-UNI-33)
    Then after attempt 3 the item status is "EXCEPTION"
    Then each of the 85 cases moves to route state "EXCEPTION_QUEUE" with a task for role "RW-PLATADM" (R-UNI-34)
    Then the item shows in the exception queue with message MSG-P2-001

  Scenario: AC4 Every file check runs before any record is used
    Given a CCMS file whose business date in the header is 2026-11-02 when 2026-11-09 is expected
    When the adapter loads it
    Then the system refuses the file with failed check "DQ-057 Business date"
    Then the run row shows status "REFUSED" and record count 0

  Scenario: AC5 File missing at the cut-off
    Given no SVAF file for business date 2026-11-09 is in the inbound folder by Monday 04:00
    When JOB-09 runs
    Then the run row for "INT-11" shows status "MISSING"
    Then the system marks on 2026-11-10 the SVAF data product stale with message MSG-P1-001

  Scenario: AC6 Same file delivered twice
    Given the CCMS file for business date 2026-11-09 with hash "9f2c" was loaded at 04:05
    When the same file arrives again at 04:40
    Then the system writes a run row with status "DUPLICATE"
    Then the system passes no record to the loader

  Scenario: AC7 Duplicate application event ignored
    Given consumer "booking-confirmation" processed event key "EV-10:TRT-0001:v1"
    When the same event arrives again with the same key
    Then the consumer does not act
    Then the hit count for that key becomes 2 (R-UNI-40)

  Scenario: AC8 Two senders pick the same item
    Given outbound item "OB-0001" is due
    When two sender threads run at 10:00:00
    Then the system sends the file once
    Then the attempt count is 1

  Scenario: AC9 Resend from the exception queue
    Given outbound item "OB-0002" has status "EXCEPTION" after 3 attempts
    When a platform administrator resends it
    Then the item status is "PENDING" with attempt count 0
    Then the system writes the resend to the ACE audit log with the user and the time
    Then the response carries message MSG-GEN-005
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | No component calls a system of record directly; files move only through the adapters | ADR-005; DT12; REQ-DRI-006 |
| BR2 | A file that fails a business date, structure, control total or key check is refused in full and the previous load stays in use | DQ-057 to DQ-060; CTL-02; ifspec INT-10 error handling |
| BR3 | A data product is marked stale one business day after its file was due | ifspec INT-10 to INT-16, Retry column |
| BR4 | An outbound file is sent again on the intervals in its configuration row; after the third failure a task goes to the owning team | ifspec INT-14; interface_config.max_attempts (new) |
| BR5 | A system that is unavailable queues the action and retries | R-UNI-33, R-UNI-35, R-UNI-36 |
| BR6 | An item that fails after the retry limit moves to the exception queue with a task for the owner | R-UNI-34; REQ-DRI-007 |
| BR7 | An event with a key already processed by the consumer is ignored and the hit is counted | R-UNI-40; events.txt Rules sheet, Duplicates |
| BR8 | Retry counts, intervals, folders, patterns and owners are data rows, never code | Principle 1; DT02 |

### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANY_ACTIVE (route state) | SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE | First failed attempt of an outbound file for the case | RETRY_QUEUE |
| RETRY_QUEUE | RETRY_SUCCEEDED | A later attempt is sent | RESUME_STATE |
| RETRY_QUEUE | RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED | Attempt count equals max attempts | EXCEPTION_QUEUE |
| ANY_ACTIVE (route state) | DUPLICATE_EVENT | Key already processed | RESUME_STATE |

The case status (recovery_case.status) does not change. P3 moves the route state when the adapter raises the event. The story also changes interface_run.status (RECEIVED, LOADED, REFUSED, MISSING, DUPLICATE) and outbound_item.status (PENDING, SENT, RETRY, EXCEPTION, ACKNOWLEDGED).

### 12. Contract

**Job JOB-09 File loads.** Trigger: Quartz, weekly Monday 04:00 for CCMS, SVAF, RPS and WIN; monthly on the 2nd working day for AMIS and GL. Input: the file matching interface_config.file_pattern in inbound_path. Output: one interface_run row per file; records passed to the owning loader. Events: none from P2; the P1 loader publishes LoadCompleted (EV-26) or LoadRefused (EV-27). Idempotency key: interface_id + business_date + file hash. Restart: a rerun for the same key writes DUPLICATE and loads nothing; a run that stopped before LOADED is rerun from the start.

**Job JOB-10 WIN outbound notices.** Trigger: Quartz, daily 16:00. Input: approved notices from P6 through OutboundFiles.enqueue. Output: one outbound_item for the day's file. Idempotency key: "INT-14:" + business date. Restart: a second run for the same date finds the key and adds nothing.

**Job JOB-11 Outbox sender.** Trigger: Quartz, every minute. Input: outbound_item rows with status PENDING or RETRY and next_attempt_at at or before now, read with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Output: SFTP transfer; item status. Restart: an item in SENT without acknowledgment after 30 minutes (assumed; DL11) is retried.

**Published interfaces (package recovery.integration.adapter.api).**

```java
public interface FileLoadAdapter {
    InterfaceRunResult run(String interfaceId, LocalDate businessDate);
}
public interface OutboundFiles {
    UUID enqueue(OutboundFileRequest request); // request: interfaceId, idempotencyKey, payloadRef, caseIds
}
public interface IdempotencyGuard {
    boolean firstTime(String consumer, String idempotencyKey); // false means already processed; hit counted
}
public interface RecordLoader<T> { // implemented by the owning module, for example P1 CollateralLoader
    LoadOutcome load(String interfaceId, LocalDate businessDate, Stream<T> records);
}
```

**Endpoints (new, recorded in additions).**

| Method and path | Request | Response | Errors | Authorization | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /admin/outbound-items?status=EXCEPTION&interfaceId=INT-14 | Query: status, interfaceId, from, to | Array of OutboundItem: id, interfaceId, status, attemptCount, lastError, caseCount, ownerRole, updatedAt | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no right (MSG-P4-002); 503 store unavailable (MSG-GEN-006) | Platform administration, R | Read only |
| POST /admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend | None; header If-Match with the item version | OutboundItem | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown item (MSG-P4-003); 409 item not in EXCEPTION or version changed (MSG-GEN-004); 503 | Platform administration, U | A second resend of an item already PENDING returns 409 and changes nothing |

### 13. Solution plan

- **Package.** folder `src/main/java/recovery/integration/adapter`, Java package `recovery.integration.adapter`, with `api`, `inbound`, `outbound` and `idempotency` sub-packages.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| IntegrationController | Controller | The two exception queue endpoints; maps errors to problem responses |
| FileLoadAdapterImpl | Service | Lists the inbound folder, writes the run row, runs the file checks, passes records to the RecordLoader |
| FileCheckRunner | Service | Runs the business date, structure, control total and key checks from the DQ rows for the interface |
| OutboundFilesImpl | Service | Writes outbound_item in the caller's transaction |
| OutboundSender | Job | JOB-11; sends due items, applies retry intervals, moves items to EXCEPTION, raises case events through P3 |
| SftpTransport | Service | The only class that opens SFTP sessions; credentials from the key store |
| IdempotencyGuardImpl | Service | Inserts into processed_event; on conflict increments hit_count and returns false |
| InterfaceConfigRepository, InterfaceRunRepository, OutboundItemRepository, ProcessedEventRepository | Repository | The four P2 tables only |
| InterfaceRun, OutboundItem, ProcessedEvent, InterfaceConfig | Entity | JPA entities with the standard columns |
| FileLoadJob | Job | JOB-09 entry point per interface |
| AdapterBoundaryTest | Test | ArchUnit rule: no SFTP, file system or HTTP client use outside recovery.integration.adapter |

- **Database:** Flyway migration `V2026_11_07__p2_adapter_tables.sql` creates interface_config, interface_run, outbound_item and processed_event in schema recovery, each with the standard columns. Constraints: unique (interface_id, business_date, file_hash) on interface_run; unique (idempotency_key) on outbound_item; primary key (consumer, idempotency_key) on processed_event; index (status, next_attempt_at) on outbound_item.
- **Configuration and reference data:** interface_config rows for INT-10 to INT-16 and INT-25, loaded by RW-REFADM through the reference data load; DQ-057 to DQ-098 load check rows (P1 reference data); property `rwb.integration.sftp.host` per environment; SFTP key in the key store.
- **Build steps:**
  1. Write the migration and the four entities and repositories with repository tests.
  2. Build FileCheckRunner with one test per check type on synthetic header and trailer files.
  3. Build FileLoadAdapterImpl with the run row, refusal path (calls P1 DataProductStatus.markStale) and duplicate path.
  4. Build OutboundFilesImpl and OutboundSender with SKIP LOCKED, retry intervals from the row and the EXCEPTION move.
  5. Wire the P3 calls: CaseEvents.raise for SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE, RETRY_SUCCEEDED, RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED and OUTBOUND_FAILED; TaskApi.raiseTask for the owner task.
  6. Build IdempotencyGuardImpl and use it in every event listener of the recovery module through a shared base listener.
  7. Build the two endpoints with the access check and the ACE audit write on resend.
  8. Add the contract test template and the AdapterBoundaryTest to the pipeline.
- **Feature flag:** `rwb.integration.file-adapters`.
- **Done when:** the tests in section 16 pass, the boundary test runs in the pipeline, and the INT-10 and INT-14 contract tests pass in SIT.

### 17. Guardrails

- Outbound items carry case IDs, never addresses or names.

## RWB-E1-008 Decision log store v1, append only and hash chained

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-008 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P7 Decision center and log |
| Feature | FEAT-DRI-01 Store decision log entries append-only and hash-chained |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-001, REQ-DRI-002, REQ-DRI-003 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.7; Business Requirements Program, section 5.7 |
| L3 process | 17 Run the decision center |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **an append-only decision log store holding the seven field groups of every decision, with each entry hashed to the one before it**, so that **every decision from Epic 1 is recorded once, cannot be changed or deleted, and any change to a stored entry is found by recomputing the chain**.

### 2. Business rationale

Documentation and audit trail findings (5 of 29 in the audit summary behind CTL-06) show that why a route was chosen, who approved it and on what figures is spread across e-mails and files. This story builds the store that every later decision writes to: one record per decision with inputs, versions, recommendation, approver, final call, actions and outcome; refusal of every update and delete in the database; a single hash chain; and a verifier that finds a break. It meets REQ-DRI-001, REQ-DRI-002 and REQ-DRI-003 and implements ADR-009. The measure is every decision reproducible from the log (NFR-033).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: table decision_log_entry exists with the trigger tr_declog_append_only and the function refuse_change from Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql.
- The database role of the ACE service holds INSERT and SELECT on decision_log_entry and no UPDATE or DELETE grant.
- The ACE notification path can send to the Compliance and PDPA officer group, and the ACE incident path is available.

### 4. Flow

1. Writer (SY-DECLOG, built in RWB-E1-027): calls DecisionLogStore.append with a validated record inside the caller's transaction, as its last statement.
2. Store (DecisionLogStore): takes the chain lock (a PostgreSQL transaction advisory lock on the key "decision_log_chain").
3. Store: reads the chain_seq and entry_hash of the last entry; sets chain_seq to last plus 1 and prev_hash to the last entry_hash, or 64 zeros for the first entry.
4. Store: builds the canonical form of the entry and sets entry_hash to its SHA-256 in lower-case hexadecimal.
5. Store: inserts the row; the caller's transaction commits the action and the entry together and releases the lock.
6. Store: on any failure, raises DecisionLogUnavailableException; the caller's transaction rolls back and the action does not happen.
7. Database: refuses any UPDATE or DELETE on decision_log_entry through tr_declog_append_only; the ACE service writes the refused attempt to the ACE audit and SOC log.
8. Verifier (HashChainVerifier): reads entries in chain_seq order over a range, recomputes each entry_hash and checks each prev_hash against the entry before it.
9. Verifier: returns the result with the count checked, the last chain_seq and its entry_hash; on a break, it names the first entry that fails, raises an incident and sends MSG-P7-008 to Compliance within 15 minutes.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | An UPDATE or DELETE is attempted on a stored entry | The database refuses it; the attempt is written to the ACE audit and SOC log | None (database error, logged) | AC1 |
| X2 | A stored entry was changed outside the service, for example in a test environment | The verifier names the first entry whose hash does not match; an incident is raised; Compliance is told within 15 minutes | MSG-P7-008 | AC4 |
| X3 | Two writers append at the same moment | The chain lock orders them; chain_seq values are consecutive and each prev_hash names the entry before | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A decided entry is wrong | A new entry is written that names the corrected entry; the original stays | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The store cannot be written | The append fails, the caller's action rolls back and the caller shows its message | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without Decision log R reads an entry | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the table from RWB-E1-001; every later writer depends on it |
| Negotiable | The canonical form and the hash algorithm are fixed by this story; retention follows DL26 |
| Valuable | Every decision from Epic 1 is recorded once and any change to it is found |
| Estimable | One store, one migration, one verifier, two read endpoints |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Decision log store v1, append only and hash chained

  Background:
    Given the environment is DEV with synthetic data
    Given the decision log store is empty

  Scenario: AC1 Append only
    Given an entry with chain_seq 1 and final call "OWNER_ASSIGNED" is stored for case "RW-2026-000123"
    When an UPDATE setting final_call to "CASE_TRANSFERRED" and a DELETE of the entry are attempted through the ACE service's database role and again through the schema owner role
    Then the system refuses all four statements : by the missing grant for the service role, and with "decision_log_entry is append only" from tr_declog_append_only for the schema owner
    Then the entry is unchanged
    Then the system writes the refused attempts to the ACE audit log with the table, the operation and the entry ID

  Scenario: AC2 Hash chain
    Given 100 entries are appended
    When the chain verifier runs from chain_seq 1 to 100
    Then every entry_hash equals the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form
    Then every prev_hash equals the entry_hash of the entry before it, and the first prev_hash is 64 zeros
    Then the result holds count 100, last chain_seq 100 and that entry's entry_hash

  Scenario: AC3 Seven field groups
    Given an entry is appended for decision "D6" on case "RW-2026-000123" with rule "R-UNI-14", rule version "UNI-2026.11", inputs reference "inputs/2026-12-03/7f3a", recommendation, approver "U-6101", approval level "L6", final call "APPROVED", actions and outcome
    When it is read with GET /decision-log/{entryId}
    Then the response holds inputsRef, ruleId and ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId and approvalLevel, finalCall, actions and outcome
    Then decidedAt, prevHash and entryHash are present

  Scenario: AC4 Hash chain verified daily
    Given the store holds 10,000 entries
    Given the actions of the entry with chain_seq 7,412 were changed in the DEV database with the trigger disabled
    When the chain verifier runs from chain_seq 1 to 10,000
    Then the result names chain_seq 7,412 and its entry ID as the first break
    Then the system raises an incident and MSG-P7-008 is sent to the Compliance group within 15 minutes of the run start

  Scenario: AC5 Two appends at the same moment form one chain
    Given entries up to chain_seq 50 are stored
    When two writers append one entry each in parallel transactions
    Then the entries get chain_seq 51 and 52
    Then the prev_hash of 52 equals the entry_hash of 51, and the prev_hash of 51 equals the entry_hash of 50

  Scenario: AC6 A correction is a new entry
    Given entry "E-1" records owner "U-6102" by mistake
    When a correction entry is appended with corrects_entry_id "E-1" and the right owner "U-6103"
    Then entry "E-1" is unchanged
    Then GET /decision-log for case "RW-2026-000123" returns both entries in chain order with the correction naming "E-1"

  Scenario: AC7 A failed append leaves nothing behind
    Given the database connection for the store is closed in the test double
    When a writer appends an entry inside a transaction that also changes the case owner
    Then the system raises decisionLogUnavailableException
    Then the system stores no entry , the case owner is unchanged and chain_seq is not used

  Scenario: AC8 Reading an entry needs the Decision log right
    Given test user "U-6104" holds only RW-PHONECOL, whose Decision log letter is "-"
    When the user calls GET /decision-log/{entryId}
    Then the system refuses the call with status 403 and message MSG-P4-002
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every decision writes one entry holding the seven field groups: inputs, versions, recommendation, approver, final call, actions and outcome | REQ-DRI-001; DF-DEC-004 to DF-DEC-015 |
| BR2 | A stored entry is never updated or deleted; a correction is a new entry naming the entry it corrects | REQ-DRI-002; R-UNI-24; tr_declog_append_only in Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql; ADR-009 |
| BR3 | Entries form one chain in chain_seq order; prev_hash is the entry_hash of the entry before, and 64 zeros for the first | REQ-DRI-003; DF-DEC-017, DF-DEC-018 |
| BR4 | entry_hash is the SHA-256, in lower-case hexadecimal, of the canonical form: the entry's fields except entry_hash and the standard columns, as JSON with keys in alphabetical order, UTF-8, no spaces, timestamps in ISO 8601 UTC with microseconds, numbers as strings and empty fields as null | This story; ADR-009 |
| BR5 | The append is the last statement of the caller's transaction, so the action and its entry commit or roll back together | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR6 | A break found by the verifier is reported to Compliance within 15 minutes and raises an incident | NFR-035; REQ-DRI-003 |
| BR7 | Retention of entries follows the bank retention schedule | DL26 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. A stored entry has no states; it exists from its append onward.

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/decision/log` in the recovery module; Java package `recovery.decision.log`.
- Components:

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DecisionCenterAndLogController | Controller | GET /decision-log/{entryId} and GET /decision-log by case |
| DecisionLogStore | Service | Chain lock, chain_seq and prev_hash, canonical form, hash, insert |
| CanonicalEntryForm | Service | Builds the canonical JSON per BR4; one implementation used by the store and the verifier |
| HashChainVerifier | Service | Recomputes a range in chain_seq order in batches of 1,000 and reports the first break |
| ChainBreakNotifier | Service | Raises the incident and sends MSG-P7-008 to the Compliance group |
| DecisionCenterAndLogRepository | Repository | Inserts and reads decision_log_entry; no update or delete method exists |
| DecisionLogEntry | Entity | Maps decision_log_entry with the new columns; immutable |

- Database: Flyway migration V_E1_008__declog_chain.sql adds chain_seq bigint not null unique, corrects_entry_id uuid references decision_log_entry (id), actor_user_id uuid; makes case_id nullable with check constraint ck_declog_case (case_id IS NOT NULL OR decision_code LIKE 'AC-%'); adds index ix_declog_actor_time on (actor_user_id, decided_at) and ix_declog_rule on (rule_id, rule_version); revokes UPDATE and DELETE on decision_log_entry from the service role. The trigger tr_declog_append_only stays.
- Configuration and reference data: property rwb.decision.chain.genesis-hash (64 zeros); notification group for Compliance in the ACE notification path; retention class per DL26.
- Build steps:
  1. Write the migration and confirm the trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE; test AC1.
  2. Build CanonicalEntryForm with golden test vectors (fixed entry to fixed hash) checked into the test resources.
  3. Build DecisionLogStore with the advisory lock and the insert; tests for AC2, AC5 and AC7.
  4. Build the correction path (corrects_entry_id) and its read order; test AC6.
  5. Build HashChainVerifier in batches with the break report; test AC4 on 10,000 synthetic entries.
  6. Build ChainBreakNotifier on the ACE incident and notification paths.
  7. Build the two read endpoints with scope through the case; tests for AC3 and AC8.
- Feature flag: `rwb.decision.log-store`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass and the golden hash vectors give the same result on the build server and on a developer machine.

## RWB-E1-009 CCMS and SVAF loads

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-009 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-05 Load collateral records from CCMS; FEAT-RDF-06 Load appraisal values from SVAF |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-004 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | 07 Route, settle and claim; 09 Dispose assets and sell debt |
| Decision | D6.1 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-003, RWB-E1-015, RWB-E1-007 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **collateral records from CCMS and appraisals from SVAF loaded from their weekly files and linked to the loan accounts**, so that **the collateral and asset data product DP06 is current without anyone looking the values up in CCMS or SVAF**.

### 2. Business rationale

Case owners and sale officers look up collateral and appraisal values in CCMS and SVAF by hand today, and the appraisal used for a decision is often more than a year old without anyone seeing it. This story loads the weekly CCMS (INT-10) and SVAF (INT-11) files that the file adapters receive and check, links each collateral to its accounts, and flags every appraisal older than the age limit at load. It meets REQ-RDF-004 and supports control CTL-27 (an asset is priced only on an appraisal inside its age limit).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-007 is done: JOB-09 File loads in the P2 adapter receives each file, writes its interface_run, runs the business date, structure, control total and key checks, refuses a repeated file, and passes the records to the `RecordLoader` the owning module provides.
- RWB-E1-003 is done: load_run, dq_exception, the mapping tables and the load check runner exist, and loan_account is loaded.
- RWB-E1-015 is done: `FreshnessStampService.recordLoad` stamps each load, and its freshness check marks a weekly product stale when its file has not loaded.
- The mapping versions for INT-10 and INT-11 and the code maps for LOV-COLL-TYPE, LOV-PROVINCE and LOV-APPRAISAL are loaded and approved.
- Parameters are loaded: `appraisal.max.age` 365 days (assumed, MSG-S5-002 and CTL-27; DL11), `load.hold.tolerance.pct` 0.50 and `load.movement.tolerance.pct` 10.00 (assumed, DL25).
- S1 code owners accept the published interface `ValuationRecordApi` and its writer in package `recovery.valuation`, built in this story.
- The loaders run as service identity SY-DATALOAD.

### 4. Flow

1. File adapter (P2): JOB-09 receives the CCMS file for the week, passes its file checks, and calls `CcmsCollateralLoader.load("INT-10", businessDate, records)`.
2. System: opens a load_run for INT-10 with the interface_run reference.
3. System: runs DQ-061 references (each account link matches loan_account) and DQ-062 lists of values; above 0.50 percent the file is refused.
4. System: upserts collateral by collateral_no and replaces the account_collateral links of each loaded collateral, in one transaction.
5. System: runs DQ-063 movement, calls `FreshnessStampService.recordLoad` for DP06, sets COMPLETED, publishes LoadCompleted and returns the LoadOutcome to the adapter.
6. File adapter (P2): after INT-10, calls `SvafAppraisalLoader.load("INT-11", businessDate, records)` for the SVAF file.
7. System: opens a load_run for INT-11 and runs DQ-068 references (each appraisal names a collateral in DP06) and DQ-069 lists of values.
8. System: for each appraisal, computes the age in days at the file's business date and sets the stale flag when the age is above `appraisal.max.age`.
9. System: writes the appraisals through `ValuationRecordApi.upsertAppraisals` in the same transaction as the load_run status; runs DQ-070 movement and the sample check; stamps DP06; publishes LoadCompleted.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | An appraisal is older than the age limit | Loaded with stale_flag true and its age in days | None (flag on the row) | AC3 |
| X2 | The adapter refuses the CCMS file at a file check | The CCMS loader is not called; collateral keeps the previous week; the SVAF file still loads | None from P1 (the adapter alerts, RWB-E1-007) | AC4 |
| X3 | Account links to unknown accounts at or below 0.50 percent (DQ-061) | Those links held; the rest loaded | None (count on the load_run) | AC5 |
| X4 | An appraisal names a collateral not in DP06 (DQ-068) | The appraisal held | None (count on the load_run) | AC6 |
| X5 | A collateral type code is not in the code map (DQ-062) | The record held | None (count on the load_run) | AC7 |
| X6 | Unknown references above 0.50 percent | The file is refused in full; LoadRefused published; alert sent | MSG-P1-002 | AC8 |
| X7 | No SVAF file has loaded for the week | No INT-11 load_run; valuation unchanged; DP06 stale through RWB-E1-015 | MSG-P1-001 | AC9 |
| X8 | ValuationRecordApi fails during the write | The INT-11 transaction rolls back; status FAILED; rerun | None (alert to the platform administrator) | AC10 |
| X9 | The loader is called again for a file it has COMPLETED | Nothing is written; the earlier outcome is returned | None | AC11 |
| X10 | A role without Platform administration U asks for a rerun | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-009-12 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the file adapters of RWB-E1-007 and the load framework of RWB-E1-003; S1 uses the valuations from Epic 4 |
| Negotiable | The age limit and the tolerances are parameters; the mappings are data |
| Valuable | Collateral and appraisal values are on the case, with old appraisals flagged |
| Estimable | Two record loaders on one framework, one published interface |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic files |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: CCMS and SVAF loads

  Background:
    Given the CCMS and SVAF files for business date 2026-11-27 are due on Monday 2026-11-30 at 04:00
    Given the parameter appraisal.max.age = 365 is in force

  Scenario: AC1 Daily load of the weekly files
    Given the adapter has passed the CCMS file with 31,200 collateral records and 33,050 account links, and the SVAF file with 2,140 appraisals
    When JOB-09 calls the CCMS and SVAF loaders at 04:00
    Then collateral holds 31,200 rows from the file and account_collateral holds 33,050 links to loan_account rows
    Then valuation holds 2,140 appraisals written through ValuationRecordApi, each linked to its collateral
    Then the system stores an appraisal date "15/03/2569" in the file as 2026-03-15
    Then both load_runs show status COMPLETED and FreshnessQuery returns DP06 with business date 2026-11-27

  Scenario: AC2 Sample matches
    Given both loads for 2026-11-27 are complete
    When the sample check picks 50 cases at random that have collateral
    Then for all 50 the collateral type, the title deed number and the latest appraised value equal the CCMS and SVAF file values after mapping
    Then the INT-11 load_run check results show "SAMPLE" = "50 of 50"

  Scenario: AC3 Appraisal age
    Given appraisal "APR-0045521" has appraisal date 2025-11-26, which is 366 days before 2026-11-27
    Given appraisal "APR-0045522" has appraisal date 2025-11-27, which is 365 days before 2026-11-27
    When the SVAF loader runs
    Then the system stores "APR-0045521" with stale_flag true and age_days 366
    Then the system stores "APR-0045522" with stale_flag false and age_days 365

  Scenario: AC4 CCMS file refused by the adapter
    Given the adapter refuses the CCMS file for 2026-11-27 at DQ-059 control total
    When JOB-09 runs
    Then the system does not call the CCMS loader and no collateral or account_collateral row changes
    Then the SVAF loader is still called, and appraisals for collateral not yet in DP06 are held with check code "DQ-068"

  Scenario: AC5 Links to unknown accounts within the tolerance
    Given 120 of the 33,050 account links name an account key not in loan_account, which is 0.36 percent
    When the CCMS loader runs
    Then the system writes 32,930 links
    Then the system writes 120 dq_exception rows with check code "DQ-061" and the account key

  Scenario: AC6 Appraisal for an unknown collateral
    Given 4 appraisals name collateral numbers not in collateral
    When the SVAF loader runs
    Then the system holds the 4 appraisals in dq_exception with check code "DQ-068"
    Then the system writes 2,136 appraisals

  Scenario: AC7 Collateral type missing from the code map
    Given 2 CCMS records carry collateral type code "K7", which is not in the code map for LOV-COLL-TYPE
    When the CCMS loader runs
    Then the system holds the 2 records in dq_exception with check code "DQ-062"
    Then the system writes 31,198 collateral rows

  Scenario: AC8 Unknown references above the tolerance
    Given 180 of the 33,050 account links name an account key not in loan_account, which is 0.54 percent
    When the CCMS loader runs
    Then the system refuses the INT-10 load at DQ-061 and no collateral or account_collateral row changes
    Then one LoadRefused event is in the outbox with failedCheck "DQ-061"
    Then the data steward group receives MSG-P1-002 "The INT-10 load for 2026-11-27 was refused: references. The previous load is still in use."

  Scenario: AC9 SVAF file not received
    Given no SVAF file for 2026-11-27 has passed the adapter by Tuesday 2026-12-01 04:00
    When the data steward lists the jobs for INT-11
    Then there is no INT-11 load_run for 2026-11-27 and valuation keeps the appraisals of 2026-11-20
    Then FreshnessQuery returns DP06 with status STALE, and the data steward group has received MSG-P1-001 from the freshness check

  Scenario: AC10 Valuation write fails
    Given ValuationRecordApi raises an error after 1,000 of 2,140 appraisals
    When the SVAF loader runs
    Then the system stores no appraisal from the file
    Then the INT-11 load_run status is FAILED
    Then a rerun by the platform administrator stores 2,140 appraisals

  Scenario: AC11 Loader called twice for one file
    Given the INT-10 load for 2026-11-27 is COMPLETED for interface run "IR-0000451"
    When the adapter calls the CCMS loader again for "IR-0000451"
    Then no row changes and the loader returns the outcome of the completed load
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Collateral and appraisals arrive by weekly file through the file adapters; no call to CCMS or SVAF | INT-10, INT-11; JOB-09; ADR-005; RWB-E1-007 |
| BR2 | The adapter runs the business date, structure, control total and key checks; the loader runs the reference, list and movement checks | DQ-057 to DQ-070; CTL-02 |
| BR3 | Records with unknown references or codes are held; above 0.50 percent the file is refused | Parameter load.hold.tolerance.pct (assumed, DL25) |
| BR4 | An appraisal older than appraisal.max.age days at the business date is stale | Parameter appraisal.max.age, 365 assumed (MSG-S5-002, CTL-27; DL11) |
| BR5 | The data product is stale when the week's file has not loaded | INT-10 and INT-11 retry rule; RWB-E1-015; MSG-P1-001 |
| BR6 | Buddhist Era years become Gregorian; amounts are THB with two decimals | Mapping rules "Dates" and "Amounts" |
| BR7 | A file already loaded is not loaded again | R-UNI-40 |
| BR8 | Valuations are written only through the S1 published interface | ADR-002; DT08 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the INT-10 and INT-11 load_run status (RUNNING to COMPLETED, REFUSED or FAILED). The freshness status of DP06 is changed by RWB-E1-015.

| RW-DATASTEW, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-SECADM | List runs (Platform administration R) |

### 12. Contract

**Record loaders** (P1 implements the P2 interface of RWB-E1-007)

```java
public interface RecordLoader<T> {
    LoadOutcome load(String interfaceId, LocalDate businessDate, Stream<T> records);
}
// P1 provides CcmsCollateralLoader implements RecordLoader<CcmsCollateralRecord> for INT-10
// and SvafAppraisalLoader implements RecordLoader<SvafAppraisalRecord> for INT-11
```

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | JOB-09 File loads (P2), weekly Monday 04:00 or on a file arriving after its due time; the adapter calls INT-10 before INT-11 |
| Job name | JOB-09 File loads |
| Input | Checked records of the CCMS and SVAF files with the interface run ID and business date |
| Output | collateral, account_collateral, valuation (through S1), load_run, dq_exception, the DP06 freshness stamp; LoadOutcome (status, rows read, loaded, held, failed check) back to the adapter |
| Events published | LoadCompleted (EV-26) per interface; LoadRefused (EV-27) when the loader refuses |
| Idempotency key | interface_run_id; and interface_id with business_date for COMPLETED runs |
| Restart | A refused or failed load is rerun by POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun, which asks the adapter to pass the stored file again |

**Published interface** (S1, built in this story)

```java
public interface ValuationRecordApi {
    int upsertAppraisals(List<AppraisalRecord> records, UUID loadRunId); // insert or update by appraisal_no, in the caller's transaction
}

public record AppraisalRecord(String appraisalNo, UUID collateralId, String appraisalType, BigDecimal appraisedValue,
        BigDecimal forcedSaleValue, LocalDate appraisalDate, boolean staleFlag, int ageDays) {}
```

**GET /admin/jobs** and **POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun** as in RWB-E1-003; Job.type is INT-10 or INT-11.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folders `recovery/dataengine/load/ccms` and `recovery/dataengine/load/svaf`, Java packages `recovery.dataengine.load.ccms` and `recovery.dataengine.load.svaf`; the S1 interface in `recovery/valuation/api`, its writer in `recovery/valuation`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CcmsCollateralLoader | Service (RecordLoader) | DQ-061 to DQ-063; maps and writes collateral and account_collateral |
| SvafAppraisalLoader | Service (RecordLoader) | DQ-068 to DQ-070; maps, computes age and stale flag, calls ValuationRecordApi; sample check |
| AppraisalAgeCalculator | Service | Age in days from appraisal date to business date; stale when above the parameter |
| CollateralRepository, AccountCollateralRepository | Repository | Upsert by collateral_no; replace links per loaded collateral |
| ValuationRecordApi, ValuationRecordWriter | Published interface | S1 interface and its JPA writer for valuation |
| LoadCheckRunner, SourceMappingService, LoadEventPublisher | Service (from RWB-E1-003) | Run the checks; map through the approved versions; publish events |

**Database.** Writes collateral, account_collateral and valuation. Migration `V1_009__valuation_age.sql` adds stale_flag boolean not null default false and age_days integer to valuation, `uk_collateral_no UNIQUE (collateral_no)`, `uk_account_collateral UNIQUE (account_id, collateral_id)` and `uk_valuation_appraisal_no UNIQUE (appraisal_no)`, and adds interface_run_id uuid to load_run with a unique index on (interface_run_id).

**Configuration and reference data.** Parameters `appraisal.max.age`, `load.hold.tolerance.pct` and `load.movement.tolerance.pct` from the parameter catalog, loaded by the center of excellence analyst. Mapping versions and code maps loaded by the reference data administrator and approved by the data steward. File locations, due times and file checks belong to the adapter configuration of RWB-E1-007.

**Build steps**

1. Write migration V1_009 and the repositories; test the unique keys.
2. Write CcmsCollateralLoader with the INT-10 checks and the link replacement; test held links and the 0.50 percent boundary.
3. Write ValuationRecordApi and ValuationRecordWriter in the S1 package with a contract test.
4. Write AppraisalAgeCalculator; test 365 and 366 days and a leap year.
5. Write SvafAppraisalLoader with the INT-11 checks and the call to ValuationRecordApi in one transaction.
6. Connect both loaders to the adapter and test the repeated call for one interface run.
7. Add the FreshnessStampService call and the events; add the sample check over 50 cases with collateral.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.collateral-load`. Off: the loaders return status SKIPPED and write nothing.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-002 | Loader refuses a file above the tolerance | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-P1-001 | DP06 stale (sent by the freshness check of RWB-E1-015) | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-S5-002 is shown to the sale officer when pricing on a stale appraisal; that check belongs to S5.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The data steward receives the alerts and reads the runs through GET /admin/jobs. Collateral and valuations appear on the case record view through RWB-E1-023; SCR-44 shows the file loads from E2.
