| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **every inventoried tracker with a load decision loaded into its data product, with the row counts reconciled and the team manager's sign-off**, so that **the teams' own lists are held in the Workbench data store**.

### 2. Business rationale

The recovery teams hold case facts in trackers that only they can see, so the facts are lost when the tracker is retired unless they are loaded first. This story loads each tracker file with a LOAD decision into the tracker content of its target data product, rejects rows that cannot be matched to an account, drops fields tagged as personal data, and records the team manager's sign-off that the counts match the file. It meets the load and reconcile part of REQ-RDF-006; the retirement is RWB-E1-012.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-005 is done: the tracker inventory is loaded and each LOAD tracker names its target data product and its field list with personal data tags.
- RWB-E1-003 is done: load_run, dq_exception and loan_account exist and loan_account is loaded.
- The team has exported the tracker to an .xlsx or .csv file with a header row whose column names match the field list in the inventory.
- The data steward holds Reference data U. The team manager of the tracker's team holds Queue and allocation A.
- The tracker file store (ACE storage pattern, write-once container `recovery-tracker-files`) is configured.

### 4. Flow

1. Data steward: calls `POST /admin/trackers/{trackerId}/loads` with the tracker file.
2. System: checks the tracker has decision LOAD and status LISTED or LOADED, the file type, and that the file hash has not been loaded before.
3. System: stores the file in the write-once tracker file store, opens a load_run for the tracker and returns 202 with the Job.
4. System: checks that the header columns match the field list; a mismatch refuses the file.
5. System: for each row, rejects it if the account number is empty (TRK-01) or not in loan_account (TRK-02), and writes the rejection to dq_exception with the row number.
6. System: drops every field tagged as personal data and writes the other fields of each accepted row to tracker_row with the target data product, the file name and the row number, in one transaction; rows of an earlier load of the same tracker are replaced.
7. System: sets the file rows, loaded rows and rejected rows on the tracker, sets status LOADED and sends MSG-P1-008 to the data steward and the team manager.
8. Team manager: calls `POST /admin/trackers/{trackerId}/sign-off` with the row count of the file the team knows.
9. System: checks the signer is not the person who loaded the file, belongs to the tracker's team, and that the confirmed count equals the file rows, which equal loaded plus rejected rows.
10. System: sets status SIGNED_OFF with the signer and the time.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Rows with no account number | Rows rejected with TRK-01; the rest loaded; counts reported | MSG-P1-008 | AC3 |
| X2 | Fields tagged personal in the field list | Not stored; counted on the load_run | None | AC4 |
| X3 | Rows whose account number is not in loan_account | Rows rejected with TRK-02 | MSG-P1-008 | AC5 |
| X4 | The confirmed count at sign-off differs from the file rows | Sign-off refused; status stays LOADED | MSG-P1-009 | AC6 |
| X5 | The signer loaded the file | Sign-off refused | MSG-P7-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | The signer is a team manager of another team | Sign-off refused | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |
| X7 | The tracker's decision is not LOAD, or it is already SIGNED_OFF or RETIRED | Load refused; no file stored | MSG-P1-010 | AC9 |
| X8 | The same file is uploaded again | 409; nothing changes | MSG-P1-011 | AC10 |
| X9 | A new file for a tracker already LOADED and not signed off | The earlier rows are replaced; the earlier load_run is SUPERSEDED | MSG-P1-008 | AC11 |
| X10 | The file is not .xlsx or .csv | 415; nothing stored | MSG-P1-018 | AC12 |
| X11 | The header does not match the field list | Load refused at structure; no row written | MSG-P1-002 | AC13 |
| X12 | A role without Reference data U uploads a file | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-010-14 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the inventory of RWB-E1-005 and the account data of RWB-E1-003; the retirement story builds on it |
| Negotiable | The field list and the target product are data in the inventory; the story fixes the checks and the sign-off |
| Valuable | The teams' case facts are kept in the Workbench before any tracker is retired |
| Estimable | One upload endpoint, one sign-off endpoint, one batch step, one table |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic tracker files |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Only a tracker with decision LOAD is loaded, into the target data product its inventory row names | REQ-RDF-006; RWB-E1-005 BR2 |
| BR2 | A row is loaded only when its account number matches loan_account; other rows are rejected with a reason | References load check (INT load checks); CTL-02 |
| BR3 | Fields tagged personal in the field list are not stored | CTL-11; PDPA minimization (FEAT-RDF-15) |
| BR4 | The file rows equal the loaded rows plus the rejected rows, and the team manager confirms the file row count | REQ-RDF-006 |
| BR5 | The person who loaded the file cannot sign it off | Separation of duty, "a person may not approve a decision they prepared"; CTL-05 |
| BR6 | A file already loaded (same hash) is not loaded again | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | The stored file is write-once and kept as the read-only archive copy | ADR-007 storage pattern; REQ-RDF-006 |
| BR8 | Tracker rows are held as tracker content until the owning module maps them into its own tables | Case file item "Tracker content"; ADR-002 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the tracker status and the load_run status.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| LISTED | Tracker file loaded | Decision LOAD; structure check passed | LOADED |
| LOADED | New tracker file loaded | Not signed off | LOADED (earlier load_run SUPERSEDED) |
| LOADED | Sign-off | Counts match; signer is in the team and did not load the file | SIGNED_OFF |

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Uploads a tracker file (Reference data U) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager of the tracker's team | Signs off the counts (Queue and allocation A, scope Team) |
| SY-DATALOAD, data load from COLLINS | Runs the load; writes tracker_row, load_run, dq_exception and the tracker counts |
| RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-PLATADM, RW-AUDIT | List the runs (Platform administration R) and the rejected rows |

The sign-off is not an approval within the delegation of authority; no approval level applies.

### 12. Contract

**POST /admin/trackers/{trackerId}/loads** (new endpoint, recorded in the additions file)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: `file` (binary, .xlsx or .csv, at most 20 MB); header `Idempotency-Key` |
| Response 202 | `Job`: id, type "TRACKER", businessDate (upload date), status RUNNING, startedAt |
| 403 | Role lacks Reference data U (MSG-P4-002) |
| 404 | No tracker with that id (MSG-P4-003) |
| 409 | Decision not LOAD or status not LISTED or LOADED (MSG-P1-010); same file hash already loaded (MSG-P1-011) |
| 413 | File above 20 MB (MSG-P1-018) |
| 415 | File type not allowed (MSG-P1-018) |
| 401, 503 | MSG-P4-001; storage or database unavailable |
| Authorization | Reference data U |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header; the file SHA-256 hash per tracker |

**POST /admin/trackers/{trackerId}/sign-off** (new endpoint, recorded in the additions file)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | `TrackerSignOff`: confirmedFileRows (integer, required), comment (string, up to 400 characters) |
| Response 200 | `Tracker` with status SIGNED_OFF, signedOffBy, signedOffAt |
| 400 | confirmedFileRows missing (MSG-GEN-001) |
| 403 | Role lacks Queue and allocation A, or the signer is not in the tracker's team (MSG-P4-002) |
| 409 | Status not LOADED (MSG-P1-010); counts do not match (MSG-P1-009); signer loaded the file (MSG-P7-002); record changed by someone else (MSG-GEN-004) |
| Authorization | Queue and allocation A, scope Team |
| Idempotency | A second sign-off of a SIGNED_OFF tracker by the same user returns 200 with the same Tracker |

**Job.** The load runs as Spring Batch job `trackerLoadJob`, launched by the upload; it is not a scheduled job and has no entry in the daily timeline. Restart: a FAILED run is rerun by POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun (Platform administration U) from the stored file.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dataengine/tracker`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.tracker`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TrackerLoadController | Controller | The upload and sign-off endpoints; capability checks; Problem mapping |
| TrackerLoadService | Service | Pre-checks, file store, load_run, launch of trackerLoadJob |
| TrackerFileReader | Service | Reads .xlsx (Apache POI streaming) and .csv; checks the header against the field list |
| TrackerLoadJobConfig | Job (Spring Batch) | Row checks, personal field drop, replace and write of tracker_row, counts |
| TrackerRow | Entity | Maps tracker_row |
| TrackerRowRepository | Repository | Deletes the tracker's earlier rows and inserts the new ones in one transaction |
| TrackerSignOffService | Service | Team scope, separation of duty, count check, status change with optimistic lock |
| TrackerFileStore | Service | Writes the file to the write-once container and returns its reference and hash |

**Database.** Migration `V1_010__tracker_row.sql` creates tracker_row (tracker_id uuid references tracker_inventory, load_run_id uuid references load_run, row_no integer, account_no varchar(20), target_product varchar(4), source_file_name varchar(200), field_values jsonb, loaded_on date, standard columns; index on tracker_id and on account_no); adds file_rows, loaded_rows, rejected_rows integer, last_load_run_id uuid, signed_off_by uuid, signed_off_at timestamptz and source_file_ref varchar(400) to tracker_inventory; adds tracker_id uuid, rows_rejected integer, loaded_by uuid, source_file_name varchar(200) and source_file_hash char(64) to load_run, with a unique index on (tracker_id, source_file_hash), and SUPERSEDED to the load_run status values.

**Configuration and reference data.** The field list and target product per tracker come from the inventory (RWB-E1-005). File size limit `tracker.file.max.mb` 20 (assumed, DL11) from the parameter catalog. Container name set by the platform administrator.

**Build steps**

1. Write migration V1_010, TrackerRow and its repository.
2. Write TrackerFileStore and TrackerFileReader; test .xlsx, .csv, a wrong type and a header mismatch.
3. Write TrackerLoadService pre-checks (decision, status, hash) and the 202 response.
4. Write TrackerLoadJobConfig with TRK-01 and TRK-02 rejections, the personal field drop and the replace of earlier rows.
5. Write the counts, the LOADED status, the SUPERSEDED earlier run and MSG-P1-008 through the ACE notification path.
6. Write TrackerSignOffService with the team scope, the separation of duty check and the count check.
7. Write TrackerLoadController with both endpoints and their capability checks.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.tracker-load`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and the 14 LOAD trackers of the SIT inventory load from synthetic files.

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-008 | Load complete | {loaded} rows loaded from {file}. {rejected} rows rejected; the reject list is on the load. |
| MSG-P1-009 | Counts do not match at sign-off | The counts do not match: {confirmed} rows confirmed, {fileRows} rows in the file, {loaded} loaded, {rejected} rejected. Sign-off is not allowed. |
| MSG-P1-010 | Tracker not loadable | {tracker} cannot be loaded: its decision is {decision} and its status is {status}. |
| MSG-P1-011 | Same file again | The {source} load for {date} is already complete or running. It was not run again. |
| MSG-P1-018 | File type or size not allowed | Use an .xlsx or .csv file of at most {size} MB for a tracker load. |
| MSG-P1-002 | Header does not match | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-P7-002 | Signer loaded the file | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Confirmed count missing | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Tracker changed by someone else | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role or team without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: field lists, target products and the size limit are data.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. Personal fields are dropped before storage; rejected rows are named by tracker code and row number only; test files are synthetic.
- No read of another module's tables. Tracker rows stay in tracker_row; no write to legal_action or any other module's table.
- The stored tracker file is never changed or deleted by the Workbench.

## RWB-E1-011 Reconciliation and data quality report

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-011 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-11 Reconcile the data store to ALS daily; FEAT-RDF-12 Publish the daily reconciliation and data quality report; FEAT-RDF-13 Hold the publish when reconciliation breaks tolerance; FEAT-RPT-05 Reconcile case counts across sources; FEAT-RPT-09 Manage a data quality break |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-007, REQ-RDF-008 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.1 and 3.8; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes; 15 Manage performance, data and AI |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-002, RWB-E1-006 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **a daily reconciliation of the case list to ALS, with the variance by product and the data quality results in one Power BI report**, so that **everyone sees whether today's case list can be trusted**.

### 2. Business rationale

No one can say today whether the recovery teams' lists cover every account at 90 days past due, so missing accounts are found late or not at all. This story runs the reconciliations REC-01 (account count by product) and REC-02 (balance by product) every working day, lists every account that breaks, holds the publish of the case list when a product is outside the tolerance, and publishes the result with the data quality results in one report. It meets REQ-RDF-007 and REQ-RDF-008, applies control CTL-01, and serves the accuracy measure "reconciliation breaks cleared within one day, 100 percent".

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-002 is done: the case list step builds case_list_row and writes its extract for the publish step.
- RWB-E1-006 is done: the data quality rules write dq_exception for the business date.
- The INT-01 load for the business date is COMPLETED, as `LoadRunQuery` of RWB-E1-003 reports.
- Parameters are loaded: `recon.tolerance.pct` 0.00 for REC-01 and REC-02 (assumed, DL25), `case.entry.dpd` 90 (DL16).
- The reporting and BI analyst has built the Power BI report "Reconciliation and data quality" on the lake extracts and scheduled its refresh at 07:30.
- JOB-04 runs as service identity SY-DATALOAD.

### 4. Flow

1. System: JOB-04 Daily reconciliation runs its reconciliation step after the case list step for the business date.
2. System: checks through `LoadRunQuery` that the INT-01 load for the business date is COMPLETED.
3. System: for each product group, counts the ALS accounts at or above 90 days past due less the accounts excluded at entry, and the case list rows at or above 90 days past due (REC-01).
4. System: for each product group, sums total_balance on both sides (REC-02).
5. System: computes the variance and the variance percent and compares it with the tolerance; writes one reconciliation_result per reconciliation and product.
6. System: writes one dq_exception per account that breaks, with check code REC-01 and the account number: in ALS and not on the case list, or on the case list and not in ALS.
7. System: if every result is PASS, releases the case list extract for publish; if any is BREAK, holds the case list publish for the business date and alerts the data steward, the platform administrator and the team managers.
8. System: writes the reconciliation extract and the data quality extract to the data lake.
9. Power BI: the 07:30 refresh shows each product as green, red or not run, the variance, the break rows and the data quality failures by rule.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A product's variance is above the tolerance | Result BREAK; red on the report; case list publish held; break rows listed; alert | MSG-P1-012 | AC2 |
| X2 | The variance equals the tolerance | Result PASS | None | AC3 |
| X3 | The INT-01 load for the business date is not COMPLETED | Reconciliation not run; report shows not run; case list publish held | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X4 | The reconciliation runs again for the same date after a fix | Results for that date replaced; publish released if every result passes | None | AC5 |
| X5 | Two runs for the same date | Results written once per reconciliation, product and date | None | AC6 |
| X6 | A role without Platform administration R lists the break rows | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-011-07 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the case list of RWB-E1-002 and the rule results of RWB-E1-006; changes no case |
| Negotiable | The tolerance per reconciliation is a parameter; the report layout belongs to the BI analyst |
| Valuable | Teams see each morning whether the list is complete, and a broken list is not published |
| Estimable | One batch step, one table, one hold flag, two extracts |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic data |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Reconciliation and data quality report

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-11-30 and DP01 is loaded for 2026-11-30
    Given the parameter recon.tolerance.pct = 0.00 is in force for REC-01 and REC-02

  Scenario: AC1 Variance under limit
    Given the ALS accounts at 90 days past due or more less the exclusions are MORTGAGE 12,256, HIRE_PURCHASE 12,960 and SSME 2,903
    Given the case list rows at 90 days past due or more are MORTGAGE 12,256, HIRE_PURCHASE 12,960 and SSME 2,903, with equal balance sums
    When the reconciliation step of JOB-04 runs
    Then the system writes six reconciliation_result rows , REC-01 and REC-02 for each product, each with variance 0 and result PASS
    Then the system releases the case list extract for 2026-11-30 for publish
    Then the report after the 07:30 refresh shows all three products green

  Scenario: AC2 Variance over limit
    Given the ALS count for SSME is 2,903 and the case list holds 2,891 SSME rows at 90 days past due or more, a variance of 12 accounts, 0.41 percent
    When the reconciliation step runs
    Then the REC-01 result for SSME is BREAK with variance 12 and variance percent 0.41
    Then the system writes 12 dq_exception rows with check code "REC-01" and the 12 account numbers
    Then the system holds the case list publish for 2026-11-30 and the lake keeps the case list of 2026-11-27
    Then the data steward, platform administrator and team manager groups receive MSG-P1-012 "The case list for 2026-11-30 does not reconcile to ALS for SSME: a difference of 12 accounts, 0.41 percent."
    Then the report shows SSME red with the 12 break rows, and MORTGAGE and HIRE_PURCHASE green

  Scenario: AC3 Variance equal to the tolerance
    Given the parameter recon.tolerance.pct for REC-01 is changed by a reference load to 0.10 from 2026-11-30
    Given the MORTGAGE variance is 0.10 percent and the SSME variance is 0.11 percent
    When the reconciliation step runs
    Then the MORTGAGE result is PASS and the SSME result is BREAK

  Scenario: AC4 Account data not loaded
    Given the INT-01 load for 2026-11-30 is LATE and not COMPLETED
    When JOB-04 reaches the reconciliation step
    Then the system writes no reconciliation_result for 2026-11-30
    Then the system holds the case list publish for 2026-11-30
    Then the report shows every product as not run with the reason "DP01 is from 2026-11-27"

  Scenario: AC5 Rerun after a fix
    Given the SSME result for 2026-11-30 is BREAK and the publish is held
    Given P3 has created the 12 missing cases and the case list step has been rerun
    When the platform administrator reruns the reconciliation step for 2026-11-30
    Then the system replaces the six results for 2026-11-30 and all are PASS
    Then the system sets the 12 REC-01 exceptions CLEARED with cleared_on 2026-11-30
    Then the system releases the case list extract for 2026-11-30 for publish

  Scenario: AC6 Two runs for the same date
    Given two JOB-04 runs for 2026-11-30 start on two nodes
    When both reach the reconciliation step
    Then reconciliation_result holds one row per reconciliation, product and date, six rows in all
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Accounts at 90 days past due in the ALS load are compared with open recovery cases, by count per product, every day | REC-01; CTL-01; REQ-RDF-007 |
| BR2 | Balances in the ALS load are compared with the balances on the case accounts, by sum per product | REC-02 |
| BR3 | A result is a break when the variance percent is above the tolerance | Parameter recon.tolerance.pct, 0.00 assumed (DL25) |
| BR4 | A break holds the publish of the case list for the business date and lists the break rows for the data steward | FEAT-RDF-13; REC-01 "Break list to the data steward" |
| BR5 | Accounts excluded at entry are explained and do not count as breaks | REC-01 "zero unexplained"; REQ-CWC-004 |
| BR6 | No reconciliation runs until the INT-01 load for the business date is COMPLETED | MSG-P1-001; RWB-E1-003 BR1 |
| BR7 | Report grades: green, every reconciliation for the product passed; red, at least one break; not run, the reconciliation did not run, with the reason | FEAT-RDF-12 |
| BR8 | A repeated run for the same date replaces that date's results | R-UNI-40 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It writes reconciliation_result (PASS or BREAK), sets dq_exception rows OPEN or CLEARED, and sets the case list publish of the business date to HELD or RELEASED.

### 12. Contract

**Job step**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | JOB-04 Daily reconciliation, reconciliation step, after the case list step; before the publish step |
| Job name | JOB-04 Daily reconciliation |
| Input | loan_account; case_list_row; `LoadRunQuery`; `CaseQueryApi.excludedAccountsByProduct(businessDate)`; parameters |
| Output | reconciliation_result; dq_exception (REC-01, REC-02); publish status of the case list; extracts `reconciliation/<businessDate>.csv` and `data-quality/<businessDate>.csv` to the data lake through the outbound adapter (INT-19) |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | rec_code, business_date and product_group (unique) |
| Restart | Rerun by POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun replaces the date's results |

**Published interface used** (P3, extends the interface of RWB-E1-002)

```java
Map<String, Long> excludedAccountsByProduct(LocalDate businessDate); // product group to count of accounts excluded at entry
```

**GET /admin/data-quality/exceptions** (API-P1-003): with `product=DP03` returns the REC-01 and REC-02 break rows with the rule results; Platform administration R; 401, 403 (MSG-P4-002), 503; read only.

**GET /admin/jobs** (API-P1-001): the JOB-04 run shows checks REC-01 and REC-02 per product (PASS, BREAK or NOT_RUN) and PUBLISH (RELEASED or HELD).

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dataengine/recon`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.recon`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ReconciliationStepConfig | Job (Spring Batch step in JOB-04) | Runs REC-01 and REC-02 per product, writes results and breaks, sets the publish status |
| ReconciliationService | Service | Computes counts, sums, variances and results against the tolerance |
| ReconciliationResult | Entity | Maps reconciliation_result |
| ReconciliationResultRepository | Repository | Replaces the results of one business date |
| CaseListPublishGate | Service | Sets HELD or RELEASED on the date's case list; the publish step writes the case list extract only when RELEASED |
| ReconciliationExtractWriter | Service | Writes the reconciliation and data quality extracts |
| LoadAlertNotifier | Service (from RWB-E1-003) | Sends MSG-P1-012 |

**Database.** Migration `V1_011__reconciliation_result.sql` creates reconciliation_result (rec_code varchar(6), business_date date, product_group varchar(15), source_count integer, workbench_count integer, source_amount numeric(18,2), workbench_amount numeric(18,2), variance_count integer, variance_pct numeric(9,4), tolerance_pct numeric(9,4), result varchar(8) check in ('PASS','BREAK'), standard columns, unique (rec_code, business_date, product_group)); adds publish_status varchar(10) default 'PENDING' check in ('PENDING','HELD','RELEASED') to case_list_row.

**Configuration and reference data.** Parameters `recon.tolerance.pct` per reconciliation and `case.entry.dpd` from the parameter catalog, loaded by the center of excellence analyst; a tolerance change also needs Risk approval (reference data change process, step 4). Alert recipient groups as configuration. The report and its refresh belong to the reporting and BI analyst.

**Build steps**

1. Write migration V1_011, ReconciliationResult and its repository; test the replace of one date.
2. Write ReconciliationService for REC-01 and REC-02 with the exclusions; unit test variance 0, the tolerance boundary and a break.
3. Write the break row listing in both directions and the CLEARED update on a passing rerun.
4. Write CaseListPublishGate and change the publish step of RWB-E1-002 to write the case list extract only when RELEASED; this replaces the total count check of RWB-E1-002.
5. Write the path for an INT-01 load that is not COMPLETED, with the NOT_RUN checks and the held publish.
6. Write ReconciliationExtractWriter for both extracts and add them to the publish step.
7. Add the checks to the JOB-04 Job mapping.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.reconciliation`. Off: the case list publishes as in RWB-E1-002 with its count check.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and the Power BI report shows the three grades from the SIT extracts.

| MSG-P1-001 | INT-01 not complete; reconciliation not run | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |

## RWB-E1-012 Retire local copies

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-012 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-09 Retire a local tracker copy |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-022, RWB-E1-010 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **to confirm in the Workbench that my team's Excel or SharePoint tracker is replaced by the case list, with the location of the read-only archive recorded**, so that **there is one list and no shadow copy**.

### 2. Business rationale

A tracker that stays in use after its data is loaded becomes a second version of the truth, and the two drift apart within days. This story lets the team manager retire each tracker after its load is signed off and the team has worked from the case list for two working days, records where the read-only archive is, logs the tracker fields that no data product carries, and gives the Tribe lead one report of the six teams for the business sign-off before the release. It completes REQ-RDF-006 (local copy retired with the owner's confirmation and a read-only archive kept).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-010 is done: trackers with a LOAD decision are loaded and signed off, and the stored file is in the write-once tracker file store.
- RWB-E1-022 is done: team managers sign in with Entra ID and hold RW-TEAMMGR with their team scope.
- The team has made the tracker read-only in its current location, or moved it to a read-only archive location, before it confirms the retirement.
- Parameters are loaded: `tracker.retire.parallel.days` 2 working days, `tracker.inventory.teams` (from RWB-E1-005).
- The working day calendar is loaded in the reference data service.

### 4. Flow

1. Team manager: works from the case list for at least two working days after the tracker's load is signed off.
2. Team manager: sets the tracker read-only in SharePoint or moves it to the archive location.
3. Team manager: calls `POST /admin/trackers/{trackerId}/retire` with the archive location.
4. System: checks the caller belongs to the tracker's team and holds Queue and allocation A.
5. System: checks the tracker can be retired: decision LOAD with status SIGNED_OFF and at least two working days since sign-off, or decision RETIRE with status LISTED.
6. System: lists the fields of the tracker's field list that are not personal and have no data product field mapped to them.
7. System: sets status RETIRED with the archive location, the time, the confirming user and the list of fields no feed carries, using the optimistic lock version.
8. Data steward or team manager: calls `GET /admin/trackers?status=RETIRED` and reads the archive location, the date and the stored file reference.
9. Tribe lead (RW-TRIBE): on 26 November 2026, calls `GET /admin/trackers/retirement-report` and files the report with the release checklist.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The tracker is LOADED and not signed off, or its decision is KEEP | Retirement refused | MSG-P1-013 | AC4 |
| X2 | Fewer than two working days since sign-off | Retirement refused with the first allowed date | MSG-P1-014 | AC5 |
| X3 | No archive location in the request | 400 | MSG-GEN-001 | AC6 |
| X4 | The caller is a team manager of another team | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X5 | The tracker is already RETIRED | 200 with the existing retirement; nothing changes | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Two retire calls on one tracker at the same time | The second is refused | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | A team still has a tracker that is not retired on the report date | The report lists the team as outstanding with the tracker codes | None | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Queue and allocation A calls the retirement | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-012-11 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the signed-off loads of RWB-E1-010 and the team manager sign-in of RWB-E1-022 |
| Negotiable | The parallel period is a parameter; the archive location is the team's choice |
| Valuable | Ends the shadow copies and gives the release one report for the business sign-off |
| Estimable | One action endpoint, one report endpoint, two status checks |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic trackers |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Retire local copies

  Background:
    Given the parameter tracker.retire.parallel.days = 2
    Given tracker "LIT-07 Litigation case tracker" of team LIT has decision LOAD, status SIGNED_OFF and signed off on Friday 2026-11-20

  Scenario: AC1 Team confirmation
    Given the LIT team has worked from the case list on Monday 2026-11-23 and Tuesday 2026-11-24
    When the LIT team manager calls POST /admin/trackers/{trackerId}/retire on 2026-11-25 with archive location "https://sharepoint.example/sites/lit/archive/LIT-07"
    Then the system retires the tracker status with retired_at 2026-11-25, the team manager's user ID and the archive location
    Then the system keeps the stored tracker file in the write-once store unchanged

  Scenario: AC2 Archive location
    Given LIT-07 was retired on 2026-11-25
    When the data steward calls GET /admin/trackers with status RETIRED
    Then the row for LIT-07 shows archive location "https://sharepoint.example/sites/lit/archive/LIT-07", retired on 2026-11-25, the confirming user and the stored file reference
    Then it lists the 3 fields "Hearing note", "Firm contact" and "Court room" as fields no feed carries

  Scenario: AC3 Business sign-off
    Given the six teams TDR, DIL, LIT, NPA, DEBT_SALE and WRITE_OFF have retired all their LOAD and RETIRE trackers by 2026-11-26

  Scenario: AC5 Parallel period not yet complete
    Given LIT-07 was signed off on 2026-11-20
    When the LIT team manager calls the retirement on Monday 2026-11-23
    Then the system refuses the retirement with MSG-P1-014 "LIT-07 can be retired from 2026-11-25, after 2 working days of use of the case list."

    Given LIT-07 can be retired
    When the NPA team manager calls the retirement for LIT-07
    Then the response is 403 with MSG-P4-002
    Then the status stays SIGNED_OFF

  Scenario: AC8 Retirement repeated
    Given LIT-07 was retired on 2026-11-25
    When the LIT team manager calls the retirement again on 2026-11-26
    Then the response is 200 with retired_at 2026-11-25 and no field changes

  Scenario: AC9 Two retirements at the same time
    Given two sessions of the LIT team manager read LIT-07 at version 4
    When both call the retirement
    Then one succeeds and the other is refused with 409 and MSG-GEN-004

  Scenario: AC10 A team with an outstanding tracker
    Given team NPA has retired 3 of its 4 LOAD and RETIRE trackers and NPA-02 is still LOADED on 2026-11-26
    When the Tribe lead calls GET /admin/trackers/retirement-report on 2026-11-26
    Then the NPA row shows outstanding 1 with tracker code "NPA-02" and status LOADED
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A tracker is retired only with its team manager's confirmation and a read-only archive location | REQ-RDF-006 |
| BR2 | A LOAD tracker is retired only after its load is signed off and the team has used the case list for the parallel period | Parameter tracker.retire.parallel.days, 2 working days |
| BR3 | A RETIRE tracker is retired from LISTED with no load; a KEEP tracker is never retired | RWB-E1-005 BR2 |
| BR4 | The retirement logs every non-personal field of the tracker that no data product field carries | FEAT-RDF-09 |
| BR5 | The stored tracker file is kept unchanged as the Workbench archive copy | ADR-007 storage pattern; RWB-E1-010 BR7 |
| BR6 | A repeated retirement has no further effect | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | Only the team manager of the tracker's team may confirm | Scope Team (roles key); CTL-09 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the tracker status.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| SIGNED_OFF | Retirement confirmed | Decision LOAD; parallel period passed; archive location given; caller in the team | RETIRED |
| LISTED | Retirement confirmed | Decision RETIRE; archive location given; caller in the team | RETIRED |

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager of the tracker's team | Confirms the retirement (Queue and allocation A, scope Team) |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Reads the trackers and the retirement report (Reference data R) |
| RW-COE, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-AUDIT | Read the trackers and the report (Reference data R) |
| RW-TRIBE, Tribe lead and squad members | Read the report for the release checklist (Reference data R) |

The confirmation is not an approval within the delegation of authority; no approval level applies.

### 12. Contract

**POST /admin/trackers/{trackerId}/retire** (new endpoint, recorded in the additions file)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | `TrackerRetirement`: archiveRef (string, up to 400 characters, required), version (integer, the version read) |
| Response 200 | `Tracker` with status RETIRED, archiveRef, retiredAt, retireConfirmedBy, unfedFields |
| 400 | archiveRef missing (MSG-GEN-001) |
| 403 | Role lacks Queue and allocation A, or the caller is not in the tracker's team (MSG-P4-002) |
| 404 | No tracker with that id (MSG-P4-003) |
| 409 | Not retirable (MSG-P1-013); parallel period not passed (MSG-P1-014); version changed (MSG-GEN-004) |
| 401, 503 | MSG-P4-001; database unavailable |
| Authorization | Queue and allocation A, scope Team |
| Idempotency | A call on a RETIRED tracker returns 200 with the existing retirement |

**GET /admin/trackers/retirement-report** (new endpoint, recorded in the additions file)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query `asOf` (date, default today) |
| Response 200 | `TrackerRetirementReport[]`: team, trackers (LOAD and RETIRE), retired, outstanding (count and list of tracker code and status), confirmations (tracker code, user ID, date) |
| 401, 403, 503 | MSG-P4-001; MSG-P4-002; database unavailable |
| Authorization | Reference data R |
| Idempotency | Read only |

**GET /admin/trackers** (from RWB-E1-005) adds archiveRef, retiredAt, retireConfirmedBy, sourceFileRef and unfedFields to `Tracker`.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dataengine/tracker`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.tracker`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TrackerRetirementService | Service | Team scope, retirable check, parallel period by working days, unfed field list, status change with optimistic lock |
| TrackerRetirementReportService | Service | Builds the per-team report from tracker_inventory and the team list parameter |
| TrackerLoadController | Controller (from RWB-E1-010) | Adds the retire and report endpoints |
| TrackerInventoryRepository | Repository (from RWB-E1-005) | Reads and updates tracker_inventory |
| WorkingDayCalendar | Service (reference data service) | Adds working days to the sign-off date |

**Database.** Migration `V1_012__tracker_retirement.sql` adds archive_ref varchar(400), retired_at timestamptz, retire_confirmed_by uuid and unfed_fields jsonb to tracker_inventory. The field_list entries of RWB-E1-005 gain an optional `mappedTo` (entity.field) used for the unfed field list.

**Configuration and reference data.** Parameter `tracker.retire.parallel.days` from the parameter catalog, loaded by the center of excellence analyst. The working day calendar from the reference data service. The team list from `tracker.inventory.teams`.

**Build steps**

2. Write TrackerRetirementService with the retirable check for LOAD and RETIRE trackers; unit test each status and decision.
3. Add the parallel period check with the working day calendar; test the boundary on the second working day and across a weekend.
4. Add the unfed field list from the field list entries that are not personal and have no mappedTo.
5. Add the team scope check, the optimistic lock and the repeat handling.
6. Write TrackerRetirementReportService with the outstanding list.
7. Add both endpoints to TrackerLoadController with their capability checks and Problem mapping.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.tracker-retire`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and the SIT retirement report shows the six teams.

## RWB-E1-013 Baseline measures

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-013 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P9 Reporting |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-19 Publish baseline measures for the recovery portfolio; FEAT-RPT-01 Publish the reporting baseline |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-012 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.8 and 4 |
| L3 process | 15 Manage performance, data and AI |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-029, RWB-E1-018 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As the **Tribe lead (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **cases by route, age and queue, realized recovery, time in stage and turnaround per route published as the baseline, with definitions agreed by the Tribe**, so that **every later epic is measured against the same baseline**.

### 2. Business rationale

Measures are counted by hand from spreadsheets at month end today, and each team counts a case differently. This story holds each measure's definition, data product and formula as an approved data row, publishes the values for business date 27 November 2026 as a frozen baseline, and sends the nightly extract to the data lake for the Power BI data set. It serves REQ-RDF-012 and NFR-065 (measures from Workbench records, not a separate count), and the FSD P9 measure "measures read from the decision log and Workbench records, 100 percent".

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-018 is done: the case record holds route, stage, queue, entry date and stage clock start.
- RWB-E1-029 is done: versioned reference loads with validation run.
- The COLLINS load and case creation for business date 2026-11-27 have passed their checks (JOB-01, JOB-02).
- The measure definition file is prepared with the six baseline measures and the Tribe lead's approval on each row.
- The baseline date is configured: `rwb.reporting.baseline-date` = 2026-11-27.
- The data lake load area for INT-19 is available to the ACE service.

### 4. Flow

1. Reference data administrator: loads the measure definition file through POST /admin/reference-loads with table "measure_definition".
2. System: checks each row has a measure code, name, formula, data product, unit, approver and approval date; any failure refuses the whole load.
3. JOB-15 Reporting extract, nightly 01:30: reads the case facts of the previous business date through the P3 reporting interface and the payments since entry through the P1 interface.
4. System: computes each measure in force by its definition: counts by route, age band and queue; realized recovery; median time in stage; median turnaround per route.
5. System: writes one measure_snapshot row per measure, product and dimension value, with the definition version and business date.
6. System: on the baseline business date, marks the rows as baseline and frozen; frozen rows are never changed.
7. System: writes the extract files of INT-19 to the data lake with the business date and the freshness stamp, and records the run in the job monitor.
8. Reporting and BI analyst: the Power BI data set refreshes at 07:30 from the extract; the report shows the previous day and the baseline side by side.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A definition row has no formula or no data product | Load refused in full | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The baseline is published a second time | Refused; frozen values unchanged | MSG-P9-001 | AC5 |
| X3 | The loads of the baseline date failed | Baseline not published; it runs after the next good load for that date | MSG-P1-001 | AC6 |
| X4 | The data lake is unavailable | Publish held; alert; run again in the next window | MSG-GEN-006 | AC7 |
| X5 | A measure in the extract has no definition in force | Not published; listed in the run record | MSG-P9-003 | AC8 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads case and payment facts through interfaces; no screen |
| Negotiable | The measures, formulas and age bands are data rows the Tribe agrees |
| Valuable | Every later epic is measured against one frozen baseline |
| Estimable | Two tables, one job, six measure calculators |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against a synthetic case set with known answers |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
    Given each row names its data product, formula, unit and approver "TRB-0001" with approval date 2026-11-20
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Each measure is published only under a definition in force that names its data product, formula, unit and approver | REQ-RDF-012; Principle 1 |
| BR2 | The baseline is the snapshot of the configured baseline business date and is frozen once written | REQ-RDF-012; FEAT-RPT-01 |
| BR3 | Measures are computed from Workbench records read through the owning modules, never from a separate count | NFR-065 |
| BR4 | A measure is computed only from loads that passed their checks; stale data is not published as the baseline | CTL-02; MSG-P1-001 rule |
| BR5 | The extract to the data lake holds the publish and alerts on failure, and runs again in the next window | INT-19 error handling |
| BR6 | Age bands are a reference list | Principle 1 |
| BR7 | A definition load with any invalid row is refused in full | refdata.txt change process, step 3 |

## RWB-E1-014 Decision log copy to the data lake

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-014 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-20 Copy the decision log to the lake; FEAT-DRI-06 Stream the decision log to the data lake; FEAT-RPT-04 Publish operations reporting from the decision log |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-009, REQ-RDF-013 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-DRI-009, REQ-RDF-013) |
| L3 process | 17 Run the decision center; 15 Manage performance, data and AI |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Should |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-056, RWB-E1-017 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the decision log copied to the data lake each night, with a retention rule applied to the copy**, so that **reporting reads the log without touching the live log and nothing in the copy is kept longer than its rule**.

### 2. Business rationale

Reporting, audit sampling and model feedback need the full decision history, and queries against the live log slow the write path that every action depends on (ADR-009). A nightly copy that matches the live log on row count and last hash gives Power BI and audit one checked source (REC-08). The copy carries its own retention rule, so the lake does not keep decisions longer than the bank schedule allows. Serves REQ-DRI-009 and REQ-RDF-013; measure: copy matched on count and last hash on 99 percent of days (FSD P1 A2.20.1).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-008 (decision log store) and RWB-E1-027 (decision log writer) are done, and P7 publishes the DecisionLogExport interface in section 12.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: JOB-13 has a run book, and its runs show in the job monitor.
- RWB-E1-017 is done: the retention rule table holds a row for product DP12, table decision_log_entry, record class LAKE_COPY (assumed 120 months; DL26).
- The data lake intake container for INT-19 exists in each environment and the job's service identity SY-DATALOAD can write to it.
- Quartz holds the JOB-13 trigger at 01:00 Asia/Bangkok.

### 4. Flow

1. Quartz: starts JOB-13 Decision log copy at 01:00 for business date D (the previous calendar day).
2. DecisionLogLakeCopyService: reads the watermark (last copied entry hash and cumulative count) from lake_copy_watermark.
3. DecisionLogLakeCopyService: calls DecisionLogExport.head() and fixes the cut-off: the live count and last entry hash at start.
4. DecisionLogLakeCopyService: calls DecisionLogExport.entriesAfter(watermarkHash, 5000) in chain order until it reaches the cut-off hash.
5. LakeFileWriter: writes the entries to `decision-log/business_date=D/` as Parquet files and writes `_manifest.json` with the row count, first hash, last hash and cumulative count.
6. LakeCopyReconciler: reads the manifest back from the lake and compares the cumulative count and last hash with the cut-off (REC-08, tolerance zero).
7. LakeCopyReconciler: on a match, marks the partition complete, moves the watermark forward and records the checks on the job run.
8. LakeRetentionService: reads the retention rule for DP12 LAKE_COPY and moves each partition older than the rule to the archive tier, recording the partition list, the count and the rule version on the job run.
9. Data steward: reads the run result in GET /admin/jobs and the break, if any, in the morning.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The lake count or last hash differs from the cut-off | Partition not marked complete; watermark not moved; break recorded; data steward alerted; JOB-13 runs again the next night | MSG-P1-019 | AC3 |
| X2 | JOB-13 runs again for a business date already copied | The same chain range is written to the same partition; no duplicate rows | None | AC4 |
| X3 | DecisionLogExport is unavailable or the lake write fails | Job ends Failed; previous copy and watermark kept; alert raised; rerun from the job monitor | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X4 | No decision was written since the last copy | Empty partition with a manifest of zero rows and the unchanged last hash; checks pass | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A second start of JOB-13 while one is running | Second start refused; 409 on a manual rerun | MSG-P2-006 | AC7 |
| X6 | A partition is exactly at its retention age | The partition is kept; only partitions older than the rule move | None | AC8 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the decision log store and writer (RWB-E1-008, RWB-E1-027), the job monitoring (RWB-E1-056) and the retention rule table (RWB-E1-017), all earlier in Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | File size, lake path and retention period are configuration and data; the story fixes the copy, the match and the archive behavior |
| Valuable | Reporting and audit read the log without load on the live store |
| Estimable | One job, one watermark table, one published interface call, no screen |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test against a test lake container |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The copy matches the live log on count and last hash with zero tolerance, or it is not published | REC-08; DL25 |
| BR2 | The copy reads the decision log only through the P7 published interface | ADR-002; DT08 |
| BR3 | Analysis reads the lake copy, not the live log | ADR-009 |
| BR4 | A lake partition older than the retention rule for DP12 LAKE_COPY moves to the archive tier | retention_rule (RWB-E1-017); DL26 |
| BR5 | The retention period is a data row with a version, never a code value | Principle 1; DT02 |
| BR6 | A failed copy is rerun the next night; the previous copy stays in use | JOB-13, batch.txt |

### 12. Contract

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz cron `0 0 1 * * ?`, Asia/Bangkok |
| Job name | JOB-13 Decision log copy |
| Schedule | Nightly 01:00; before JOB-15 at 01:30 and JOB-14 at 02:00 |
| Input | Decision log entries after the watermark hash, up to the head at job start, through DecisionLogExport |
| Output | Parquet files and `_manifest.json` under `decision-log/business_date=YYYY-MM-DD/` in the INT-19 intake container; the watermark row; checks on the job run (rows, REC-08 result, partitions archived, rule version) |
| Events published | None. JOB-13 publishes no event in events.txt |
| Idempotency key | Business date. A rerun for a date rewrites the same partition from the same chain range |
| Restart behavior | A failed run leaves the watermark unchanged; the next run or a manual rerun starts from the watermark. Quartz `@DisallowConcurrentExecution` |

**Published interface (P7 to P1)**

```java
package recovery.decisionlog.api;

public interface DecisionLogExport {
    /** Live count and last entry hash at the moment of the call. */
    ChainHead head();

    /** Entries after the given hash in chain order, at most limit entries. Genesis hash is 64 zeros. */
    List<DecisionLogEntryView> entriesAfter(String afterEntryHash, int limit);
}

public record ChainHead(long count, String lastEntryHash, OffsetDateTime lastDecidedAt) {}
```

DecisionLogEntryView carries the 18 fields of DecisionLogEntry in api.yaml, with the same names.

**Endpoints used**

| Method and path | Request | Response | Errors | Authorization | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs | Query: type=JOB-13, status, from, to | Job[]: id, type, businessDate, status, startedAt, endedAt, checks | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 role lacks the right (MSG-P4-002); 503 store down | Platform administration, R | Not applicable |
| POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun | Path: jobId; header Idempotency-Key | Job | 401; 403; 404 unknown job (MSG-P4-003); 409 job running (MSG-P2-006); 503 | Platform administration, U | Idempotency-Key header; a repeat key returns the first result |

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/dataengine/lake`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.lake`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DecisionLogLakeCopyJob | Job | Quartz job for JOB-13; one run per business date; no concurrent run |
| DecisionLogLakeCopyService | Service | Reads the watermark, fixes the cut-off, pages entries through DecisionLogExport |
| LakeFileWriter | Service | Writes Parquet files and the manifest to the intake container |
| LakeCopyReconciler | Service | Reads the manifest back and checks REC-08; records the result on the job run |
| LakeRetentionService | Service | Applies the DP12 LAKE_COPY retention rule to lake partitions |
| LakeCopyWatermarkRepository | Repository | Reads and writes lake_copy_watermark |
| LakeCopyWatermark | Entity | One row per copy name |
| DecisionLogExport | Published interface | P7 interface used to read the log; built in P7 if not present |

- Database: table lake_copy_watermark (new, Flyway migration in this story): copy_name varchar(40) primary key, last_entry_hash char(64) not null, last_decided_at timestamptz, rows_copied_total bigint not null, business_date date not null, plus the standard columns. No read of decision_log_entry in P1 code. Reads retention_rule (RWB-E1-017).
- Configuration and reference data: properties `rwb.dataengine.lake.container`, `rwb.dataengine.lake.path-prefix=decision-log`, `rwb.dataengine.lake.page-size=5000`, `rwb.dataengine.lake.rows-per-file=50000` (platform administrator, per environment); retention rule row DP12 LAKE_COPY loaded by the reference data administrator and approved by Compliance (RWB-E1-017).
- Build steps:
  1. Flyway migration for lake_copy_watermark; seed row copy_name `DECISION_LOG`, last_entry_hash 64 zeros, rows_copied_total 0.
  2. DecisionLogExport in P7 with head() and entriesAfter(); unit tests on chain order.
  3. DecisionLogLakeCopyService paging from the watermark to the cut-off; test with 12,480 synthetic entries.
  4. LakeFileWriter with Parquet output and manifest; test against an Azurite or local file system container.
  5. LakeCopyReconciler with REC-08 checks and MSG-P1-019 on a mismatch; watermark moves only on a match.
  6. LakeRetentionService reading the rule row; partitions older than retention_months move to the archive tier.
  7. DecisionLogLakeCopyJob on Quartz with `@DisallowConcurrentExecution`, run record and checks through the RWB-E1-056 job monitoring.
  8. Integration tests for AC1 to AC8 and the access test.
- Feature flag: `rwb.dataengine.lake-copy`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass, JOB-13 shows in GET /admin/jobs with its checks, and the run book from RWB-E1-056 covers the rerun.

## RWB-E1-015 Freshness stamp per data product

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-015 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-14 Stamp each data product with its freshness; FEAT-DRI-12 Carry a freshness stamp on every decision input |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-009 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-RDF-009) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes; 17 Run the decision center |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-003, RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-064, RWB-E1-006 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **every data product to carry the source extract time and the load time, exposed to every consumer and shown on the case record view**, so that **every decision input states how old it is and stale facts are visible**.

### 2. Business rationale

Recovery data arrives by end of day batch and weekly or monthly file loads (ADR-005), so a fact on the case can be one day or one week old, and nobody can see which. A stamp per product and load, shown on the case record and copied into each decision's inputs snapshot, makes the age of every input visible to the person deciding and to audit. A product whose load has not arrived by its expected time is flagged stale the same morning. Serves REQ-RDF-009; measure: loads on time and complete on 99 percent of days (FSD P1 A2.14.1).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the recovery tables exist, and loan_account and account_payment carry data_as_of.
- RWB-E1-003 is done: the ALS load (JOB-01) commits DP01 rows and publishes LoadCompleted or LoadRefused.
- RWB-E1-064 is done: the data_product table holds DP01 to DP14 with refresh cycle and expected-by time (assumed 08:00 for daily COLLINS products and Monday 08:00 for weekly file products; DL11).
- RWB-E1-006 is done: the data quality exception list exists and GET /admin/data-quality/exceptions reads it.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the P7 decision log writer builds an inputs snapshot for each entry.
- The reader holds Case record R (case roles) or Platform administration R (data steward, platform administrator).

### 4. Flow

1. Load job (JOB-01 or JOB-09): commits a load for product DP01 and business date D.
2. FreshnessStampService: in the same transaction, writes one data_product_load row with business date D, the source extract time from the COLLINS control record and the load time.
3. JOB-01 freshness step: at each product's expected-by time, checks that a load for the expected business date exists.
4. FreshnessStampService: for a product with no load, sets the latest row to status STALE, writes a data quality exception with check FRESHNESS and sends the operations alert.
5. StaleMarkerListener: on LoadRefused, marks the product STALE at once.
6. Consumer (case record view, P3 or P7): calls FreshnessQuery or GET /data-products/freshness and receives business date, source extract time, load time and status per product.
7. Case record view: shows the stamp in the data panel, with MSG-P1-001 when the product is stale.
8. P7 inputs snapshot builder: calls FreshnessQuery.stampsFor() for the products a decision reads and writes each stamp into the snapshot that inputs_ref points to.
9. Load job: a later load for date D sets status LOADED and clears the stale flag.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No load for the expected business date by the expected-by time | Product set STALE; exception FRESHNESS written; operations alert sent; case record shows the stale warning | MSG-P1-001 | AC2 |
| X2 | The load is refused at a check | LoadRefused marks the product STALE at once; previous stamp stays in use | MSG-P1-002, MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X3 | The same load is stamped twice for one product and business date | One data_product_load row; the repeat is counted (R-UNI-40) | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A late load arrives after the stale flag | Status LOADED; stale flag cleared; exception closed | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A load is committed one minute before the expected-by time | Product not flagged stale | None | AC7 |
| X6 | A weekly product inside its weekly cycle | Product not flagged stale on the days between loads | None | AC8 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the tables (RWB-E1-001), the ALS load (RWB-E1-003), the data product table (RWB-E1-064) and the exception list (RWB-E1-006) |
| Negotiable | Expected-by times and refresh cycles are data rows on data_product; the story fixes the stamping and the stale check |
| Valuable | Every decision and every case record shows the age of its data |
| Estimable | One new table, one service, one listener, one endpoint, one panel |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against a test clock and synthetic loads |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Freshness stamp per data product

  Background:
    Given data product "DP01" Account and arrears has refresh cycle "DAILY" and expected-by time 08:00
    Given data product "DP06" Collateral and asset has refresh cycle "WEEKLY" and expected-by time Monday 08:00

  Scenario: AC1 Freshness on the row
    Given the account and arrears product for business date 2026-11-30 loaded at 06:50 on 2026-12-01 from an extract taken at 23:30 on 2026-11-30
    Given loan account "ACC-SYN-000101" has data_as_of 2026-11-30
    When the row is read through FreshnessQuery.stampForRow("DP01", 2026-11-30) and GET /data-products/freshness?product=DP01
    Then the row carries source time 2026-11-30T23:30+07:00 and load time 2026-12-01T06:50+07:00
    Then the status is "LOADED"

  Scenario: AC2 Stale product flagged
    Given no DP01 load for business date 2026-11-30 exists at 08:00 on 2026-12-01
    When the freshness step runs at 08:00
    Then the system flags the product "STALE"
    Then a data quality exception with product "DP01" and check "FRESHNESS" is raised on 2026-12-01
    Then the alert goes to the operations channel
    Then the case record view shows the stamp in the data panel with "Account and arrears is from 2026-11-30. Today's load has not arrived."

  Scenario: AC3 Freshness in the decision log
    Given a decision log entry for case "RW-2026-000101" read DP01 for 2026-11-30 and DP06 for 2026-11-23
    When the entry and its inputs snapshot are read
    Then the snapshot lists DP01 with load time 2026-12-01T06:50+07:00 and status "LOADED"
    Then the snapshot lists DP06 with load time 2026-11-24T04:40+07:00 and status "LOADED"

  Scenario: AC4 A refused load marks the product stale at once
    Given the DP01 load for 2026-11-30 is refused at check "Control totals" at 05:20
    When LoadRefused is processed
    Then DP01 is "STALE" from 05:20
    Then the stamp for business date 2026-11-30 stays the one in use

  Scenario: AC5 The same load stamped twice
    Given DP01 for business date 2026-11-30 is stamped at 06:50
    When the same stamp is written again for DP01 and 2026-11-30
    Then one data_product_load row exists for DP01 and 2026-11-30
    Then the duplicate count for that stamp is 1

  Scenario: AC6 A late load clears the stale flag
    Given DP01 was flagged "STALE" at 08:00 on 2026-12-01
    When the DP01 load for 2026-11-30 commits at 08:40
    Then DP01 status is "LOADED" with load time 2026-12-01T08:40+07:00
    Then the FRESHNESS exception for DP01 on 2026-12-01 is closed

  Scenario: AC7 A load one minute before the expected-by time
    Given the DP01 load for 2026-11-30 commits at 07:59 on 2026-12-01
    When the freshness step runs at 08:00
    Then the system does not flag DP01 stale

  Scenario: AC8 A weekly product between its loads
    Given the DP06 load for business date 2026-11-30 committed at 04:40 on Monday 2026-11-30
    When the freshness step runs at 08:00 on Thursday 2026-12-03
    Then the system does not flag DP06 stale
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every committed load writes one freshness stamp per product and business date, in the same transaction as the load | REQ-RDF-009; mapping rule "Business date", s2t.txt |
| BR2 | A product with no load for its expected business date by its expected-by time is stale | data_product.expected_by (RWB-E1-064); DL11 |
| BR3 | A refused load leaves the previous load in use and marks the product stale | DQ checks "Refuse the load", dq.txt; CTL-02 |
| BR4 | Every decision records the freshness of each data product it read | REQ-RDF-009; FEAT-DRI-12; DF-DEC-008 meaning |
| BR5 | A repeat stamp for the same product and business date is ignored and counted | R-UNI-40 |
| BR6 | Expected-by times and refresh cycles are data rows, not code | Principle 1; DT02 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the freshness status of a data product load: LOADED to STALE when the expected load is missing or refused, and STALE to LOADED when a later load commits.

| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Reads stamps and stale exceptions (Platform administration R) |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads stamps and stale exceptions; receives the operations alert |
| Case roles with Case record R, for example RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR | Read the stamp in the case record data panel |

| DF-OPS-003 | data_product_load | source_system | Write |
| DF-OPS-004 | data_product_load | business_date | Write |
| DF-OPS-005 | data_product_load | source_extracted_at | Write |
| DF-OPS-006 | data_product_load | loaded_at | Write |
| DF-OPS-007 | data_product_load | status | Write |
| DF-OPS-008 | data_product_load | stale_flagged_at | Write |
| DF-OPS-009 | data_product_load | duplicate_count | Write |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**Endpoint (new, see additions)**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Method and path | GET /data-products/freshness |
| Request | Query: product (optional, DP01 to DP14), asOf (optional, business date) |
| Response | DataProductFreshness[]: productCode, productName, businessDate, sourceExtractedAt, loadedAt, status (LOADED or STALE), staleSince |
| Errors | 400 malformed product or date (MSG-GEN-001); 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 role lacks the right (MSG-P4-002); 503 store down (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Case record, R. No case scope applies: the stamp holds no case data |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**Published interface (P1 to P3 and P7)**

```java
package recovery.dataengine.freshness.api;

public interface FreshnessQuery {
    FreshnessStamp stampFor(String productCode);
    FreshnessStamp stampForRow(String productCode, LocalDate dataAsOf);
    Map<String, FreshnessStamp> stampsFor(Set<String> productCodes);
}

public record FreshnessStamp(String productCode, LocalDate businessDate,
        OffsetDateTime sourceExtractedAt, OffsetDateTime loadedAt,
        FreshnessStatus status, OffsetDateTime staleSince) {}
```

**Job step and events**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz trigger per product at data_product.expected_by, Asia/Bangkok |
| Job name | JOB-01 COLLINS load check and intake, freshness step (file products: JOB-09 File loads) |
| Input | data_product rows; data_product_load rows for the expected business date |
| Output | Status STALE on the product's latest stamp; data quality exception check FRESHNESS; operations alert |
| Events consumed | EV-27 LoadRefused (marks the product stale) |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | Product code and business date (unique key on data_product_load) |
| Restart behavior | The step reads state each time; a rerun after a failure flags the same products and writes no second exception for the same product and day |

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/dataengine/freshness`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.freshness`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| FreshnessStampService | Service | Writes stamps in the load transaction; marks and clears stale |
| FreshnessCheckStep | Job | Freshness step of JOB-01 and JOB-09 at each expected-by time |
| StaleMarkerListener | Listener | Consumes LoadRefused from the outbox and marks the product stale |
| DataProductLoadRepository | Repository | Reads and writes data_product_load |
| DataProductLoad | Entity | One row per product and business date |
| FreshnessQuery | Published interface | Stamps for other modules |
| FreshnessController | Controller | GET /data-products/freshness |
| DataFreshnessPanel | React component | Data panel on SCR-03 with business date, load time and the stale warning |

- Database: table data_product_load (new, Flyway migration in this story) with columns id uuid, product_code varchar(4), source_system varchar(40), business_date date, source_extracted_at timestamptz, loaded_at timestamptz, status varchar(10), stale_flagged_at timestamptz, duplicate_count integer default 0, plus the standard columns; unique (product_code, business_date); index (product_code, loaded_at desc). Reads data_product (RWB-E1-064). Reads loan_account.data_as_of and account_payment.data_as_of for row stamps.
- Configuration and reference data: data_product.refresh_cycle and expected_by, loaded by the data steward through RWB-E1-064; property `rwb.dataengine.freshness.alert-channel` set by the platform administrator.
- Build steps:
  1. Flyway migration for data_product_load with its unique key.
  2. FreshnessStampService.recordLoad(productCode, businessDate, sourceExtractedAt, loadedAt) called by the DP01 load of RWB-E1-003 in its commit transaction; repeat increments duplicate_count.
  3. FreshnessCheckStep with one Quartz trigger per product built from data_product; writes STALE, the FRESHNESS exception and the alert.
  4. StaleMarkerListener on LoadRefused, idempotent on the event ID.
  5. FreshnessQuery and FreshnessController with DataProductFreshness responses.
  6. P7 inputs snapshot builder (RWB-E1-027) calls stampsFor() and writes each stamp into the snapshot.
  7. DataFreshnessPanel on SCR-03 with the Stale input state and MSG-P1-001.
  8. Tests for AC1 to AC8 with a fixed test clock, and the access test.
- Feature flag: `rwb.dataengine.freshness-stamp`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass and every Epic 1 load job calls recordLoad.

| MSG-GEN-001 | Malformed product code or date in the query | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

## RWB-E1-016 Access control per data product and catalog entries

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-016 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-15 Set access control per data product for PDPA; FEAT-RDF-16 Maintain the data catalog entry per data product |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-010, REQ-RDF-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-RDF-010, REQ-RDF-011) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-037, RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-064 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **read access to each data product granted by role, PDPA fields tagged, every read logged, and a catalog entry per product with owner, system of record, freshness and fields**, so that **personal data is read only by the roles that need it and every product is findable**.

### 2. Business rationale

Audit findings record staff sending debtor data outside the bank and users holding access they did not need (CTL-11, CTL-09). Access per data product, held as data rows, limits each role to the products its work needs; PDPA tags on each field drive masking; and every read goes to the PII access log. The catalog gives one entry per product so a developer, an analyst or an auditor finds the owner, the source, the freshness rule, the retention and the personal fields without asking. Serves REQ-RDF-010 and REQ-RDF-011.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the 14 data products have tables, and sys_objects and sys_fields hold the 108 entities and 1,256 fields with is_personal set.
- RWB-E1-037 is done: P4 holds the role to permission matrix and the masking rules, and publishes the masking interface in section 12.
- RWB-E1-064 is done: data_product holds DP01 to DP14 with owner role, system of record and refresh cycle.
- data_product_access version "DPA-2026.11" is loaded and approved: for example RW-CASEOWN and RW-AUDIT read DP02; RW-PHONECOL reads DP01, DP02, DP03 and DP05 and not DP06.
- The masking rules from Compliance may be empty (DL26). Until they load, every personal field is masked for every role.
- The ACE common module PII access logging is available.

### 4. Flow

1. User: opens a data product view, which calls GET /data-products/{productCode}/records?caseId=.
2. DataProductAccessService: checks the capability right Case record R through the ACE access check.
3. DataProductAccessService: checks data_product_access for a row in force for one of the user's roles and the product.
4. DataProductAccessService: calls the P3 case scope interface for the case's accounts and parties in the user's scope.
5. DataProductRecordService: reads the product rows for those accounts or parties from P1 tables.
6. DataProductRecordService: for each field tagged is_personal in sys_fields, applies the P4 masking interface for the user's roles.
7. DataProductAccessService: writes the read to the PII access log with user, product, case, field list and time.
8. Controller: returns the rows with the product's freshness stamp.
9. User with Platform administration R: calls GET /admin/data-products and reads the 14 catalog entries with owner, system of record, refresh cycle, retention and fields with PDPA tags.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No data_product_access row for the user's roles and the product | 403; no row read; refusal written to the access log | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X2 | An access load names a role code not in the roles table | Load refused in full; previous version stays in force | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | The case is outside the user's scope | 404; no row read; refusal logged | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | No masking rule is loaded for a personal field | The field is masked for every role | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The PII access log cannot be written | Read refused with 503; no personal data returned | MSG-GEN-006 | AC7 |
| X6 | An access row has a valid-from date after today | The row is not in force; the read is refused until that date | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the tables and the metadata tables (RWB-E1-001), the P4 masking (RWB-E1-037) and the data product table (RWB-E1-064) |
| Negotiable | Which role reads which product, and which field is masked for whom, are data rows; the story fixes the checks |
| Valuable | Personal data reaches only the roles that need it, and every read is logged |
| Estimable | One access table, two endpoints, one read service, calls to three published interfaces |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is one API test with synthetic parties and roles |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Access control per data product and catalog entries

  Background:
    Given data product access version "DPA-2026.11" is in force from 2026-11-20
    Given case "RW-2026-000102" has borrower party "PTY-SYN-0102" with mobile contact point value "0812345678" stored as token
    Given no masking rule from Compliance is loaded for party or contact_point fields

  Scenario: AC1 Role access
    Given user "u-audit-01" holds read-only role RW-AUDIT, which reads DP02
    When the user calls GET /data-products/DP02/records?caseId=RW-2026-000102
    Then the mobile number shows as "******5678" and the national ID token is returned as "MASKED"
    Then the PII access log holds one entry with user "u-audit-01", product "DP02", case "RW-2026-000102" and the time of the read

  Scenario: AC2 Catalog entry
    Given the 14 data products DP01 to DP14
    When a data steward calls GET /admin/data-products
    Then the system returns 14 entries

    Then the DP02 entry lists 20 fields of which 9 are tagged personal

  Scenario: AC3 Access denied

  Scenario: AC4 An access load with an unknown role is refused

  Scenario: AC8 An access row not yet in force
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A role reads a data product only through a data_product_access row in force for that role and product | REQ-RDF-010; FEAT-RDF-15 |
| BR2 | A personal field is masked unless the masking rules let the role see it | CTL-11; masking rules reference table; DL26 |
| BR3 | With no masking rule loaded, every personal field stays masked | DL26 ("Masking rules load with no values") |
| BR4 | Every read of personal data is written to the PII access log; a read that cannot be logged is refused | REQ-ACA-006; CTL-11 |
| BR5 | A record outside the caller's scope is refused | CTL-09; permission matrix |
| BR6 | An access load with an exception is refused in full; the previous version stays in force | Reference data change process, step 3; CTL-08 |
| BR7 | Each data product has one catalog entry with owner, system of record, refresh cycle, retention and fields with PDPA tags | REQ-RDF-011; sys_fields.is_personal |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the version in force of data_product_access when an approved load reaches its valid-from date.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Prepares the access rows for their products; reads the catalog (Platform administration R) |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Submits the access load through POST /admin/reference-loads (Reference data C) |
| RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Owns the masking rules (DL26); reads the catalog |
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | Owns the role to permission matrix; reads the access log |
| RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-PLATADM | Read the catalog (Platform administration R) |
| Roles with Case record R and an access row, for example RW-CASEOWN, RW-AUDIT | Read a data product for a case in scope |
| SY-DATALOAD, data load | Applies an approved access version to data_product_access |
