### 12. Contract

**Endpoints (new, see additions)**

| Item | GET /data-products/{productCode}/records | GET /admin/data-products |
|---|---|---|
| Request | Path: productCode (DP01 to DP14); query: caseId (required), page, size | Query: product (optional) |
| Response | DataProductRecordPage: items (record id, entity, fields map with masked values), freshness (FreshnessStamp from RWB-E1-015), page, size, total | DataProductCatalogEntry[]: productCode, productName, definition, ownerRole, systemOfRecord, refreshCycle, expectedBy, retentionClass, fields (entity, fieldName, fieldId, dataType, isPersonal) |
| Errors | 400 missing caseId (MSG-GEN-001); 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no capability right or no access row (MSG-P4-002); 404 case not found or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 503 PII log or store down (MSG-GEN-006) | 401; 403; 503 |
| Authorization | Case record, R; plus a data_product_access row in force | Platform administration, R |
| Idempotency | Not applicable | Not applicable |

**Endpoint used for the access load**

POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads with table `data_product_access`, file and validFrom (Reference data, C); approval through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve (Reference data, A). Errors 409 version clash (MSG-GEN-004), 422 field invalid (MSG-GEN-001). The P4 reference data service hands approved rows to P1 through DataProductAccessLoader.

**Published interfaces**

```java
// P1, called by the reference data service after approval
package recovery.dataengine.access.api;
public interface DataProductAccessLoader {
    LoadResult apply(String accessVersion, LocalDate validFrom, List<DataProductAccessRow> rows);
}

// P3, called by P1 to resolve a case to its accounts and parties within the caller's scope
package recovery.casewf.api;
public interface CaseScopeQuery {
    CaseLinks linksInScope(UUID caseId, UserContext user) throws CaseNotInScopeException;
}
public record CaseLinks(UUID caseId, List<UUID> accountIds, List<UUID> partyIds) {}

// P4, from RWB-E1-037
package recovery.access.api;
public interface MaskingPolicy {
    String apply(String objectName, String fieldName, String value, Set<String> roleCodes);
}
```

PII access logging goes through the ACE common module logging interface to PII Kafka with user, product, case, field names and time; no field value is logged.

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/dataengine/access`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.access`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DataProductController | Controller | GET /data-products/{productCode}/records and GET /admin/data-products |
| DataProductAccessService | Service | Capability check, access row check, scope call, PII log write |
| DataProductRecordService | Service | Reads rows of the product's entities and applies masking by sys_fields.is_personal |
| DataProductCatalogService | Service | Builds catalog entries from data_product, sys_objects, sys_fields and retention_rule |
| DataProductAccessRepository | Repository | Reads and writes data_product_access |
| DataProductAccess | Entity | One row per product, role and version |
| DataProductAccessLoader | Published interface | Applies an approved access version |
| Data product access rule table | Rule table | data_product_access rows by version and valid-from date |

- Database: table data_product_access (new, Flyway migration in this story) with id uuid, product_code varchar(4), role_code varchar(20), can_read boolean, access_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, standard columns; unique (product_code, role_code, access_version); index (role_code, product_code, valid_from). Reads sys_objects, sys_fields, data_product, retention_rule, party, contact_point, loan_account, collateral and the other P1 product tables. No read of role or permission tables: the capability check uses the ACE access check, and role codes come from the session.
- Configuration and reference data: access version "DPA-2026.11" prepared by the data steward and loaded by the reference data administrator; masking rules loaded by Compliance under RWB-E1-037 (DL26).
- Build steps:
  1. Flyway migration for data_product_access.
  2. DataProductAccessLoader with whole-load validation: known product code, known role code, no overlapping rows; refuse with MSG-P1-002.
  3. DataProductAccessService with the order: capability right, access row in force, scope through CaseScopeQuery.
  4. DataProductRecordService with masking from sys_fields.is_personal through MaskingPolicy; mask every personal field when no rule exists.
  5. PII access log write before the response is returned; refuse with 503 when it fails.
  6. DataProductCatalogService and GET /admin/data-products.
  7. Contract tests for both new endpoints from the additions schema (RWB-TE-003).
  8. Tests for AC1 to AC8 and the access test.
- Feature flag: `rwb.dataengine.product-access`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass and the catalog returns 14 complete entries in SIT.

| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P1-002 | Access load refused at a check | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | caseId missing | Enter {field}. |

## RWB-E1-017 Retention and archive rule for the data store

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-017 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-17 Apply the retention and archive rule to the data store |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-013 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-RDF-013) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Should |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-043, RWB-TE-012, RWB-E1-064 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **Compliance and PDPA officer (RW-COMPLY)**, I want **a retention rule per data product and table, held as reference data, applied by a job that archives rows past their rule and logs the action**, so that **the store holds what the policy allows and nothing older**.

### 2. Business rationale

PDPA and the bank retention schedule limit how long personal data is kept, and today recovery records stay in spreadsheets and systems with no end date. A retention rule per data product and table, loaded as versioned data, lets Compliance set and change periods without a release. A monthly job archives rows past their period to a write-once archive container and removes them from the live store, keeps every row of a case under legal hold, and records what it did. Serves REQ-RDF-013 and the retention requirements NFR-031 and NFR-072.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the recovery tables and sys_objects exist.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: the reference data service validates and approves versioned loads.
- RWB-E1-064 is done: data_product holds DP01 to DP14.
- RWB-TE-012 is done: a write-once archive container exists in each environment, writable by SY-DATALOAD.
- Retention rule version "RET-2026.11" is loaded and approved: DP05 interaction at 24 months on occurred_at (assumed until Compliance supplies the bank schedule; DL26).
- P3 publishes CaseHoldQuery (section 12), returning the cases with legal_hold = true.
- Quartz holds the JOB-17 trigger for the first Sunday of each month at 02:30 Asia/Bangkok.

### 4. Flow

1. Reference data administrator: loads a retention rule version through POST /admin/reference-loads with table retention_rule; the owner approves it.
2. RetentionRuleLoader: validates the rows (known product, known table in sys_objects, months between 1 and 600, table not decision_log_entry) and stores the version.
3. Quartz: starts JOB-17 Retention job on the first Sunday of the month.
4. RetentionService: reads the rules in force on the run date.
5. RetentionService: calls CaseHoldQuery.casesOnLegalHold() and excludes every row of those cases.
6. RetentionService: selects, per rule, the rows whose age-basis field is older than the run date minus the retention months.
7. ArchiveWriter: writes the selected rows per table to the archive container with a manifest (row count and SHA-256 per file) and reads the manifest back.
8. RetentionService: after the manifest matches, deletes the archived rows from the live table in one transaction per table and rule, under the purge setting the append-only trigger allows.
9. RetentionService: records on the job run the counts per product and table, the rule version, the archive location and the hold report (case numbers and row counts kept).
10. Compliance officer: reads the run result through GET /admin/jobs and the summary alert (MSG-P1-020).

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A case is on legal hold | Its rows are kept and listed in the hold report | MSG-P1-020 | AC3 |
| X2 | A rule row has months outside 1 to 600 | Load refused in full; previous version stays in force | MSG-GEN-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | The archive write or the manifest check fails | No row deleted; run Failed; alert raised; rerun from the job monitor | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X4 | JOB-17 runs again for the same month | Rows already archived are gone; the rerun archives only rows still past their rule | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A row is exactly at its retention age | The row is kept | None | AC7 |
| X6 | A rule names table decision_log_entry | Load refused in full; the decision log is never archived by this job | MSG-P1-002 | AC8 |
| X7 | A rerun is posted while JOB-17 runs | 409; one run continues | MSG-P2-006 | AC9 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the tables (RWB-E1-001), the reference data service (RWB-E1-043), the data product table (RWB-E1-064) and the archive container (RWB-TE-012) |
| Negotiable | Periods, tables and age-basis fields are rule rows; the story fixes the archive, purge and hold behavior |
| Valuable | The store keeps no row longer than its rule, and each removal is recorded |
| Estimable | One rule table, one job, one archive writer, one trigger change |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic rows with a test clock |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Retention and archive rule for the data store

  Background:
    Given retention rule version "RET-2026.11" holds product "DP05", table "interaction", age basis "occurred_at", 24 months
    Given the run date is Sunday 2026-12-06

  Scenario: AC1 Retention rule applied
    Given 1,250 interaction rows with occurred_at before 2024-12-06 and 4,800 rows from 2024-12-06 onward
    When JOB-17 runs
    Then 1,250 rows move to the archive container under "retention/2026-12-06/interaction/"
    Then the 1,250 rows are no longer in the live interaction table
    Then the job run logs count 1,250 for DP05 interaction under rule version "RET-2026.11"

  Scenario: AC2 Rule changed as data
    Given retention rule version "RET-2027.01" changes DP05 interaction to 36 months, approved and valid from 2027-01-01
    Given interaction rows with occurred_at on 2024-01-15 and on 2023-12-20
    When JOB-17 runs on Sunday 2027-01-03
    Then the row from 2024-01-15 stays in the live table
    Then the row from 2023-12-20 moves to the archive container
    Then the job run logs rule version "RET-2027.01"

  Scenario: AC3 Legal hold
    Given case "RW-2024-000311" is marked legal hold and has 40 interaction rows older than 24 months
    When JOB-17 runs

  Scenario: AC5 The archive write fails

  Scenario: AC6 A repeat run in the same month
    Given JOB-17 archived 1,250 rows on 2026-12-06
    When JOB-17 is rerun on 2026-12-06
    Then the system archives 0 rows
    Then the archive container still holds one set of the 1,250 rows

  Scenario: AC7 A row exactly at its retention age
    Given an interaction row with occurred_at 2024-12-06T00:00+07:00
    When JOB-17 runs on 2026-12-06
    Then the row stays in the live table

  Scenario: AC8 A rule for the decision log is refused
    Given a retention load version "RET-2026.12" with a row for product "DP12", table "decision_log_entry"
    When the load is validated
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-002 and check "decision_log_entry is not archived by the retention job"

  Scenario: AC9 A rerun while the job is running
    Given JOB-17 is running
    When a platform administrator posts a rerun of JOB-17
    Then the system refuses the rerun with status 409 and MSG-P2-006
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Each data product and table has one retention rule in force, held as a versioned data row | Retention classes reference table (refdata.txt); DL26; Principle 1 |
| BR2 | A row older than its retention period on its age-basis field is archived and removed from the live store | retention_rule.retention_months; REQ-RDF-013 |
| BR3 | A legal hold keeps every row of the case, overriding the retention rule | R-UNI-20; recovery_case.legal_hold; NFR-072 |
| BR4 | A row is removed only after its archive copy is written and checked | Archive container (RWB-TE-012); NFR-074 |
| BR5 | The decision log is not archived by this job; its retention is set by Compliance | NFR-030; ADR-009; DL26 |
| BR6 | A retention load with an exception is refused in full | Reference data change process, step 3; CTL-08 |
| BR7 | A new version applies from its valid-from date; earlier runs keep their recorded version | R-UNI-38 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the JOB-17 run status (Running, Complete, Failed) and the retention rule version in force.

### 12. Contract

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz cron `0 30 2 ? * SUN#1`, Asia/Bangkok |
| Job name | JOB-17 Retention job |
| Schedule | Monthly, first Sunday |
| Input | Retention rules in force on the run date; rows of each named table; legal hold cases from CaseHoldQuery |
| Output | Archive files and manifest under `retention/YYYY-MM-DD/<table>/` in the write-once container; deleted live rows; job run checks with counts per product and table, rule version, archive location and the hold report; summary alert MSG-P1-020 to Compliance |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | Run date and rule version. Selection reads live rows, so a rerun finds only rows not yet archived |
| Restart behavior | Each table and rule is one unit: archive, check, delete. A failure before the delete leaves the live rows; a rerun repeats the unit. A failure after the delete leaves a complete archive |

**Endpoints used**

| Method and path | Use | Authorization | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads | Load retention_rule rows with validFrom | Reference data, C | 409 version clash (MSG-GEN-004); 422 invalid row (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002) |
| POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve | Approve the version | Reference data, A | 404; 409 |
| GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs | Read the JOB-17 run and its checks | Platform administration, R | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002); 503 |
| POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun | Rerun a failed JOB-17; header Idempotency-Key | Platform administration, U | 404; 409 job running (MSG-P2-006) |

**Published interfaces**

```java
// P1, called by the reference data service after approval
package recovery.dataengine.retention.api;
public interface RetentionRuleLoader {
    LoadResult apply(String ruleVersion, LocalDate validFrom, List<RetentionRuleRow> rows);
}

// P3, called by JOB-17
package recovery.casewf.api;
public interface CaseHoldQuery {
    Set<UUID> casesOnLegalHold();
    Map<UUID, String> caseNumbers(Set<UUID> caseIds);
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/dataengine/retention`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.retention`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RetentionJob | Job | Quartz job for JOB-17; no concurrent run |
| RetentionService | Service | Reads rules in force, selects rows, excludes legal holds, deletes after the archive check |
| ArchiveWriter | Service | Writes JSON lines files and the manifest to the write-once container; verifies count and SHA-256 |
| RetentionRuleLoader | Published interface | Validates and stores an approved retention version |
| RetentionRuleRepository | Repository | Reads and writes retention_rule |
| RetentionRule | Entity | One row per product, table and version |
| Retention rule table | Rule table | retention_rule rows by version and valid-from date |

- Database: table retention_rule (new, Flyway migration in this story) with id uuid, product_code varchar(4), table_name varchar(60) referencing sys_objects(object_name), record_class varchar(20), retention_months integer check between 1 and 600, age_basis_field varchar(60), rule_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, approved_by uuid, standard columns; unique (product_code, table_name, record_class, rule_version). Flyway migration replacing refuse_change() so that DELETE on interaction is allowed only when the transaction setting `recovery.retention_purge` is 'on', set by RetentionService inside its delete transaction; UPDATE stays refused, and decision_log_entry keeps the unconditional refusal. Index ix_interaction_case_time (case_id, occurred_at) from Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql serves the selection.
- Configuration and reference data: retention version "RET-2026.11" (assumed 24 months for DP05 interaction until the bank schedule arrives; DL26) prepared by Compliance and loaded by the reference data administrator; properties `rwb.dataengine.retention.archive-container` and `rwb.dataengine.retention.batch-size=5000`.
- Build steps:
  1. Flyway migration for retention_rule and the refuse_change() change; test that UPDATE and DELETE are still refused outside the purge setting and on decision_log_entry always.
  2. RetentionRuleLoader with whole-load validation: product in data_product, table in sys_objects, not decision_log_entry, months 1 to 600, age-basis field in sys_fields for the table.
  3. RetentionService selection by rule and run date, with the legal hold exclusion from CaseHoldQuery.
  4. ArchiveWriter with manifest write and read-back check.
  5. Delete step per table and rule, after the check, under the purge setting.
  6. Job run checks, hold report and the MSG-P1-020 summary alert.
  7. RetentionJob on Quartz with `@DisallowConcurrentExecution`.
  8. Tests for AC1 to AC9 and the access test.
- Feature flag: `rwb.dataengine.retention`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass and the JOB-17 run book from RWB-E1-056 covers a failed run.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-020 | Retention run summary to Compliance (new, see additions) | {count} rows of {product} were archived under rule {rule} version {version}. {held} cases on legal hold were kept. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | retention_months outside 1 to 600 | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P1-002 | Retention load refused at a check | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | Archive container unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P2-006 | Rerun while JOB-17 runs | {job} is already running. Wait for it to finish before you rerun it. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right on the job monitor | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

No screen in this story. Compliance reads the run result, the counts and the hold report through GET /admin/jobs and the summary alert. Retention classes show on SCR-47 Personal data from Epic 8; until then they are loaded by file.

### 17. Guardrails

## RWB-E1-018 Case ID issuance and case record v1

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-018 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-01 Generate the case ID; FEAT-CWC-02 Create one case per customer and product; FEAT-CWC-03 Hold the case state in the ACE database; FEAT-CWC-04 Apply the entry rule at 90 days past due; FEAT-CWC-05 Apply the exclusion rules as data; FEAT-CWC-20 Expose the workflow admin API; FEAT-CWC-21 Log every workflow event |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-001, REQ-CWC-002, REQ-CWC-003, REQ-CWC-004, REQ-CWC-005, REQ-CWC-016, REQ-CHO-004 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, section 5.3 |
| L3 process | 6.1 Take over the case at 90 days past due |
| Decision | D6 entry |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-016, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-042 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **product owner**, I want **every account at 90 days past due or more that is not excluded placed on one recovery case per customer and product, with a case ID in the form RW-YYYY-NNNNNN issued at creation and never reused, a status and its linked accounts, created by rule from the daily load**, so that **every team, letter and document refers to one case ID**.

### 2. Business rationale

Recovery teams keep their own lists today, so one account can be on several trackers under different references, and some accounts at 90 days past due have no owner at all (control CTL-01 answers this audit finding). This story creates the case by rule the morning after the account reaches 90 days past due, blocks excluded accounts with a logged reason, and gives the case an ID that every later document carries. It meets REQ-CWC-001 to REQ-CWC-005 and REQ-CWC-016, and supports reconciliation REC-01 (accounts at 90 days past due against open cases, zero unexplained).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-016 is done: the account, arrears and party data products are readable by SY-CASEWF through the P1 published interface.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available.
- RWB-E1-042 is done: parameter `case.entry.dpd` = 90 is in force (DL16).
- The exclusion rows (rule table EXCLUSION) are loaded with reason codes DECEASED, FRAUD, BANKRUPTCY, ACTIVE_PLAN and OPEN_DISPUTE (REQ-CWC-004).
- The exposure band table is served by the reference data service (RWB-E1-043, LOV-EXPOSURE).
- JOB-01 has passed its load checks for the business date and published LoadCompleted (EV-26).
- The job runs as SY-CASEWF. Readers hold Case record R (roles.txt permission matrix).

### 4. Flow

1. JOB-01: publishes LoadCompleted for source COLLINS and business date 2026-12-01.
2. CaseCreationJob (JOB-02): starts on LoadCompleted and reads the entry threshold parameter `case.entry.dpd`.
3. CaseCreationJob: asks the P1 interface for every account with days_past_due at or above 90 on the business date that has no open case link.
4. EntryRuleEvaluator (SY-RULES): evaluates the exclusion rows in force for each account; an excluded account gets an exclusion record with the reason code, rule ID and version, and no case.
5. CaseGrouping: groups the remaining accounts by primary customer and product group; an existing open case for the same pair receives the new account link instead of a new case.
6. CaseNumberIssuer: takes the next number from the sequence for the entry year and formats RW-2026-000123.
7. CaseCreationService: in one transaction writes recovery_case with status NEW, case_account rows, the BORROWER case_party row and CaseCreated (EV-01) in the outbox.
8. CaseCreationService: as the last step before commit, calls DecisionLogWriter.write with decision code "D6", final call "CASE_CREATED", the entry rule version and the inputs; a failed write rolls the transaction back.
9. CaseCreationJob: records counts (accounts read, excluded, linked, created, failed) on the job record; JOB-03 starts after it.
10. Case owner: opens the case through GET /cases/{caseId} and its accounts through GET /cases/{caseId}/accounts.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The account matches an exclusion row | No case; exclusion record with reason code and rule version | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X2 | The account's customer already has an open case for the same product | The account is linked to that case; no new case | None | AC3 |
| X3 | Days past due is 89 | No case; the account is read again the next day | None | AC7 |
| X4 | JOB-02 runs again for the same business date | No duplicate case, link or number | None | AC8 |
| X5 | The COLLINS load was refused or is late | JOB-02 does not start; no case from stale data; runs after the next good load | MSG-P1-001 | AC9 |
| X6 | Decision log write fails | The case is not created and no number is consumed by a visible case; the account is retried in the next run | MSG-P7-003 | AC10 |
| X7 | The yearly number range RW-2026-999999 is used | Creation stops for the year's remaining accounts; incident raised | MSG-P3-025 | AC11 |
| X8 | The same customer has a Mortgage and a hire purchase account at 90 days past due | Two cases, one per product | None | AC12 |
| X9 | A role without Case record R reads a case | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-018-13 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the data products (RWB-E1-016), the decision log writer (RWB-E1-027) and the parameter service (RWB-E1-042); allocation follows in RWB-E1-020 |
| Negotiable | Threshold, exclusion reasons and exposure bands are data values; the story fixes the behavior |
| Valuable | Gives about 28,100 accounts at 90 days past due one case each at go-live (DL15) |
| Estimable | One job, one numbering service, one entry evaluator, two read endpoints |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin

  Background:
    Given parameter "case.entry.dpd" is 90
    Given the exclusion rows version "EXCL-2026.11" are in force
    Given the business date is 2026-12-01
    Given the COLLINS load for 2026-12-01 has passed its checks

  Scenario: AC1 Case created at 90 days past due
    Given account A-5001 of customer P-0101, product group "HIRE_PURCHASE", reaches 90 days past due in the load with no exclusion

    When the entry rule runs
    Then case RW-2026-000123 exists with status "NEW", no stage code and entry date 2026-12-01
    Then the system links account A-5001 as the primary account and P-0101 as "BORROWER"
    Then the system publishes caseCreated with case number RW-2026-000123

  Scenario: AC2 Exclusion applied
    Given account A-5002 at 92 days past due with tdr_flag = true
    When the entry rule runs
    Then the system creates no case for A-5002
    Then an exclusion record holds account A-5002, reason "ACTIVE_PLAN", the exclusion rule ID and version "EXCL-2026.11"

  Scenario: AC3 One case per customer and product
    Given customer P-0102 has two hire purchase accounts A-5003 and A-5004, both at 95 days past due
    When the entry rule runs
    Then one case exists for P-0102 and "HIRE_PURCHASE" with both accounts linked
    Then total outstanding at entry is the sum of the two balances, THB 412,350.00

  Scenario: AC4 ID never reused
    Given case RW-2026-000123 was closed on 2026-12-15
    When a new case is created on 2026-12-16
    Then it receives RW-2026-000124
    Then case RW-2026-000123 is still returned by a search on its case number

  Scenario: AC5 State model as data
    Given the list LOV-CASE-STATUS gains the value "WAITING_COURT" through a list load with valid from 2027-01-01
    When a case moves to "WAITING_COURT" on 2027-01-02
    Then the case service accepts the value without a code change
    Then the decision log entry for the move carries the list version in force

  Scenario: AC6 Exclusion rules as data
    Given the exclusion rows include reason "OPEN_DISPUTE"
    When account A-5005 at 90 days past due with an open dispute arrives
    Then the system creates no case
    Then the exclusion record for A-5005 holds reason "OPEN_DISPUTE"

  Scenario: AC7 The entry threshold boundary
    Given account A-5006 at 89 days past due and account A-5007 at 90 days past due, both with no exclusion
    When the entry rule runs
    Then the system creates a case for A-5007
    Then the system creates no case for A-5006

  Scenario: AC8 A repeated run creates nothing new
    Given JOB-02 has created case RW-2026-000125 for account A-5008 on 2026-12-01
    When JOB-02 runs again for 2026-12-01
    Then account A-5008 has one case link
    Then the system issues no case number in the second run

  Scenario: AC9 No cases from a refused load
    Given the COLLINS load for 2026-12-02 was refused at the control total check
    When the morning schedule runs
    Then JOB-02 does not start for 2026-12-02
    Then the job monitor shows MSG-P1-001 for the account data product
    Then JOB-02 runs for 2026-12-02 after the next load passes

  Scenario: AC10 The decision log write fails
    Given the decision log store is unavailable
    When the entry rule runs for account A-5009
    Then no case exists for A-5009
    Then the job record lists A-5009 as failed with MSG-P7-003
    Then the system takes A-5009 again in the next run

  Scenario: AC11 The yearly number range is used up
    Given the last case number issued in 2026 is RW-2026-999999
    When account A-5010 qualifies for a new case on 2026-12-30
    Then the system creates no case for A-5010
    Then the job record carries MSG-P3-025 with year 2026
    Then the system raises an incident to the platform administrator

  Scenario: AC12 Two products give two cases
    Given customer P-0103 has mortgage account A-5011 and hire purchase account A-5012, both at 91 days past due
    When the entry rule runs
    Then two cases exist for P-0103, one with product group "MORTGAGE" and one with "HIRE_PURCHASE"
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | An account enters recovery when days past due is at or above the entry threshold | Parameter case.entry.dpd = 90; DL16 |
| BR2 | One case per customer and product, with every qualifying account linked | DL17; REQ-CWC-003 |
| BR3 | An account matching an exclusion row gets no case; the reason is recorded | Exclusion rows (rule table EXCLUSION); REQ-CWC-004 |
| BR4 | The case number is RW, the entry year and a six-digit number from a yearly sequence; it is issued once and never reused | recovery_case.case_no (DF-CAS-002); uk_recovery_case |
| BR5 | A new case has status NEW and no owner until allocation | casemodel.txt Case status "New" |
| BR6 | Status values are read from the list, not from code | LOV-CASE-STATUS; Principle 1 |
| BR7 | No case is created from a load that failed its checks | CTL-02; JOB-02 "No cases from stale data" |
| BR8 | Every case creation writes its decision log entry in the same transaction; a failed write rolls the creation back | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR9 | Exposure band is set from the total outstanding at entry using the band table in force | recovery_case.exposure_band (DF-CAS-015); LOV-EXPOSURE |
| BR10 | A case created on bad data is canceled by rule, never deleted | R-UNI-16 (Epic 2 handling) |

### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | LoadCompleted (EV-26), entry rule | days_past_due at or above 90, no exclusion, no open case for the customer and product | New |
| New | Allocation rule matched | Handled by RWB-E1-020 | Assigned |

### 12. Contract

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | LoadCompleted (EV-26) for source COLLINS with all checks passed |
| Job name | JOB-02 Case creation |
| Schedule | Daily after JOB-01 |
| Input | Account snapshots at or above the threshold from the P1 interface; exclusion rows in force; exposure band table |
| Output | recovery_case, case_account, case_party and case_entry_exclusion rows; decision log entries; job record counts |
| Events published | CaseCreated (EV-01: caseId, caseNo, productGroup, accounts, businessDate) |
| Idempotency key | accountId and businessDate for the entry decision; uniqueness of an open case per primary customer and product group |
| Restart | Rerun from the job monitor; accounts already linked or excluded for the date are skipped; a failed account is retried |

**Endpoints**

| Item | GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId} | GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/accounts |
|---|---|---|
| Request | Path caseId (uuid) | Path caseId (uuid) |
| Response | Case: id, caseNo, productGroup, primaryCustomerId, status, entryDate, dpdAtEntry, exposureBand, totalOutstandingAtEntry, deviationOpen, legalHold | CaseAccount[]: id, caseId, accountId, isPrimary, linkedFrom, linkedTo |
| Errors | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002); 404 not found or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 503 store down | Same |
| Authorization | Case record, right R, scope applied | Case record, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable | Not applicable |

GET /api/recovery/v1/cases is used for the case number search in AC4 with a new query parameter caseNo (see additions).

**Published interfaces**

```java
// P3, package recovery.casewf.casecreation (published)
public interface CaseRecordService {
    Optional<CaseView> findByCaseNo(String caseNo);
    Optional<CaseView> findOpenCase(UUID primaryCustomerId, String productGroup);
}

// P1, used by this story (RWB-E1-016)
public interface RecoveryDataQuery {
    List<AccountEntrySnapshot> accountsAtOrAbove(int daysPastDue, LocalDate businessDate);
}
public record AccountEntrySnapshot(UUID accountId, UUID primaryPartyId, String productGroup,
        String regionCode, int daysPastDue, BigDecimal totalBalance, boolean tdrFlag,
        boolean disputeOpen, boolean deceased, boolean bankrupt, boolean fraud, LocalDate dataAsOf) {}

// P7, used by this story (RWB-E1-027)
// package recovery.decision.writer; called inside the caller's transaction as the last step before commit
public interface DecisionLogWriter {
    DecisionLogEntryRef write(DecisionLogRecord record)
        throws DecisionLogRecordInvalidException, DecisionLogUnavailableException;
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery/casewf/casecreation`, Java package `recovery.casewf.casecreation`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseCreationJob | Job | JOB-02; listens for LoadCompleted; runs the entry rule per account; writes job counts |
| EntryRuleEvaluator | Service | Applies the threshold and the exclusion rows; returns ENTER or EXCLUDE with reason and rule version |
| CaseGrouping | Service | Groups accounts by primary customer and product group; finds an open case to link to |
| CaseNumberIssuer | Service | Draws from sequence case_no_seq_YYYY and formats RW-YYYY-NNNNNN; refuses above 999999 |
| CaseCreationService | Service | Decision log write, then case, account links, party link and outbox event in one transaction |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | recovery_case, case_account, case_party, case_entry_exclusion |
| CaseAndWorkflowController | Controller | GET /cases/{caseId}, GET /cases/{caseId}/accounts, caseNo search on GET /cases |
| CaseStatusCatalog | Service | Reads LOV-CASE-STATUS through the P4 list interface; no Java enum of statuses |
| ExclusionRuleTable | Rule table | Rule rows with rule table EXCLUSION, read through RuleTableReader (P4) |

**Database**

- Writes recovery_case (all columns), case_account (all columns), case_party (all columns), case_entry_exclusion (new), outbox.
- Constraint: partial unique index `ux_case_open_customer_product ON recovery_case (primary_customer_id, product_group) WHERE closed_date IS NULL`.
- Constraint: unique `case_account (account_id) WHERE linked_to IS NULL`, so an account is on one open case.
- Migration in this story: `V018_1__case_creation.sql` creates table case_entry_exclusion (id, account_id, business_date, reason_code, rule_id, rule_version, standard columns, unique (account_id, business_date)), the yearly sequences case_no_seq_2026 and case_no_seq_2027 (created ahead by the job each December), and the two indexes above.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Parameter `case.entry.dpd` = 90 (RWB-E1-042; DL16), owner RW-COE.
- Exclusion rows "EXCL-2026.11" with the five reason codes, loaded by RW-COE through RWB-E1-029.
- LOV-EXPOSURE bands and LOV-CASE-STATUS from the reference data service (RWB-E1-043).

**Build steps**

1. CaseNumberIssuer with the yearly sequence and the 999999 limit; unit and integration tests for AC1, AC4, AC11.
2. EntryRuleEvaluator over the threshold parameter and the exclusion rows; tests for AC2, AC6, AC7.
3. CaseGrouping with the open case lookup; tests for AC3, AC12.
4. CaseCreationService: the case, links and outbox row, then the decision log write as the last step in the same transaction; test for AC10.
5. CaseCreationJob on LoadCompleted with idempotent skip; tests for AC8, AC9.
6. CaseStatusCatalog reading statuses from the list; test for AC5.
7. Controller endpoints with access check and scope; caseNo search; access test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.casecreation`. Off: JOB-02 does not create cases.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and REC-01 shows zero unexplained difference on the SIT data set.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the threshold, the exclusion reasons, the bands and the status list are data.
- No personal data in logs, tests, events or prompts. Test data uses synthetic account and customer IDs only.
- No read of another module's tables: account and party data come through RecoveryDataQuery (P1); rules through RuleTableReader (P4).
- The case number is printed on every outbound document; other modules take it from CaseRecordService, never from a copy.

## RWB-E1-019 Roles, teams and queues as data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-019 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-06 Hold roles, teams and queues as data; FEAT-ACA-03 Hold roles as data |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-006, REQ-ACA-002 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3 and 3.4; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.4 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-038, RWB-E1-043 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **reference data administrator (RW-REFADM)**, I want **queues, queue membership and capacity, each tied to a team code and a role code, held as versioned reference data loaded from the Excel template**, so that **the organization changes without a code release**.

### 2. Business rationale

Team structure and who works which list are held in spreadsheets today, and a change of team needs a change request to IT. This story holds every queue, its team, its role, its method, its cap, its overflow queue and its members as versioned tables QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER, loaded from one template through the reference data service, with an approver and a one-call rollback, and applies the version in force to the queue tables the engines use. It meets REQ-CWC-006 and REQ-ACA-002 and is the input to allocation (RWB-E1-020), to scope by team (RWB-E1-037) and to control CTL-08.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-043 is done: ReferenceVersionRegistry and ReferenceDataService hold versions of reference tables, and POST /admin/reference-loads calls them; QUEUE is a LOV-REF-TABLE code and QUEUE_MEMBER is added to it (see additions).
- RWB-E1-038 is done: the reference approval pattern is in use for the delegation table.
- The ROLE and TEAM tables have a version in force (RWB-E1-043); TEAM holds "TDR-BKK", "DIL-BKK", "LIT-BKK", "NPA-BKK", "DS-BKK" and "WO-BKK" (assumed codes; owner Shared operations), each with its region code.
- The loader holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C). The approver is the table owner for queues, Shared operations, acting through RW-TEAMMGR with Reference data A (assumed grant; DL01).
- Queue member user IDs are Entra ID object IDs of people who hold the queue's role.

### 4. Flow

1. RW-REFADM: fills the Queues template (sheets QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER) and calls POST /admin/reference-loads once per sheet with valid from 2026-11-30.
2. QueueTableChecks: runs the queue checks on top of the RWB-E1-043 row checks: team code in TEAM, role code in ROLE, method in LOV-ASSIGN, cap range, overflow queue exists and forms no loop, member holds the queue role.
3. ReferenceVersionRegistry (RWB-E1-043): on any failed row refuses the load whole and names every failed row; on a clean file stores the version with status VALIDATED.
4. RW-TEAMMGR: approves through POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve; refused if the approver is the author.
5. QueueVersionApplier: on the valid from date, applies the QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER versions in force to the queue and queue_member tables: upsert by queue code keeping the queue ID, replace active member rows, set table_version.
6. CapacityService: answers capacity questions for the allocation engine from the applied version.
7. QueueMembershipQuery: answers the teams and regions of a user for scope by team (RWB-E1-037).
8. RW-REFADM: if the version is wrong, calls POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback; the previous version is in force again and QueueVersionApplier re-applies it in one transaction.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A queue names a team code not in TEAM | Load refused in full; the row is named | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X2 | A cap outside 1 to 500 | Load refused in full | MSG-GEN-002 | AC5 |
| X3 | The approver is the author | Approval refused; version stays VALIDATED | MSG-P7-002 | AC6 |
| X4 | Rollback with no earlier version | Refused; current version unchanged | MSG-P3-015 | AC7 |
| X5 | The same file is loaded again for the same valid from | The existing load is returned; nothing new is written (RWB-E1-043 idempotency) | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Valid from is in the future | The version waits; the current version stays in force until that date | None | AC9 |
| X7 | A member does not hold the queue's role | Load refused in full; the member row is named | MSG-P1-002 | AC10 |
| X8 | Overflow queues form a loop | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC11 |
| X9 | A required column is empty | Load refused in full | MSG-GEN-001 | AC12 |
| X10 | A role without Reference data C loads a file | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-019-13 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the reference data service of RWB-E1-043; adds the queue checks, the apply step and two read interfaces |
| Negotiable | Team codes, queues, caps and members are data; the template layout can change with the checks |
| Valuable | A team change takes one load and one approval instead of a release |
| Estimable | One check set, one applier, two read services, one migration |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Roles, teams and queues as data

  Background:
    Given TEAM holds "TDR-BKK", "DIL-BKK", "LIT-BKK", "NPA-BKK", "DS-BKK" and "WO-BKK"
    Given the loader holds RW-REFADM and the approver holds RW-TEAMMGR

  Scenario: AC1 Tables loaded
    Given the Queues template with 12 queues for the TDR, DIL, litigation, NPA, debt sale and write-off teams and 48 member rows
    When the QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER sheets are loaded as version 1 with valid from 2026-11-30 and approved
    Then 12 queue rows are in force with table version 1
    Then each queue holds its team code and the role that works it, for example "LIT-BKK-OFF" with "LIT-BKK" and RW-LITOFF
    Then 48 member rows are in force
    Then the reference version holds the author, the approver and the approval time

  Scenario: AC2 Rollback
    Given QUEUE version 3 is in force with an error in queue "DIL-BKK-CO"
    Given QUEUE version 2 was in force before it
    When rollback is called once for version 3
    Then QUEUE version 2 is in force for every queue row
    Then each queue keeps its record ID, so cases in the queue keep their queue
    Then the system records the rollback with the caller, the time and the reason

  Scenario: AC3 Capacity
    Given member U-11 of queue "TDR-BKK-CO" has capacity 40 and holds 40 open cases
    When a 41st case is offered for U-11
    Then the capacity service answers "AT_CAP" for U-11
    Then names the overflow queue "TDR-BKK-OVF" for the case

  Scenario: AC4 Unknown team code
    Given the QUEUE sheet has queue "XYZ-CO" on row 7 with team code "XYZ"
    When it is loaded
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-002 naming row 7 and check "team code not in TEAM"
    Then no queue or member row changes

  Scenario: AC5 Cap outside its range
    Given queue "NPA-BKK-CO" has capacity cap 0
    When the QUEUE sheet is loaded
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-GEN-002 for capacity cap with minimum 1 and maximum 500

  Scenario: AC6 Author cannot approve
    Given QUEUE version 4 was loaded by user U-90
    When U-90 approves it
    Then the system refuses the approval with MSG-P7-002
    Then version 4 stays VALIDATED and is not in force

  Scenario: AC7 Rollback with no earlier version
    Given QUEUE version 1 is the only version
    When rollback is called for version 1
    Then the system refuses the call with MSG-P3-015
    Then version 1 stays in force

  Scenario: AC8 The same file loaded twice
    Given the QUEUE sheet for valid from 2026-12-15 was loaded as version 5
    When the same file is loaded again for valid from 2026-12-15
    Then the response returns version 5
    Then the system writes no new version

  Scenario: AC9 A version with a future valid from
    Given QUEUE version 2 is in force and version 3 is approved with valid from 2026-12-15
    When the capacity service is asked on 2026-12-14
    Then it answers from version 2
    Then on 2026-12-15 it answers from version 3

  Scenario: AC10 Member without the queue role
    Given member U-12 on row 22 of the QUEUE_MEMBER sheet is listed on queue "LIT-BKK-OFF" and does not hold RW-LITOFF
    When the sheet is loaded
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P1-002 naming row 22 and check "member does not hold the queue role"

  Scenario: AC11 Overflow loop
    Given queue "DS-BKK-CO" overflows to "DS-BKK-OVF" and "DS-BKK-OVF" overflows to "DS-BKK-CO"
    When the QUEUE sheet is loaded
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P1-002 and check "overflow queues form a loop"

  Scenario: AC12 Required column empty
    Given queue row 3 has no assignment method
    When the QUEUE sheet is loaded
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-GEN-001 for assignment method on row 3
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every queue belongs to one team and one role | queue.team_code (DF-WRK-004), queue.role_code (DF-WRK-005); LOV-TEAM, LOV-ROLE |
| BR2 | A load with any failed row is refused in full | Reference data change process, step 3; CTL-08 |
| BR3 | A version takes effect on its valid from date after approval; open cases keep the queue they are in | Reference data change process, steps 5 and 6; R-UNI-38 |
| BR4 | The author of a load cannot approve it | Separation of duty table; CTL-08 |
| BR5 | Rollback returns the previous version in one call | Reference data change process, step 7; REQ-CWC-006 |
| BR6 | A person's capacity is the lower of their member capacity and the queue cap | queue.capacity_cap (DF-WRK-007); DL23 |
| BR7 | Assignment method is one of ROUND_ROBIN, LOWEST_LOAD, NAMED_OWNER, SKILL | LOV-ASSIGN |
| BR8 | Cap range 1 to 500 | Parameter `queue.cap.max` = 500 (assumed; DL23), RWB-E1-042 |
| BR9 | A member must hold the queue's role | ROLE table; P4 role directory |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the status of a reference version (RWB-E1-043): VALIDATED, APPROVED, ROLLED_BACK, and the table_version applied to the queue rows.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Load | Every row passes | VALIDATED |
| VALIDATED | Approve | Approver is not the author | APPROVED; applied on its valid from date |
| APPROVED | Rollback | An earlier approved version exists | ROLLED_BACK; the earlier version is applied |

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-REFADM | Loads the sheets and calls rollback (Reference data CRUD) |
| RW-TEAMMGR | Approves a queues version as the Shared operations owner (Reference data A, assumed grant; DL01) |
| RW-COE | Reads versions (Reference data CRUD); may load |
| RW-RISK | No part in queue loads; may not hold RW-REFADM (separation of duty) |
| SY-CASEWF | Applies the version on its valid from date and answers capacity and membership questions |
| No delegation of authority level applies | Queue structure is not a credit decision |

### 12. Contract

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads** (P4 endpoint, RWB-E1-043)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file (xlsx sheet), table = "QUEUE" or "QUEUE_MEMBER", validFrom (date) |
| Response | 201 ReferenceLoad: id, table, validFrom, status, rows |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Reference data C (MSG-P4-002); 422 a row fails (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002; queue checks as MSG-P1-002 with the rows in Problem.detail); 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right C |
| Idempotency | Table code, valid from and content hash (RWB-E1-043) |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve** (P4 endpoint)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Response | 200 ReferenceLoad with status APPROVED |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Reference data A; 404; 409 approver is the author (MSG-P7-002) or the version changed (MSG-GEN-004); 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right A |

**POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback** (new endpoint, see additions)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path loadId (uuid); body { reason: string, required } |
| Response | 200 ReferenceLoad with status ROLLED_BACK |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Reference data U; 404; 409 no earlier version (MSG-P3-015); 422 reason empty (MSG-GEN-001); 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right U |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the first result |

**Published interfaces**

```java
// P3, package recovery.casewf.queues.api (published)

    CapacityAnswer check(UUID queueId, UUID userId, LocalDate onDate);
    List<QueueMemberView> membersInForce(UUID queueId, LocalDate onDate);
}

}
public interface QueueMembershipQuery {

}
// P3 checks plugged into the RWB-E1-043 registry for table codes QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery/casewf/queues`, Java package `recovery.casewf.queues`; published types in `recovery.casewf.queues.api`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| QueueTableChecks | Service | ReferenceTableCheck for QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER: team, role, method, cap range, overflow loop, member role |
| QueueVersionApplier | Job | Daily at 00:05, and on approval or rollback, applies the QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER versions in force to queue and queue_member |
| CapacityService | Published interface | Open cases against capacity for the applied version |
| QueueMembershipQuery | Published interface | Teams, regions and queues of a user, for scope (RWB-E1-037) |
| ReferenceRollbackHandler | Service | Rollback for reference loads: marks the version ROLLED_BACK through the registry and triggers the applier |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | queue, queue_member, open case counts |

**Database**

- Writes queue (all columns plus table_version) and queue_member.
- Reads recovery_case (owner_user_id, queue_id, status) for open case counts (index ix_case_owner_status).
- Migration in this story: `V019_1__queue_member.sql` creates queue_member (id, queue_id, user_id, capacity, skill_codes, table_version, valid_from, valid_to, standard columns; index on (queue_id) where is_active; index on (user_id) where is_active) and adds queue.table_version.

**Configuration and reference data**

- TEAM, ROLE, QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER through ReferenceDataService (RWB-E1-043); LOV-ASSIGN through the P4 list interface.
- Parameter `queue.cap.max` = 500 (assumed; DL23) from RWB-E1-042.
- The Queues template, owned by Shared operations.

**Build steps**

1. QueueTableChecks with one check per rule; unit tests for AC4, AC5, AC10, AC11, AC12.
2. Add the checks to the RWB-E1-043 registry for QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER; test AC8 through the registry's idempotency.
3. Approval through the registry; test AC6.
4. QueueVersionApplier: upsert queues by queue code keeping the ID, replace member rows; tests AC1, AC9.
5. ReferenceRollbackHandler and the rollback endpoint; tests AC2, AC7.
6. CapacityService with the lower of member capacity and queue cap; test AC3.
7. QueueMembershipQuery for RWB-E1-037.
8. Access test on the load endpoint.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.queuetables`. Off: the applier does not run and the queue rows from the seed migration stay.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the SIT queue set for six teams loads, approves and rolls back.

| MSG-GEN-002 | Cap outside 1 to 500 | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |

| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

## RWB-E1-020 Allocation and assignment engine v1

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-020 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-07 Run the allocation rule table; FEAT-CWC-08 Run the assignment engine by load and continuity; FEAT-CWC-09 Send a case to the overflow queue when no rule matches |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-007, REQ-CWC-008, REQ-CWC-009, REQ-CWC-016 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, section 5.3 |
| L3 process | 18.3.2 Allocate work to teams, people and partners by rule; 6.1 Take over the case at 90 days past due |
| Decision | D6 entry, take over and own the case |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-019, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-056 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **every new recovery case placed in a queue and given an owner by the allocation and assignment rule tables on the morning it arrives**, so that **each case at 90 days past due has one owner from its first day and nobody allocates cases by hand**.

### 2. Business rationale

Cases are allocated today from team spreadsheets, and ownership is agreed by email, so a case can wait days with no owner. This story places every new case in a queue and gives it an owner by rule before 07:00 on the morning after case creation, with the rule row and version on a decision log entry. It meets REQ-CWC-007, REQ-CWC-008, REQ-CWC-009 and REQ-CWC-016, and serves the business measure "cases inside the service level" (target set with DL22) and control CTL-03.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-018 is done: new cases exist with status NEW, product group, region and exposure band.
- RWB-E1-019 is done: queues, queue members and caseload caps are loaded; queue "MTG-BKK-CO" belongs to team "MTG-BKK" and role RW-CASEOWN.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available through its published interface.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: JOB-03 has a run book and appears in the job monitor.
- The allocation table version "ALLOC-2026.11" is loaded and approved (rule rows with rule table ALLOCATION; DL24). Every row holds row ID, product group, region, exposure band, target queue, valid from, valid to, approver and test case ID.
- Parameters loaded through RWB-E1-042: `allocation.exception.queue.code` = "RWB-EXC" and `allocation.deviation.queue.code` = "DEV-HANDLER" (assumed values; DL23).
- JOB-02 case creation has completed for today's business date after JOB-01 passed its load checks.
- The job runs as service identity SY-CASEWF; rules are evaluated as SY-RULES.

### 4. Flow

1. Quartz: starts JOB-03 Morning allocation after JOB-02 completes for business date 2026-12-01.
2. AllocationJob: selects every case with status NEW whose last allocation date is before the business date.
3. AllocationService: locks the case row and reads deviation_open; a case with an open deviation goes to the deviation handler queue (R-DEV-01).
4. AllocationRuleEvaluator (SY-RULES): reads the allocation rows in force on the business date and returns the first row, in row order, whose product group, region and exposure band match the case.
5. AssignmentEngine: reads the target queue's method (DF-WRK-006) and cap (DF-WRK-007), counts the open cases of each queue member and picks the owner below the cap by the method.
6. AllocationService: in one transaction sets queue, team, owner, status ASSIGNED, stage clock start and rule version, writes the assignment with reason ALLOCATION, sets the last allocation date and writes CaseAllocated (EV-02) to the outbox.
7. AllocationService: as the last step before commit, calls DecisionLogWriter.write with the row ID, table version, queue, owner and inputs; a failed write rolls the allocation back.
8. AllocationJob: after the last case, builds the allocation summary per team (MSG-P3-011, MSG-P3-012) and sends it to the team manager through the ACE notification path.
9. AllocationJob: records the run result (cases read, assigned, overflow, exception, failed) on the job record for the monitor.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Every owner in the target queue is at or above the cap | Case goes to the overflow queue of the target queue; status stays NEW; counted in the summary | MSG-P3-011 | AC4 |
| X2 | No allocation row matches the case | Case goes to the exception queue; status stays NEW; rule gap logged; CaseAllocationFailed (EV-03) published | MSG-P3-012 | AC5 |
| X3 | Decision log write fails | Allocation rolled back; case stays NEW with no queue change; retried in the next run | MSG-P3-013 | AC6 |
| X4 | Case has deviation_open = true | Case goes to the deviation handler queue; no case owner is chosen | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The run is repeated for the same business date | Cases already allocated for that date are skipped; no second assignment or log entry | None | AC8 |
| X6 | No case has status NEW | Run completes with zero counts; summary says 0 | MSG-P3-011, MSG-P3-012 with count 0 | AC9 |
| X7 | JOB-02 has not completed for the business date | JOB-03 does not start; job monitor shows it waiting; cases stay NEW | MSG-P1-001 | AC10 |
| X8 | A rerun starts while the first run still holds a case | The case row lock stops the second worker; each case is allocated once | None | AC11 |
| X9 | The overflow queue is not set on a queue whose owners are all at the cap | Case goes to the exception queue with the reason "no overflow queue" | MSG-P3-012 | AC13 |
| X10 | A user without the right reruns JOB-03 | Refused with 403; nothing runs | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-020-14 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the case record (RWB-E1-018), the roles, teams and queues table (RWB-E1-019), the decision log writer (RWB-E1-027) and the job monitoring (RWB-E1-056), all earlier in Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | The allocation method per queue, the cap and the queue codes are data values. The story fixes the behavior, not the values |
| Valuable | Ends allocation from spreadsheets for every new case, about 3,110 a month (DL15) |
| Estimable | One rule table, one service, one batch step, no screen |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Allocate a new recovery case to a queue and an owner

  Background:
    Given the allocation table version "ALLOC-2026.11" is in force from 2026-11-30
    Given the queue "MTG-BKK-CO" belongs to team "MTG-BKK" and role RW-CASEOWN
    Given the queue uses the method "ROUND_ROBIN" with a caseload cap of 150
    Given the queue "MTG-BKK-CO" has the overflow queue "MTG-BKK-OVF"
    Given the business date is 2026-12-01

  Scenario: AC1 A new case is placed in the queue its row names
    Given a new case RW-2026-000201 with status "NEW", product group "MORTGAGE", region "BKK" and exposure band "B2"
    Given allocation row "ALLOC-014" matches product group "MORTGAGE", region "BKK" and any exposure band, with target queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
    When the morning allocation run starts
    Then the system places the case in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
    Then the case team is "MTG-BKK" and the region is "BKK"

  Scenario: AC2 The owner is chosen by the queue's method
    Given queue "MTG-BKK-CO" holds three case owners U-01, U-02 and U-03 with 120, 95 and 140 open cases
    Given the last owner given a case in the queue was U-02
    When case RW-2026-000201 is placed in the queue
    Then the system gives the case to U-03
    Then the case status becomes "ASSIGNED"
    Then the system writes an assignment record with reason "ALLOCATION" and rule ID "ALLOC-014"

  Scenario: AC3 An owner at the caseload cap is skipped
    Given the last owner given a case was U-02
    Given U-03, the next owner in turn, holds 150 open cases
    Given U-01 holds 120 open cases
    When case RW-2026-000202 is placed in the queue
    Then the system gives the case to U-01, the following owner below the cap

  Scenario: AC4 Every owner is at the cap
    Given U-01, U-02 and U-03 each hold 150 open cases
    When case RW-2026-000203 is placed in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
    Then the system places the case in the overflow queue "MTG-BKK-OVF"
    Then the case status stays "NEW" and no owner is set
    Then the team manager of "MTG-BKK" receives the allocation summary with MSG-P3-011 and count 1

  Scenario: AC5 No allocation row matches
    Given a new case RW-2026-000204 with product group "SSME" and region "NE3" that matches no allocation row
    When the morning allocation run starts
    Then the system places the case in the exception queue "RWB-EXC"
    Then the case status stays "NEW"
    Then the system writes a decision log entry with final call "RULE_GAP", product group "SSME" and region "NE3"
    Then the system publishes caseAllocationFailed with reason "NO_ROW_MATCHED"
    Then the allocation summary carries MSG-P3-012 with count 1

  Scenario: AC6 Every allocation is logged
    Given case RW-2026-000205 matches row "ALLOC-014" and owner U-02 is below the cap
    When the case is placed in the queue and given an owner
    Then the system writes one decision log entry with rule ID "ALLOC-014", rule version "ALLOC-2026.11", queue "MTG-BKK-CO", owner U-02 and the inputs used
    Then if the decision log write fails, the allocation is not made, the case stays "NEW" with no queue and the job record carries MSG-P3-013 for the case

  Scenario: AC7 A case with an open deviation is not allocated to a case owner
    Given a new case RW-2026-000206 with deviation_open = true
    When the morning allocation run starts
    Then the system places the case in the deviation handler queue "DEV-HANDLER" named by rule R-DEV-01
    Then the system sets no case owner and the status stays "NEW"

  Scenario: AC8 A repeated run for the same date has no further effect
    Given the morning allocation run for 2026-12-01 has assigned case RW-2026-000201 to U-03
    When the run for 2026-12-01 is started again from the job monitor
    Then case RW-2026-000201 keeps owner U-03 and its one assignment record
    Then the system writes no second decision log entry for the case
    Then the job record shows 1 case skipped as already allocated

  Scenario: AC9 A run with no new cases
    Given no case has status "NEW" on 2026-12-01
    When the morning allocation run starts
    Then the run completes with 0 cases read
    Then the allocation summary for each team shows 0 in overflow and 0 in the exception queue

  Scenario: AC10 The run waits for case creation
    Given JOB-02 has not completed for 2026-12-01 because the COLLINS load was refused
    When 07:00 passes
    Then JOB-03 has not started for 2026-12-01
    Then the job monitor shows JOB-03 waiting on JOB-02 with MSG-P1-001
    Then every NEW case keeps no queue and no owner

  Scenario: AC11 Two runs at the same time allocate each case once
    Given a first run is allocating case RW-2026-000207
    When a rerun for 2026-12-01 reaches the same case at the same time
    Then the rerun skips the locked case
    Then the case has exactly one assignment record and one decision log entry for 2026-12-01

  Scenario: AC12 An owner one case below the cap gets the case
    Given U-03 is next in turn and holds 149 open cases
    When case RW-2026-000208 is placed in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
    Then the system gives the case to U-03
    Then U-03 now holds 150 open cases

  Scenario: AC13 A queue with no overflow queue sends the case to the exception queue
    Given queue "HP-CEN-CO" has no overflow queue
    Given every owner in queue "HP-CEN-CO" holds 150 open cases
    When case RW-2026-000209 is placed in queue "HP-CEN-CO"
    Then the system places the case in the exception queue "RWB-EXC" with reason "NO_OVERFLOW_QUEUE"
    Then the case status stays "NEW"
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A case is allocated by the first row of the allocation table, in row order, whose product group, region and exposure band match the case. "Any" in a column matches every value | Allocation table (rule_row, rule table ALLOCATION), DL24; REQ-CWC-008 |
| BR2 | The owner is chosen by the method held on the queue: ROUND_ROBIN, LOWEST_LOAD, NAMED_OWNER or SKILL | queue.assignment_method (DF-WRK-006), LOV-ASSIGN |
| BR3 | An owner at or above the queue's caseload cap is skipped. Open cases are cases in the queue owned by the person with status other than CLOSED | queue.capacity_cap (DF-WRK-007); values DL23 |
| BR4 | A case that cannot be given an owner goes to the overflow queue of its queue | queue.overflow_queue_id (DF-WRK-008) |
| BR5 | A case that matches no row goes to the exception queue, and the gap is logged. R-UNI-41 handles the case once a person decides | R-UNI-41; FEAT-CWC-09 |
| BR6 | A case with an open deviation goes to the deviation handler queue | R-DEV-01 |
| BR7 | A decision that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR8 | A case is allocated at most once per business date | R-UNI-40; events.txt rule "Duplicates" |
| BR9 | Each allocation records the rule row and the table version | REQ-CWC-016; CTL-03 |

### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| New | Allocation rule matched | Row matched and an owner below the cap | Assigned |
| New | Allocation rule matched | Row matched and every owner at the cap | New, in the overflow queue |
| New | Allocation rule matched | No row matched | New, in the exception queue |
| New | DEVIATION_FLAGGED (R-DEV-01) | deviation_open = true | New, in the deviation handler queue |

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-RULES, rules component | Evaluates the allocation table (Rules and parameters R) |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Updates the case and writes the assignment (Case record CRU; Queue and allocation CRU) |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Writes the entry (Decision log C) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the queue and the allocation summary for their team (Queue and allocation R) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the cases given to them (Case record R, scope Own) |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reruns JOB-03 from the job monitor (Platform administration U) |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Prepares the allocation table load file; the load is RWB-E1-029 |
| Process owner for L1 18, Shared operations | Approves each allocation table version (reference data change process, step 4). No delegation of authority level applies |

### 12. Contract

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz, after JOB-02 completes for the business date |
| Job name | JOB-03 Morning allocation |
| Schedule | Daily after JOB-02, complete by 07:00 Asia/Bangkok |
| Input | Cases with status NEW and last_allocation_date before the business date; allocation rows in force on the business date; queues and queue members |
| Output | Case queue, team, owner, status and rule version; assignment rows; decision log entries; allocation summary per team; job record with counts |
| Events published | CaseAllocated (EV-02: caseId, queueId, ownerId, ruleId, ruleVersion); CaseAllocationFailed (EV-03: caseId, reason, ruleGap) |
| Idempotency key | caseId and businessDate. A case with last_allocation_date equal to the business date is skipped |
| Restart | Rerun from the job monitor (POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun). A rerun processes only cases not yet allocated for the date. Chunk commit per case, so a failure in one case does not undo the others |

**Endpoint used to read the result**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Method and path | GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId} |
| Request | Path caseId (uuid) |
| Response | Case: queueId, teamCode, ownerUserId, status, ruleVersion |
| Errors | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 role lacks Case record R (MSG-P4-002); 404 not found or outside scope (MSG-P4-003); 503 store unavailable |
| Authorization | Case record, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**Endpoint used to rerun the job (P1)**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Method and path | POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun |
| Response | Job: id, type, businessDate, status, checks |
| Errors | 401; 403 role lacks Platform administration U (MSG-P4-002); 404 job not found; 409 job already running (MSG-GEN-004) |
| Authorization | Platform administration, right U |
| Idempotency | The rerun follows the job's idempotency key above |

**Published interfaces**

```java
// P3, package recovery.casewf.allocation (published)
public interface AllocationService {
    AllocationOutcome allocate(UUID caseId, LocalDate businessDate);
}
public record AllocationOutcome(UUID caseId, OutcomeType type, UUID queueId,
        UUID ownerUserId, String ruleId, String ruleVersion, String reason) {}
public enum OutcomeType { ASSIGNED, OVERFLOW, EXCEPTION, DEVIATION_QUEUE, SKIPPED, FAILED_LOG }

// P7, used by this story (RWB-E1-027)
// package recovery.decision.writer; called inside the caller's transaction as the last step before commit
public interface DecisionLogWriter {
    DecisionLogEntryRef write(DecisionLogRecord record)
        throws DecisionLogRecordInvalidException, DecisionLogUnavailableException;
}

// P4, used by this story: rule rows are P4 tables
public interface RuleTableReader {
    RuleTableVersion rowsInForce(String ruleTable, LocalDate onDate);
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `src/main/java/.../recovery/casewf/allocation`, Java package `recovery.casewf.allocation`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AllocationJob | Job | Quartz job for JOB-03; selects NEW cases, calls AllocationService per case, builds the summary, writes job counts |
| AllocationService | Published interface | Implementation AllocationServiceImpl: lock, deviation check, rule match, owner choice, decision log write, case update, outbox event |
| AllocationRuleEvaluator | Service | Evaluates the allocation rows returned by RuleTableReader in row order; first match wins |
| AssignmentEngine | Service | Applies ROUND_ROBIN, LOWEST_LOAD, NAMED_OWNER or SKILL with the cap |
| OwnerLoadRepository | Repository | Counts open cases per owner in a queue (ix_case_owner_status) |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | Reads and updates recovery_case, queue, queue_member, assignment |
| AllocationSummaryBuilder | Service | Counts overflow and exception cases per team; fills MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-012 |
| AllocationRuleTable | Rule table | Rule rows with rule table ALLOCATION, read through RuleTableReader |

**Database**

- Reads: recovery_case (id, case_no, product_group, region_code, exposure_band, deviation_open, status, last_allocation_date), queue (id, queue_code, team_code, role_code, assignment_method, capacity_cap, overflow_queue_id), queue_member (user_id, capacity).
- Writes: recovery_case (status, owner_user_id, queue_id, team_code, stage_clock_start, rule_version, last_allocation_date, version), queue (rr_cursor_user_id), assignment (all columns), outbox.
- Lock: `SELECT ... FROM recovery_case WHERE id = ? AND status = 'NEW' FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; optimistic version column on update.
- Migration in this story: `V020_1__allocation_columns.sql` adds recovery_case.last_allocation_date (date) and queue.rr_cursor_user_id (uuid). queue_member is created by RWB-E1-019.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Allocation table version "ALLOC-2026.11" (rule_row, rule table ALLOCATION), prepared by RW-REFADM, loaded by RW-COE through RWB-E1-029, approved by the Shared operations process owner.
- Queues and members from RWB-E1-019; caps DL23.
- Parameters from RWB-E1-042: `allocation.exception.queue.code`, `allocation.deviation.queue.code`.
- Lists LOV-ASSIGN, LOV-ASSIGN-REASON, LOV-CASE-STATUS (P4 lov_value).

**Build steps**

1. AllocationRuleEvaluator: given a case snapshot and the rows of a version, return the first matching row or none. Unit tests per BR1 with "any" values.
2. AssignmentEngine: implement the four methods with cap skipping and the round robin cursor. Unit tests for AC2, AC3, AC12 boundary.
3. OwnerLoadRepository: open case count per owner and queue; integration test on PostgreSQL with Testcontainers.
4. AllocationServiceImpl: lock, deviation branch, rule match, overflow and exception branches, then case update, assignment and outbox row in one transaction with the decision log write as its last step.
5. Idempotency: skip when last_allocation_date equals the business date; return SKIPPED.
6. AllocationJob: Quartz job with `@DisallowConcurrentExecution`, dependency on JOB-02 completion, per-case transaction, job counts.
7. AllocationSummaryBuilder and the call to the ACE notification path for each team manager.
8. System tests TC-E1-020-01 to TC-E1-020-15 on the synthetic case set.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.allocation`. Off: JOB-03 does not run and cases stay NEW.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; TC-E1-020-01 and TC-E1-020-08 are in the regression suite; JOB-03 finishes 3,110 synthetic cases inside 15 minutes in SIT (assumed target; DL11).

### 17. Guardrails

- No allocation value is written in code. Product groups, regions, bands, queues, methods, caps and queue codes are read from tables and parameters.
- No personal data in the allocation summary, the logs, the events or the test data. Cases are named by case number only.
- The service never reads tables owned by another module. Rule rows come through RuleTableReader (P4); the decision log through DecisionLogWriter (P7).
- The decision log entry is written in the same transaction as the case change; a failed write leaves the case unchanged.
