## RWB-E1-021 Transfer rules and engine v1

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-021 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-10 Run the transfer rule table and engine |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-010, REQ-CWC-016 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, section 5.3 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-028, RWB-E1-020, RWB-E1-027 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **cases moved between queues and roles by the transfer rule table on stage change, route decided, timer expired, deviation raised or cleared, approval needed, document received, payment missed, or a manual request with a reason**, so that **hand-offs between teams run without email**.

### 2. Business rationale

A case changes hands between the TDR, litigation, NPA and debt sale teams by email today, and the case can wait between teams with nobody holding it. This story moves the case by rule when one of eight triggers fires, picks the owner in the receiving queue, ends the old assignment and records the rule and version, and gives the team manager a programmatic transfer with a coded reason before the Epic 2 screens. It meets REQ-CWC-010 and REQ-CWC-016.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-020 is done: AssignmentEngine and the queue structure are in use.
- RWB-E1-028 is done: timers publish TimerDue when a timer other than a service level expires. A service level breach (TimerBreached) never moves the case (R-UNI-30).
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available.
- The transfer rows version "TRF-2026.11" (rule table TRANSFER) are loaded through RWB-E1-029. Each row holds trigger event, condition, target queue code and row order.
- The transfer reason list LOV-TRANSFER-REASON holds R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral and R06 Wrong queue (DL23).
- Manual transfer callers hold Queue and allocation U (RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CAPACITY). Hold and release callers hold Case record U (for example RW-LITOFF acting on a Legal instruction).

### 4. Flow

1. Event source: writes a trigger event to the outbox: CaseStateChanged for a stage change or a route decided (rule event ROUTE_APPROVED), TimerDue, DeviationRaised, DeviationCleared, ApprovalRequested, DocumentStored or PaymentMissed.
2. TransferListener: receives the event once per event ID; a repeated event ID is ignored (R-UNI-40).
3. TransferRuleEvaluator (SY-RULES): reads the transfer rows in force and returns the first row, in row order, whose trigger and condition match the case.
4. TransferService: skips an automated transfer when legal_hold is true (R-UNI-20) and logs the skip.
5. TransferService: locks the case by its version, picks the owner in the target queue with AssignmentEngine, and checks the move is allowed from the case status.
6. TransferService: in one transaction ends the open assignment, writes the new assignment (reason TRANSFER), updates queue, team and owner, and writes CaseTransferred (EV-04).
7. TransferService: as the last step before commit, writes the decision log entry with the row ID, version, from and to queue and owner, and the trigger.
8. Team manager: calls POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer with reason code MANUAL, transfer reason R03 and a target owner or queue; steps 5 to 7 run with reason MANUAL.
9. Litigation officer: calls POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold with action place or lift; the case goes to On hold or back to the status it paused in.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Two transfers reach the same case in the same second | First commits; second refused on the version check and logged as rejected | MSG-GEN-004 | AC3 |
| X2 | Manual transfer without a transfer reason | Refused with 422; nothing changes | MSG-P3-001 | AC6 |
| X3 | Named target owner at the caseload cap | Refused with 422; nothing changes | MSG-P3-002 | AC7 |
| X4 | Transfer of a closed case | Refused with 409 | MSG-P3-005 | AC8 |
| X5 | Decision log write fails | Refused with 503 for a manual call; event retried for a rule transfer; nothing changes | MSG-P7-003 | AC9 |
| X6 | Rule trigger arrives while legal_hold is true | No automated transfer; skip logged | None | AC10 |
| X7 | The same event arrives twice | Second ignored; one transfer | None | AC11 |
| X8 | No owner below the cap in the target queue | Case placed in the target queue's overflow queue with no owner; team manager told | MSG-P3-011 | AC12 |
| X9 | Hold placed on a case already on hold | Refused with 409 | MSG-P3-005 | AC13 |
| X10 | No transfer row matches the event | No transfer; nothing logged as a decision | None | AC14 |
| X11 | A role without Queue and allocation U calls the transfer | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-021-15 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on the assignment engine (RWB-E1-020) and the timer events (RWB-E1-028); no screen |
| Negotiable | Trigger rows, target queues and the reason list are data |
| Valuable | Removes email hand-offs between the six recovery teams |
| Estimable | One listener, one service, one rule table, two endpoints |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A case moves by the first transfer row, in row order, whose trigger and condition match | Transfer rows (rule table TRANSFER); REQ-CWC-010 |
| BR2 | The eight triggers are stage change, route decided, timer expired, deviation raised, deviation cleared, approval needed, document received and payment missed, plus manual request | REQ-CWC-010; events EV-05, EV-06, EV-07, EV-09, EV-12, EV-16, EV-18 |
| BR3 | A manual transfer needs a transfer reason from the list | LOV-TRANSFER-REASON (assumed); REQ-WKM-003; VR-P3-010-1 |
| BR4 | A transfer to an owner at the cap is refused | queue.capacity_cap; VR-P3-010-2 |
| BR5 | A case is in exactly one queue with one open assignment | REQ-CWC-005 |
| BR6 | No automated transfer while a legal hold is in force | R-UNI-20 |
| BR7 | Lifting a hold returns the case to the status it paused in | R-UNI-21; casemodel.txt status transitions |
| BR8 | An event with the same ID is processed once | R-UNI-40 |
| BR9 | Every transfer is logged with rule ID and version before it takes effect | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; REQ-CWC-016 |
| BR10 | A transfer keeps the case status and the clocks | R-UNI-18 (same principle for reallocation) |

### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| New, Assigned, In progress, any Waiting | LEGAL_HOLD_PLACED (R-UNI-20) | Placed through the legal-hold endpoint | On hold |
| On hold | LEGAL_HOLD_LIFTED (R-UNI-21) | Lifted through the legal-hold endpoint | The status it paused in |

A rule or manual transfer changes the queue, the team and the owner, not the status.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TEAMMGR | Transfers and reassigns cases in team scope (Queue and allocation U) |
| RW-CAPACITY | Transfers cases (Queue and allocation U) |
| RW-LITOFF and other roles with Case record U | Place and lift a legal hold on a Legal or court instruction (Case record U) |
| RW-CASEOWN | Reads the case; may not transfer (Queue and allocation R) |
| SY-RULES | Evaluates the transfer rows |
| SY-CASEWF | Carries out rule transfers (Queue and allocation CRU) |
| SY-DECLOG | Writes the entries |

### 12. Contract

**POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/transfer**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | TransferRequest: toOwnerId (uuid) or toQueueId (uuid), reasonCode = "MANUAL", note, and transferReasonCode (new field, LOV-TRANSFER-REASON) |
| Response | 200 Assignment: id, caseId, assigneeUserId, assignedAt, reason, ruleId |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Queue and allocation U (MSG-P4-002); 404 not found or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 409 status does not allow the move (MSG-P3-005) or version changed (MSG-GEN-004); 422 no reason (MSG-P3-001), owner at cap (MSG-P3-002); 503 decision not recorded (MSG-P7-003) |
| Authorization | Queue and allocation, right U, scope Team |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header; a repeat with the same key returns the first response |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-hold**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | LegalHoldRequest: action (place, lift), reason (required), reference |
| Response | 200 Case with status and legalHold |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Case record U (MSG-P4-002); 404; 409 already on hold or not on hold (MSG-P3-005); 503 (MSG-P7-003) |
| Authorization | Case record, right U, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header |

**Events.** Consumes CaseStateChanged (EV-05), DeviationRaised (EV-06), DeviationCleared (EV-07), ApprovalRequested (EV-09), PaymentMissed (EV-12), DocumentStored (EV-16), TimerDue (EV-18). Publishes CaseTransferred (EV-04: caseId, fromOwner, toOwner, reasonCode) and CaseStateChanged (EV-05) for hold and release.

**Published interface**

```java
// P3, package recovery.casewf.transfer (published)
public interface TransferService {
    TransferResult transferByRule(UUID caseId, String triggerEvent, UUID eventId);
    TransferResult transferManual(UUID caseId, ManualTransfer request, UUID callerId, String idempotencyKey);
    CaseView placeLegalHold(UUID caseId, String reason, String reference, UUID callerId);
    CaseView liftLegalHold(UUID caseId, String reason, UUID callerId);
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery/casewf/transfer`, Java package `recovery.casewf.transfer`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TransferListener | Listener | Reads the eight trigger events from the outbox, deduplicates by event ID, calls transferByRule |
| TransferRuleEvaluator | Service | First matching transfer row in row order for an event and a case snapshot |
| TransferService | Published interface | Lock, hold check, owner choice, decision log, assignment swap, event |
| LegalHoldService | Service | Place and lift with status_before_hold |
| CaseAndWorkflowController | Controller | POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer and POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | recovery_case, assignment, queue, processed event IDs |
| TransferRuleTable | Rule table | Rule rows with rule table TRANSFER through RuleTableReader (P4) |

**Database**

- Writes recovery_case (queue_id, team_code, owner_user_id, status, legal_hold, status_before_hold, rule_version, version), assignment (end the open row, insert the new row), processed_event (event_id unique), outbox.
- Update with `WHERE id = ? AND version = ?`; zero rows updated means the version changed (MSG-GEN-004).
- Constraint: partial unique index `ux_assignment_open_case ON assignment (case_id) WHERE ended_at IS NULL AND task_id IS NULL`.
- Migration in this story: `V021_1__transfer.sql` adds recovery_case.status_before_hold, assignment.transfer_reason_code, the partial unique index and table processed_event (event_id uuid primary key, consumer varchar(60), processed_at).

**Configuration and reference data**

- Transfer rows "TRF-2026.11" loaded by RW-COE through RWB-E1-029.
- LOV-TRANSFER-REASON (R01 to R06; DL23) loaded by RW-REFADM through RWB-E1-043.
- Queues from RWB-E1-019.

**Build steps**

1. TransferRuleEvaluator with unit tests for each trigger (AC4) and no match (AC14).
2. TransferService.transferByRule with version lock, hold check and assignment swap; tests AC1, AC3, AC10, AC12.
3. TransferListener with processed_event deduplication; test AC11.
4. transferManual with reason and cap validation; tests AC2, AC6, AC7, AC8.
5. LegalHoldService place and lift; tests AC5, AC13.
6. Decision log write as the last step of each transaction, including the rejected transfer; test AC9.
7. Controller endpoints with access checks and Idempotency-Key; access test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.transfer`. Off: no rule transfers and the two endpoints return 404.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and each of the eight triggers moves a case in SIT.

| MSG-P3-001 | Manual transfer without a reason | Choose a reason for the transfer. |
| MSG-P3-002 | Target owner at the cap | {owner} is at the caseload cap. Choose another owner or the team queue. |
| MSG-P3-005 | Move not allowed from the status | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P3-011 | Target queue full, case in overflow | {count} new cases are waiting in the overflow queue for {team}. Every owner is at the caseload cap. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Second transfer on a changed record | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

No screen in this story. SCR-02 Case list (list; filtered) and SCR-03 Case record (read only; on hold) show the new queue, owner and the hold banner. The transfer screen SCR-05 comes in Epic 2 (RWB-E2-012).

## RWB-E1-022 Sign-on with SSO, MFA and the first roles

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-022 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P4 Access and administration |
| Feature | FEAT-ACA-01 Sign on through Entra ID with single sign-on; FEAT-ACA-02 Enforce multi-factor authentication; FEAT-ACA-03 Hold roles as data |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-ACA-001, REQ-ACA-002, REQ-ACA-010 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.4; Business Requirements Program, section 5.4 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-019 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **to sign in to the Workbench once through Entra ID with multi-factor authentication and see only the screens and actions my Workbench roles allow**, so that **access is controlled from the first release and nobody holds a Workbench password or a local account**.

### 2. Business rationale

Access to recovery data today is granted system by system, and the bank cannot show who could see a case on a given date. This story makes Entra ID group membership the only way to hold a Workbench role: one group per role per environment, granted through the bank IAM, read at each sign-in and turned into a session with roles, scope and the permission matrix version in force. It meets REQ-ACA-001, REQ-ACA-002 and REQ-ACA-010 and supports control CTL-09 (access by role and scope). The measure is the access test set in section 16 passing for every role with real users at the release (DL39: administration roles at Epic 1).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the role and permission tables exist in the recovery schema.
- RWB-E1-019 is done: the 54 role rows are loaded, and each environment's role rows carry that environment's Entra ID group name in role.entra_group, for example RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN in SIT (pattern from the Single sign-on sheet; final names DL40).
- Permission matrix version PM-2026.11 is loaded from the Users, roles and permissions workbook (54 roles against 14 capability areas).
- Separation of duty version SOD-2026.11 is loaded into the role conflict table (new, see section 11) from the Separation of duty sheet.
- The ACE common module sign-in is configured for the Workbench application in Entra ID (INT-21), with the bank conditional access policy that requires a second factor.
- The person was added to the Entra ID group for their role through the bank IAM: the line manager requested it, the role owner approved it and the access administrator carried it out (section 10).

### 4. Flow

1. Person: opens the Workbench in the ACE front end.
2. ACE common module: redirects to Entra ID; the person signs in with password and second factor; Entra ID returns an OpenID Connect token with the groups claim and the amr claim.
3. Workbench (SessionResolver): checks that the amr claim contains "mfa".
4. Workbench: maps each group in the groups claim to an active role row by role.entra_group; groups with no active role row are ignored.
5. Workbench: checks the resulting role set against the role conflict table version in force.
6. Workbench: resolves the session: user reference, roles, the permission matrix version in force at that time, and the default scope of each role.
7. Workbench: writes the sign-in event through the AccessEventPublisher (ACE audit log and SOC log through INT-22).
8. ACE front end: calls GET /me/session and shows the first screen with one line naming the roles and the scope, for example "Case owner. Scope: own cases.", and a menu holding only screens whose capability area has R for at least one role.
9. Person: calls any endpoint; AccessCheck evaluates the capability area and right the endpoint declares against the session's matrix version and allows or refuses the call.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without the right calls an endpoint, for example the admin API | Refused with 403; the refusal is written to the access event stream with the area and right | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |
| X2 | The person is in no Workbench group | Session refused with 401; the access request page shows the message and no data | MSG-P4-001 | AC3 |
| X3 | The token has no second factor in the amr claim | Session refused with 401; the refusal is logged | MSG-P4-005 | AC4 |
| X4 | The groups give a role pair listed in the role conflict table | Session refused; an incident is raised to the security administrator; the refusal is logged | MSG-P4-006 | AC6 |
| X5 | A service identity calls an area its role does not hold | Refused with 403, exactly as for a person | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A group maps to no active role row | The group is ignored; if no other group maps, X2 applies | MSG-P4-001 | AC8 |
| X7 | A new matrix version takes effect while a session is open | The open session keeps the version it resolved; the next session uses the new one | None | AC9 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the tables (RWB-E1-001) and the role rows (RWB-E1-019). The decision log write of access events is added in RWB-E1-039 |
| Negotiable | Group names, roles, conflicts and permissions are data. The story fixes the behavior, not the values |
| Valuable | Every Epic 1 administration user signs in with one bank identity and sees only what the role allows |
| Estimable | One resolver, one access check, one session endpoint, no business screen |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Sign-on with SSO, MFA and the first roles

  Background:
    Given the environment is SIT
    Given permission matrix version "PM-2026.11" is in force from 30 November 2026
    Given separation of duty version "SOD-2026.11" is in force
    Given role RW-CASEOWN has entra_group "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN" and default scope "OWN"

  Scenario: AC1 SSO sign-in
    Given test user "U-1001" is in Entra ID group "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN"
    When the user opens the Workbench and signs in with password and second factor
    Then the session holds roles "RW-CASEOWN", scope "OWN" and matrix version "PM-2026.11"
    Then GET /me/session returns the line "Case owner. Scope: own cases."
    Then the menu shows the screens of the capability areas where RW-CASEOWN holds R, and no Administration menu

  Scenario: AC2 Role denied
    Given test user "U-1002" holds only RW-PHONECOL, whose Platform administration letter is "-"
    When the user calls GET /admin/roles
    Then the system refuses the call with status 403 and message MSG-P4-002 with action "read roles"
    Then the system writes one refusal event with user "U-1002", area "PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION", right "R" and result "REFUSED"

  Scenario: AC3 Not in group
    Given test user "U-1003" has an Entra ID account and no group whose name starts "RWB-SIT-"
    When the user opens the Workbench
    Then the access request page shows MSG-P4-001 and no case, queue or reference data
    Then every recovery endpoint returns status 401 for that token
    Then the system writes one refusal event with reason "NO_ROLE"

  Scenario: AC4 Sign-in without a second factor is refused
    Given test user "U-1004" is in group "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN"
    Given the token's amr claim holds "pwd" and not "mfa"
    When the token reaches the Workbench
    Then the system refuses the session with status 401 and message MSG-P4-005
    Then the system writes one refusal event with reason "NO_MFA"

  Scenario: AC5 Two roles give the permissions of both
    Given test user "U-1005" is in groups "RWB-SIT-RW-LITOFF" and "RWB-SIT-RW-LEGAL"
    When the user signs in
    Then the session holds roles "RW-LITOFF" and "RW-LEGAL"
    Then the Documents letters are "CRUA", the union of "CRU" and "CRUA"
    Then no permission comes from any role the user does not hold

  Scenario: AC6 A conflicting role pair is refused
    Given test user "U-1006" is in groups "RWB-SIT-RW-SECADM" and "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN"
    Given the role conflict table says RW-SECADM may not hold any business role
    When the user signs in
    Then the system refuses the session with message MSG-P4-006 naming "RW-SECADM" and "RW-CASEOWN"
    Then the system raises an incident to the security administrator queue
    Then the system writes one refusal event with reason "ROLE_CONFLICT"

  Scenario: AC7 A service identity is checked like a person
    Given managed identity "SY-RULES" is in group "RWB-SIT-SY-RULES"
    When it calls GET /admin/roles
    Then the system refuses the call with status 403 and message MSG-P4-002
    Then the system writes one refusal event with user "SY-RULES"

  Scenario: AC8 An unmapped or inactive group gives no role
    Given test user "U-1008" is in groups "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN" and "RWB-SIT-LEGACY01"
    Given no active role row has entra_group "RWB-SIT-LEGACY01"
    When the user signs in
    Then the session holds only "RW-CASEOWN"
    Then the system writes the unmapped group name on the sign-in event

  Scenario: AC9 An open session keeps the versions it resolved
    Given test user "U-1009" signed in at 09:00 on 1 December 2026 under matrix version "PM-2026.11"
    Given matrix version "PM-2026.12" takes effect at 10:00 on 1 December 2026 and removes R in Reporting from RW-CASEOWN
    When the user calls GET /reports/measures at 10:30 in the same session
    Then the system checks the call against "PM-2026.11" and allowed
    Then after the user signs in again at 11:00 the same call is refused with MSG-P4-002
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Membership of the Entra ID group mapped to a role is the only way to hold the role. The Workbench holds no password and no local account | role.entra_group (DF-REF-039); DT07; Admin and access model, section 4.2 |
| BR2 | A session is refused unless the token carries a second factor | NFR-049; FEAT-ACA-02 |
| BR3 | No role inherits from another. A person with two roles holds the union of both roles' letters | permission.letters (DF-REF-043) |
| BR4 | A capability area with no letter for any of the session's roles refuses every action in that area | Permission matrix; CTL-09 |
| BR5 | A role pair listed in the role conflict table may not be held in one session | Separation of duty sheet, roles.txt; role conflict table (new) |
| BR6 | A service identity holds a role in the same table and is checked the same way as a person | REQ-ACA-010; NFR-051 |
| BR7 | A session keeps the matrix and conflict versions it resolved at sign-in until it ends | Admin and access model, section 4.2 |
| BR8 | Group names, roles, letters and conflicts are data rows with a version; none is written in code | Principle 1; DT02 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It creates a session with the states Resolved and Refused, and the session ends at sign-out or token expiry.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Line manager (bank IAM, level 4) | Requests a Workbench role for a team member in the bank IAM, naming the person, the role and the reason. May not approve the request they raised |
| Role owner (bank IAM, level 2), the head of the unit whose staff hold the role | Approves or rejects each grant of a role they own after checking the separation of duty table |
| Access administrator (bank IAM, level 3), Chief Debt Recovery Management Office (assumed, DL01) | Adds the person to the Entra ID group of the approved role in each environment requested. Approves no grant |
| Application owner (level 1), Tribe Lead of the Collections and Recovery Tribe (assumed, DL02) | Approves the roles table and each group to role mapping |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Maintains the Entra ID groups and the IAM link (DL40); receives the conflict incident in AC6 |
| RW-REFADM Reference data administrator | Loads an approved role or group mapping version. Approves none |
| RW-CASEOWN and every bank role | Signs in and uses the screens of the role |
| RW-PHONECOL Phone collector | Signs in; refused on Platform administration (AC2) |
| SY-RULES and the other service identities | Act under their managed identity and their own role row |
| RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-SECADM | Read GET /admin/roles (Platform administration R) |

The four administration levels act in the bank IAM, not in the Workbench. If the bank chooses central administration (DL01), level 3 moves to the central IAM team and nothing in this build changes.

### 12. Contract

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/roles** (API-P4-007)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | None |
| Response | Array of Role: id, roleCode, roleName, roleClass, defaultScope, entraGroup |
| Errors | 401 no valid session or no role (MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-005, MSG-P4-006); 403 the session's roles hold no R in Platform administration (MSG-P4-002); 503 the ACE sign-in service is unavailable (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Platform administration, right R |
| Idempotency | Not applicable, read only |

**GET /me/session** (new, recorded in the additions file)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | None |
| Response | Session: userRef, roles (roleCode, roleName, defaultScope), matrixVersion, conflictVersion, scopeLine, resolvedAt, breakGlass (active, endsAt; filled by RWB-E1-039) |
| Errors | 401 as above |
| Authorization | Any resolved session; no capability area, because the endpoint returns only the caller's own session |
| Idempotency | Not applicable, read only |

**Published interface AccessCheck** (package recovery.access.signin), called by every module's controller through a Spring method interceptor:

```java
AccessDecision check(SessionContext session, CapabilityArea area, Right right);
SessionContext resolve(VerifiedToken token); // throws SessionRefusedException(reasonCode, messageId)
```

**Published interface AccessEventPublisher** (package recovery.access.signin):

```java
void publish(AccessEvent event); // E1: ACE audit and SOC log through INT-22; RWB-E1-039 adds the decision log
```

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/access/signin` in the recovery module; Java package `recovery.access.signin`. Front end: `recovery/access` folder in the ACE front end.
- Components:

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AccessAndAdministrationController | Controller | GET /admin/roles and GET /me/session; maps refusals to problem responses with messageCode |
| SessionResolver | Service | Checks the amr claim, maps groups to role rows, applies the conflict check, builds SessionContext |
| AccessCheckService | Published interface | Implements AccessCheck: unions the letters of the session's roles in the area and tests the right |
| AccessCheckInterceptor | Service | Reads the capability area and right declared on each endpoint (x-capability) and calls AccessCheck before the handler |
| AccessEventPublisher | Published interface | Writes sign-in and refusal events to the ACE audit and SOC log |
| AccessAndAdministrationRepository | Repository | Reads role, permission and role_conflict rows in force |
| RoleConflict | Entity | Maps the new role_conflict table |
| SessionBanner | React component | Shows the one-line roles and scope from GET /me/session |
| AccessRequestPage | React component | Shows MSG-P4-001 and no data when the session is refused with NO_ROLE |

- Database: reads role (id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope, entra_group, is_active), permission (role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version, is_active). Creates table role_conflict (id uuid, role_code varchar(20), conflicts_with varchar(30), reason varchar(200), conflict_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, plus the standard columns) with Flyway migration V_E1_022__role_conflict.sql; conflicts_with holds a role code or the class values ANY_BUSINESS_ROLE and ANY_OTHER_ROLE. Index ix_role_entra_group on role (entra_group) where is_active.
- Configuration and reference data: role rows and group names (loaded by RW-REFADM after RWB-E1-019; names DL40); permission matrix PM-2026.11 (loaded by RW-REFADM, approved per RWB-E1-037); role conflict version SOD-2026.11 (loaded by RW-REFADM from the Separation of duty sheet); LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-SCOPE; scope line wording from labels per DL10. Property `rwb.access.required-amr=mfa`.
- Build steps:
  1. Create the role_conflict migration and entity; load SOD-2026.11 into SIT with six rows from the Separation of duty sheet that name Workbench roles.
  2. Build SessionResolver: amr check, group to role mapping on active rows, conflict check, SessionContext with versions; unit tests for AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC8.
  3. Build AccessCheckService with letter union per area; unit tests for every letter and the dash.
  4. Build AccessCheckInterceptor reading the declared area and right; contract test that every operation in api.yaml has one.
  5. Build AccessEventPublisher to the ACE audit and SOC log; refusal reason codes NO_ROLE, NO_MFA, ROLE_CONFLICT, NO_RIGHT.
  6. Build GET /admin/roles and GET /me/session with problem responses.
  7. Build SessionBanner, menu filtering by capability area and AccessRequestPage.
  8. Hold the resolved versions on the session and test AC9 with two matrix versions.
- Feature flag: `rwb.access.sso-roles`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass, a test user per Epic 1 administration role signs in with MFA in SIT, and the contract test finds no endpoint without a declared capability area.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | Sign-in with no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action outside the role's permission | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-005 | Token without a second factor (new) | Sign in again with your second factor. The Workbench needs multi-factor authentication. |
| MSG-P4-006 | Conflicting role pair at sign-in (new) | Your roles {role} and {otherRole} cannot be held together. Access is refused and the security administrator has been told. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | ACE sign-in service unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

Thai text for each message follows DL10; proposed Thai for the new messages is in the additions file.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The ACE front end shell shows the session line from GET /me/session at the top of every page and hides menu entries whose capability area the session cannot read. A person with no role sees the access request page with MSG-P4-001 and no data. Epic 1 has no business screens (DL39); RW-CASEOWN test users exist in SIT and UAT only.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: group names, roles, letters, scopes and conflicts are read from tables with their version.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. Access events carry the Entra ID object reference, never the person's name or e-mail.

- No local password, local account or role cache that outlives the session.

## RWB-E1-023 Case record view v1, read only

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-023 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-ACA-11 Show the case record view read only |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-OCC-007, REQ-RDF-009, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3, 3.4 and 3.6; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.1, 5.4 and 5.6 |
| L3 process | 06 Take over and own the case |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-037, RWB-E1-039 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **one read-only screen per case with the case ID, accounts, arrears, owner, queue, stage, status, contact history and documents, read from the data products with the business date of each**, so that **I stop searching files and systems to understand a case**.

### 2. Business rationale

A case owner opens EFS, ALS, shared drives and team spreadsheets today to answer one question about a case. This story puts the case, its accounts and arrears, its parties, its contact history and its documents on SCR-03, each section showing the business date of the data product it comes from, with personal fields masked by role and every view of personal data written to the access log. It meets REQ-OCC-007, REQ-RDF-009, REQ-ACA-005 and REQ-ACA-006.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-018 is done: cases, account links and party links exist.
- RWB-E1-024 is done: the document hub lists documents by case.
- RWB-E1-037 is done: masking rules by role are in force (DL26).
- RWB-E1-039 is done: access events are published to the access log.
- The account, arrears and party data products carry their data_as_of date from the COLLINS load (DL20).
- The user holds a role with Case record R and the case is in the user's scope.
- Personal data access is logged through AccessEventPublisher (RWB-E1-039), which also sends the PII access record to PII Kafka through the ACE common module.

### 4. Flow

1. Case owner: opens a case from SCR-02 Case list; SCR-03 shows the Loading state.
2. CaseRecordPage: calls GET /cases/{caseId}, GET /cases/{caseId}/accounts, GET /cases/{caseId}/parties, GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions and GET /cases/{caseId}/documents in parallel.
3. CaseAndWorkflowController: checks Case record R and the scope; out of scope returns 404.
4. CaseRecordQueryService: reads the case from P3 tables, and the account balances, arrears and party facts through the P1 interface with their data_as_of dates.
5. CaseRecordQueryService: applies the masking rules for the caller's role through FieldMasker and publishes one AC-READ access event with the field IDs read and their masked flags.
6. DocumentHub (P5): returns the document list for the case through its endpoint.
7. CaseRecordPage: shows the header (case number, product, status, stage, route, owner, queue, entry date, prescription date, deviation and hold flags), then Accounts, Parties, Contact history and Documents, each with its business date (read only state).
8. CaseRecordPage: shows the stale banner with MSG-P1-001 on any section whose business date is before the latest business date.
9. CaseRecordPage: shows the on hold banner with MSG-P3-004 when the case is on hold.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A data product is from an earlier date | Section shows with its date and the stale banner | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The case is outside the user's scope | 404; nothing shows | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
| X3 | The document hub does not answer | Documents section shows the section message; the rest shows | MSG-P3-023 | AC6 |
| X4 | The personal data access log cannot be written | Personal fields stay masked; the rest shows | MSG-P3-023 | AC7 |
| X5 | The role may not see a personal field unmasked | Field shows masked | None | AC8 |
| X6 | The case is on hold | On hold banner with the prescription date | MSG-P3-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | The case has no documents and no contact history | Each section shows its empty sentence | MSG-P3-024 | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Case record R opens the view | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-023-11 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads data other stories write; no write in this story |
| Negotiable | Section order and the masking rules are data and design choices |
| Valuable | One screen answers the case owner's first questions |
| Estimable | One page, five read endpoints, one query service |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case record view v1, read only

  Background:
    Given case owner U-81 owns case RW-2026-000701, a hire purchase case with 2 accounts
    Given the latest business date is 2026-12-02

  Scenario: AC1 Loads fast
    Given case RW-2026-000701 has 50 documents and 120 contact history entries
    When U-81 opens the case record view
    Then the header, accounts, parties, contact history and the first page of documents show in under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile over 50 openings

  Scenario: AC2 Data from products
    Given the account data product for 2026-12-02 holds days past due 97 and total balance THB 206,175.00 for account A-7001
    When the view opens
    Then the Accounts section shows 97 days past due and THB 206,175.00 for A-7001
    Then the section shows business date 2026-12-02
    Then the header shows queue "TDR-BKK-CO", owner U-81, status "IN_PROGRESS" and entry date 2026-11-30

  Scenario: AC3 Customer facts from the load
    Given the customer profile for the borrower arrived in the COLLINS load of 2026-12-02
    When the view opens
    Then the Parties section shows the borrower with role "BORROWER", segment "RETAIL" and business date 2026-12-02
    Then the contact history shows the EFS entries with channel, direction, result and time

  Scenario: AC4 Stale data product
    Given the COLLINS load for 2026-12-03 was refused and the account data product is from 2026-12-02
    When U-81 opens the view on 2026-12-03
    Then the Accounts section shows business date 2026-12-02
    Then the stale banner shows MSG-P1-001 for the account data product with date 2026-12-02

  Scenario: AC5 Case outside the scope
    Given case RW-2026-000702 belongs to team "LIT-BKK" and U-81 has scope Own
    When U-81 opens case RW-2026-000702
    Then the response is 404 with MSG-P4-003
    Then no case data shows

  Scenario: AC6 Document hub unavailable
    Given the document hub does not answer within 3 seconds
    When U-81 opens the view
    Then the Documents section shows MSG-P3-023 for "Documents"
    Then the header, accounts, parties and contact history show

  Scenario: AC7 Personal data access log unavailable
    Given the personal data access log cannot be written
    When U-81 opens the view
    Then the borrower's name and customer number show masked
    Then the Parties section shows MSG-P3-023 for "Personal details"

  Scenario: AC8 Masking by role
    Given phone collector U-82 may not see the customer number unmasked
    Given the case is in U-82's scope
    When U-82 opens the view
    Then the customer number shows masked as "xxxxxx4821"
    Then the access log holds the read with user U-82 and the masked result

  Scenario: AC9 Case on hold
    Given case RW-2026-000701 has status "ON_HOLD" for deviation X1 with prescription date 2028-03-15
    When U-81 opens the view
    Then the on hold banner shows MSG-P3-004 with "X1" and 2028-03-15

  Scenario: AC10 No documents and no contact history
    Given case RW-2026-000703 has no documents and no contact history
    When its owner opens the view
    Then the Documents and Contact history sections each show MSG-P3-024
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every section shows the business date of the data product it reads | REQ-RDF-009; VR-P3-001-1 |
| BR2 | A section older than the latest business date shows the stale banner | MSG-P1-001; screens.txt Common states "Stale input" |
| BR3 | Personal fields show masked unless the role may see them | REQ-ACA-005; CTL-11; DL26 |
| BR4 | Every read of personal data is written to the access log | REQ-ACA-006 |
| BR5 | Only cases in the caller's scope open; others return 404 | CTL-09; REQ-ACA-009 |
| BR6 | The view has no edit control in Epic 1 | SCR-03 "E1 read only" |
| BR7 | The view loads in under 2 seconds with 50 documents | NFR-009 |
| BR8 | Customer facts come from the profile ACE receives through COLLINS | DL20 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It reads the case and shows its status.

| RW-CONDUCT, RW-AUDIT | Open every case (scope All) |
| RW-REFADM, RW-SECADM | No Case record right; refused |
| SY-CASEWF | Reads P1 data through the published interface |

### 12. Contract

| Endpoint | Request | Response | Errors | Authorization |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId} | Path caseId | Case | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 404 (MSG-P4-003); 503 | Case record R, scope applied |
| GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/accounts | Path caseId | CaseAccount[] with new fields accountNo, daysPastDue, principalOutstanding, totalBalance, bucket, dataAsOf (see additions) | Same | Case record R, scope applied |
| GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/parties | Path caseId | CaseParty[] masked by role, with new fields displayName, customerNo, segment, dataAsOf (see additions) | Same | Case record R, scope applied |
| GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions | Path caseId; query channel, from, to, page, size | InteractionPage | Same | Case record R, scope applied |
| GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents | Path caseId; query type, page, size | DocumentPage (P5) | Same | Documents R, scope applied |

Idempotency: not applicable; every endpoint is a read.

```java
// P1, used by this story
public interface RecoveryDataQuery {
    List<AccountView> accountsFor(List<UUID> accountIds);       // balances, arrears, data_as_of
    List<PartyView> partiesFor(List<UUID> partyIds);            // profile facts, data_as_of
}
// P4, package recovery.access.matrix (RWB-E1-037)
<T> T mask(T dto, SessionContext session);               // FieldMasker
ScopeFilter scopeFor(SessionContext session);            // ScopeService
// P4, package recovery.access.accesslog (RWB-E1-039)
public interface AccessEventPublisher {
    void publish(AccessEvent event) throws DecisionLogUnavailableException;   // eventCode AC-READ with field IDs and masked flags
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Back end `recovery/casewf/caserecord` (Java package `recovery.casewf.caserecord`); front end `src/modules/recovery/casewf/caserecord`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseAndWorkflowController | Controller | The four P3 read endpoints with access check and scope |
| CaseRecordQueryService | Service | Composes case, accounts, parties and interactions; adds data_as_of per section |
| MaskingApplier | Service | Calls FieldMasker (RWB-E1-037) and publishes AC-READ through AccessEventPublisher; masks every personal field when the publish fails |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | recovery_case, case_account, case_party, interaction, queue |
| CaseRecordPage | React component | SCR-03 read only layout with Loading, read only and on hold states |
| CaseHeader, AccountsPanel, PartiesPanel, ContactHistoryPanel, DocumentsPanel | React component | One section each, each with a DataDateBadge |
| StaleBanner, OnHoldBanner, SectionMessage | React component | MSG-P1-001, MSG-P3-004, MSG-P3-023 and MSG-P3-024 |

**Database**

- Reads recovery_case, case_account, case_party, interaction, queue only. Uses ix_interaction_case_time for the contact history page.
- No migration.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Masking rules (RWB-E1-037; DL26), labels (DL10), LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-CONTACT-RESULT, LOV-PARTY-ROLE.
- Parameter `caserecord.section.timeout.ms` = 3000 (assumed; DL11) from RWB-E1-042.

**Build steps**

1. CaseRecordQueryService with P1 reads and data_as_of per section; tests AC2, AC3.
2. MaskingApplier with the access log call and the masked fallback; tests AC7, AC8.
3. Scope check returning 404; test AC5.
4. CaseRecordPage with parallel calls, per-section timeout and section messages; tests AC6, AC10.
5. StaleBanner and OnHoldBanner; tests AC4, AC9.
6. Performance test with 50 documents and 120 interactions; test AC1.
7. Access test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.caserecordview`. Off: SCR-03 shows the case header only.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the view meets NFR-009 in SIT.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | A section's data product is from an earlier date | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P3-004 | Case on hold | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P3-024 | A section has nothing to show | Nothing is recorded in {section} yet. |
| MSG-P3-023 | A section cannot be shown | {section} cannot be shown now. The rest of the case is shown. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. |

### 15. Screens and states

SCR-03 Case record. Loading: skeleton rows per section. Read only: fields without edit controls; the header and five sections with their business dates. On hold: the banner with the deviation or legal hold and the prescription date. Stale input: MSG-P1-001 above the section. Error: MSG-P3-023 in the section that failed.

## RWB-E1-024 Document store and index

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-024 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-01 Store documents with a write-once container for legal types; FEAT-DCM-02 Index documents by case, type, date and extracted fields; FEAT-DCM-19 Keep the Workbench document hub as the system of record for documents; FEAT-DCM-20 Version a document and keep its history |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-001, REQ-DCM-002, REQ-DCM-003, REQ-DCM-008 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence; L2 13.3 Store and retain documents |
| Decision | D7.2 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-025, RWB-TE-012, RWB-E1-001 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **every document stored against its case with its type, date, source and extracted fields, legal types held in a write-once container, and every version kept**, so that **I find a document by case ID, type and date, and a legal document cannot be changed after it is stored**.

### 2. Business rationale

Recovery documents are held today in folders, shared drives and with couriers; originals go missing and evidence is rebuilt for each audit (FSD P5 A1.3). This story builds the store and the index that every other document story writes to: one document record in the Workbench document hub per file, the file in blob storage, legal types write-once (DT06, ADR-007, control CTL-12). It meets REQ-DCM-001, REQ-DCM-002, REQ-DCM-003 and REQ-DCM-008. The module measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.1.1), which can only be counted once every document is indexed against its case.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the tables document and document_field exist in the recovery schema.
- RWB-TE-012 is done: the intake container, rwb-docs (standard), rwb-docs-legal (write-once) and rwb-quarantine exist, reached by managed identity through DocumentStorage.
- RWB-E1-018 is done: cases exist and the P3 published interface CaseDirectory returns a case by ID.
- RWB-E1-025 is done: document type table version DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force with the six types, the write-once flag and the retention class of each type.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the P7 published interface DecisionLogWriter writes an entry inside the caller's transaction.
- Document hub parameters loaded (this story creates the table): INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES = PDF, JPG, PNG; INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB = 25, assumed (DL11). RWB-E1-053 and RWB-E1-057 read the same table.
- The caller is the upload service (RWB-E1-026, user with Documents C) or the intake (RWB-E1-032, SY-OCR). A reader holds Documents R with the case in scope.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.store is on.

### 4. Flow

1. Caller: calls DocumentStore.store with the case ID, the document type, the source, the file in the intake container, its SHA-256 hash and any extracted fields.
2. DocumentStoreService: gets the case through CaseDirectory.findById and refuses the call if the case does not exist.
3. DocumentStoreService: reads the type row from the document type table version in force: write_once and retention_class.
4. DocumentStoreService: checks the file type by its content signature and the file size against INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES and INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB.
5. DocumentStoreService: looks for an active document on the case with the same type and hash; if one exists, returns it and stops.
6. DocumentStoreService: in one transaction, writes the decision log entry (decision code DOCATT, final call STORED) through DecisionLogWriter, inserts the document row with doc_version 1 and state COPY_PENDING, inserts the document_field rows and writes DocumentStored (EV-16) to the outbox.
7. DocumentStoreService: after commit, calls DocumentStorage.store (RWB-TE-012), which writes the file to rwb-docs-legal when write_once is true and to rwb-docs otherwise, at {container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1; the service sets storage_ref and state STORED.
8. User with Documents R: opens the document from the case documents screen (SCR-30); GET /documents/{documentId} returns the metadata, the extracted fields and the version list; GET /documents/{documentId}/content returns the file. The ACE common module writes each read to the PII access log.
9. User with Documents U: adds a version with POST /documents/{documentId}/versions; the service inserts a new document row with doc_version n+1 and previous_version_id set to the current row, and marks the earlier row is_active = false. The earlier version stays readable.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Delete or content replace of a write-once document, through the service or directly on the container | Refused; the file and the row are unchanged; an audit event DOCUMENT_CHANGE_REFUSED is written | MSG-P5-002 | AC2 |
| X2 | Document type not in the type table in force | Refused with 422; nothing stored | MSG-P5-006 | AC5 |
| X3 | File content is not PDF, JPG or PNG | Refused with 415; nothing stored | MSG-P5-001 | AC6 |
| X4 | File above INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB | Refused with 413; nothing stored | MSG-P5-017 | AC7 |
| X5 | The same file is stored again on the same case with the same type | The existing document is returned; no second row, entry or event | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Two users add a version to the same document at the same time | The first succeeds; the second gets 409; one new version exists | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | A version is added to a document that is not the latest version | Refused with 409 | MSG-P5-025 | AC10 |
| X8 | The copy to the container fails after commit | The row stays COPY_PENDING; the copy is retried by the next document intake run (JOB-12); content reads return 503 until it is stored | MSG-GEN-006 | AC11 |
| X9 | The reader's role scope does not include the case | Refused with 403; nothing is returned | MSG-P4-003 | AC12 |
| X10 | The caller's role lacks the Documents right | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-024-13 (Access) |
| X11 | The decision log write fails | Nothing is stored; incident raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-024-14 (Principle 5) |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the tables (RWB-E1-001), the containers (RWB-TE-012), the case (RWB-E1-018), the type table (RWB-E1-025) and the decision log writer (RWB-E1-027), all earlier in Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | File types, size limit, write-once flag and retention class are data rows; the story fixes the behavior |
| Valuable | Every later document path (upload, OCR intake, generation) stores through this one service |
| Estimable | One service, one published interface, three endpoints, one detail panel, one migration |
| Small | Fits within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every document is held against one case, with type, source, stored date and extracted fields | REQ-DCM-001; document.case_id is mandatory |
| BR2 | The document hub is the system of record; the file is held only in the hub containers | DT06; DL27; REQ-DCM-002 |
| BR3 | The write-once flag and the retention class come from the document type table version in force, never from the caller | Document type table (New); principle 1; DT02 |
| BR4 | A write-once document is never deleted or changed; a change is a new version | CTL-12; REQ-DCM-003; NFR-029 |
| BR5 | File types and the size limit are parameters | Document hub parameter table (New); DL11 |
| BR6 | A store with the same case, type and hash returns the existing document | R-UNI-40; events.txt rule Duplicates |
| BR7 | Only the latest version of a document takes a new version | FEAT-DCM-20 |
| BR8 | A store that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR9 | Every read checks role, capability area and scope, and is written to the access log | CTL-09; REQ-ACA-006 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It sets the document record state (standard column state): new row COPY_PENDING; COPY_PENDING to STORED when the copy succeeds; on a new version the earlier row changes is_active from true to false.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Stores documents through DocumentStore (Documents C) |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-LITOFF, RW-RESTRUCT and the other roles with Documents C | Store through the upload in RWB-E1-026 |
| Roles with Documents U (for example RW-CASEOWN, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL, RW-COMPLY) | Add a new version |
| Roles with Documents R (for example RW-TEAMMGR, RW-AUDIT, RW-PHONECOL) | Read metadata and content inside their scope |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Writes the DOCATT entry |
| Nobody | Deletes or changes a write-once document |

### 12. Contract

**GET /documents/{documentId}**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path documentId (uuid) |
| Response | 200 Document: id, caseId, partyId, documentType, source, storageRef, classificationConfidence, reviewStatus, retentionClass, writeOnce, docVersion. Extended with storedAt, previousVersionId, versions and fields (see additions) |
| Errors | 401 not signed in; 403 no Documents R (MSG-P4-002) or case out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 404 no such document; 503 store unavailable (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/documents/{documentId}/content**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path documentId (uuid) |
| Response | 200 application/octet-stream, the file of that version |
| Errors | 401; 403 as above; 404; 503 while state is COPY_PENDING (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**POST /documents/{documentId}/versions**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file (binary), reason (string, required) |
| Response | 200 Document, the new version |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Documents U (MSG-P4-002) or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 404; 409 not the latest version (MSG-P5-025) or concurrent change (MSG-GEN-004); 413 file above the limit (MSG-P5-017, see additions); 415 file type (MSG-P5-001); 503 decision log write failed (MSG-P7-003) |
| Authorization | Documents, right U, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header; a repeat with the same key returns the first result |

**Published interface (P5, used by RWB-E1-026, RWB-E1-032 and the retention job in RWB-E1-041)**

```java
public interface DocumentStore {
    StoredDocument store(StoreRequest request);          // caseId, documentType, source, intakeBlobRef, sha256, fields, partyId
    StoredDocument addVersion(UUID documentId, BlobRef file, String reason, UUID actor);
    void delete(UUID documentId, String reason, UUID actor);          // throws WriteOnceViolationException when write_once
    void replaceContent(UUID documentId, BlobRef file, UUID actor);   // throws WriteOnceViolationException when write_once
    Optional<StoredDocument> findById(UUID documentId);
}
```

**Event published:** DocumentStored (EV-16), payload documentId, caseId, type, source, written to the outbox in the store transaction.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dochub/store`, Java package `recovery.dochub.store`.

**Components.**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DocumentHubController | Controller | GET document, GET content, POST versions; maps exceptions to problem responses with the message ID |
| DocumentStore | Published interface | The contract in section 12 for other modules and P5 packages |
| DocumentStoreService | Service | Validation, type lookup, duplicate check, decision log write, insert, outbox event, version rules |
| DocumentHubRepository | Repository | Reads and writes document and document_field only |
| DocumentEntity, DocumentFieldEntity | Entity | Map the two tables, with the optimistic lock column version |
| DocumentTypeReader | Repository | Reads the document type table version in force (table from RWB-E1-025) |
| DocumentHubParameters | Rule table | Reads document_hub_parameter rows in force, cached for 5 minutes; used by every P5 package |
| DocumentStorage | Published interface | From RWB-TE-012: writes, opens and refuses overwrite of blobs; called, never reimplemented |
| CopyPendingStep | Job | Step of JOB-12 Document intake that retries copies for rows in COPY_PENDING |
| DocumentDetailPanel | React component | Opens from SCR-30; shows metadata, extracted fields, versions and the download button |

**Database.**
- Reads and writes document (all columns) and document_field (all columns).
- Flyway migration `V1_5_024__document_store.sql`: adds document.previous_version_id uuid null with a foreign key to document(id) and document.content_sha256 char(64) not null; creates document_hub_parameter (id, param_code varchar(40), param_value varchar(200), unit varchar(20), table_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, load_id uuid, standard columns) with unique (param_code, table_version).
- Indexes: ix_document_case_type_created on document (case_id, document_type, created_at); unique partial index uk_document_case_type_hash on document (case_id, document_type, content_sha256) where is_active; ix_document_previous_version on document (previous_version_id).

**Configuration and reference data.**
- Document type table (RWB-E1-025), loaded by the reference data administrator.
- Parameters INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES and INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB in document_hub_parameter, loaded by the reference data administrator.
- Container names rwb-docs and rwb-docs-legal from RWB-TE-012, held as properties per environment.
- Decision code DOCATT, assumed; the LOV-DECISION list is loaded by the data steward.

**Build steps.**
1. Write the migration and the entities; test the unique partial index refuses a second active row with the same case, type and hash.
2. Build DocumentHubParameters and DocumentTypeReader with the valid_from and valid_to rule of the type table; unit test the version in force on a boundary date.
3. Build DocumentStoreService.store with validation (case, type, content signature, size) and the duplicate check; unit test AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8.
4. Add the transaction: DecisionLogWriter call, inserts and outbox event; integration test that a forced writer failure leaves no row and no event.
5. Call DocumentStorage after commit and build CopyPendingStep; integration test against the SIT storage account with rwb-docs-legal under its immutability policy for AC1, AC2 and AC11.
6. Build addVersion with the latest-version rule and optimistic locking; test AC4, AC9, AC10.
7. Build delete and replaceContent with the write-once refusal and the audit event; test AC2.
8. Build the controller endpoints with the access check and scope; API tests for AC1, AC12 and the access test.
9. Build DocumentDetailPanel; component test for the version list and the download.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.dochub.store`. Off: the endpoints return 404 and DocumentStore.store refuses with a feature-off error.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the boundary test on module tables passes, and a 1.2 MB PDF is stored and listed within 2 seconds in SIT.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-001 | File content is not an allowed type | This file type cannot be stored. Use PDF, JPG or PNG. |
| MSG-P5-002 | Delete or change of a write-once document | Legal documents cannot be changed. Add a new version instead. |
| MSG-P5-017 | File above the size limit | This file is larger than {size} MB and cannot be stored. |
| MSG-P5-025 | New version on a superseded version | This is not the latest version of the document. Open the latest version to add a new one. |
| MSG-P5-006 | Document type not in the type table in force | {value} is not a document type in force. Choose a type from the list. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Concurrent version | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | Content requested while the copy is pending | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: file types, size limit, write-once flag, retention class and container names are data rows or properties.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. Test files are synthetic; extracted field values in logs are replaced by the field name.
- No read of another module's tables: the case is read through CaseDirectory, the decision log is written through DecisionLogWriter.
- The service never overwrites a blob; every version is a new blob path.
- The PII access log entry for each read is written by the ACE common module, never by this package.

## RWB-E1-025 Document types and fields agreed

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-025 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-03 Agree the six document types and their fields |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-004 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | D7.2 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-012 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the first six document types (demand letter, court notice, appraisal report, title deed, settlement agreement, guarantor notice) with their key fields agreed with Legal and NPA and held as versioned reference data**, so that **the OCR pipeline, classification and extraction have one signed target list**.

### 2. Business rationale

Classification and extraction cannot be built or measured until the bank fixes which types are read and which fields come out of each (REQ-DCM-004, DL19). Today no signed list exists, so the model would train on a list that may change. This story turns the agreed list into a versioned table that the store (RWB-E1-024), classification (RWB-E1-050) and extraction (RWB-E1-053) read, and that changes by a data load without a code release (DT02). The measure it serves is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.3.1).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-012 is done: the local trackers are listed with their owners, so the types in the current trackers are known.
- The load file "DOCTYPE-2026.11" is prepared by the reference data administrator with the six types, 26 fields and the sign-offs of a legal counsel user and a Head of NPA user.
- LOV-RETENTION holds the codes LEGAL10Y and GENERAL05Y, assumed until the bank retention schedule arrives (DL26), loaded by the data steward.
- The loader holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C). The approver holds Reference data A (see section 10).
- The P4 endpoint POST /admin/reference-loads exists and calls the P5 ReferenceTableLoader for table code DOCUMENT_TYPE.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.doctypes is on.

### 4. Flow

1. Center of excellence analyst: prepares the list of six types and 26 fields; legal counsel and the Head of NPA review it and sign with a date.
2. Reference data administrator: uploads the file with POST /admin/reference-loads, table DOCUMENT_TYPE, validFrom 2026-11-30.
3. P4 reference load service: passes the rows to DocumentTypeLoader through the ReferenceTableLoader interface.
4. DocumentTypeLoader: validates every row: type code unique, label present, write-once flag present, retention class in LOV-RETENTION, at least one field, both sign-offs with a user ID and a date.
5. DocumentTypeLoader: on any failure refuses the load whole and returns the row errors; the version in force is unchanged.
6. DocumentTypeLoader: on success writes the rows as table version DOCTYPE-2026.11 with status LOADED, not yet in force.
7. Approver: approves with POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve; a different person from the loader.
8. DocumentTypeLoader: sets the version APPROVED; from validFrom the readers return it as the version in force; the previous version gets valid_to of the day before.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A row has no Legal or no NPA sign-off, or a sign-off without a date | Load refused in full; version in force unchanged | MSG-P3-027 | AC3 |
| X2 | A row has a retention class not in LOV-RETENTION, or repeats a type code | Load refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X3 | The same table version is loaded a second time | Refused with 409; the first load is kept | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X4 | A new version with a future valid from date | The current version stays in force until that date; open work keeps the version it used | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The loader tries to approve their own load | Refused with 409 | MSG-P7-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without Reference data C uploads the file | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-025-08 (Access) |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the tracker list (RWB-E1-012) and the P4 reference load endpoint |
| Negotiable | The type list and fields are data; the bank list replaces the six proposed types under DL19 |
| Valuable | Gives the OCR, classification and extraction stories one signed target |
| Estimable | One table, one loader, one validation set |
| Small | Under one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The document types and their fields are signed by Legal and NPA before extraction is built | REQ-DCM-004; DL19 |
| BR2 | Each type row carries the write-once flag, the retention class and the field list | Document type table (New); DT02 |
| BR3 | A load with any invalid row is refused in full | refdata.txt change process, step 3; CTL-08 |
| BR4 | A version takes effect on its valid from date; work already done keeps the version it used | refdata.txt change process, step 6; R-UNI-38 |
| BR5 | The person who loads a version does not approve it | roles.txt separation of duty; CTL-08 |
| BR6 | Retention class codes come from LOV-RETENTION | LOV-RETENTION; DL26 |
| BR7 | The six proposed types apply until the bank provides its own list | DL19 |

The initial field lists are assumed until the sign-off (DL19): DEMAND_LETTER case_no, account_no, letter_date, amount_demanded, pay_by_date; COURT_NOTICE court_name, black_case_no, notice_date, hearing_date; APPRAISAL_REPORT appraisal_no, appraisal_date, appraised_value, title_doc_no; TITLE_DEED title_doc_no, land_office, owner_name, area_sq_wa; SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT case_no, agreement_date, settlement_amount, installment_count, borrower_name; GUARANTOR_NOTICE case_no, guarantor_name, notice_date, amount_claimed. Fields account_no, owner_name, borrower_name and guarantor_name are marked personal. Write-once true for every type except APPRAISAL_REPORT; retention LEGAL10Y for the write-once types and GENERAL05Y for APPRAISAL_REPORT (assumed; DL26, DL27).

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the reference load status: LOADED on a valid load; REFUSED on a failed check; APPROVED on approval, in force from valid from.

### 12. Contract

**POST /admin/reference-loads** (P4 endpoint; this story adds the table code DOCUMENT_TYPE)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file (binary, the load file in the Excel template), table = "DOCUMENT_TYPE", validFrom (date) |
| Response | 201 ReferenceLoad: id, table, validFrom, status (LOADED or REFUSED), rows |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Reference data C (MSG-P4-002); 409 version already loaded (MSG-P3-027); 422 a row fails validation (MSG-P3-027 with row and error); 503 store unavailable (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Reference data, right C |
| Idempotency | The table code and the table version; a second load of the same version is refused with 409 |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path loadId (uuid) |
| Response | 200 ReferenceLoad with status APPROVED |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Reference data A (MSG-P4-002); 404; 409 approver is the loader (MSG-P7-002) or status is not LOADED; 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right A |
| Idempotency | Approving an APPROVED load returns it unchanged |

**Published interfaces**

```java
// P5 implements the P4 loader contract for its own tables
public interface ReferenceTableLoader {
    String tableCode();                                           // "DOCUMENT_TYPE"
    LoadResult validateAndStage(UUID loadId, String tableVersion, LocalDate validFrom, List<Map<String, String>> rows);
    void approve(UUID loadId, UUID approverId);
}

// P5 reader used by RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-050 and RWB-E1-053
public interface DocumentTypeCatalog {
    DocumentTypeVersion inForce(LocalDate businessDate);         // version, types, fields
    Optional<DocumentTypeDef> type(String docTypeCode, LocalDate businessDate);
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dochub/types`, Java package `recovery.dochub.types`.

**Components.**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DocumentTypeLoader | Service | Implements ReferenceTableLoader for DOCUMENT_TYPE: parse, validate, stage, approve |
| DocumentTypeCatalog | Published interface | Returns the version in force and a type by code for a business date |
| DocumentTypeCatalogService | Service | Implements DocumentTypeCatalog with a 5-minute cache, cleared on approval |
| DocumentTypeRepository | Repository | Reads and writes document_type only |
| DocumentTypeEntity | Entity | Maps document_type |
| document_type rows | Rule table | The six types as data |

**Database.**
- Flyway migration `V1_5_025__document_type.sql` creates document_type: id uuid, doc_type_code varchar(30), label_en varchar(120), label_th varchar(120), write_once boolean, retention_class varchar(10), field_definitions jsonb, legal_signoff_by uuid, legal_signoff_date date, npa_signoff_by uuid, npa_signoff_date date, table_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, load_id uuid, plus the standard columns.
- Constraints: unique (doc_type_code, table_version); not null on both sign-off columns.
- Index ix_document_type_valid on (valid_from, valid_to).

**Configuration and reference data.**
- The load file DOCTYPE-2026.11, prepared by the reference data administrator, signed by legal counsel and the Head of NPA.
- LOV-RETENTION values, loaded by the data steward (DL26).

**Build steps.**
1. Write the migration and the entity; test the constraints.
2. Build the row parser for the Excel template columns; unit test a valid file of 6 rows.
3. Build the validation rules and the refuse-whole behavior; unit test AC3 and AC4.
4. Build staging, the version check and approval with the separation of duty check; test AC1, AC2, AC5 and AC7.
5. Build DocumentTypeCatalogService with the valid from rule; test AC6 on the boundary dates.
6. Add the loader to the table codes of the P4 reference load service; API test through POST /admin/reference-loads and the access test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.dochub.doctypes`. Off: the table code DOCUMENT_TYPE is refused by the reference load endpoint.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and version DOCTYPE-2026.11 is approved in SIT with both sign-offs.

|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | A document hub reference load fails a check | The {table} load was refused: {error} at row {row}. The version in force is unchanged. |
| MSG-P7-002 | Loader approves their own load | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

## RWB-E1-026 Attach and search screen

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-026 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-04 Attach a document to a case; FEAT-DCM-05 Search documents within a case |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-008, REQ-DCM-001 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-025, RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-041, RWB-E1-045, RWB-E1-030 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **to upload, see and search the documents of a case from the case record view**, so that **the case file is complete and I find a document by type and date without leaving the case**.

### 2. Business rationale

Case owners hold documents in shared drives and email today, so the case file is never complete in one place (FSD P5 A1.3). This story puts the case documents screen SCR-30 on the case record view: upload with a type, a list of every document on the case, a search by type and date, and a checklist placeholder showing which of the six agreed types are present. It meets REQ-DCM-008 (search by case, type and date from the case record view) and REQ-DCM-001 (every document stored against its case with type, date and source). The measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.4.1), which needs documents on the case first.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-024 is done: DocumentStore stores, versions and reads documents.
- RWB-E1-025 is done: document type table DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force.
- RWB-E1-041 is done: the malware scan runs on every file before storage.
- RWB-E1-045 and RWB-E1-030 are done: product parameters and the queue measures used by the case record view exist.
- Parameters INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB = 25 (assumed, DL11) and INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES = PDF, JPG, PNG are in force.
- The user holds a role with Documents C to upload and Documents R to list, with the case in scope.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.casedocs is on.

### 4. Flow

1. Case owner: opens case RW-2026-000123 on the case record view (SCR-03) and the Documents tab (SCR-30, state Loading then list).
2. Front end: calls GET /cases/{caseId}/documents and GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist and shows the list and the checklist placeholder.
3. Case owner: chooses Upload, picks a file and a document type from the list, and submits; the front end checks the size against INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB before sending and sends an Idempotency-Key.
4. CaseDocumentUploadService: puts the file in the intake container, calls the malware scan (RWB-E1-041) and, if clean, calls DocumentStore.store with source UPLOAD.
5. DocumentStore (RWB-E1-024): writes the decision log entry, the document row and DocumentStored, then copies the file.
6. Front end: on 201 refreshes the list; the new document shows within 5 seconds of submit.
7. Case owner: enters a type and a date range in the search bar; GET /cases/{caseId}/documents with type, dateFrom and dateTo returns only the matching documents, newest first, 20 per page.
8. Case owner: opens a document; DocumentDetailPanel (RWB-E1-024) shows it.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Upload with no document type | Refused with 422; nothing stored | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The file fails the malware scan | Refused with 422; file held in quarantine; nothing stored | MSG-P5-016 | AC5 |
| X3 | The file type is not allowed | Refused with 415; nothing stored | MSG-P5-001 | AC6 |
| X4 | The same file and type is already on the case | The existing document is returned and highlighted; no second document | MSG-P5-024 | AC7 |
| X5 | The submit is sent twice with the same Idempotency-Key | One document; the second call returns the first result | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Date from is after date to | Search not run | MSG-GEN-003 | AC9 |
| X7 | Search matches nothing | Empty state with the sentence and the clear filter action | None | AC10 |
| X8 | Case is outside the user's scope | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-003 | AC11 |
| X9 | Role without Documents C uploads | Refused with 403; Upload button hidden | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-026-12 (Access) |
| X10 | The decision log write fails during the store | Nothing stored; the dialog shows the message | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-026-13 (Principle 5) |

### 6. INVEST check

|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the store (RWB-E1-024), the types (RWB-E1-025) and the scan (RWB-E1-041), all earlier in Epic 1; no other screen depends on it |
| Negotiable | Page size, sort order and the placeholder layout can change; the endpoints stay |
| Valuable | Case owners attach and find documents on the case instead of in shared drives |
| Estimable | Two endpoints changed or added, one service, one tab with three parts |
| Small | Fits within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |
