### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A user upload carries a document type from the type table in force and source UPLOAD | REQ-DCM-001; LOV-DOC-SOURCE |
| BR2 | Every upload is scanned for malware before it is stored | REQ-DCM-010; FEAT-DCM-18 |
| BR3 | The list and the search show only cases in the user's scope | CTL-09 |
| BR4 | The date filter applies to the stored date of the document in Epic 1 | FSD P5 A2.5; REQ-DCM-008 |
| BR5 | The checklist placeholder lists the types of the type table in force; the required items per case type come in RWB-E1-040 | REQ-DCM-011; FEAT-DCM-16 |
| BR6 | A repeated upload with the same file, type and case returns the existing document | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | A store that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |

None. This story does not change a case status. A successful upload creates a document record in state COPY_PENDING, then STORED (RWB-E1-024).

| DF-DOC-026 | document | content_sha256 | Read |
| DF-REF-219 | document_type | doc_type_code | Read |
| DF-REF-220 | document_type | label_en | Read |
| DF-REF-246 | document_hub_parameter | param_value | Read |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | all fields | Write, through DocumentStore and DecisionLogWriter |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**POST /cases/{caseId}/documents**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file (binary), type (doc_type_code, required), source (must be "UPLOAD" for a user call; other values refused with 422) |
| Response | 201 Document for a new document; 200 Document with messageCode MSG-P5-024 for a duplicate |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Documents C (MSG-P4-002) or case out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 404 case not found; 413 above INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB (MSG-P5-017); 415 file type (MSG-P5-001); 422 type missing (MSG-GEN-001), type not in the table (MSG-P5-006) or malware found (MSG-P5-016); 503 decision log write failed (MSG-P7-003) |
| Authorization | Documents, right C, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header, kept 24 hours per user; a repeat returns the first response |

**GET /cases/{caseId}/documents**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query type, page, size (api.yaml) plus dateFrom and dateTo (date, see additions); size default 20, maximum 100 |
| Response | 200 DocumentPage: items (Document), page, size, total; only active versions |
| Errors | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003); 404 case not found; 422 dateFrom after dateTo (MSG-GEN-003); 503 |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist** (new, see additions)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path caseId |
| Response | 200 DocumentChecklist: caseId, checklistVersion (here the type table version), items [documentType, label, required, presentCount], missingCount, complete |
| Errors | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003); 404; 503 |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

The placeholder returns required = false for every item, missingCount 0 and complete null until RWB-E1-040 sets the required items.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dochub/casedocs`, Java package `recovery.dochub.casedocs`; front end folder `recovery/documents`.

**Components.**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DocumentHubController | Controller | Adds POST and GET /cases/{caseId}/documents and GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist |
| CaseDocumentUploadService | Service | Intake container write, malware scan call, DocumentStore.store, idempotency key handling |
| CaseDocumentQueryService | Service | List and search by case, type and stored date with paging |
| ChecklistPlaceholderService | Service | Builds the six-type placeholder from DocumentTypeCatalog and the counts per type |
| CaseDocumentQueryRepository | Repository | Reads document only, filtered by case, type, active flag and created_at |
| CaseDocumentsTab | React component | SCR-30 with the list, the search bar and the checklist placeholder |
| UploadDocumentDialog | React component | File picker, type list from LOV-DOC-TYPE, size check, error display |

**Database.**
- Reads document (id, case_id, document_type, source, retention_class, write_once, doc_version, is_active, created_at, content_sha256).
- Uses the index ix_document_case_type_created from RWB-E1-024. No new table.

**Configuration and reference data.**
- Document type table (RWB-E1-025); document hub parameters INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB and INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES (RWB-E1-024).
- Property rwb.dochub.casedocs.page-size = 20.

**Build steps.**
1. Extend the list endpoint with dateFrom and dateTo and the date order check; API tests for AC2, AC9, AC10 and AC11.
2. Build CaseDocumentUploadService with the scan call and the store call; integration tests for AC1, AC4, AC5 and AC6.
3. Add the duplicate response and the Idempotency-Key handling; tests for AC7 and AC8.
4. Build ChecklistPlaceholderService and the checklist endpoint; test AC3.
5. Build CaseDocumentsTab and UploadDocumentDialog with the states Loading, list, upload, empty and error; component tests for each state.
6. Browser test of upload to list within 5 seconds in SIT, and the access test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.dochub.casedocs`. Off: the Documents tab is hidden and the endpoints return 404.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and a 2 MB upload shows in the list within 5 seconds in SIT.

## RWB-E1-027 Decision log writer v1

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-027 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P7 Decision center and log |
| Feature | FEAT-DRI-02 Write a decision log entry for every decision; FEAT-DRI-03 Record the rule ID, rule version and inputs on each entry; FEAT-DRI-04 Record the approver and the limit applied; FEAT-DRI-05 Block an action when the decision log write fails; FEAT-DRI-08 Expose the decision service to the workflow |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-004, REQ-DRI-005 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.7; Business Requirements Program, section 5.7 |
| L3 process | 17 Run the decision center |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-008, RWB-E1-056 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As the **case workflow module (SY-CASEWF)**, I want **one writer that validates and records case created, owner assigned, case transferred and document attached, with the rule ID and version used, in the same transaction as the action**, so that **the first decision records exist in Epic 1 and no action proceeds without its record**.

### 2. Business rationale

Without one writer, each module would build its own record and some actions would go unrecorded. This story gives every module one published interface that checks each record against the seven field groups, refuses an incomplete record, writes it in the caller's transaction so that a failed write stops the action, ignores a repeated event and publishes DecisionRecorded. It meets REQ-DRI-004 and REQ-DRI-005 and is the automated part of control CTL-06. The measure is decisions with a log entry: target 100 percent, and no action without one (NFR-034).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-008 is done: the store appends hash-chained entries and holds the columns chain_seq, corrects_entry_id and actor_user_id.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: the writer's failure alert and run book are in the job and service monitoring.
- LOV-DECISION is loaded by RW-DATASTEW with the decision codes, including the access event codes for RWB-E1-039.
- Parameters in the catalog: rwb.decision.code.CASE_CREATED=D6, rwb.decision.code.OWNER_ASSIGNED=D6, rwb.decision.code.CASE_TRANSFERRED=D6, rwb.decision.code.DOCUMENT_ATTACHED=D6 (assumed; D6 is the entry and ownership decision; owner RW-DATASTEW).
- The ACE outbox (RWB-TE-006) is available in the same database transaction.

### 4. Flow

1. Calling module (for example SY-CASEWF in the morning allocation): builds a DecisionLogRecord with the case, the event, the rule ID and version, the inputs reference, the actor and an idempotency key, inside its own transaction.
2. Calling module: calls DecisionLogWriter.write as the last step before commit.
3. Writer (DecisionLogWriterService): checks that a transaction is open; refuses the call if not.
4. Writer: checks the idempotency key; for a key already written, returns the first entry reference and counts the repeat.
5. Writer (DecisionLogRecordValidator): checks the required fields and the version group; refuses an incomplete record with the missing field named.
6. Writer: calls DecisionLogStore.append (RWB-E1-008).
7. Writer: writes the DecisionRecorded event to the outbox in the same transaction.
8. Calling module: commits; the action, the entry and the event are stored together.
9. Writer: on a refused record or a failed append, raises the exception; the caller's transaction rolls back, an incident is raised and the caller shows MSG-P7-003 or its own message.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A record misses the version group, the inputs reference, the final call or the case | Refused; the writer logs the error with the missing field; the caller's action rolls back | MSG-P7-009 | AC2 |
| X2 | A record carries a rule ID with no rule version | Refused as X1 | MSG-P7-009 | AC3 |
| X3 | The store cannot be written | The caller's action rolls back; an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC4 |
| X4 | The same event arrives twice with the same idempotency key | One entry; the repeat is counted | None | AC5 |
| X5 | The writer is called outside a transaction | Refused with IllegalTransactionStateException; nothing is written | None | AC6 |
| X6 | A record carries a decision code not in LOV-DECISION | Refused as X1 | MSG-P7-009 | AC7 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store (RWB-E1-008) and the monitoring (RWB-E1-056) |
| Negotiable | Decision codes per event are parameters; the validation rules follow the seven field groups |
| Valuable | Every Epic 1 action has a validated record or does not happen |
| Estimable | One interface, one validator, one outbox write |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Decision log writer v1

  Background:
    Given the environment is DEV with synthetic data
    Given allocation table version "ALLOC-2026.11" and transfer rule version "TRF-2026.11" are in force

  Scenario: AC1 Record per event
    Given case "RW-2026-000123" is created by JOB-02 and given owner "U-7101" by row "ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01" of "ALLOC-2026.11" in JOB-03
    When the two events are written
    Then two entries exist for the case with final calls "CASE_CREATED" and "OWNER_ASSIGNED"
    Then the second entry carries rule ID "ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01", rule version "ALLOC-2026.11", actor "SY-CASEWF" and an inputs reference
    Then both entries pass the schema check and two DecisionRecorded events are in the outbox

  Scenario: AC2 Schema enforced
    Given a record for case "RW-2026-000123" with final call "CASE_TRANSFERRED" and no rule version, model version or agent version
    When it is written
    Then the system refuses it with message MSG-P7-009 naming "versions"
    Then the writer logs the error with the case ID and the missing field
    Then the system rolls the transfer in the same transaction back

  Scenario: AC3 A rule ID with no rule version is refused
    Given a record with rule ID "R-UNI-14" and an empty rule version
    When it is written
    Then the system refuses it with message MSG-P7-009 naming "ruleVersion"

  Scenario: AC4 A failed write stops the action
    Given the decision log store is unavailable
    When JOB-03 gives case "RW-2026-000124" to owner "U-7102"
    Then the write raises DecisionLogUnavailableException
    Then the case owner stays empty and the case status stays "New"
    Then the system raises an incident to the platform administrator queue

  Scenario: AC5 A repeated event gives one entry
    Given event "EV-7f3a-0001" for document "DOC-2026-0009981" attached to case "RW-2026-000123" was written
    When the same event with idempotency key "EV-7f3a-0001" arrives again
    Then one entry exists for the event
    Then the writer returns the first entry's ID and adds 1 to the repeat count for R-UNI-40

  Scenario: AC6 A write outside a transaction is refused
    Given a caller without an open transaction
    When it calls the writer
    Then the system refuses the call with IllegalTransactionStateException and nothing is written

  Scenario: AC7 An unknown decision code is refused
    Given a record with decision code "D99"
    When it is written
    Then the system refuses it with message MSG-P7-009 naming "decisionCode"
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Epic 1 writes entries for case created, owner assigned, case transferred and document attached | REQ-DRI-004 |
| BR2 | Required on every record: decision code from LOV-DECISION, inputs reference, final call, decided at and the actor; the case unless the decision code is an access event | DF-DEC-002, DF-DEC-003, DF-DEC-008, DF-DEC-012, DF-DEC-016; LOV-DECISION |
| BR3 | The version group needs at least one of rule version, model version and agent version, except for access events; a rule ID needs its rule version | DF-DEC-004 to DF-DEC-007; NFR-034 |
| BR4 | An approver needs an approval level from LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL on the same record | DF-DEC-010, DF-DEC-011; FEAT-DRI-04 |
| BR5 | The record is written in the caller's transaction; if it cannot be written, the action does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06; REQ-DRI-005 |
| BR6 | The same event with the same idempotency key gives one entry, and the repeat is counted | R-UNI-40; events.txt, Duplicates rule |
| BR7 | Decision codes for the Epic 1 events are parameters, not code | Principle 1; parameters rwb.decision.code.* |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It makes a status change made by another module depend on its entry: when the write fails, the case stays in the status it had (for example "New" in AC4).

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-DECLOG Decision log writer | Writes entries (Decision log C) |
| SY-CASEWF Case workflow module | Calls the writer for case created, owner assigned and case transferred (Decision log C) |
| SY-OCR OCR and extraction pipeline | Calls the writer for document attached (Decision log C) |
| SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-AGENT | Call the writer for their own decisions (Decision log C) |
| RW-AUDIT, RW-COE and every role holding Decision log R | Read the entries |
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Receives the incident when a write fails |

### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | all fields | Write |
| DF-DEC-030 | decision_log_entry | actor_user_id | Write |
| DF-DEC-031 | decision_log_entry | idempotency_key | Write, read |
| DF-REF-028 | lov_value | lov_code | Read |
| DF-REF-029 | lov_value | value_code | Read |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**Published interface DecisionLogWriter** (package recovery.decision.writer), the only way any module writes to the decision log:

```java
@Transactional(propagation = Propagation.MANDATORY)
DecisionLogEntryRef write(DecisionLogRecord record)
    throws DecisionLogRecordInvalidException,  // messageId MSG-P7-009, field
           DecisionLogUnavailableException;     // messageId MSG-P7-003
// DecisionLogRecord: idempotencyKey, caseId, decisionCode, ruleId, ruleVersion, modelVersion, agentVersion, inputsRef,
//   recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, overrideReason, actions, outcome, decidedAt,
//   actorUserRef, correctsEntryId
// DecisionLogEntryRef: entryId, chainSeq, entryHash, repeated (boolean)
```

**Event published:** EV-08 DecisionRecorded, payload entryId, caseId, decisionCode, approver; written to the outbox in the same transaction; consumers ledger and reporting.

**GET /api/recovery/v1/decision-log/{entryId}** and **GET /api/recovery/v1/decision-log** (API-P7-007, API-P7-006): read the written entries; Decision log R; built in RWB-E1-008.

Idempotency: the record's idempotencyKey (the event ID from the calling module); unique index on decision_log_entry (idempotency_key).

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/decision/writer` in the recovery module; Java package `recovery.decision.writer`.
- Components:

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DecisionLogWriter | Published interface | The write method above |
| DecisionLogWriterService | Service | Transaction check, idempotency check, validation, append, outbox event |
| DecisionLogRecordValidator | Service | BR2 to BR4 checks, with the decision codes read from LOV-DECISION |
| Epic1DecisionRecords | Service | Builders for the four Epic 1 events, with the decision code from the parameter catalog |
| DecisionRecordedPublisher | Service | Writes EV-08 to the ACE outbox |
| DecisionCenterAndLogRepository | Repository | Idempotency key lookup; append through DecisionLogStore |

- Database: Flyway migration V_E1_027__declog_idempotency.sql adds idempotency_key varchar(80) to decision_log_entry with unique index uk_declog_idempotency. No other table.
- Configuration and reference data: LOV-DECISION (RW-DATASTEW); parameters rwb.decision.code.* (RW-DATASTEW, values assumed); repeat counter exposed as metric decision_log_repeats_total in the job and service monitoring (RWB-E1-056).
- Build steps:
  1. Write the migration for idempotency_key.
  2. Build DecisionLogRecordValidator with tests for AC2, AC3 and AC7.
  3. Build DecisionLogWriterService with the mandatory transaction, the idempotency check and the append; tests for AC5 and AC6.
  4. Add the outbox write of DecisionRecorded; test that a rollback leaves no event.
  5. Build the Epic 1 record builders and wire them into JOB-02, JOB-03, the transfer engine (RWB-E1-021) and document attach (RWB-E1-032) through the interface; test AC1.
  6. Test AC4 with the store switched off: the caller's change rolls back and the incident is raised.
- Feature flag: `rwb.decision.log-writer`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass and an architecture test fails the build if any class outside recovery.decision writes to decision_log_entry.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-009 | A record is refused for a missing or invalid field (new; written to the service log and the incident, not shown to customers) | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The store cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P3-013 | Allocation not made because the write failed (shown by the allocation summary) | The case was not allocated because the decision could not be recorded. It will be tried again in the next run. |

Thai text for each message follows DL10; proposed Thai for MSG-P7-009 is in the additions file.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. Entries are read through the decision log endpoints; failed writes appear as incidents in the job and service monitoring (RWB-E1-056).

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: decision codes per event are parameters and list values.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts; a refused record is logged with its case ID and field name only.

## RWB-E1-028 Service levels, timers, escalation and prescription dates

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-028 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-11 Set service levels and stage timers; FEAT-CWC-12 Set and track prescription dates; FEAT-CWC-13 Escalate a breached timer to the named point |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-011, REQ-CWC-012, REQ-CWC-016 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, section 5.3 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes; 06 Take over and own the case; 08 Litigate and enforce |
| Decision | D7 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-045, RWB-E1-020, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-043 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **a service level per queue and status, a timer on every case, a warning to the owner and a breach raised to the named escalation point by rule, and a prescription date set from the legal periods**, so that **no case waits past its limit unseen and no legal claim expires unnoticed**.

### 2. Business rationale

Deadlines are tracked in personal diaries today, and audit found litigation not filed for debtors meeting the criteria (CTL-18). This story starts a service level timer each time a case enters a queue and status, warns the owner at the warning point, raises a breach to the escalation role without moving the case, and sets the prescription date at case creation from the legal period for the product. It meets REQ-CWC-011, REQ-CWC-012 and REQ-CWC-016 and serves the measure "cases inside the service level" (target set with DL22).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-020 is done: CaseAllocated is published when a case gets a queue and owner.
- RWB-E1-045 is done: ProductParameterService serves the SERVICE_LEVEL row for a product group and a case status, with limit, unit, warning percent and escalation role.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: ReferenceDataService serves the LEGAL_PERIOD and HOLIDAY tables in force.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available.
- SERVICE_LEVEL row, values assumed until the business sets them (DL22): product group HIRE_PURCHASE, status ASSIGNED, limit 5 working days, warning percent 80, escalation role RW-TEAMMGR.
- LEGAL_PERIOD row owned by Legal: HIRE_PURCHASE 2 years from the last payment date (assumed value from the current story; other products loaded by Legal). Parameter `legal.prescription.warn.days` = 180 (assumed) from RWB-E1-042.
- The HOLIDAY table marks 2026-12-05 to 2026-12-07 as non-working days (synthetic test values).
- JOB-05 runs every 5 minutes as SY-CASEWF.

### 4. Flow

1. TimerStarter: on CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred or CaseStateChanged, stops the running SERVICE_LEVEL timer of the case.
2. TimerStarter: reads the service level for the new queue and status and starts a SERVICE_LEVEL timer with started_at, expires_at in working days and warn_at at the warning percentage.
3. PrescriptionService: on CaseCreated, reads the last payment date of each linked account through the P1 interface and the legal period for the product, and sets the earliest result as the prescription date.
4. PrescriptionService: starts a PRESCRIPTION timer with expires_at on the prescription date and warn_at 180 days before; a PRESCRIPTION timer never pauses.
5. TimerCheckJob (JOB-05): every 5 minutes finds RUNNING timers whose warn_at or expires_at has passed.
6. TimerCheckJob: for a passed warn_at, writes the decision log entry and sends MSG-P3-003 to the case owner once.
7. TimerCheckJob: for a passed expires_at of a SERVICE_LEVEL timer, writes the decision log entry with rule R-UNI-30, sets the timer EXPIRED with escalation level 1, and publishes TimerBreached with the escalation role; the case keeps its queue and owner.
8. TimerCheckJob: for a passed expires_at of any other timer type, sets it EXPIRED and publishes TimerDue.
9. TimerPauseHandler: on DeviationRaised pauses the SERVICE_LEVEL timer; on DeviationCleared resumes it and moves expires_at and warn_at by the paused time (R-UNI-43).
10. Case owner or team manager: reads the timers through GET /cases/{caseId}/timers and the prescription date through GET /cases/{caseId}.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No SERVICE_LEVEL version is in force on the date | No timer; the case is listed on the exception queue | MSG-P3-026 | AC4 |
| X2 | No legal period for the product | Prescription date not set; the case is listed on the exception queue | MSG-P3-026 | AC5 |
| X3 | An account has no last payment date | The contract date is used | None | AC6 |
| X4 | JOB-05 did not run for 40 minutes | The next run raises every missed warning and breach once | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The timer check runs again after a breach | The breach is not raised twice | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Decision log write fails at a breach | The timer stays RUNNING and the breach is raised by the next run | MSG-P7-003 | AC9 |
| X7 | A deviation is raised on the case | Service level timer paused; prescription timer keeps running | MSG-P3-004 | AC10 |
| X8 | The warning point is 4 of 5 working days | Warning sent once, at the first check after 4 working days have passed | MSG-P3-003 | AC11 |
| X9 | A role without Case record R reads the timers | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-028-12 |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A SERVICE_LEVEL timer starts each time the case enters a queue or a status, from the SERVICE_LEVEL row for its product group and status | SERVICE_LEVEL table (RWB-E1-045); DL22; VR-P3-011-1 |
| BR2 | The warning is raised at the warning percentage of the service level | SERVICE_LEVEL warning percent, 80 assumed (DL22) |
| BR3 | A breach is raised to the named escalation role. The case does not move | R-UNI-30; REQ-CWC-011; FEAT-CWC-13 |
| BR4 | The prescription date is the earliest of last payment date plus the legal period over the linked accounts; the contract date applies when no payment exists | LEGAL_PERIOD table (RWB-E1-043); REQ-CWC-012 |
| BR5 | The prescription timer never pauses | R-DEV-01; FEAT-DVH-03; Timer.paused description in api.yaml |
| BR6 | A deviation pauses the stage clock; clearing it resumes the clock and recomputes the timers | R-UNI-04, R-UNI-43 |
| BR7 | A legal hold keeps the clocks running and visible | R-UNI-20 |
| BR8 | Service levels count working days from the HOLIDAY table | HOLIDAY table (RWB-E1-043) |
| BR9 | Each timer start, warning and breach is logged with its rule and version | REQ-CWC-016; Principle 5 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the timer status (LOV-TIMER-STATUS):

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred, CaseStateChanged | Service level found | RUNNING |
| RUNNING | CaseTransferred or CaseStateChanged | New queue or status | STOPPED |
| RUNNING | DeviationRaised | Timer type SERVICE_LEVEL | PAUSED |
| PAUSED | DeviationCleared | None | RUNNING, expires_at recomputed |
| RUNNING | JOB-05 | expires_at passed | EXPIRED, TimerBreached or TimerDue |

### 12. Contract

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz schedule |
| Job name | JOB-05 Timer check |
| Schedule | Every 5 minutes |
| Input | RUNNING timers with warn_at or expires_at before now (index ix_timer_due) |
| Output | Warnings, breaches, expired timers, decision log entries |
| Events published | TimerBreached (EV-19: timerId, caseId, escalateTo); TimerDue (EV-18: timerId, caseId, timerType) |
| Idempotency key | timerId and the point (WARN or EXPIRE); a timer already EXPIRED or already warned is skipped |
| Restart | The next run picks up every missed timer (batch.txt JOB-05) |

**Events consumed.** CaseCreated (EV-01), CaseAllocated (EV-02), CaseTransferred (EV-04), CaseStateChanged (EV-05), DeviationRaised (EV-06), DeviationCleared (EV-07).

**GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path caseId (uuid) |
| Response | Timer[]: id, caseId, timerType, startedAt, expiresAt, warnAt, paused, status, escalationLevel |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002); 404 not found or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 503 |
| Authorization | Case record, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId} returns prescriptionDate (Case schema).

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery/casewf/timers`, Java package `recovery.casewf.timers`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TimerStarter | Listener | Starts and stops SERVICE_LEVEL timers on case events |
| PrescriptionService | Listener | Sets the prescription date and the PRESCRIPTION timer on CaseCreated |
| TimerPauseHandler | Listener | Pauses and resumes SERVICE_LEVEL timers on deviation events |
| TimerCheckJob | Job | JOB-05; warnings, breaches and expiries |
| WorkingDayCalculator | Service | Adds working days with the HOLIDAY table from the reference data service |
| TimerService | Published interface | Reads timers and the prescription date for other modules |
| CaseAndWorkflowController | Controller | GET /cases/{caseId}/timers |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | timer, recovery_case |

**Database**

- Writes timer (all columns), recovery_case.prescription_date, outbox.
- Reads with index ix_timer_due (expires_at WHERE status = 'RUNNING'); add `ix_timer_warn ON timer (warn_at) WHERE status = 'RUNNING'` in migration `V028_1__timer_warn_index.sql`, plus column timer.warned_at (New) to record the single warning.
- One running SERVICE_LEVEL timer per case: partial unique index `ux_timer_sl_running ON timer (case_id) WHERE timer_type = 'SERVICE_LEVEL' AND status IN ('RUNNING','PAUSED')`.

**Configuration and reference data**

- SERVICE_LEVEL rows (business lead, DL22) through ProductParameterService (RWB-E1-045).
- LEGAL_PERIOD and HOLIDAY rows through ReferenceDataService (RWB-E1-043); LEGAL_PERIOD owned by Legal.
- Parameter legal.prescription.warn.days = 180 (assumed; owner Legal) through RWB-E1-042.
- LOV-TIMER and LOV-TIMER-STATUS.

**Build steps**

1. WorkingDayCalculator with the HOLIDAY table; unit tests for AC1 and AC11.
2. TimerStarter with stop-and-start on each case event; test AC1, AC4.
3. PrescriptionService with the earliest-date rule and the contract date fallback; tests AC3, AC5, AC6.
4. TimerCheckJob warning branch with warned_at; test AC2 warning, AC11.
5. TimerCheckJob expiry branch: EXPIRED, TimerBreached in the outbox and the decision log write in one transaction; tests AC2, AC8, AC9.
6. Catch-up of missed runs in one pass ordered by expires_at; test AC7.
7. TimerPauseHandler with recomputed dates; test AC10.
8. GET /cases/{caseId}/timers with access check.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.timers`. Off: no timers start and JOB-05 does nothing.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and JOB-05 handles 26,500 open cases' timers inside one 5-minute cycle in SIT (NFR-001 volume).

## RWB-E1-029 Rule load, validation and rollback

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-029 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-14 Load a rule version with validation; FEAT-CWC-15 Roll back a rule version; FEAT-DRI-07 Run the rules component on versioned rule tables |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-013, REQ-CWC-014, REQ-DRI-004 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.7 |
| L3 process | 14 Set strategy, policy and decision rules; All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | None |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **an Excel template for the five rule tables, validation on load (schema, overlaps, unreachable rows, missing default, 50 test cases and a dry run), a load with a version, approval, rollback by one call and a change log**, so that **a rule change goes from template to production without a code release**.

### 2. Business rationale

Collection and recovery rules live in procedure documents today, and audit found the procedure not followed because the rules were not in the system (CTL-08). This story takes a rule version from one template through checks that refuse a bad table whole, an approval by Risk, a dated start and a one-call rollback, with each step in the change log. It meets REQ-CWC-013, REQ-CWC-014 and REQ-DRI-004, and covers the Epic 1 rule tables named in DL24: entry, exclusion, allocation, assignment and transfer.

### 3. Preconditions

- The five rule tables are agreed for Epic 1: ENTRY, EXCLUSION, ALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT and TRANSFER (DL24, option A).
- Each table has 50 test cases with expected results, prepared by RW-COE in the template's Tests tab (assumed count from the current story).
- The loader holds RW-COE (Rules and parameters C); the approver holds RW-RISK (Rules and parameters A). One person may not hold both (separation of duty).
- Live cases exist for the dry run (RWB-E1-018).

### 4. Flow

1. RW-COE: fills the Rules template (tabs Rows and Tests) for table ALLOCATION, version "ALLOC-2026.12", valid from 2026-12-15.
2. RW-COE: calls POST /admin/rule-versions with the file, route set UNIVERSAL_RULES and valid from.
3. RuleLoadValidator: runs the schema check (columns, types, lists), then overlap, unreachable rows and missing default.
4. RuleTestRunner: runs the 50 test cases against the new rows and compares each result with the expected queue or outcome.
5. RuleDryRun: evaluates the new rows against every open case and counts the cases whose result would change, by product and queue.
6. RuleVersionService: on any failed check, refuses the load whole and names every failed row or test case; on success stores the rows with status LOADED and writes the change log entry with author, time, check result and dry run counts.
7. RW-RISK: approves through POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve; refused if the approver is the author.
8. RuleVersionService: on the valid from date the version is in force; new decisions use it and open cases keep the version they were decided under (R-UNI-38).
9. RW-COE: if the version is wrong, calls POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/rollback; the previous version is in force again in one transaction and the change log records the rollback.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Two rows match the same case at the same row order | Load refused; both row IDs named | MSG-P3-027 | AC2 |
| X2 | A test case result differs from the expected result | Load refused; failing test case IDs named | MSG-P3-027 | AC3 |
| X3 | A required column is missing or a value is outside its list | Load refused; row and column named | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X4 | A row can never match because an earlier row covers it | Load refused; row named | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X5 | The allocation table has no default row | Load refused | MSG-P3-027 | AC7 |
| X6 | The approver is the author | Approval refused | MSG-P7-002 | AC8 |
| X7 | Rollback with no earlier version | Refused | MSG-P3-015 | AC9 |
| X8 | The same version label is loaded twice | Refused with 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC10 |
| X9 | Valid from before today | Refused with 422 | MSG-GEN-003 | AC11 |
| X10 | An empty file | Refused with 422 | MSG-GEN-001 | AC12 |
| X11 | A role without Rules and parameters C loads a file | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-029-13 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Works on the rule_row table and the change log; engines read the result through RuleTableReader |
| Negotiable | The checks are fixed; the tables, rows and test cases are data |
| Valuable | A rule change takes a load and an approval instead of a release |
| Estimable | One validator, one test runner, one dry run, three endpoints |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Rule load, validation and rollback

  Background:
    Given the loader U-41 holds RW-COE and the approver U-51 holds RW-RISK
    Given version "ALLOC-2026.11" of table ALLOCATION is in force with 24 rows

  Scenario: AC1 Valid load
    Given a template for table ALLOCATION version "ALLOC-2026.12" with 26 rows and 50 test cases that passes every check
    When U-41 loads it with valid from 2026-12-15 and U-51 approves it
    Then version "ALLOC-2026.12" is in force from 2026-12-15
    Then the change log records author U-41, approver U-51, the load and approval times, "50 of 50 test cases passed" and the dry run count

  Scenario: AC2 Overlap refused
    Given rows "ALLOC-031" and "ALLOC-032" both match product group "MORTGAGE" and region "BKK" at row order 12
    When validation runs
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 for the overlap check naming "ALLOC-031" and "ALLOC-032"
    Then version "ALLOC-2026.11" stays in force

  Scenario: AC3 Test cases
    Given the 50 test cases with expected queues
    Given test cases "TA-07" and "TA-19" expect queue "MTG-BKK-CO" and the new rows return "MTG-CEN-CO"
    When validation runs
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 for the test case check naming "TA-07" and "TA-19"

  Scenario: AC4 Rollback
    Given version 7, "ALLOC-2026.13", is in force and version 6, "ALLOC-2026.12", was in force before it
    When U-41 calls rollback once for version 7
    Then version 6 is in force
    Then the change log holds the rollback with U-41, the time and the reason
    Then a case allocated under version 7 keeps rule version "ALLOC-2026.13" on its decision log entry

  Scenario: AC5 Schema error
    Given row 9 has assignment reason "QUICK" that is not in its list
    When validation runs
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 for the schema check naming row 9 and its column

  Scenario: AC6 Unreachable row
    Given row "ALLOC-040" matches product group "SSME" in any region at row order 5
    Given row "ALLOC-041" matches product group "SSME" and region "NE3" at row order 6
    When validation runs
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 for the unreachable row check naming "ALLOC-041"

  Scenario: AC7 Missing default
    Given the allocation rows have no last row that matches every case
    When validation runs
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 for the default row check

  Scenario: AC8 Author cannot approve
    Given U-41 loaded version "ALLOC-2026.12"
    When U-41 calls approve
    Then the system refuses the call with MSG-P7-002
    Then the version stays LOADED

  Scenario: AC9 Rollback with no earlier version
    Given table TRANSFER has only version "TRF-2026.11"
    When rollback is called for "TRF-2026.11"
    Then the system refuses the call with MSG-P3-015
    Then "TRF-2026.11" stays in force

  Scenario: AC10 Same version loaded twice
    Given version "ALLOC-2026.12" is loaded
    When a file with version label "ALLOC-2026.12" is loaded again
    Then the system refuses the load with 409 and MSG-GEN-004

  Scenario: AC11 Valid from in the past
    When U-41 loads version "ALLOC-2026.14" with valid from 2026-11-01 on 2026-12-10
    Then the system refuses the load with 422 and MSG-GEN-003 for valid from

  Scenario: AC12 Empty file
    When U-41 loads a template with no rows
    Then the system refuses the load with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 for rows
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A version passes schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row and test case checks before it is stored | REQ-CWC-014; rules.txt Checks sheet |
| BR2 | A load with any failed check is refused in full | Reference data change process, step 3; CTL-08 |
| BR3 | Hit policy Unique: for one table, one trigger and one row order, one condition holds | rules.txt Key, hit policy Unique; ADR-004 |
| BR4 | The allocation table always has a default row | REQ-CWC-008 |
| BR5 | A version takes effect on its valid from date after approval; open cases keep the version they were decided under | R-UNI-38 |
| BR6 | The author cannot approve; Risk signs rule version changes | Separation of duty table; CTL-08 |
| BR7 | Rollback returns the previous version in one call | REQ-CWC-013; FEAT-CWC-15 |
| BR8 | Every load, approval and rollback is in the change log with author, approver, time and test result | REQ-CWC-013; FSD A2.14 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the status of a rule version: LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Load | Every check passes | LOADED |
| None | Load | Any check fails | REFUSED |
| LOADED | Approve | Approver is not the author | APPROVED |
| APPROVED | RULE_VERSION_EFFECTIVE (R-UNI-38) | Valid from reached | IN_FORCE; previous SUPERSEDED |
| IN_FORCE | Rollback | Earlier version exists | ROLLED_BACK; previous IN_FORCE |

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COE | Loads versions and calls rollback (Rules and parameters CRUD) |
| RW-RISK | Approves a version (Rules and parameters A); may not hold RW-COE |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads versions and the change log (Rules and parameters R) |
| RW-REFADM | Prepares load files; may not approve |
| SY-RULES | Reads the version in force for evaluation |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A rule version is not a credit decision |

### 12. Contract

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions** (P4 endpoint)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file (xlsx), routeSet = "UNIVERSAL_RULES", validFrom (date). The rule table and version label are columns in the file |
| Response | 201 RuleVersion[] for the stored rows (ruleId, ruleVersion, routeSet, fromState, eventCode, conditionExpr, actionText, toState, ownerRole, timerSpec, validFrom, validTo, approvedBy, testCaseId) |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Rules and parameters C (MSG-P4-002); 409 version label exists (MSG-GEN-004); 422 a check failed (MSG-P3-027, with the check, rows and test case IDs in Problem.detail), empty file (MSG-GEN-001), date order (MSG-GEN-003); 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right C |
| Idempotency | Version label; a repeat is refused with 409 |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Response | 200 RuleVersion |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Rules and parameters A; 404; 409 approver is the author (MSG-P7-002) or version not LOADED (MSG-GEN-004); 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right A |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query routeSet, status |
| Response | RuleVersion[] |
| Errors | 401; 403; 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right R |

**POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/rollback** (new endpoint, see additions)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Body { reason: string, required } |
| Response | 200 RuleVersion of the version now in force |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Rules and parameters U; 404; 409 no earlier version (MSG-P3-015) or version not IN_FORCE; 422 no reason (MSG-GEN-001); 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right U |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header |

**Published interfaces**

```java
// P3, package recovery.casewf.rules (published): validation and evaluation
public interface RuleLoadValidator {
    ValidationReport validate(String ruleTable, List<RuleRowDraft> rows, List<RuleTestCase> tests);
    DryRunReport dryRun(String ruleTable, List<RuleRowDraft> rows, LocalDate onDate);
}
// P4, package recovery.accessadmin.ruleversions (published): rule rows are P4 tables
public interface RuleTableReader {
    RuleTableVersion rowsInForce(String ruleTable, LocalDate onDate);
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Validation, test runner and dry run in `recovery/casewf/rules` (Java package `recovery.casewf.rules`). Endpoints and rule_row writes in the P4 package `recovery/accessadmin/ruleversions` (Java package `recovery.accessadmin.ruleversions`), which owns rule_row.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RuleTemplateParser | Service | Reads the Rows and Tests tabs; keeps row numbers |
| RuleLoadValidator | Published interface | Schema, overlap, unreachable row and default row checks |
| RuleTestRunner | Service | Runs each test case against the draft rows with the same evaluator the engines use |
| RuleDryRun | Service | Counts open cases whose result changes; reads case fields through the P3 repository |
| RuleVersionController | Controller | P4: list, load, approve, rollback endpoints |
| RuleVersionService | Service | P4: stores rows, approval check, effective date, rollback in one transaction, change log |
| RuleTableReader | Published interface | P4: version in force for a table and a date, cached per version |
| RuleEffectiveDateJob | Job | Daily at 00:01 sets APPROVED versions with today's valid from IN_FORCE |

**Database**

- Writes rule_row (all columns plus rule_table, row_order, target_queue_code) and rule_version, the version header with rule table, version label, status, author, approver, loaded and approved times, valid from, test result and dry run counts.
- Constraint uk_rule_row (rule_id, rule_version) exists; add `ix_rule_table_version ON rule_row (rule_table, rule_version) WHERE is_active` in P4 migration `V029_1__rule_table_columns.sql`, which also adds the three new columns and creates rule_version (unique (rule_table, version_label)).
- Rollback sets is_active false on the rolled back version and true on the previous one in one transaction.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The Rules template, owned by RW-COE.
- Lists used by the schema check through the P4 list interface (LOV-ASSIGN, LOV-ASSIGN-REASON, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-REGION, LOV-EXPOSURE).
- Parameter `rules.testcases.min` = 50 (assumed) through RWB-E1-042.

**Build steps**

1. RuleTemplateParser; unit tests with a valid and an empty file (AC1, AC12).
2. Schema check against the lists; test AC5.
3. Overlap and unreachable row checks on the condition columns; tests AC2, AC6.
4. Default row check for ALLOCATION; test AC7.
5. RuleTestRunner with the shared evaluator; test AC3.
6. RuleDryRun with counts by product and queue in the change log.
7. RuleVersionService: store, approve with author check, effective date job, rollback; tests AC1, AC4, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11.
8. Endpoints with access checks; access test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.ruleload`. Off: the load and rollback endpoints return 404; the version in force stays.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the five Epic 1 tables load, approve and roll back in SIT.

## RWB-E1-030 Daily rebalancing and queue measures

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-030 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-17 Rebalance queues daily; FEAT-CWC-18 Publish queue measures; FEAT-WKM-11 Reallocate when the caseload cap is breached; FEAT-RPT-02 Publish queue and ageing measures |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-015, REQ-RDF-012 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.1 and 5.3 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes; 15 Manage performance, data and AI |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-020, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-028 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **a daily job that assigns unassigned cases and moves the newest cases off owners above the cap by the assignment rules, and queue counts, ageing and service level breaches published to Power BI**, so that **queues stay balanced and every team manager sees the same numbers as the case list**.

### 2. Business rationale

Team managers rebalance work by hand today and count queues from spreadsheets that do not match. This story moves cases left in overflow or without an owner each morning, takes owners above the cap back inside it (R-UNI-19), and publishes depth, ageing, owner spread and breaches as one snapshot that reconciles to the case list. It meets REQ-CWC-015 and REQ-RDF-012.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-020 is done: AssignmentEngine and CapacityService answer for the queue version in force.
- RWB-E1-028 is done: timers are EXPIRED on a service level breach.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available.
- Caseload caps are loaded (DL23). If DL23 is late, rebalancing reports and moves nothing.
- JOB-03 has completed for the business date; JOB-06 runs as SY-CASEWF.
- JOB-15 Reporting extract copies the snapshot to the data lake for Power BI nightly (owner RW-BIANAL).

### 4. Flow

1. Quartz: starts JOB-06 at 06:30, or when JOB-03 completes for the business date if that is later.
2. RebalanceJob: lists cases in each queue with no owner and status NEW or ASSIGNED, and owners whose open cases exceed their capacity.
3. RebalanceService: for each owner above the cap, selects the newest cases by assignment time until the owner is inside the cap (R-UNI-19).
4. RebalanceService: skips cases with deviation_open or legal_hold true.
5. AssignmentEngine: picks an owner below the cap in the same queue for each selected or unassigned case.
6. RebalanceService: writes the decision log entry, ends the old assignment, writes the new one with reason REBALANCE and publishes CaseTransferred, case by case.
7. QueueMeasureService: at the end of the run, takes one snapshot per queue at one time: depth, unassigned, age in days from the entry date, owner spread and SERVICE_LEVEL timers EXPIRED.
8. QueueMeasureService: checks each queue depth against the case count for the same queue and time, and publishes the snapshot only when every queue matches.
9. JOB-15: copies the snapshot to the data lake; Power BI shows it from the next morning.
10. TimerBreachNotifier: on TimerBreached from JOB-05, sends the team manager MSG-P3-028 with the queue's breach count.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No member of the queue has capacity | Cases stay where they are; counted in the summary | MSG-P3-011 | AC4 |
| X2 | No caseload cap is loaded for the queue | The queue is reported and nothing is moved | None | AC5 |
| X3 | Decision log write fails for a case | That case is not moved; the run continues | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | JOB-06 runs again the same day | Already balanced queues give no further moves | None | AC7 |
| X5 | A case has an open deviation or a legal hold | Not moved | None | AC8 |
| X6 | The snapshot depth differs from the case count | Snapshot not published; break listed for the data steward | MSG-P3-029 | AC9 |
| X7 | An owner holds exactly the cap | No case is moved off them | None | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Platform administration U reruns JOB-06 | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-030-11 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reuses the assignment engine (RWB-E1-020) and the timers (RWB-E1-028) |
| Negotiable | Caps and the ordering of moves are data (DL23) |
| Valuable | Removes daily hand rebalancing and gives one set of queue numbers |
| Estimable | One job, one measure snapshot, one notifier |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Daily rebalancing and queue measures

  Background:
    Given queue "TDR-BKK-CO" uses "LOWEST_LOAD" with cap 150
    Given the business date is 2026-12-02

  Scenario: AC1 Rebalance
    Given queue "TDR-BKK-CO" has 12 cases with no owner
    Given members U-61 and U-62 hold 140 and 144 open cases
    When JOB-06 runs
    Then the system assigns the 12 cases , 8 to U-61 and 4 to U-62, by lowest load with ties going to the member first in the queue list
    Then each assignment has reason "REBALANCE" and a decision log entry

  Scenario: AC2 Measures reconcile
    Given the snapshot taken at 2026-12-02 06:52
    When the queue report refreshes
    Then the depth of each queue equals the case list count for that queue at 06:52
    Then queue "TDR-BKK-CO" shows depth 296, unassigned 0 and an average age of 41 days

  Scenario: AC3 Breach alert
    Given case RW-2026-000501 in queue "TDR-BKK-CO" passes its service level
    When the timer check raises the breach
    Then the team manager of "TDR-BKK" receives MSG-P3-028 with count 1 and queue "TDR-BKK-CO"
    Then the next snapshot shows 1 breach for "TDR-BKK-CO" in Power BI

  Scenario: AC4 No member has capacity
    Given every member of "TDR-BKK-CO" holds 150 open cases and 5 cases have no owner
    When JOB-06 runs
    Then the 5 cases keep no owner
    Then the team manager receives MSG-P3-011 with count 5

  Scenario: AC5 No cap loaded
    Given queue "WO-BKK-CO" has no capacity cap
    When JOB-06 runs
    Then the system moves no case in "WO-BKK-CO"
    Then the snapshot still reports "WO-BKK-CO"

  Scenario: AC6 Decision log unavailable for one case
    Given owner U-63 holds 153 open cases and the decision log write fails for the second of the 3 newest cases
    When JOB-06 runs
    Then the system moves 2 cases off U-63 and 1 stays
    Then the job record lists the case that stayed with MSG-P7-003

  Scenario: AC7 A repeated run
    Given JOB-06 has balanced "TDR-BKK-CO" on 2026-12-02
    When JOB-06 runs again on 2026-12-02
    Then the system moves no case
    Then the system writes no decision log entry

  Scenario: AC8 Held cases are not moved
    Given owner U-64 holds 152 open cases and the 2 newest have deviation_open = true
    When JOB-06 runs
    Then those 2 cases stay with U-64 and the next 2 newest are moved

  Scenario: AC9 A count difference holds the snapshot
    Given the snapshot depth for "DIL-BKK-CO" is 88 and the case count at the same time is 87
    When the snapshot is checked
    Then the system does not publish it
    Then the data steward receives MSG-P3-029 with check "queue depth against case list"

  Scenario: AC10 Owner exactly at the cap
    Given owner U-65 holds 150 open cases
    When JOB-06 runs
    Then the system moves no case off U-65
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Cases with no owner are assigned by the queue's method within the cap | queue.assignment_method, queue.capacity_cap; FEAT-CWC-17 |
| BR2 | An owner above the cap loses the newest cases until inside the cap | R-UNI-19 |
| BR3 | Cases with an open deviation or a legal hold are not moved | R-UNI-20; R-DEV-01 |
| BR4 | A queue with no cap is reported and not rebalanced | DL23 |
| BR5 | A move keeps the case status and the clocks | R-UNI-18 |
| BR6 | Measures publish only when queue depths reconcile to the case list with zero difference | DL25; REC-01 |
| BR7 | Every move is logged before it takes effect | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | A breach raises an alert to the escalation role; the case does not move | R-UNI-30 |

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the owner and the assignment of a case (reason REBALANCE), and the status of a measure snapshot (TAKEN, PUBLISHED, HELD).

### 12. Contract

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz at 06:30, after JOB-03 completes for the business date |
| Job name | JOB-06 Daily rebalancing |
| Schedule | Daily 06:30 |
| Input | Queues in force, members and capacity, open cases per owner, cases with no owner, EXPIRED service level timers |
| Output | Assignments with reason REBALANCE, decision log entries, one queue_measure snapshot per queue |
| Events published | CaseTransferred (EV-04) per move |
| Idempotency key | caseId and businessDate for a move; queueId and snapshot time for a snapshot |
| Restart | Rerun from the job monitor; balanced queues give no moves; managers rebalance by hand if the rerun fails (batch.txt) |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/cases** (used for the reconciliation test)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query queue (uuid), status, page, size |
| Response | CasePage: items, page, size, total |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002); 503 |
| Authorization | Case record, right R, scope applied |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun** (P1) for JOB-06: Platform administration U; 409 when the job is running.

**Published interface**

```java
// P3, package recovery.casewf.rebalance (published), read by P9 for Power BI
public interface QueueMeasureService {
    List<QueueMeasureView> latestPublished(LocalDate businessDate);
}
public record QueueMeasureView(String queueCode, String teamCode, OffsetDateTime asOf,
        int depth, int unassigned, BigDecimal avgAgeDays, int maxAgeDays,
        int ownerMin, int ownerMax, int breached) {}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery/casewf/rebalance`, Java package `recovery.casewf.rebalance`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RebalanceJob | Job | JOB-06; selects cases and owners, calls RebalanceService, writes counts |
| RebalanceService | Service | R-UNI-19 selection, hold checks, owner choice, decision log, assignment swap |
| QueueMeasureService | Published interface | Takes, reconciles and publishes the snapshot |
| TimerBreachNotifier | Listener | Sends MSG-P3-028 to the team manager on TimerBreached |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | recovery_case, assignment, queue, queue_member, timer, queue_measure |

**Database**

- Writes assignment, recovery_case.owner_user_id, queue_measure, outbox.
- Snapshot query in one REPEATABLE READ transaction so depth and the case count are read at the same time.
- Migration in this story: `V030_1__queue_measure.sql` creates queue_measure (id, queue_id, as_of, depth, unassigned, avg_age_days, max_age_days, owner_min, owner_max, breached, status, standard columns; unique (queue_id, as_of)).

**Configuration and reference data**

- Caps and member capacity from RWB-E1-019 (DL23).
- Measure definitions agreed with the Tribe (REQ-RDF-012), owned by RW-COE.

**Build steps**

1. Owner over cap selection by newest assignment; unit tests AC8, AC10.
2. RebalanceService with AssignmentEngine and hold checks; tests AC1, AC4, AC5.
3. One transaction per case with the decision log write as its last step; continue on failure; test AC6.
4. Idempotent rerun; test AC7.
5. QueueMeasureService snapshot and reconciliation; tests AC2, AC9.
6. TimerBreachNotifier; test AC3.
7. P9 hand-off through QueueMeasureService for JOB-15.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.rebalance`. Off: JOB-06 does not move cases; the snapshot still runs.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the Power BI queue page shows the 2026-12-02 snapshot on 2026-12-03 in SIT.

## RWB-E1-031 Queue and owner on the case list with filters

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-031 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-19 Show queue and owner on the case list |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-007, REQ-ACA-009 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3 and 3.4; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.4 |
| L3 process | 06 Take over and own the case |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-020, RWB-E1-039 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **the queue and owner columns on the case list, with filters by queue, team and status and an export to Excel**, so that **I see my queues and who owns each case without a new screen**.

### 2. Business rationale

Today a team manager asks each collector for their list to know who holds which case. With allocation by rule (RWB-E1-020), every case has a queue and an owner; this story shows both on the case list, filters by queue, team and status inside the manager's scope, and exports the filtered list with the export written to the access log for PDPA. It meets REQ-CWC-007 (the result of allocation is visible) and REQ-ACA-009 (a user sees only the cases their scope allows).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-020 is done: cases carry queue_id, team_code and owner_user_id.
- RWB-E1-039 is done: the access log interface records exports.
- The user holds a role with Case record R; the team manager's default scope is Team (roles.txt).
- Parameter `caselist.export.maxrows` = 10,000 (assumed; DL11) from RWB-E1-042.
- Owner display names come from the ACE user directory in the common module.

### 4. Flow

1. Team manager: opens SCR-02 Case list; the screen shows the Loading state.
2. CaseListPage: calls GET /cases with page 0 and size 50; the service applies the caller's scope.
3. CaseListPage: shows each row with case number, product, status, stage, queue, owner and entry date (list state).
4. Team manager: picks queue "DIL-BKK-CO", team "DIL-BKK" and status "ASSIGNED"; the page calls GET /cases with the filters (filtered state).
5. CaseQueryService: returns only cases inside the caller's scope that meet every filter, with the total.
6. Team manager: chooses Export.
7. CaseExportService: checks the row count against the limit, publishes the access event AC-EXPT with user, time, filters and row count, then builds the xlsx with masking by role (FieldMasker, RWB-E1-037).
8. Browser: downloads "Case list 20261202 1.xlsx".

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No case meets the filters | Empty state with a plain sentence | MSG-P3-020 | AC3 |
| X2 | The filtered list holds more rows than the export limit | Export refused; the user narrows the filter | MSG-P3-021 | AC4 |
| X3 | The access log cannot be written | Export not made | MSG-P7-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | A filter names a queue outside the caller's scope | Only in-scope cases return; an out-of-scope queue returns none | MSG-P3-020 | AC6 |
| X5 | A case has no owner | Owner cell is blank; the case is still listed | None | AC7 |
| X6 | Exactly 10,000 rows | Export allowed | None | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without Case record R opens the list | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-031-09 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads fields RWB-E1-020 fills; adds columns and filters to an existing screen |
| Negotiable | Column order and the export limit are configurable |
| Valuable | Team managers see ownership on one screen |
| Estimable | Two query parameters, one export endpoint, one screen change |
| Small | Fits under one week |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The list holds only cases inside the caller's scope (Own, Team, Region, All) | REQ-ACA-009; CTL-09; LOV-SCOPE |
| BR2 | Filters combine with AND | FSD A2.19 |
| BR3 | Every export is written to the access log before the file is made | REQ-ACA-006; CTL-11 |
| BR4 | Export columns follow the masking rules for the caller's role | REQ-ACA-005; DL26 |
| BR5 | An export holds at most the configured number of rows | Parameter caselist.export.maxrows = 10,000 (assumed; DL11) |
| BR6 | A screen responds in under 2 seconds | NFR-008 |

## RWB-E1-032 Automatic attach from the OCR intake

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-032 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-12 Attach an OCR-read document to its case automatically |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-007 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-050, RWB-E1-053 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **documents from the OCR intake attached to their case automatically when the case ID or the account number is read, with unmatched or ambiguous documents held for a person who sees the OCR text and the candidate cases and attaches the document**, so that **no document is filed by hand when the case is clear and none is filed on the wrong case when it is not**.

### 2. Business rationale

Scans, partner files and emails arrive without a case link; today a person reads each one and files it. This story matches each classified intake item to one open case by the case ID or the account number in its text and stores it on that case with no person involved (FSD P5 A2.12). An item that matches no case, more than one case, a closed case or no agreed type is held as unmatched, and a person attaches it from the review queue with the OCR text and the candidates in front of them. It meets REQ-DCM-007 and writes the document attached record required from Epic 1 (REQ-DRI-004, RWB-E1-027). The measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.12.1).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-024 is done: DocumentStore stores a document and writes the DOCATT decision log entry.
- RWB-E1-050 is done: intake items carry predicted_type, classification_confidence, type_candidates, classifier_version and review_reason.
- RWB-E1-053 is done: the extracted fields case_no and account_no are available for an item where they were read.
- Parameters loaded in document_hub_parameter: CASE_NO_PATTERN = "RW-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{6}", ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN = "[0-9]{10}" (assumed; DL21) and CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD = 0.80.
- The P3 published interface CaseDirectory returns a case by case number and the open cases for an account number.
- A person resolving unmatched items holds Documents C; items with no candidate are visible only to roles with scope ALL.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.autoattach is on.

### 4. Flow

1. JOB-12 Document intake: runs matchStep after the extraction step.
2. MatchStep: selects intake items with ocr_status DONE, match_status PENDING, no document_id and a predicted type (review_reason empty or LOW_CONFIDENCE), locking each row; items with review_reason UNKNOWN_TYPE or MODEL_UNAVAILABLE get match_status NO_TYPE and are held for a person.
3. CaseMatcher: collects case numbers from the extracted field case_no and from the OCR text with CASE_NO_PATTERN, and account numbers from the extracted field account_no and the text with ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN.
4. CaseMatcher: resolves each case number with CaseDirectory.findByCaseNo and each account number with CaseDirectory.findOpenCasesByAccountNo, and returns one of MATCHED, NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT or CASE_CLOSED with the candidates.
5. MatchStep: for MATCHED, calls DocumentStore.store with the case ID, predicted_type, the intake source, the file, its hash and the extracted fields; the store writes the DOCATT entry with the classifier version, the confidence and the match method, the document row and DocumentStored.
6. MatchStep: on the stored document sets classification_confidence, document_type and type_candidates; for review_reason LOW_CONFIDENCE sets review_status PENDING and write_once false, so it is held in rwb-docs and listed on SCR-31 (RWB-E1-054).
7. MatchStep: sets the intake item match_status MATCHED, case_id and document_id; for any other result sets match_status to the result and candidate_case_ids, and the item is held for a person.
8. Reviewer: opens the Unmatched list on SCR-31 (GET /intake-items), opens an item to see the scan, the OCR text and the candidates, picks the case and the type, and attaches it (POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/attach).
9. ManualAttachService: checks the case is in the reviewer's scope and the type is in force, calls DocumentStore.store with the reviewer as approver on the DOCATT entry, and sets the item match_status MATCHED.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No readable case ID or account number | Item held, match_status NO_MATCH, OCR text held for the reviewer | MSG-P5-003 | AC2 |
| X2 | The account number matches two or more open cases | Item held, match_status MULTIPLE, every candidate offered | MSG-P5-003 | AC3 |
| X3 | The case ID and the account point to different cases | Item held, match_status CONFLICT, both cases offered | MSG-P5-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | A case ID is read that does not exist | No candidate; NO_MATCH | MSG-P5-003 | AC6 |
| X5 | The only candidate case is closed | Item held, match_status CASE_CLOSED | MSG-P5-003 | AC7 |
| X6 | The same file is already on the matched case | The item is linked to the existing document; no second document | None | AC8 |
| X7 | The job runs again over attached items | No second attach, entry or event | None | AC9 |
| X8 | Classification confidence below the threshold and one case matched | Stored with review_status PENDING and write_once false | MSG-P5-003 | AC10 |
| X9 | No agreed type from classification | Item held, match_status NO_TYPE | MSG-P5-003 | AC11 |
| X10 | The reviewer picks a case outside their scope | Refused with 403; item stays held | MSG-P4-003 | AC13 |
| X11 | The reviewer picks a type not in force | Refused with 422 | MSG-P5-006 | AC14 |
| X12 | Two reviewers attach the same item at the same time | The first succeeds; the second gets 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC15 |
| X13 | The decision log write fails during an attach | Nothing stored; an automatic attach stays PENDING for the next run; a manual attach returns 503; incident raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-032-17 (Principle 5) |
| X14 | A role without Documents C attaches an item | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-032-16 (Access) |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store (RWB-E1-024), classification (RWB-E1-050) and extraction (RWB-E1-053), all earlier in Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | The patterns are data; the match outcomes and the reviewer action are fixed by the story |
| Valuable | Ends hand filing for every scan that names its case or account, and gives every other scan one place to be filed |
| Estimable | One job step, one matcher, four endpoints, one list tab |
| Small | Fits within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |


### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A classified document attaches to its case without a person when exactly one open case is found | REQ-DCM-007; FEAT-DCM-12 |
| BR2 | The case is found by the case ID or the account number read from the document; the account number is the join to other systems | DL21; parameters CASE_NO_PATTERN and ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN in document_hub_parameter (New) |
| BR3 | No match, more than one candidate, disagreement, a closed case or no agreed type goes to a person | REQ-DCM-005; FSD P5 A2.12.4 |
| BR4 | A document classified below the threshold is stored for review in the standard container, not write-once, until a person confirms its type | Parameter CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD in document_hub_parameter (New); RWB-E1-054; CTL-12 |
| BR5 | Each attach is written to the decision log with the classifier version, the confidence and the person where one decided, before the document is stored | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; REQ-DRI-004 |
| BR6 | An item attached once is not attached again | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | A reviewer attaches only to a case in their scope | CTL-09 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the intake item match_status: PENDING to MATCHED on an automatic attach; PENDING to NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED or NO_TYPE when held for a person; a held value to MATCHED when a reviewer attaches it. It creates a document record (COPY_PENDING, then STORED, in RWB-E1-024).

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Matches and attaches automatically (Documents C) |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Writes the DOCATT entry |
| Roles with Documents C and the candidate case in scope (for example RW-LITOFF, RW-CASEOWN) | See and attach unmatched items that name a candidate in their scope |
| Roles with Documents C and scope ALL (for example RW-LEGAL) | See and attach unmatched items with no candidate |
| Roles with Documents R only (for example RW-TEAMMGR) | See attached documents on cases in their scope; no attach |

### 12. Contract

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | JOB-12 Document intake, step matchStep after the extraction step |
| Job name | JOB-12 Document intake |
| Schedule | Every 15 minutes in business hours |
| Input | Intake items with ocr_status DONE, match_status PENDING, no document_id and a predicted type |
| Output | Documents stored on their case; held items with match status and candidates; counts on the job record |
| Events published | DocumentStored (EV-16), through DocumentStore |
| Idempotency key | Intake item ID, and in the store the case, type and file hash |
| Restart behavior | Items left PENDING are matched in the next run; an attach that failed on the decision log stays PENDING |

**GET /review-items** (new, see additions)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query matchStatus (default the held values NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED and NO_TYPE), page, size (default 50) |
| Response | 200 IntakeItemPage: items [id, source, receivedAt, matchStatus, predictedType, classificationConfidence, typeCandidates, candidateCases (caseId, caseNo), version], page, size, total; oldest first; only items whose candidates are in scope, and items with no candidate for scope ALL |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Documents R (MSG-P4-002); 503 |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}** and **GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content** (new, see additions)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path intakeItemId |
| Response | 200 IntakeItem with pages [pageNo, text] (personal identifiers masked by role); content returns the file |
| Errors | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003); 404; 503 |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied; each read written to the PII access log |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve** (new, see additions)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | IntakeAttachRequest: caseId (uuid, required), documentType (required), version (integer, required) |
| Response | 201 Document |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Documents C (MSG-P4-002) or case out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 404; 409 item no longer held or version changed (MSG-GEN-004); 422 type not in force (MSG-P5-006) or missing field (MSG-GEN-001); 503 decision log write failed (MSG-P7-003) |
| Authorization | Documents, right C, scope applied to the chosen case |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the first result |

**Published interfaces called**

```java
// P3
Optional<CaseSummary> findByCaseNo(String caseNo);                 // id, caseNo, status, ownerUserId
List<CaseSummary> findOpenCasesByAccountNo(String accountNo);
// P5, RWB-E1-024
StoredDocument store(StoreRequest request);                         // request carries approverUserId for a manual attach
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dochub/attach`, Java package `recovery.dochub.attach`; front end folder `recovery/documents`.

**Components.**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| MatchStep | Job | Step of JOB-12: select, match, store or hold for a person |
| CaseMatcher | Service | Reads case numbers and account numbers; resolves them through CaseDirectory; returns the result and candidates |
| MatchPatterns | Rule table | Reads the two pattern parameters from document_hub_parameter |
| AutoAttachService | Service | Builds the StoreRequest with the classification inputs; applies the review rule of BR4; updates the intake item |
| ManualAttachService | Service | Scope and type checks, optimistic lock on the item, store with the approver |
| IntakeItemController | Controller | The four intake item endpoints |
| IntakeItemRepository | Repository | Reads and writes document_intake only (table from RWB-E1-049) |
| UnmatchedIntakeTab | React component | Unmatched list on SCR-31 with the scan viewer, OCR text, candidates, case picker and type picker |

**Database.**
- Flyway migration `V1_5_032__intake_match.sql` adds to document_intake: match_status varchar(12) default 'PENDING', candidate_case_ids jsonb. The document columns document_type and type_candidates come from the RWB-E1-050 migration.
- Index ix_intake_held on document_intake (match_status, received_at) where match_status not in ('PENDING', 'MATCHED').

**Configuration and reference data.**
- Parameters CASE_NO_PATTERN, ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN and CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD in document_hub_parameter, loaded by the reference data administrator.
- No rule row; the match outcomes are the story's fixed behavior.

**Build steps.**
1. Write the migration; test the columns and the index.
2. Build MatchPatterns and the text scan; unit test pattern reads on synthetic text with Thai and English around the numbers.
3. Build CaseMatcher with the five outcomes against a CaseDirectory stub; unit test AC2 to AC7.
4. Build AutoAttachService with the store call, the review rule and the item update; integration test AC1, AC4, AC8, AC10 and AC11.
5. Build MatchStep selection and skip rules; test AC9.
6. Build IntakeItemController and ManualAttachService; API tests AC12 to AC15 and the access test.
7. Build UnmatchedIntakeTab; component tests for list, detail and attach.
8. Test the decision log failure path for the automatic and the manual attach.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.dochub.autoattach`. Off: matchStep sets every classified item to match_status NO_MATCH, and reviewers attach them by hand.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and, on the 180 synthetic samples in SIT, every item with one readable case ID and a confidence at or above 0.80 is attached in the same run.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the case number and account number patterns and the threshold are parameters.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: account numbers and OCR text are never logged; logs carry the intake ID and the outcome; test accounts are synthetic.
- No read of another module's tables: cases and accounts are resolved through CaseDirectory.
- The matcher never picks one of several candidates; any doubt goes to a person.
- A document stored for type review is never put in the write-once container before its type is confirmed (RWB-E1-054).

### 19. Out of scope

- Source pickup from scanners, SFTP and mailboxes, and the intake item base record (RWB-E1-057).
- Moving an attached document to another case (Epic 2).
- Attach of field app photos (RWB-E2-024).
