### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every sign-in, refusal, read of the case store or the document store, and export writes one access event to the decision log | REQ-ACA-006; NFR-042; FEAT-ACA-08 |
| BR2 | A read or export whose access event cannot be written returns no data | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR3 | An access event lists field IDs and their masking position, never field values | NFR-040; guardrail on personal data |
| BR4 | Break-glass needs a grant approved by the security administrator in the bank IAM, an open incident reference and a reason of at least 20 characters | Admin and access model, section 5.3; Access flow sheet, roles.txt; REQ-ACA-008 |
| BR5 | A grant ends at the earlier of the window (4 hours, assumed) and the IAM group end, with no action by anyone | rwb.access.breakglass.window-hours; DL38 |
| BR6 | Every action under break-glass is marked with the grant and the incident reference | Admin and access model, section 5.3 |
| BR7 | The security administrator reviews each use inside the review window (one working day, assumed); an unreviewed use goes to the head of SCB IT security and to Compliance | DL38; Access flow sheet, roles.txt |
| BR8 | A platform administrator holds only the letters of RW-PLATADM in the matrix version in force; any right beyond them comes only from an active break-glass grant | Admin and access model, section 3.2; permission matrix |
| BR9 | A person may not review their own break-glass use | Admin and access model, section 6.2 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. A break-glass grant moves from Active to Ended at its end time.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Requests break-glass in the bank IAM and activates an approved grant with POST /admin/break-glass (Platform administration C) |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Approves break-glass in the bank IAM and reviews each use; reads the access log (Platform administration R) |
| RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer | Reads the access log; receives unreviewed uses |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads the access log and queries access to a case through the decision log; changes nothing |
| RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW | Read the access log (Platform administration R) |
| Every bank role | Generates access events by signing in, reading and exporting |
| SY-DECLOG Decision log writer | Writes the access events (Decision log C) |
| Head of SCB IT security | Receives a break-glass use not reviewed inside the window |

### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | all fields | Write (one entry per access event) |
| DF-DEC-002 | decision_log_entry | case_id | Write; empty for sign-in, refusal, export and break-glass events (change recorded in the additions file) |
| DF-DEC-030 | decision_log_entry | actor_user_id | Write, read |
| DF-DEC-003 | decision_log_entry | decision_code | Read (query by access event code) |
| DF-DEC-014 | decision_log_entry | actions | Read (area, right, fields, filter, row count, grant, incident) |
| DF-DEC-016 | decision_log_entry | decided_at | Read |
| DF-REF-035 | role | role_code | Read |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**POST /admin/break-glass-grants** (new, recorded in the additions file)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | BreakGlassActivation: incidentReference, iamRequestId, capabilityArea (LOV-CAPABILITY), right (one of C, R, U), scope (LOV-SCOPE), reason (20 to 1000 characters) |
| Response | 201 BreakGlassGrant: grantId (the AC-BGON entry ID), incidentReference, capabilityArea, right, scope, startsAt, endsAt |
| Errors | 401 no session; 403 caller not RW-PLATADM or not in the break-glass group (MSG-P4-007); 409 a grant is already active (MSG-GEN-004); 422 field missing or invalid (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002); 503 entry could not be written (MSG-P7-003) |
| Authorization | Platform administration, right C, plus membership of the break-glass group |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/access-log** (API-P4-008)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query: user, from, to, event (an access event code), page, size (1 to 500) |
| Response | AccessLogPage of AccessLogEntry: at (decided_at), user (actor), event (decision_code), capability (actions.area), result (final_call) |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Platform administration R (MSG-P4-002); 422 from after to (MSG-GEN-003) or size outside 1 to 500 (MSG-GEN-002); 503 (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Platform administration, right R |
| Idempotency | Not applicable, read only |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/decision-log** (API-P7-006), used for "who read this case": Query caseId, decision "AC-READ", from, to, page, size; response DecisionLogPage; Decision log, right R, scope applied; errors 401, 403, 503.

**Published interface AccessEventPublisher** (package recovery.access.accesslog), extended from RWB-E1-022:

```java
void publish(AccessEvent event) throws DecisionLogUnavailableException;
// AccessEvent: eventCode (AC-SIGN|AC-DENY|AC-READ|AC-EXPT|AC-BGON), actorUserRef, caseId (nullable), area, right,
//   result, fieldIds with masked flag, filter, rowCount, documentId, reasonCode
```

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/access/accesslog` in the recovery module; Java package `recovery.access.accesslog`.
- Components:

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AccessAndAdministrationController | Controller | POST /admin/break-glass and GET /admin/access-log |
| AccessLogWriter | Service | Turns an AccessEvent into a DecisionLogRecord and calls the P7 DecisionLogWriter in the caller's transaction |
| AccessEventPublisher | Published interface | Called by P3 and P5 on every read and export; now writes through AccessLogWriter as well as the ACE audit and SOC log |
| BreakGlassService | Service | Checks the group, the incident pattern and the reason; writes AC-BGON; holds the grant on the session |
| BreakGlassGrantCheck | Service | Adds the grant's right in its area and scope to AccessCheck until endsAt; marks entries with grant and incident |
| AccessLogQueryService | Service | Maps GET /admin/access-log to the P7 DecisionLogReader interface |
| BreakGlassBanner | React component | Shows MSG-P4-004 with the end time from GET /me/session |

- Database: no table of its own; writes decision_log_entry only through the P7 writer. Index ix_declog_actor_time on decision_log_entry (actor_user_id, decided_at) is created by RWB-E1-008.
- Configuration and reference data: access event codes in LOV-DECISION (RW-DATASTEW); break-glass parameters above (values DL38); break-glass group name (DL40).
- Build steps:
  1. Build AccessLogWriter and extend AccessEventPublisher; tests for AC1, AC3, AC9.
  2. Add the publish call to the P3 case read and list export and to the P5 document content read, through the published interface; tests for AC1, AC3, AC4.
  3. Make the read fail closed when the write fails; test for AC7.
  4. Build BreakGlassService and the endpoint with validation and idempotency; tests for AC5, AC6, AC10.
  5. Build BreakGlassGrantCheck with the end time from the session; test AC2 with a clock fixed at 10:30 and moved to 14:31.
  6. Build AccessLogQueryService and the access log endpoint; test for AC8 with the decision log query.
  7. Add the session breakGlass fields to GET /me/session and the BreakGlassBanner.
- Feature flag: `rwb.access.access-log`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass and the break-glass test of the access test set (one request with an open incident, one without) passes in SIT and is signed by the security administrator.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-004 | Break-glass access is active | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. |
| MSG-P4-007 | Break-glass requested with no approved IAM grant (new) | Emergency access needs an approved break-glass request in the bank IAM with an open incident. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action after the grant has ended, or an access log query without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Incident reference empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Reason shorter than 20 characters, or page size outside 1 to 500 | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Query from date after to date | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A second activation while a grant is active | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The access event cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

Thai text for each message follows DL10; proposed Thai for MSG-P4-007 is in the additions file.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The ACE front end shell shows the MSG-P4-004 banner while a grant is active. The access log is read through GET /admin/access-log until SCR-43 Roles and access in Epic 8, and access to a case through SCR-38 Decision log query from Epic 2 (RWB-E2-005).

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the window, the incident pattern, the reason length and the review window are parameters.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. Access events carry field IDs and the masking position, never values; the reason text is free text written by the administrator and must not hold customer data.
- No read of another module's tables; the access log is read through the P7 published interface.
- No right beyond the letters of RW-PLATADM without an active grant.
- The grant end is enforced on every request, not by a job.

## RWB-E1-040 Document checklist per case type as reference data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-040 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-16 Hold the document checklist per case type as reference data |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | D7.2 |
| Priority | Should |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-043, RWB-E1-025, RWB-E1-026 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **the required documents per case type and route held as a versioned reference table that the case documents screen, the case list and the review queue read**, so that **a missing document shows on the case without a person checking a list**.

### 2. Business rationale

Litigation packs and guarantee claims fail when a required document is missing, and today the gap is found by a person reading a paper list, often at filing (CTL-19, R-LIT-17). This story holds the checklist per case stage and route as data and keeps a completeness flag per case, recomputed whenever a document is stored or the case changes stage. It meets REQ-DCM-011 and gives the pack checks of Epic 4 and Epic 5 (R-LIT-16, R-GUA-07) one checklist source. The measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.16.1).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-024 and RWB-E1-026 are done: documents are stored and GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist returns the placeholder.
- RWB-E1-025 is done: the six document types are in force.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: the reference data service serves versioned tables with valid from and valid to.
- Checklist version CHK-2026.11 loaded and approved, assumed until the bank list is signed (DL19): stage LITIGATION requires DEMAND_LETTER, COURT_NOTICE, TITLE_DEED and APPRAISAL_REPORT; stage DEED_IN_LIEU requires TITLE_DEED, APPRAISAL_REPORT and SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT.
- The P3 published interface CaseDirectory returns stage_code, route_code and owner of a case; CaseStateChanged (EV-05) is published by P3.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.checklist is on.

### 4. Flow

1. Reference data administrator: loads the checklist file with POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads, table DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST; the owner approves it.
2. ChecklistLoader: validates every row: stage in LOV-STAGE, route in LOV-ROUTE or empty, document type in the type table in force, no duplicate row; refuses the load whole on any error.
3. ChecklistEvaluator: on DocumentStored (EV-16), on CaseStateChanged (EV-05) and when a checklist version takes effect, takes the case's stage and route through CaseDirectory.
4. ChecklistEvaluator: picks the rows of the version in force for that stage, using the rows for the route where they exist and the rows with no route otherwise.
5. ChecklistEvaluator: counts the active documents of each required type on the case and writes case_document_check: checklist version, required count, present count, missing types and complete.
6. Litigation officer: opens the Documents tab (SCR-30); GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist returns each required item marked present or missing.
7. Case owner: sees the number of missing documents for each case on the case list (SCR-02) through DocumentChecklistService.missingCounts.
8. JOB-12 Document intake: the step checklistRefreshStep finds checklist versions whose valid from date has been reached since the last run and recomputes the cases of the stages they change.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case stage has no checklist rows | The checklist shows "No checklist for this case type"; complete is empty | None | AC6 |
| X2 | A checklist load names a document type not in the type table, or a stage not in LOV-STAGE | Load refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC7 |
| X3 | The same DocumentStored event arrives twice | One recompute result; the second is ignored and counted | None | AC8 |
| X4 | A document type is present only as an inactive earlier version | Counted once, through its active version | None | AC9 |
| X5 | A role without Documents R opens the checklist | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-040-10 (Access) |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store, the types and the placeholder endpoint, all earlier in Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | The items per stage and route are data under DL19; the story fixes how they are applied |
| Valuable | Missing documents show on the case and the case list before a pack is built |
| Estimable | One table, one loader, one evaluator, one stored flag |
| Small | Fits within one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Document checklist per case type as reference data

  Background:
    Given checklist version "CHK-2026.11" is in force
    Given stage "LITIGATION" requires DEMAND_LETTER, COURT_NOTICE, TITLE_DEED and APPRAISAL_REPORT
    Given stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" requires TITLE_DEED, APPRAISAL_REPORT and SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT

  Scenario: AC1 Checklist by type
    Given case "RW-2026-000123" at stage "LITIGATION" holds a demand letter and a court notice
    When the litigation officer opens the Documents tab
    Then the checklist shows the 4 items from version "CHK-2026.11" for "LITIGATION"
    Then DEMAND_LETTER and COURT_NOTICE are marked present
    Then TITLE_DEED and APPRAISAL_REPORT are marked missing

  Scenario: AC2 Change as data
    Given version "CHK-2026.12" adds GUARANTOR_NOTICE for "DEED_IN_LIEU" and is approved with valid from 1 December 2026
    When case "RW-2026-000456" at stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" is opened on 1 December 2026
    Then the checklist shows 4 items including GUARANTOR_NOTICE
    Then no code was deployed between 30 November and 1 December 2026

  Scenario: AC3 Completeness flag
    Given case "RW-2026-000456" at stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" holds a title deed and an appraisal report
    When the pack check runs after the appraisal report is stored
    Then case_document_check for the case has complete false, missing count 1 and missing type SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT
    Then the case owner sees "1 missing" for the case on the case list

  Scenario: AC4 The missing document arrives
    Given the case from AC3 with SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT missing
    When a settlement agreement is stored on the case
    Then case_document_check has complete true and missing count 0
    Then the case list shows no missing documents for the case

  Scenario: AC5 Stage change
    Given case "RW-2026-000789" at stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" with complete true
    When CaseStateChanged moves it to stage "LITIGATION"
    Then the pack check uses the "LITIGATION" rows
    Then case_document_check has complete false with the missing litigation types

  Scenario: AC6 No checklist for the stage
    Given case "RW-2026-000321" at stage "DEBT_SALE" and no rows for "DEBT_SALE"
    When the Documents tab opens
    Then the checklist shows "No checklist for this case type"
    Then case_document_check has complete empty and missing count 0

  Scenario: AC7 Load with an unknown type
    Given a load file for table "DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST" with a row for stage "LITIGATION" and type "POWER_OF_ATTORNEY"
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P3-027 naming the row and "document type not in the type table"
    Then version "CHK-2026.11" stays in force

  Scenario: AC8 The same event twice
    Given DocumentStored for one document on case "RW-2026-000123" is delivered twice with the same event ID
    When the evaluator handles both
    Then the system writes case_document_check once for that event
    Then the system counts the second delivery as a repeat

  Scenario: AC9 Earlier version of a document
    Given case "RW-2026-000123" holds an appraisal report at version 2 with version 1 inactive
    When the pack check runs
    Then APPRAISAL_REPORT counts as present once
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The checklist per case type is held as reference data so a missing document is visible | REQ-DCM-011; FEAT-DCM-16 |
| BR2 | The case type is the case stage, with route rows taking precedence over rows with no route | LOV-STAGE; LOV-ROUTE; checklist table (New) |
| BR3 | A checklist version takes effect on its valid from date, without a deployment | refdata.txt change process; R-UNI-38; DT02 |
| BR4 | Only active documents count, once per type | FEAT-DCM-20 |
| BR5 | The completeness flag is recomputed on every document stored and every stage change | EV-16; EV-05 |
| BR6 | A repeated event changes nothing | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | The checklist is the source the pack checks read in later epics | R-LIT-16, R-LIT-17, R-GUA-07, R-GUA-08 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It writes the completeness flag of the case in case_document_check: complete false while a required type is missing, true when every required type is present, empty when the stage has no checklist.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the checklist (Reference data C) |
| Approver with Reference data A | Approves the load; no role holds Reference data A in the permission matrix today; assumed granted to the legal counsel as co-owner of the checklist (DL01) |
| RW-LITOFF, RW-CASEOWN and roles with Documents R | Read the checklist and the flag for cases in their scope |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Agrees the items per stage (DL19) |
| SY-CASEWF | Publishes CaseStateChanged that triggers the recompute |

### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 | recovery_case | id | Read, through CaseDirectory |
| DF-CAS-006 | recovery_case | stage_code | Read, through CaseDirectory |
| DF-CAS-008 | recovery_case | route_code | Read, through CaseDirectory |
| DF-CAS-009 | recovery_case | owner_user_id | Read, through CaseDirectory |
| DF-DOC-002 | document | case_id | Read |
| DF-DOC-004 | document | document_type | Read |
| Standard column | document | is_active | Read |
| DF-REF-234 to DF-REF-243 | document_checklist_item | all fields | Write (this story creates the record) |
| DF-DOC-036 to DF-DOC-044 | case_document_check | all fields | Write (this story creates the record) |
| DF-REF-219 | document_type | doc_type_code | Read |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist** (new, see additions; this story fills the required items)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path caseId |
| Response | 200 DocumentChecklist: caseId, checklistVersion, stageCode, items [documentType, label, required, presentCount], missingCount, complete |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Documents R (MSG-P4-002) or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 404; 503 |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads** (table DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file, table = "DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST", validFrom |
| Response | 201 ReferenceLoad |
| Errors | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002); 409 version already loaded (MSG-P3-027); 422 row errors (MSG-P3-027); 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right C; approval with right A |
| Idempotency | Table code and table version |

**Listener**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Events consumed | DocumentStored (EV-16); CaseStateChanged (EV-05) |
| Idempotency key | Event ID; a repeat is ignored and counted (R-UNI-40) |
| Restart behavior | A failed handling retries; after the retry limit the event goes to the exception queue with the platform administrator as owner |

**Published interface (P5, used by the P3 case list and by RWB-E1-054)**

```java
public interface DocumentChecklistService {
    CaseChecklist forCase(UUID caseId, LocalDate businessDate);
    Map<UUID, Integer> missingCounts(Collection<UUID> caseIds);   // at most 500 IDs per call
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dochub/checklist`, Java package `recovery.dochub.checklist`; front end folder `recovery/documents`.

**Components.**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ChecklistLoader | Service | Implements ReferenceTableLoader for DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST |
| ChecklistEvaluator | Service | Picks the rows for the stage and route; counts documents; writes case_document_check |
| DocumentStoredChecklistListener, CaseStateChangedChecklistListener | Listener | Call the evaluator; keep the event ID for repeats |
| ChecklistRefreshStep | Job | Step of JOB-12 that recomputes cases when a version takes effect |
| DocumentChecklistService | Published interface | Section 12 |
| ChecklistRepository, CaseDocumentCheckRepository | Repository | Read and write the two new tables only |
| DocumentChecklistPanel | React component | Replaces the placeholder on SCR-30 with required items present or missing |
| MissingDocumentsBadge | React component | Count shown on the SCR-02 case list rows |

**Database.**
- Flyway migration `V1_5_040__document_checklist.sql` creates document_checklist_item (id, stage_code varchar(20), route_code varchar(4), document_type varchar(30), required boolean, sort_order integer, table_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, load_id uuid, standard columns) with unique (stage_code, route_code, document_type, table_version); and case_document_check (id, case_id uuid, checklist_version varchar(20), required_count integer, present_count integer, missing_types jsonb, complete boolean, checked_at timestamptz, last_event_id uuid, standard columns) with unique (case_id).
- Index ix_checklist_stage on document_checklist_item (stage_code, valid_from).

**Configuration and reference data.**
- Checklist CHK-2026.11, prepared by the reference data administrator, agreed with legal counsel and the litigation officers (DL19).
- No property beyond the feature flag.

**Build steps.**
1. Write the migration; test the unique keys.
2. Build ChecklistLoader with validation against LOV-STAGE, LOV-ROUTE and the type table; test AC7.
3. Build ChecklistEvaluator with the route precedence and the active-version rule; unit test AC1, AC6 and AC9.
4. Build the two listeners with the repeat check; test AC3, AC4, AC5 and AC8.
5. Build ChecklistRefreshStep; test AC2 on 30 November and 1 December 2026.
6. Extend the checklist endpoint and build DocumentChecklistPanel and MissingDocumentsBadge; component tests and the access test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.dochub.checklist`. Off: the endpoint returns the RWB-E1-026 placeholder and no flag is written.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the case list shows the missing count for the synthetic litigation cases in SIT.

| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. |

### 17. Guardrails

## RWB-E1-041 Retention classes and virus scan on intake

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-041 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-17 Apply retention classes to stored documents; FEAT-DCM-18 Virus scan every document on intake |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-010, REQ-DCM-016 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence; L2 13.3 Store and retain documents |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-049 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **compliance and PDPA officer (RW-COMPLY)**, I want **every uploaded or scanned file checked for malware before it is stored, and a retention class per document type that the store applies and a monthly job acts on**, so that **the store holds only safe files and keeps each document for the time the policy sets, never removing one silently or while a legal hold is in place**.

### 2. Business rationale

Files reach the bank from branches, partners and email; one infected file in the store reaches every user who opens it. Documents also have no retention rule today, so nothing shows when a document may be archived (FSD P5 A2.17, A2.18). This story scans every file before storage and quarantines a failed file, holds the retention classes as data, and runs JOB-17 to archive documents past their class or list them for the Compliance review. It meets REQ-DCM-010 and REQ-DCM-016 (legal hold overrides retention), with NFR-028, NFR-072 and NFR-074.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-024 is done: documents carry retention_class and write_once from the type table.
- RWB-E1-049 is done: document_intake and JOB-12 Document intake exist.
- The quarantine container exists (RWB-TE-012) and the bank malware scanning service is reachable through MalwareScanClient under SY-OCR (assumed: the scanning service of the ACE storage pattern, DL27).
- Retention class table loaded through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads, table RETENTION_CLASS, version RET-2026.11: LEGAL10Y 120 months, end action REVIEW; GENERAL05Y 60 months, end action ARCHIVE (assumed; DL26).
- The P3 published interface CaseDirectory returns legal_hold for a case.
- Feature flags rwb.dochub.malware-scan and rwb.dochub.retention are on.

### 4. Flow

1. JOB-12 Document intake: runs scanStep first, before ocrStep.
2. ScanStep: selects intake items with no scan_result and sends each file to MalwareScanClient.
3. ScanStep: on CLEAN, sets scan_result CLEAN and scanned_at, so ocrStep may read the item; on INFECTED, moves the file to the quarantine container, sets scan_result INFECTED, writes the audit event MALWARE_BLOCKED and alerts the platform administrator; the file is never stored.
4. Upload (RWB-E1-026): calls MalwareScanService.scanNow before DocumentStore.store; INFECTED returns 422 MSG-P5-016; if the scanning service does not answer, the call returns 503 MSG-P5-022 and nothing is kept.
5. DocumentStore (RWB-E1-024): stores clean files with the retention class of the type; legal types go to the write-once container.
6. JOB-17 Retention job: runs on the first Sunday of each month; for each active document computes expiry date = stored date plus period_months of its class.
7. RetentionJob: skips a document whose case has legal_hold true and counts it as held.
8. RetentionJob: for a due document with end action ARCHIVE, writes the decision log entry DOCRET, moves the blob to the archive tier and sets the document state ARCHIVED; for end action REVIEW, adds it to the review list for Compliance and changes nothing.
9. RetentionJob: writes the review list to retention/review/{runDate}.csv in the standard container and the counts (due, archived, listed, held, exceptions) to the job record.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The scan finds malware on an intake file | File quarantined, not stored, audit event, platform administrator alerted | MSG-P5-016 | AC1 |
| X2 | The scanning service does not answer | Intake item stays unscanned and is not read by OCR; retried in the next run; alert after two failed runs; an upload returns 503 and nothing is stored | MSG-P5-022 | AC6 |
| X3 | A due document is on a case with a legal hold | Not archived, not listed; counted as held | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A document carries a class not in the retention table | Listed as an exception RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING; nothing changes | None | AC7 |
| X5 | JOB-17 runs again in the same month | Documents already archived or listed for that month are not acted on again | None | AC8 |
| X6 | A retention class load holds an end action other than ARCHIVE or REVIEW, or a period of 0 months | Load refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC9 |
| X7 | The decision log write fails for an archive | The document stays as it is; picked up by the next run; incident raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-041-12 (Principle 5) |
| X8 | A role without Reference data C loads retention classes | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-041-11 (Access) |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store (RWB-E1-024) and the intake (RWB-E1-049); the upload (RWB-E1-026) calls this scan |
| Negotiable | Retention periods and end actions are data under DL26; the scanning service is reached through an adapter |
| Valuable | No infected file reaches a user; every document has a retention rule from day one |
| Estimable | One job step, one monthly job, one table, one adapter |
| Small | Fits within one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every file is scanned for malware before it is stored; an infected file is quarantined and never stored | REQ-DCM-010; FEAT-DCM-18 |
| BR2 | Every document carries a retention class from its type | REQ-DCM-010; NFR-028 |
| BR3 | Retention periods and end actions are data owned by Compliance | Retention classes reference table; DL26 |
| BR4 | A legal hold stops archive and expiry for as long as it is in place | REQ-DCM-016; NFR-072; recovery_case.legal_hold |
| BR5 | No document is removed by the retention job; an end action REVIEW lists it for a recorded decision | NFR-074; REQ-DCM-019 (Epic 2) |
| BR6 | A document with a class missing from the table is listed as an exception | R-WO-48 |
| BR7 | An archive that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | A document is due when its expiry date is on or before the run date | Retention classes reference table; JOB-17 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the intake item scan result (none to CLEAN or INFECTED) and the document state (STORED to ARCHIVED for end action ARCHIVE).

| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Receives scan alerts; reruns JOB-12 and JOB-17 |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Writes the DOCRET entry |

### 12. Contract

**Job: scan step**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | JOB-12 Document intake, step scanStep, first step |
| Job name | JOB-12 Document intake |
| Schedule | Every 15 minutes in business hours |
| Input | Intake items with no scan_result |
| Output | scan_result per item; quarantined files; audit events; alert after two failed runs |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | Intake item ID; an item with a scan_result is not scanned again |
| Restart behavior | Unscanned items are taken by the next run |

**Job: retention**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz schedule of JOB-17 |
| Job name | JOB-17 Retention job |
| Schedule | Monthly, first Sunday, Asia/Bangkok |
| Input | Active documents with their class; retention class version in force; legal hold per case |
| Output | Archived documents; review list file; job counts |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | Document ID and the run month; a document acted on in that month is not acted on again |
| Restart behavior | A stopped run resumes from the last committed chunk of 500 documents; rerun from SCR-44 through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads** (table RETENTION_CLASS)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file, table = "RETENTION_CLASS", validFrom |
| Response | 201 ReferenceLoad |
| Errors | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002); 409 version already loaded (MSG-P3-027); 422 row errors (MSG-P3-027); 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right C; approval with right A |
| Idempotency | Table code and table version |

**Published interface (P5, used by RWB-E1-026 and RWB-E1-057)**

```java
public interface MalwareScanService {
    ScanResult scanNow(BlobRef file, Duration timeout);   // CLEAN or INFECTED; throws ScanUnavailableException
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dochub/retention` and `recovery/dochub/scan`, Java packages `recovery.dochub.retention` and `recovery.dochub.scan`.

**Components.**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ScanStep | Job | First step of JOB-12; scan, quarantine, audit, alert |
| MalwareScanService, MalwareScanClient | Service | Calls the scanning service; maps results and timeouts |
| QuarantineMover | Service | Moves an infected file from the intake container to the quarantine container |
| RetentionJob | Job | JOB-17; expiry computation, hold check, archive or list |
| RetentionClassLoader | Service | Implements ReferenceTableLoader for RETENTION_CLASS |
| RetentionClassRepository | Repository | Reads and writes retention_class only |
| RetentionReviewWriter | Service | Writes the review list file |

**Database.**
- Flyway migration `V1_5_041__retention_class.sql` creates retention_class (id, class_code varchar(10), period_months integer, end_action varchar(12), table_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, load_id uuid, standard columns) with unique (class_code, table_version), check period_months > 0 and check end_action in ('ARCHIVE','REVIEW'); adds to document_intake: scanned_at timestamptz, the time of the malware scan (scan_result is created in RWB-E1-049).
- Adds table retention_action (id, document_id, run_month char(7), action varchar(12), decided_entry_id uuid, standard columns) with unique (document_id, run_month) for the idempotency key.
- Index ix_document_retention on document (retention_class, created_at) where is_active.

**Configuration and reference data.**
- Retention classes RET-2026.11, loaded by the reference data administrator and owned by Compliance (DL26).
- Properties rwb.dochub.container.quarantine and rwb.dochub.scan.timeout-seconds = 30.
- Decision code DOCRET, assumed; LOV-DECISION is loaded by the data steward.

**Build steps.**
1. Write the migration; test the constraints and the unique run key.
2. Build MalwareScanClient against a stub that flags the EICAR signature; test AC1 and the upload call.
3. Build ScanStep with quarantine, audit and the two-failure alert; test AC6.
4. Build RetentionClassLoader with validation; test AC9.
5. Build RetentionJob expiry and hold rules; unit test AC5, AC7 and AC10 on fixed dates.
6. Add archive with the decision log entry and the review list; integration test AC3, AC4 and AC8.
7. Test the access and the decision log failure paths.

**Feature flags.** `rwb.dochub.malware-scan` and `rwb.dochub.retention`. With the scan flag off, intake items stay unscanned and are not read; uploads are refused with 503 and MSG-P5-022. With the retention flag off, JOB-17 lists due documents and archives none.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the EICAR file is quarantined in SIT on every intake path.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-016 | Malware found | This file was not stored because the malware scan found a threat. It is held in quarantine. |
| MSG-P3-027 | Retention class load fails a check | The {table} load was refused: {error} at row {row}. The version in force is unchanged. |
| MSG-P5-022 | Scanning service unavailable on upload | The malware scan is not available, so the file was not stored. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The compliance and PDPA officer reads the review list file and the JOB-17 counts; SCR-47 Personal data, which shows retention classes, comes in Epic 8. The platform administrator sees scan alerts and job results on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor (states Running; failed; complete). An uploader sees MSG-P5-016 or MSG-P5-022 in the upload dialog of SCR-30.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: periods, end actions and the scan timeout are data or properties.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: audit events carry the intake ID and the source, never the file name or content; test files are synthetic.
- No read of another module's tables: legal hold comes through CaseDirectory.
- The retention job never deletes a blob and never changes a write-once blob's content.

| REQ-DCM-010 | Every document carries a retention class; intake runs a virus scan before storage | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5 | FEAT-DCM-18, FEAT-DCM-17 | L2 13.3 Store and retain documents | R-WO-48, R-UNI-39 | TC-E1-041-01 to TC-E1-041-04, TC-E1-041-06 to TC-E1-041-12 |
| REQ-DCM-016 | A legal hold stops deletion and expiry, overriding the class | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5 | FEAT-DCM-17 | L2 13.3 Store and retain documents | None | TC-E1-041-05 |

### 19. Out of scope

- Disposal or extension of a document at the end of its class by a recorded decision (Epic 2, REQ-DCM-019).
- Applying retention on case closure (FEAT-COM-08, Epic 4).
- Placing or lifting a legal hold (P3, POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-hold).
- The retention and personal data screen SCR-47 (Epic 8).
- Retention of the decision log and the interaction ledger (RWB-E1-014, RWB-E2-034).

## RWB-E1-042 Central configuration service and parameter catalog

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-042 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-22 Hold the parameter catalog and configuration service |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-010 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.7 |
| L3 process | 14 Set strategy, policy and decision rules |
| Decision | D6 entry |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-044 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **every environment setting and business parameter read from one configuration service and listed in a parameter catalog with name, type, default, owner, environment and where it is used**, so that **no value is hard-coded and every parameter has an owner**.

### 2. Business rationale

Thresholds such as the 90-day entry point are written into code and spreadsheets today, so a change needs a release and nobody can say who owns a value. This story holds every parameter definition in a catalog with an owner and a default, holds business values as approved, dated versions per environment, serves them to every engine at run time, and fails the build when code carries a literal business value or reads a parameter the catalog does not list. It meets REQ-DRI-010 and puts Principle 1 (DT02) into the build pipeline.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-044 is done: the recovery schema exists in each environment.
- The catalog seed file `config/parameter-catalog.csv` is in the repository, owned by RW-COE, with the Epic 1 entries, including `case.entry.dpd` (default 90; DL16), `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` (default 300; DL11) and `caselist.export.maxrows` (default 10000; DL11).
- The ACE secret store holds secrets per environment; the catalog lists them and never holds their values.
- Loaders hold Reference data C (RW-COE, RW-REFADM). Approvers hold Reference data A: the parameter owner, and RW-RISK where a threshold or a limit moves (assumed grant; DL01).
- The build pipeline runs the checks of this story on every pull request (DL37 code owners).

### 4. Flow

1. Squad member: adds a parameter to `config/parameter-catalog.csv` with key, kind, type, unit, range, default, scope, required, owner role, environments and used by; the pull request is reviewed by the owner.
2. Build: generates the `ParameterKeys` class from the catalog file; code reads a value only through ParameterService with a generated key.
3. Build: runs the magic number check over the recovery packages and the catalog completeness check.
4. Flyway: loads the catalog rows and the default values into parameter_catalog and parameter_value at deployment.
5. RW-COE: loads a new value version through POST /admin/reference-loads with table "PARAMETER", for example `case.entry.dpd` = 91 in PROD valid from 2026-12-10.
6. ParameterLoadChecks: checks key in catalog, type, range, environment and required values; refuses the load whole on any failure.
7. Owner: approves through POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve; refused if the approver is the author.
8. ParameterService: from the valid from date returns the new value; every instance refreshes its cache on ParameterVersionApproved and at the latest after the cache time to live.
9. Engines: read values at run time with the version number, and record the version in their decision log inputs.
10. Any role with Rules and parameters R: reads the catalog and the values in force through GET /admin/parameters.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X3 | A required parameter has no value for the environment at start-up | The service does not start; the health check names the key | MSG-P3-032 | AC4 |
| X4 | A loaded value is outside its range | Load refused in full | MSG-GEN-002 | AC5 |
| X5 | A loaded value has the wrong type | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC6 |
| X6 | The approver is the author | Approval refused | MSG-P7-002 | AC7 |
| X7 | A secret is asked for through the catalog read | The value is not returned | None | AC9 |
| X8 | Rollback of a value version | The previous version is in force | MSG-P3-015 when none exists | AC10 |
| X10 | A new version is approved before its valid from date | The current value stays until that date; no restart is needed | None | AC11 |
| X9 | A role without Rules and parameters R reads the catalog | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-042-12 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the schema and migrations (RWB-E1-044); every later engine reads through it |
| Negotiable | The catalog columns and the build check rules can be tuned; the values are data |
| Valuable | No business value in code, and every parameter has an owner |
| Estimable | Two tables, one service, one load check, two build checks, one read endpoint |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Central configuration service and parameter catalog

  Background:
    Given the catalog lists "case.entry.dpd" as INTEGER, range 1 to 365, default 90, scope GLOBAL, required, owner RW-COE, used by "recovery.casewf.casecreation"

  Scenario: AC1 Parameter read at run time
    Given the parameter "case.entry.dpd" set to 90 in PROD, version 1
    When the case service evaluates entry on 2026-12-01
    Then it uses 90 from the service, not a constant in code
    Then the entry decision records parameter version 1

  Scenario: AC4 Required value missing at start-up
    Given "refdata.cache.ttl-seconds" is required and has no value and no default for UAT
    When the service starts in UAT
    Then the health check fails with MSG-P3-032 for "refdata.cache.ttl-seconds" and "UAT"
    Then the service takes no traffic

  Scenario: AC5 Value outside its range
    When RW-COE loads "case.entry.dpd" = 400 for PROD
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-GEN-002 with minimum 1 and maximum 365

  Scenario: AC6 Wrong type
    When RW-COE loads "case.entry.dpd" = "ninety" for PROD
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P1-002 and check "value is not INTEGER"

  Scenario: AC7 Author cannot approve
    Given RW-COE user U-41 loaded value version 3
    When U-41 approves version 3
    Then the system refuses the approval with MSG-P7-002

  Scenario: AC8 Values per environment
    Given "refdata.cache.ttl-seconds" is 30 in SIT and 300 in PROD
    When the reference data service reads it in SIT and in PROD
    Then SIT uses 30 and PROD uses 300

  Scenario: AC9 Secrets are listed, never served
    Given the catalog lists "ace.db.password" as kind ENVIRONMENT with secret = true
    When GET /admin/parameters is called by RW-COE
    Then the entry shows owner, environments and used by
    Then the system returns no value for "ace.db.password"

  Scenario: AC10 Rollback of a value version
    Given value version 2 of "case.entry.dpd" is in force and version 1 was in force before it
    When RW-COE calls rollback for version 2
    Then version 1 is in force and the service returns 90

  Scenario: AC11 A new value takes effect on its valid from date
    Given version 2 sets "case.entry.dpd" to 91 for PROD with valid from 2026-12-10 and is approved on 2026-12-05
    When the case service evaluates entry on 2026-12-09 and on 2026-12-10
    Then it uses 90 on 2026-12-09 and 91 on 2026-12-10
    Then the system restarts no instance
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every value a business person may change is a parameter row with a version, never a constant in code | Principle 1; DT02; BR-P3-022 |
| BR2 | Every parameter in use has a catalog entry with owner, type, default, environments and used by | REQ-DRI-010 |
| BR3 | A business value changes only through a checked, approved, dated load | CTL-08; reference data change process |
| BR4 | The author of a load cannot approve it; Risk approves where a threshold or a limit moves | Separation of duty table; reference data change process, step 4 |
| BR5 | Open decisions keep the version they were taken under; new decisions use the version in force | R-UNI-38 |
| BR6 | Secrets are listed in the catalog and held only in the secret store | DL26; REQ-ACA-005 |
| BR7 | A service does not start without every required parameter for its environment | Principle 1 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the status of a parameter value version: VALIDATED, APPROVED, ROLLED_BACK.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Load | Every check passes | VALIDATED |
| VALIDATED | Approve | Approver is not the author | APPROVED; in force from valid from |
| APPROVED | Rollback | An earlier approved version exists | ROLLED_BACK |

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COE | Owns the catalog; loads value versions (Reference data C; Rules and parameters CRUD) |
| RW-RISK | Approves a value version where a threshold or a limit moves (Reference data A, assumed grant; DL01) |
| RW-PLATADM | Owns environment settings; reads the catalog (Rules and parameters R) |
| RW-TRIBE | Adds catalog entries through reviewed pull requests |
| Every role with Rules and parameters R | Reads the catalog |
| RW-PHONECOL | No Rules and parameters right; refused |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A parameter is not a credit decision |

### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-132 to DF-REF-146 | parameter_catalog | all fields | Write |
| DF-REF-147 to DF-REF-158 | parameter_value | all fields | Write |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**GET /admin/parameters** (new endpoint, see additions)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query key (prefix), kind, owner, environment |
| Response | 200 array of { key, kind, type, unit, min, max, default, scope, required, owner, environments, usedBy, secret, valueInForce (absent when secret), versionNo, validFrom } |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Rules and parameters R (MSG-P4-002); 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right R |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads** with table "PARAMETER" (P4 endpoint; this story builds the PARAMETER handler)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file (rows of key, environment, value), table = "PARAMETER", validFrom |
| Response | 201 ReferenceLoad: id, table, validFrom, status, rows |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Reference data C (MSG-P4-002); 422 range (MSG-GEN-002), type or unknown key (MSG-P1-002), empty file (MSG-GEN-001); 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right C |
| Idempotency | Table, valid from and content hash; a repeat returns the existing load |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve**: Reference data A; 409 when the approver is the author (MSG-P7-002). **POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback** (new endpoint, recorded with RWB-E1-019): Reference data U; 409 when no earlier version exists (MSG-P3-015).

**Event.** Publishes ParameterVersionApproved (new internal event, see additions: paramKeys, versionNo, validFrom) to the outbox; every instance refreshes its cache.

**Published interface**

```java
// P3, package recovery.casewf.config.api (published)
public interface ParameterService {
    <T> ParameterValue<T> get(ParameterKey<T> key, LocalDate businessDate);
    <T> ParameterValue<T> get(ParameterKey<T> key, String productGroup, LocalDate businessDate);
    CatalogEntry entry(String key);
}
public record ParameterValue<T>(String key, T value, int versionNo, LocalDate validFrom, String environment) {}
// ParameterKeys is generated from config/parameter-catalog.csv, for example
// ParameterKeys.CASE_ENTRY_DPD : ParameterKey<Integer>
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery/casewf/config` (Java package `recovery.casewf.config`); published types in `recovery.casewf.config.api`; build checks in `build-tools/rwb-checks`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ParameterService | Published interface | Typed read by key, environment and date, with version; cache with refresh on ParameterVersionApproved |
| ParameterCatalogRepository | Repository | parameter_catalog |
| ParameterValueRepository | Repository | parameter_value versions |
| ParameterLoadChecks | Service | Key, type, range, environment and required checks for table PARAMETER |
| ParameterLoadHandler | Service | Handler behind POST /admin/reference-loads for table PARAMETER; approve and rollback |
| ParameterCatalogController | Controller | GET /admin/parameters with secrets left out |
| ParameterStartupCheck | Service | Health indicator that fails when a required value is missing for the environment |
| ParameterKeysGenerator | Build tool | Generates ParameterKeys from the catalog file |
| RwbMagicNumberCheck | Build tool | Fails on numeric and string business literals in recovery packages; allowed: 0, 1, -1, test code; names catalog keys whose default equals the literal |
| CatalogCompletenessCheck | Build tool | Compares keys read through ParameterService with the catalog file; fails on a missing key, owner or default |

**Database**

- Migration in this story: `V042_1__parameter_catalog.sql` creates parameter_catalog (param_key varchar(100) primary key, kind, value_type, unit, min_value, max_value, default_value, scope, required, owner_role, environments, used_by, secret, description, standard columns) and parameter_value (id, param_key references parameter_catalog, environment, param_value, product_group, version_no, valid_from, valid_to, status, author_user_id, approver_user_id, approved_at, standard columns; unique (param_key, environment, product_group, version_no); index (param_key, environment, valid_from) where status = 'APPROVED').
- `V042_2__parameter_seed.sql` is generated from the catalog file and loads the defaults; the schema name comes from the Flyway placeholder.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The catalog file, owned by RW-COE; the Epic 1 entries named in section 3.
- Cache time to live `config.cache.ttl-seconds` = 60 (assumed; DL11), itself a catalog entry.
- Environment settings come from the environment and the secret store; only their catalog entries are in the tables.

**Build steps**

1. Migration, entities and repositories; constraint tests on PostgreSQL.
2. ParameterKeysGenerator and the generated keys from the catalog file.
3. ParameterService with date and environment resolution, version in the result and the cache; tests AC1, AC8, AC10, AC11.
4. ParameterLoadChecks and ParameterLoadHandler with approve and rollback; tests AC5, AC6, AC7, AC10.
5. ParameterStartupCheck; test AC4.
6. ParameterCatalogController with secrets left out; tests AC9 and access.
7. RwbMagicNumberCheck and CatalogCompletenessCheck in the build; fixture tests on both checks.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.configservice`. Off: services read the defaults from the generated keys only, and value loads are refused.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the build on main runs both checks with zero findings.

| MSG-P1-002 | Wrong type or unknown key in a load | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Empty load file | Enter {field}. |

| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: every limit, threshold, name and timer is a catalog entry with a value row; the build check enforces it.
- No personal data in parameters, logs, tests or prompts; no secret value in the tables, the logs or any response.
- No read of another module's tables: other modules read values only through ParameterService.
- A value change never needs a deployment; a new parameter needs a reviewed catalog entry.

## RWB-E1-043 Reference data service with versioned tables

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-043 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-23 Run the reference data service with versioned tables |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-011, REQ-CWC-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3 and 4; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.7 |
| L3 process | 14 Set strategy, policy and decision rules |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-042, RWB-E1-044 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **reference data administrator (RW-REFADM)**, I want **products, regions, exposure bands, roles, teams, queues, service levels, document types, templates, delegation of authority, legal periods and holidays held as versioned reference data with valid from, valid to, author and approver**, so that **business values change by a data release and not by code, and every engine can say which version it used**.

### 2. Business rationale

Today the values that drive allocation, timers and approval limits live in team spreadsheets and in procedure documents, so nobody can say which value applied to a case on a given day. This story gives every reference table a version with a valid from date, an author and a different approver, and serves the version in force to the engines. It meets REQ-DRI-011 and REQ-CWC-006 and supports control CTL-08 (a rule, limit or list changes only through a validated load approved by its owner). The measure is that every value an engine reads carries a table code and a version number in its log line.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-044 is done: Flyway migrations run with the schema name taken from a parameter.
- RWB-E1-042 is done: the configuration service serves `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` (assumed 300; DL11) and the list of reference table codes.
- The list LOV-REF-TABLE (new, see Additions) is loaded with the 13 table codes in section 8, BR1.
- The reference load endpoint `POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads` (P4) is deployed and calls this story's published interface.
- The loader holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C). The approver holds the approve right in Reference data (assumed RW-RISK; see section 10).
- The business date of the ACE service is set (the COLLINS business date from JOB-01).

### 4. Flow

1. Reference data administrator: uploads a load file for one table code with a valid from date through `POST /admin/reference-loads`.
2. P4 load handler: passes the file rows, the table code, the valid from date and the caller's user ID to `ReferenceVersionRegistry.recordVersion(...)`.
3. Reference data service: checks the table code, the row schema for that table, the row keys, the valid from date and the author; computes the content hash and the next version number.
4. Reference data service: writes one `reference_version` row with status VALIDATED and one `reference_row` row per file row, in one transaction.
5. Approver: approves the load through `POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve`.
6. Reference data service: checks that the approver is present, is not the author and holds the approve right; sets status APPROVED, `approver_user_id` and `approved_at`.
7. Reference data service: sets `valid_to` of the version it replaces to the day before the new valid from date.
8. Case service, allocation engine and timer engine: on start and on each cache expiry, call `ReferenceDataService.rows(tableCode, businessDate)` and receive the approved version whose valid from is the latest on or before the business date.
9. Each engine: writes one log line per table read, with the table code, the version number and the business date.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Approval attempted with no approver, or by the author | The version stays VALIDATED and is never served | MSG-P7-002 | AC2, AC5 |
| X2 | A row fails the schema or key check for its table | The load is refused in full; no version is written | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X3 | The valid from date is before the business date | The load is refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X4 | The same file is loaded twice for the same table and valid from date | No second version; the first load is returned | None | AC7 |
| X5 | Two approvals of the same load arrive at the same time | One succeeds; the other is refused | MSG-GEN-004 | AC8 |
| X6 | No approved version is in force for a table on the business date | The engine does not start its run and raises an alert to the platform administrator | MSG-P3-027 | AC9 |
| X7 | The load file is empty | The load is refused in full | MSG-GEN-001 | AC10 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the migration tool (RWB-E1-044) and the configuration service (RWB-E1-042). The P4 load endpoint calls this story's interface |
| Negotiable | The list of table codes is data (LOV-REF-TABLE). The story fixes the versioning behavior, not the tables |
| Valuable | Every later rule, timer and approval reads a dated, approved value instead of a spreadsheet |
| Estimable | Two tables, one registry service, one read service, one cache |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests; no screen |
| Testable | Every criterion below is one automated test against a PostgreSQL test container |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Reference data service with versioned tables

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-11-25
    Given the table "EXPOSURE_BAND" has version 3 approved with valid from 2026-11-30 and bands "E1" to "E4"
    Given user "U-REF-01" holds RW-REFADM and user "U-RSK-01" holds the approve right in Reference data

  Scenario: AC1 Versioned row
    Given "U-REF-01" loads table "EXPOSURE_BAND" with bands "E1" to "E5" and valid from 2026-12-01
    Given "U-RSK-01" approves the load
    When the allocation engine reads "EXPOSURE_BAND" for business date 2026-11-30
    Then version 4 exists with status "APPROVED" and 5 rows
    Then version 3 stays readable with its 4 rows and has valid to 2026-11-30
    Then the service returns version 3 for business date 2026-11-30
    Then the service returns version 4 for business date 2026-12-01

  Scenario: AC2 Approver recorded
    Given "U-REF-01" loads table "DELEGATION_LIMIT" with 24 rows and valid from 2026-12-01
    When "U-REF-01" tries to approve the same load
    Then the system refuses the approval with MSG-P7-002
    Then the version stays "VALIDATED" with no approver
    Then the service still returns the previous "DELEGATION_LIMIT" version for business date 2026-12-01

  Scenario: AC3 Read by services
    Given approved versions are in force for "QUEUE" version 7, "SERVICE_LEVEL" version 2 and "HOLIDAY" version 1
    When the case service and the allocation engine start for business date 2026-11-30
    Then each reads every table it uses from the reference data service
    Then each writes one log line per table with the table code, the version number and the business date
    Then no log line contains a party identifier

  Scenario: AC4 Row fails the schema check
    Given a "SERVICE_LEVEL" load file whose row 12 has the text "five" in the column "limit_days"
    When "U-REF-01" loads it
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 naming row 12 and column "limit_days"
    Then no version and no rows are written

  Scenario: AC5 Approval with no approver
    Given a "HOLIDAY" version 2 with status "VALIDATED" and valid from 2026-12-01
    When the business date reaches 2026-12-01 with no approval recorded
    Then the service returns "HOLIDAY" version 1
    Then version 2 stays "VALIDATED"

  Scenario: AC6 Valid from in the past
    Given the business date is 2026-11-25
    When "U-REF-01" loads table "LEGAL_PERIOD" with valid from 2026-11-24
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 naming the valid from date
    Then the system writes no version

  Scenario: AC7 Same file loaded twice
    Given "U-REF-01" has loaded a "REGION" file with content hash "a1b2" and valid from 2026-12-01 as version 5
    When "U-REF-01" loads the same file with the same valid from date again
    Then the response returns the version 5 load
    Then there is still exactly one version 5 and no version 6

  Scenario: AC8 Two approvals at once
    Given a "QUEUE" version 8 with status "VALIDATED"
    When "U-RSK-01" and "U-RSK-02" approve it at the same moment
    Then the system records exactly one approval
    Then the system refuses the other with MSG-GEN-004

  Scenario: AC9 No version in force
    Given the table "TEAM" has no approved version with valid from on or before 2026-11-30
    When the allocation engine starts for business date 2026-11-30
    Then the engine does not start its run
    Then an alert names table "TEAM" and business date 2026-11-30 with MSG-P3-027

  Scenario: AC10 Empty load file
    Given a "DOCUMENT_TYPE" load file with a header row and no data rows
    When "U-REF-01" loads it
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-GEN-001 naming "rows"
    Then the system writes no version
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The reference tables served are PRODUCT, REGION, EXPOSURE_BAND, ROLE, TEAM, QUEUE, SERVICE_LEVEL, DOCUMENT_TYPE, TEMPLATE, DELEGATION_LIMIT, LEGAL_PERIOD, HOLIDAY and PRODUCT_PARAMETER. The list is data and changes by a load of LOV-REF-TABLE | Principle 1; DT02; refdata.txt Reference tables |
| BR2 | Each load creates one version, numbered one above the highest version of that table. A version is never changed after it is written | ADR-004; refdata.txt Change process step 5 |
| BR3 | The version in force on a business date is the approved version with the latest valid from on or before that date | R-UNI-38 |
| BR4 | A version takes effect only after an approver who is not the author approves it | CTL-08; roles.txt Separation of duty (Reference data administrator and Risk and model risk officer) |
| BR5 | A load with any failed check is refused in full | refdata.txt Change process step 3; CTL-02 |
| BR6 | A valid from date before the current business date is refused. Open cases keep the version they were decided under | R-UNI-38 |
| BR7 | Every engine logs the table code and version of every table it reads | REQ-CWC-016; ADR-004 |
| BR8 | Approving a new version sets the valid to of the version it replaces to the day before the new valid from | refdata.txt Key (Valid from) |
| BR9 | An engine that finds no version in force for a table it needs does not run on stale or missing values | Principle 5; NFR-033 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It moves a reference version through these statuses (field `reference_version.status`, new):

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Load received | Every check passes | VALIDATED |
| None | Load received | Any check fails | Not written; load refused |
| VALIDATED | Approval | Approver present, not the author, holds the approve right | APPROVED |
| APPROVED | Rollback (RWB-E1-029 for rule tables; same call for reference tables) | A later version is rolled back | ROLLED_BACK |

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads a version (Reference data C). Reads versions (R) |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Loads a version of the tables it owns (Reference data C) |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves a version. Assumed: RW-RISK holds the approve right in Reference data, because no role holds it in the permission matrix today. The permission matrix change is loaded through RWB-E1-037; holders by name follow DL18 |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Reads the version in force (Reference data R) |
| SY-RULES, rules component | Reads the version in force (Reference data R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads versions and their author and approver (Reference data R) |

The same person may not hold RW-REFADM and RW-RISK (separation of duty table). Approval of DELEGATION_LIMIT follows doa.txt How it applies, rule 11: a change is a data load approved by Risk.

### 12. Contract

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads** (P4 endpoint; calls this story's interface)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: `file` (CSV or XLSX, one sheet), `table` (a LOV-REF-TABLE code), `validFrom` (date) |
| Response | 201 `ReferenceLoad`: `id`, `table`, `validFrom`, `status` (VALIDATED), `rows` |
| Errors | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Reference data C (MSG-P4-002); 409 an approved version of the table already has this valid from (MSG-P3-027); 422 a check failed (MSG-P3-027) or the file has no rows (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the store is unavailable |
| Authorization | Reference data, right C |
| Idempotency | Table code, valid from and content hash. A repeat returns the existing load and writes nothing |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve** (P4 endpoint)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path `loadId` (uuid). No body |
| Response | 200 `ReferenceLoad` with `status` APPROVED |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Reference data A (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown load (MSG-P4-003); 409 the approver is the author (MSG-P7-002) or the version changed since it was read (MSG-GEN-004); 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right A |
| Idempotency | A second approval of an APPROVED version returns 200 with the same body and changes nothing |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}** (P4 endpoint) reads a list with its versions (`ListOfValues`). Reference data R. Used by AC1 to read version 3.

**Published interfaces** (package `recovery.casewf.refdata.api`):

```java
public interface ReferenceVersionRegistry {
    ReferenceVersion recordVersion(String tableCode, LocalDate validFrom, UUID authorUserId,
                              UUID loadId, List<Map<String, Object>> rows);
    ReferenceVersion approve(UUID loadId, UUID approverUserId);
}

public interface ReferenceDataService {
    VersionedRows rows(String tableCode, LocalDate businessDate);
    ReferenceVersion versionInForce(String tableCode, LocalDate businessDate);
    List<ReferenceVersion> versions(String tableCode);
}

public record ReferenceVersion(UUID id, String tableCode, int versionNo, LocalDate validFrom,
                               LocalDate validTo, String status, UUID authorUserId,
                               UUID approverUserId, Instant approvedAt, int rowCount, String contentHash) {}

public record VersionedRows(String tableCode, int versionNo, LocalDate validFrom,
                            List<Map<String, Object>> rows) {}
```

`rows(...)` throws `NoVersionInForceException(tableCode, businessDate)` when no approved version applies. No events are published; the outbox carries none for this story.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery.casewf.refdata` in the recovery module; folder `recovery/casewf/refdata`. Published types in `recovery.casewf.refdata.api`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ReferenceVersionRegistryImpl | Service | Runs the load checks, numbers the version, writes the version and its rows, approves |
| ReferenceDataServiceImpl | Service | Resolves the version in force for a date; serves rows from the cache |
| ReferenceRowCache | Service | In-memory cache keyed by table code and business date; entry time to live from `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` |
| ReferenceTableSchemas | Rule table | Column names, types and key columns per table code, read from the parameter catalog (RWB-E1-042) |
| ReferenceVersionRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `reference_version` |
| ReferenceRowRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `reference_row` |
| ReferenceVersionEntity, ReferenceRowEntity | Entity | JPA mappings of the two tables, with the standard columns |
| ReferenceVersionRegistry, ReferenceDataService | Published interface | The Java interfaces in section 12 |
| ReferenceVersionLogger | Service | Writes the one log line per table read (table code, version, business date) |

**Database.** Flyway migration `V<next>__rwb_e1_043_reference_versions.sql` (this story creates both tables; schema from the `${recoverySchema}` placeholder):

- `reference_version`: `id uuid PK`, `table_code varchar(30) NOT NULL`, `version_no integer NOT NULL`, `valid_from date NOT NULL`, `valid_to date`, `status varchar(15) NOT NULL`, `author_user_id uuid NOT NULL`, `approver_user_id uuid`, `approved_at timestamptz`, `row_count integer NOT NULL`, `content_hash char(64) NOT NULL`, `load_id uuid NOT NULL`, plus the seven standard columns. Constraints: `UNIQUE (table_code, version_no)`; `UNIQUE (table_code, valid_from, content_hash)`; `CHECK (approver_user_id IS NULL OR approver_user_id <> author_user_id)`; partial unique index on `(table_code, valid_from) WHERE status = 'APPROVED'`.
- `reference_row`: `id uuid PK`, `version_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES reference_version (id)`, `row_key varchar(200) NOT NULL`, `row_data jsonb NOT NULL`, plus the standard columns. `UNIQUE (version_id, row_key)`; index on `version_id`.
- Both tables append only: an update trigger refuses changes to `reference_row`, and to `reference_version` except `status`, `approver_user_id`, `approved_at`, `valid_to` and the standard columns.

**Configuration and reference data.** `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` = 300 (assumed; DL11), loaded by the platform administrator in the configuration service. LOV-REF-TABLE values and the column definitions per table code, loaded by the reference data administrator. The first version of each of the 13 tables is loaded by the reference data administrator before SIT and approved by Risk.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration and the two entities and repositories; test the constraints in a PostgreSQL test container.
2. Build `ReferenceTableSchemas` from the parameter catalog and the row check (type, required, key uniqueness) with a check result per row and column.
3. Build `recordVersion(...)`: table code check, empty file check, valid from check against the business date, content hash (SHA-256 over the rows sorted by key), idempotent return on the same hash, version numbering, one transaction.
4. Build `approve(...)`: approver present and different from the author, approve right checked through the ACE access check, optimistic lock on `version`, set `valid_to` of the replaced version.
5. Build `versionInForce` and `rows` with `NoVersionInForceException`, and the cache.
6. Build `ReferenceVersionLogger` and call it from the case service, the allocation engine and the timer engine start-up hooks (one line per table; no row content).
7. Wire the P4 load and approve handlers to the published interface; map exceptions to the problem responses in section 12.
8. Write the tests in section 16.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.refdata-versions`. Off: the engines read the reference values loaded before this story.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the 13 tables each have version 1 approved in SIT, and the boundary test (RWB-TE-001) shows no read of `reference_version` or `reference_row` from outside `recovery.casewf.refdata`.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | A load check fails, the valid from is in the past, or no version is in force for a table an engine needs | The {table} load was refused: {check}. Version {version} stays in force. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The author approves their own load | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | The load file has no data rows | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Two approvals of one version at once | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right loads or approves | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-027 is new (see Additions). Thai text follows DL10.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code. Table codes, columns, bands, periods and limits are rows; the code holds only the versioning behavior.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. Log lines carry table codes and version numbers only. Test files use synthetic codes.
- No read of another module's tables. `lov_value` is read through the P4 published interface; P4 reaches the registry only through `ReferenceVersionRegistry`.
- A version row is never updated in place except for its status, approver and valid to; a correction is a new version.
- The cache never serves a version that is not APPROVED.
