## RWB-E1-044 Database migrations versioned with parameterized schema names

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-044 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-24 Run versioned migrations with parameterized schema names |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-001, REQ-RDF-014 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3 and 4; Business Requirements Epic 2, section 4; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | None |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **every schema change applied by a versioned Flyway migration, one migration per story, forward-only in PROD, with the schema name taken from a parameter**, so that **the database in every environment is the sum of known migrations and nothing else**.

### 2. Business rationale

The recovery tables share the ACE database with the collection module, and two squads change it from one repository (DT07, DT08). A column added by hand in one environment makes SIT and UAT test a database that PROD does not have. This story makes every change a numbered, checksummed migration with no schema name written in the file, and fails the pipeline on drift. It supports REQ-RDF-001 (the 14 data products held in the ACE database) and REQ-RDF-014 (stage 2 tables exist before the first treatment goes live). The measure is zero schema differences between a clean build and each environment at every release.

### 3. Preconditions

- The recovery tables are defined in the Logical Data Model and Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql.
- The recovery module folder and boundary test exist (RWB-TE-001).
- Each environment has a database account for migrations and a read-only account for the drift check, held in the key store (NFR-052).
- The schema parameter `RWB_SCHEMA` is set per environment (DEV, SIT, UAT, PROD). Assumed value `recovery` in every environment, as in Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql.
- Deployment slots are booked (DL35).

### 4. Flow

1. Developer: adds one migration file for the story under `recovery/src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery/`, named `V<number>__<description>.sql`, with the header line `-- Story: <story key>`.
2. Pipeline: runs the migration lint: no literal schema name, exactly one story key per file, no story key in two files, no undo file.
3. Pipeline: starts a clean PostgreSQL container and applies all migrations with `RWB_SCHEMA` set.
4. Pipeline: runs the drift check: dumps the schema object list of the clean database and of the target environment, and compares them.
5. Deployment: on service start, Flyway applies each pending migration once, in version order, and writes its checksum to the history table.
6. Deployment: Flyway validates the checksums of applied migrations; a changed file stops the start.
7. Platform administrator: reads the migration run on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor.

### 5. Exception paths

None.

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the table definitions in the Logical Data Model; it comes first so every later table is a migration |
| Negotiable | The schema name and the history table name are parameters; the story fixes the process |
| Valuable | Every later story changes the database the same way, and environments stay equal |
| Estimable | Flyway configuration, two pipeline checks and a lint |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs in the pipeline against PostgreSQL containers |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

None. The former criteria covered development and delivery procedures and have been removed from the story set.

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every schema change is a versioned migration in the repository; no change is made by hand in any environment | ADR-002; DT08 |
| BR2 | No migration file contains a literal schema name; the schema comes from the environment through the Flyway `${recoverySchema}` placeholder and the default schema | Principle 1 |
| BR3 | One migration file per story that changes the database, carrying the story key in its header | DL04 (merge owner per module) |
| BR4 | PROD runs forward only: clean is disabled, undo files are refused, a fix is a new compensating migration | DT11; NFR-027 |
| BR5 | An applied migration is never edited; checksums are validated on every start | DT11 (untested code is not merged) |
| BR6 | The recovery module keeps its own Flyway history table so its versions do not collide with the ACE and collection modules | DT07; DT08 |
| BR7 | The drift check runs before every deployment to SIT, UAT and PROD | CTL-02 (checks before use) |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the migration state of each environment: a migration moves from pending to applied (or failed) in `flyway_schema_history_recovery`.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Runs deployments and reruns a failed migration job (Platform administration CRUD); reads migration runs on SCR-44 |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Reads migration runs (Platform administration R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads migration runs (Platform administration R) |
| Pipeline migration account | Applies migrations with the migration database account from the key store; not a Workbench role |

### 11. Data

No business field. The story writes the Flyway history table `flyway_schema_history_recovery`, which is a tool table and is not in the Logical Data Model. It reads the schema object list (`information_schema`) in each environment for the drift check.

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs** (P1 endpoint) lists migration runs with `type=MIGRATION`.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query `type` = MIGRATION, `status`, `from`, `to` |
| Response | 200 `Job[]`: `id`, `type`, `businessDate`, `status` (APPLIED, FAILED), `startedAt`, `endedAt`, `checks` (version, checksum, drift result) |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Platform administration R (MSG-P4-002); 503 |
| Authorization | Platform administration, right R |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**Migration job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Service start in each environment, and the pipeline step `migrate` |
| Job name | Not a scheduled job in batch.txt; it runs at deployment |
| Input | The files in `db/migration/recovery`, `RWB_SCHEMA`, the migration account |
| Output | Applied objects in schema `RWB_SCHEMA`; rows in `flyway_schema_history_recovery`; one `Job` record per run through the P1 job monitor |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | Migration version. An applied version is never applied again |
| Restart behavior | A failed migration rolls back; after a fix is merged as a new version, the next start applies it |

**Configuration** (Spring Boot properties, values from the configuration service):

```properties
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.flyway.locations=classpath:db/migration/recovery
spring.flyway.schemas=${RWB_SCHEMA}
spring.flyway.default-schema=${RWB_SCHEMA}
spring.flyway.table=flyway_schema_history_recovery
spring.flyway.placeholders.schema=${RWB_SCHEMA}
spring.flyway.validate-on-migrate=true
spring.flyway.out-of-order=false
spring.flyway.clean-disabled=true
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery.casewf.migration` (configuration and checks); migration files in `recovery/src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery`; pipeline scripts in `recovery/build/migration-checks`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RecoveryFlywayConfig | Service | Builds the recovery Flyway instance from the properties above; refuses clean in every profile |
| MigrationRunRecorder | Service | Writes one job record per migration run through the P1 job monitor interface |
| MigrationLint | Job | Build step: refuses literal schema names (pattern on `<identifier>.` before a table name for every name in `sys_objects`), missing or repeated story keys, and `U*.sql` files |
| SchemaDriftCheck | Job | Pipeline step: applies all migrations to a clean container, lists tables, columns, types, constraints and indexes of `RWB_SCHEMA`, compares with the target environment through the read-only account, reports each difference |
| V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql | RWB-E1-001 baseline | Built from Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql with the `${recoverySchema}` placeholder and `SET search_path` removed; applied by RWB-E1-001 (D-RCV-28) |

**Database.** No business table changes. Flyway creates `flyway_schema_history_recovery` in `RWB_SCHEMA`. The baseline migration creates the 43 tables of Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql; the initial seed rows (`lov_value`, `role`, `permission`, `delegation_limit`, `sys_objects`, `sys_fields`, `data_product`) ship with the RWB-E1-001 baseline `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` (D-RCV-28, D-RCV-29); later dictionary changes are reference loads through RWB-E1-043, not migrations.

**Configuration and reference data.** The schema value is the placeholder `${recoverySchema}`, fixed to `recovery` in every environment (D-RCV-28); no per-environment override. Migration and read-only database accounts in the key store, set by the platform administrator.

**Build steps**

Ruled 2026-11-05 as D-RCV-28: recovery Flyway files are named `V<seq>__<story>_<name>.sql` with a four-digit sequence taken in merge order; line 1 is `-- Story: <story key>`; the schema is referenced only as `${recoverySchema}` and is `recovery` in every environment. The RWB-E1-001 baseline is `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql`; RWB-E1-044 ships no production migration file. Former open point: The rule in this story is a single rising number with the placeholder ${schema} fed by RWB_SCHEMA. The other 51 stories that name a migration file use four other rules, 30 of them V<epic>_<story>__<name>.sql with the placeholder ${recoverySchema} as in RWB-E1-001. The lint rule reports and fails the build for a name that breaks the rule.

1. Add Flyway to the recovery module and `RecoveryFlywayConfig` with the properties in section 12; prove start-up applies and records a test migration.
2. Convert Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql into the RWB-E1-001 baseline `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` with the `${recoverySchema}` placeholder; prove it creates every table in the recovery schema.
3. Build `MigrationLint` and add it to the build; test each refusal with fixture files.
4. Build `SchemaDriftCheck` and add it before each deployment stage; test with a hand-added column.
5. Build `MigrationRunRecorder` and show runs on the job monitor.
6. Prove forward only: clean refused, undo files refused, failed migration rolls back.
7. Prove the lock with two instances starting together.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.migration-drift-gate`. On in SIT, UAT and PROD: drift fails the deployment. Off in DEV: drift is reported and the deployment continues.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and DEV and SIT show no drift against the baseline.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-016 | Drift found, checksum mismatch, lint failure, a refused clean or undo, or a failed migration | Schema check failed in {schema}: {object}. The deployment was stopped. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Platform administration R reads migration runs | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-016 is new (see Additions). It is shown in the pipeline log and on SCR-44, not to business users.

### 15. Screens and states

SCR-44 Interface and job monitor, state Running, Failed or Complete: the platform administrator reads each migration run with its version, checksum and drift result. No new screen in this story.

### 16. Test cases

None.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code or in a migration. Seed values are reference loads (RWB-E1-043), not migration inserts.
- No personal data in migrations, tests or logs. No migration copies production rows.
- No read of another module's tables. Each module owns its migrations; the recovery history table holds recovery versions only.
- No literal schema name in any migration or repository query.
- No manual change in any environment; a hotfix is a new migration through the pipeline.

### 18. Traceability

| Requirement ID | Requirement (short) | BRD section | Feature | L3 process | Rules | Test cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-RDF-001 | Recovery data held in 14 data products in the ACE database | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 4; Program, section 5.1 | FEAT-CWC-24 | All recovery processes | CTL-02; DT08 | None |
| REQ-RDF-014 | Stage 2 data products exist before the first treatment goes live | Business Requirements Epic 2, section 4; Program, section 5.1 | FEAT-CWC-24 | All recovery processes | DT11 | None |

### 19. Out of scope

- The table definitions themselves (RWB-E1-001 and each story that adds a table).
- Seed reference data (RWB-E1-043).
- Code owners and the browser test runner in the pipeline (DL37, RWB-TE-002).
- Deployment slots and release windows (DL34, DL35).

## RWB-E1-045 Multi-product parameters for Mortgage, HP and SSME

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-045 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-25 Set product parameters without a code change |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-010, REQ-CWC-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3 and 4; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.7 |
| L3 process | 14 Set strategy, policy and decision rules |
| Decision | D6 entry |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-042, RWB-E1-043, RWB-E1-012 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **every product-specific value (entry rule, exclusion list, service levels, notice and cure periods, exposure bands) keyed by product in the reference data**, so that **a new product or a product change needs no code change**.

### 2. Business rationale

Mortgage, hire purchase and SSME follow different notice periods, service levels and bands, and today each difference is held in a team procedure. If the engines carry these values as constants, every product change waits for a release. This story keys each value by product group in the versioned reference tables of RWB-E1-043 and refuses a load that leaves a product without a required value. It meets REQ-DRI-010 and REQ-CWC-011. The measure is that a product is added or changed by a reference load with no deployment.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-043 is done: versioned reference tables, the registry and the read service.
- RWB-E1-042 is done: the parameter catalog marks each parameter with scope PRODUCT or GLOBAL, required yes or no, type, unit and allowed range (new catalog fields, see Additions).
- RWB-E1-012 is done: the local copies that held product values are retired.
- Tables PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL have an approved version in force.
- The timer engine (RWB-E1-028), case creation (RWB-E1-018) and the allocation engine (RWB-E1-020) read product values only through `ProductParameterService`.
- The loader holds RW-COE or RW-REFADM (Reference data C); the approver holds the approve right in Reference data.

### 4. Flow

1. Center of excellence analyst: prepares a PRODUCT_PARAMETER load with one row per product group and parameter code, and a SERVICE_LEVEL load with one row per product group and case status.
2. Reference data administrator: loads each file through `POST /admin/reference-loads`.
3. Reference data service: runs the RWB-E1-043 checks, then the product completeness check: every product in the PRODUCT version in force on the valid from date has a row for every catalog parameter with scope PRODUCT and required yes, and a SERVICE_LEVEL row for every status in the parameter `servicelevel.required-statuses`.
4. Reference data service: checks each value against the catalog type and range.
5. Approver: approves the version; it takes effect on its valid from date.
6. Timer engine: when it starts a notice timer for a case, calls `ProductParameterService.get(productGroup, "NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS", businessDate)` and sets `expires_at` from the value and its unit.
7. Case creation and allocation: read the entry threshold, the exclusion list and the exposure bands for the case's product group the same way.
8. Each engine: records the PRODUCT_PARAMETER version used in its decision log entry inputs (written by the owning story).

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A product has no SERVICE_LEVEL row for a required status | The load is refused in full and the missing product and status are named | MSG-P3-034 | AC3 |
| X2 | A parameter value is outside the catalog range or of the wrong type | The load is refused in full | MSG-GEN-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | Two rows for the same product and parameter | The load is refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X4 | A PRODUCT version removes a product that still has open cases | The load is refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X5 | At run time a case's product has no parameter row in force | No timer is set; the case goes to the exception queue; the gap is named | MSG-P3-034 | AC7 |
| X6 | A parameter changes while a timer is running | The running timer keeps its expiry; new timers use the new value from its valid from date | None | AC8 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on the reference data service of RWB-E1-043 and the catalog of RWB-E1-042 only |
| Negotiable | The parameter list and every value are data; the story fixes the lookup and the completeness check |
| Valuable | A product change becomes a reference load approved by its owner |
| Estimable | One read service, one completeness check, three call sites changed |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against a PostgreSQL test container with synthetic cases |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Multi-product parameters for Mortgage, HP and SSME

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-12-01
    Given PRODUCT_PARAMETER version 2 is in force with NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS 30 calendar days for "MORTGAGE" and 60 calendar days for "HIRE_PURCHASE"
    Given PRODUCT version 1 is in force with "MORTGAGE", "HIRE_PURCHASE", "SSME" and "UNSECURED"

  Scenario: AC1 Product value differs
    Given case "RW-2026-000101" with product group "MORTGAGE" and case "RW-2026-000102" with product group "HIRE_PURCHASE"
    When the timer engine sets the notice timer on both cases on 2026-12-01
    Then the notice timer of "RW-2026-000101" expires on 2026-12-31
    Then the notice timer of "RW-2026-000102" expires on 2027-01-30
    Then each timer start records PRODUCT_PARAMETER version 2

  Scenario: AC2 New product added
    Given PRODUCT version 2 adds product group "AUTO_LEASE" with valid from 2026-12-05
    Given PRODUCT_PARAMETER version 3 and SERVICE_LEVEL version 3 add every required row for "AUTO_LEASE" with valid from 2026-12-05
    Given all three versions are approved
    When the COLLINS load of 2026-12-05 carries an "AUTO_LEASE" account at 90 days past due
    Then the system creates a case with product group "AUTO_LEASE"
    Then the system sets its timers from the "AUTO_LEASE" rows
    Then no deployment took place between 2026-12-01 and 2026-12-05

  Scenario: AC3 Missing parameter blocked
    Given a SERVICE_LEVEL load with valid from 2026-12-10 that has no row for "SSME" and status "WAITING_PARTNER"
    When the load validates
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-034 naming "SSME" and "WAITING_PARTNER"
    Then SERVICE_LEVEL version 3 stays in force

  Scenario: AC4 Value outside its range
    Given the catalog range for NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS is 1 to 365
    When a PRODUCT_PARAMETER load sets NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS to 0 for "SSME"
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-GEN-002 naming "NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS", 1 and 365

  Scenario: AC5 Duplicate product row
    Given a PRODUCT_PARAMETER load with two NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS rows for "MORTGAGE", 30 and 45
    When the load validates
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 naming "MORTGAGE" and "NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS"

  Scenario: AC6 Product removed while cases are open
    Given 3 open cases with product group "UNSECURED"
    When a PRODUCT load with valid from 2026-12-15 leaves out "UNSECURED"
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 naming "UNSECURED" and 3 open cases

  Scenario: AC7 No parameter in force at run time
    Given case "RW-2026-000140" with product group "SSME" and no NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS row for "SSME" in force
    When the timer engine sets the notice timer on 2026-12-01
    Then the system writes no notice timer
    Then the system places the case in the exception queue with MSG-P3-034 naming "SSME" and "NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS"

  Scenario: AC8 Value changes while a timer runs
    Given the notice timer of "RW-2026-000101" started on 2026-12-01 and expires on 2026-12-31
    Given PRODUCT_PARAMETER version 4 with NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS 45 for "MORTGAGE" takes effect on 2026-12-03
    When the timer engine sets a notice timer on Mortgage case "RW-2026-000150" on 2026-12-03
    Then the timer of "RW-2026-000101" still expires on 2026-12-31
    Then the timer of "RW-2026-000150" expires on 2027-01-17
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every product-specific value is a PRODUCT_PARAMETER or SERVICE_LEVEL row keyed by product group; no engine holds a product value or a product name in code | Principle 1; DT02 |
| BR2 | The parameters required per product are those the catalog marks with scope PRODUCT and required yes: ENTRY_DPD, EXCLUSION_LIST, NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS, CURE_PERIOD_DAYS and EXPOSURE_BAND_SET. Values per product are the business's (entry 90 days, DL16; service levels DL22; caps DL23) | RWB-E1-042 catalog; DL16; DL22 |
| BR3 | Every product in force has one SERVICE_LEVEL row per status in `servicelevel.required-statuses` (assumed NEW, ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_CUSTOMER, WAITING_PARTNER, WAITING_APPROVAL; DL22) | REQ-CWC-011; casemodel.txt Case status |
| BR4 | A load that leaves a required row missing, a value out of range or a duplicate key is refused in full | CTL-08; refdata.txt Change process step 3 |
| BR5 | A product with open cases cannot be removed from PRODUCT | R-UNI-38 |
| BR6 | A timer takes the value in force on the date it starts and keeps it; new values apply from their valid from date | R-UNI-38 |
| BR7 | A value in unit WORKING_DAYS skips the dates in the HOLIDAY table in force; a value in CALENDAR_DAYS does not | refdata.txt Reference tables |
| BR8 | A case whose product has no required value in force is not timed and goes to the exception queue | Principle 5; R-UNI-41 handles the case once a person decides |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes how the timer engine sets `timer.expires_at` and adds the completeness check to reference version validation (status VALIDATED or refused, RWB-E1-043). A case sent to the exception queue under X5 keeps status New or its current status.

| RW-PRODHEAD, product head | Owns the values for the product (LOV-PRODUCT owner in refdata.txt); reads versions (Reference data R) |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves a version where a limit or threshold moves (refdata.txt Change process step 4; assumed approve right as in RWB-E1-043) |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Reads product values and writes timers |
| SY-RULES, rules component | Reads product values for allocation |

### 12. Contract

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads** (P4 endpoint; the completeness check runs inside the RWB-E1-043 registry)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: `file`, `table` (PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER or SERVICE_LEVEL), `validFrom` |
| Response | 201 `ReferenceLoad` (`id`, `table`, `validFrom`, `status`, `rows`) |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 409 open cases on a removed product (MSG-P3-027); 422 missing required row (MSG-P3-034), value out of range (MSG-GEN-002), duplicate key (MSG-P3-027); 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right C |
| Idempotency | As RWB-E1-043: table code, valid from and content hash |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers** (P3) returns `Timer[]` (`timerType`, `startedAt`, `expiresAt`, `warnAt`, `status`). Case record R. Errors 401, 403, 404 (MSG-P4-003), 503. Used to check AC1, AC2 and AC8.

**Published interface** (package `recovery.casewf.refdata.api`):

```java
public interface ProductParameterService {
    ProductParameter get(String productGroup, String parameterCode, LocalDate businessDate);
    ServiceLevel serviceLevel(String productGroup, String caseStatus, LocalDate businessDate);
}

public record ProductParameter(String productGroup, String parameterCode, String value,
                               String unit, String tableCode, int versionNo) {}

public record ServiceLevel(String productGroup, String caseStatus, int limit, String unit,
                           int warnPercent, String escalateToRole, int versionNo) {}
```

Both methods throw `MissingProductParameterException(productGroup, parameterCode, businessDate)` when no row is in force. No events are published by this story.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery.casewf.refdata.product` in the recovery module; published types in `recovery.casewf.refdata.api`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ProductParameterServiceImpl | Service | Reads PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL rows in force through `ReferenceDataService`; converts value and unit |
| ProductCompletenessCheck | Service | Load check for PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL: required rows, range, duplicates, products with open cases |
| OpenCaseCounter | Repository | Counts open cases by product group in `recovery_case` (status not CLOSED) |
| DueDateCalculator | Service | Adds calendar or working days, reading HOLIDAY rows in force |
| TimerEngine (RWB-E1-028) | Service | Changed: takes the period from `ProductParameterService` instead of its own table |
| CaseEntryService (RWB-E1-018), AllocationService (RWB-E1-020) | Service | Changed: take ENTRY_DPD, EXCLUSION_LIST and EXPOSURE_BAND_SET from `ProductParameterService` |
| ProductParameterService | Published interface | The interface in section 12 |

**Database.** No new table. Reads `reference_version` and `reference_row` (RWB-E1-043) through the published service, and `recovery_case` (status, product group). Writes `timer` through the timer engine. Index `ix_case_status_queue` on `recovery_case (status, queue_id)` serves the open case count.

**Configuration and reference data.** PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER, SERVICE_LEVEL and HOLIDAY versions, loaded by the reference data administrator and owned by the product heads (values per DL16, DL22, DL23). Catalog entries for the five parameters in BR2 with scope, required, type, unit and range, loaded by the center of excellence analyst through RWB-E1-042. Parameter `servicelevel.required-statuses` (assumed list in BR3; DL22).

**Build steps**

1. Build `DueDateCalculator` with the calendar and working day rules; unit test across the 2026-12-31 year end and a holiday row.
2. Build `ProductParameterServiceImpl` over `ReferenceDataService` with `MissingProductParameterException`.
3. Build `ProductCompletenessCheck` and add it as a table check for PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL in the RWB-E1-043 registry.
4. Change the timer engine to take the notice and cure periods from the service and keep the started value on running timers.
5. Change case creation and allocation to take ENTRY_DPD, EXCLUSION_LIST and EXPOSURE_BAND_SET from the service; remove any product name or number from their code.
6. Add the X5 path: on `MissingProductParameterException`, place the case in the exception queue and name the gap.
7. Write the tests in section 16 with synthetic products and cases.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.product-parameters`. Off: the engines use the values they read before this story.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and a search of the recovery module code finds no product group code literal outside test fixtures and the generated API types.

| MSG-P3-027 | Duplicate row, or a product with open cases removed | The {table} load was refused: {check}. Version {version} stays in force. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | A value is outside its catalog range | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Reference data C loads a file | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-027 and MSG-P3-034 are new (see Additions). Thai text follows DL10.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code. No product group code, period, threshold or band is written in Java or TypeScript; the generated API types treat product group as a string checked against LOV-PRODUCT, not as a closed enum.

- No read of another module's tables. Reference rows are read through `ReferenceDataService`; LOV-PRODUCT through the P4 published interface.
- A running timer is never recalculated when a parameter changes.

## RWB-E1-046 Template and merge field catalog as data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-046 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P6 Communications |
| Feature | FEAT-DRI-16 Hold the template catalog with merge fields |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-OCC-001, REQ-OCC-002 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.6 and 4 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | D7.1 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-012 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **letter and document templates and their merge fields held as versioned data with the Legal approval record on each version**, so that **a template change is a data release approved by Legal and never a code release**.

### 2. Business rationale

Letters and notices are prepared by hand today, so the wording and the facts on a notice depend on who typed it. This story holds every template version, the merge fields it draws from the case and the Legal approval as data rows, so the letter engine (RWB-E1-052) can only use a version Legal approved and can only fill fields the catalog knows. It serves REQ-OCC-001 and REQ-OCC-002 and the FSD P6 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent", which needs every notice to come from a known template version (CTL-14).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-012 is done: recovery data comes only from the recovery tables.
- The template table exists in schema recovery (Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql) and the reference data load path of P4 (POST /admin/reference-loads) is live.
- Lists LOV-LANG, LOV-PRODUCT and LOV-NOTICE are loaded (refdata.txt).
- The merge field catalog load file is prepared by the reference data administrator (RW-REFADM), one row per merge field, each naming its BR Field ID in the Logical Data Model.
- The person loading holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C). Legal counsel (RW-LEGAL) approves each template version through RWB-E1-034, or through the approval columns of the load file in Epic 1 before that screen is live.

### 4. Flow

1. Reference data administrator: loads the merge field catalog file through POST /admin/reference-loads with table "merge_field" and a valid from date.
2. System: checks every row: merge code unique, BR Field ID present in sys_fields, source entity and field present, required flag set. A row that fails refuses the whole load (refdata change process, step 3).
3. Reference data administrator: loads a template version file through POST /admin/reference-loads with table "template", carrying template code, language, product group, channel, notice type, signature basis, the body file reference, the merge codes used and, where Legal has signed, the approver and approval date.
4. System: reads every merge code in the body and in the merge code list and checks each one against the catalog in force. An unknown code refuses the load and names the code (MSG-P6-006).
5. System: assigns the next version number for the template code and language, keeps every earlier version readable and sets state Approved only where the approver and approval date are present, otherwise Draft.
6. System: the published interface TemplateCatalog returns, for a template code, language and date, the current version: the Approved version with the highest version number whose valid from date is on or before that date.
7. Letter engine (RWB-E1-052): asks TemplateCatalog for the current version. If none is Approved, the catalog refuses and names the missing approval (MSG-P6-005).
8. System: writes the load result (rows loaded, rows refused, version numbers) to the reference load record and the ACE audit log.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Generation asks for a template whose versions are all Draft | TemplateCatalog throws TemplateNotApprovedException; nothing is generated | MSG-P6-005 | AC2 |
| X2 | A template uses a merge code that is not in the catalog | The whole load is refused; the unknown code is named | MSG-P6-006 | AC3 |
| X3 | A catalog row names a BR Field ID that is not in the data dictionary | The whole catalog load is refused | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X4 | A template row has no template code, language or body reference | The whole load is refused; the field is named | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X5 | The same template file is loaded twice | The second load creates no new version | MSG-P1-002 | AC6 |
| X6 | The only Approved version is withdrawn | TemplateCatalog returns no current version; generation holds | MSG-P6-003 | AC7 |
| X7 | A version has valid from in the future | The earlier Approved version stays current until that date | None | AC8 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the recovery tables (RWB-E1-012) and the P4 reference load path; the screen comes in RWB-E1-034 |
| Negotiable | The merge codes and the templates are data; the story fixes the checks and the selection of the current version |
| Valuable | Every notice from Epic 1 on is traceable to one Legal-approved version |
| Estimable | One new table, one validator, one published interface, two load handlers |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test against synthetic load files |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Template and merge field catalog as data

  Background:
    Given the merge field catalog version "MF-2026.11" is in force with merge codes "CASE_NO", "CUSTOMER_NAME", "POSTAL_ADDRESS", "TOTAL_OUTSTANDING" and "NOTICE_DATE"
    Given template "DEMAND-MTG" in language "TH" has version 1 Approved by user "LEG-0001" on 2026-10-01

  Scenario: AC1 Template versioned
    Given a load file for template "DEMAND-MTG" language "TH" approved by user "LEG-0001" on 2026-11-10 with valid from 2026-11-10
    When it is loaded on 2026-11-10
    Then the system creates version 2 of "DEMAND-MTG" with state "Approved", approver "LEG-0001" and approval date 2026-11-10
    Then TemplateCatalog returns version 2 as current for "DEMAND-MTG", "TH" on 2026-11-10
    Then version 1 stays readable with its own approver and approval date

  Scenario: AC2 Unapproved template blocked
    Given template "RECALL-HP" in language "TH" has only version 1 in state "Draft"
    When the letter engine asks TemplateCatalog for the current version of "RECALL-HP", "TH"
    Then the catalog refuses with TemplateNotApprovedException
    Then the refusal carries MSG-P6-005 naming "RECALL-HP" version 1

  Scenario: AC3 Merge fields checked
    Given a load file for template "GUARANTOR-SSME" whose body uses the merge code "GUARANTOR_EMAIL"
    Given "GUARANTOR_EMAIL" is not in the catalog
    When it is loaded
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P6-006 naming "GUARANTOR_EMAIL"
    Then the system creates no version of "GUARANTOR-SSME"

  Scenario: AC4 Catalog row with an unknown field ID is refused
    Given a catalog load file of 12 rows where row 7 names a BR Field ID "XX-CAS-999" that is not in the data dictionary
    When it is loaded
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-002 naming the check "field ID not in the data dictionary"
    Then catalog version "MF-2026.11" stays in force

  Scenario: AC5 Template row with a missing required field is refused
    Given a template load file whose row has no body reference
    When it is loaded
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-GEN-001 naming "body_ref"

  Scenario: AC6 Repeated load creates no new version
    Given the load file of AC1 has been loaded once and version 2 exists
    When the same file with the same file hash is loaded again
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P1-002 naming the check "repeat of load"
    Then "DEMAND-MTG" still has 2 versions

  Scenario: AC7 Withdrawn current version leaves no current version
    Given version 2 of "DEMAND-MTG" "TH" was Approved and current and is now in state "Withdrawn"
    When the letter engine asks TemplateCatalog for the current version of "DEMAND-MTG", "TH" on 2026-11-20
    Then TemplateCatalog returns no current version and throws TemplateWithdrawnException
    Then the refusal carries MSG-P6-003 naming "DEMAND-MTG"

  Scenario: AC8 Future valid from date keeps the earlier version current
    Given version 3 of "DEMAND-MTG" "TH" is Approved with valid from 2026-12-01
    When TemplateCatalog is asked on 2026-11-30 and on 2026-12-01
    Then it returns version 2 on 2026-11-30
    Then it returns version 3 on 2026-12-01
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A template version is used only when its state is Approved and it carries the Legal approver and approval date | REQ-OCC-002; CTL-14 |
| BR2 | The current version for a template code and language on a date is the Approved version with the highest version number whose valid from is on or before that date | R-LIT-03 (template_status = current) |
| BR3 | A withdrawn template has no current version, and generation holds until Legal approves a new one | R-LIT-04, R-LIT-06 |
| BR4 | Every merge code a template uses exists in the catalog in force, and every catalog row names a BR Field ID in the data dictionary | REQ-OCC-001; Principle 1 |
| BR5 | A load with any refused row is refused in full and the previous version stays in force | refdata.txt change process, step 3 |
| BR6 | Earlier versions are never changed or deleted; open cases keep the version they were generated under | refdata.txt change process, step 6; R-UNI-38 |
| BR7 | Templates are owned by Legal counsel as reference data | refdata.txt reference table "Letter and notice templates"; DL28 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It sets the template version state (standard column state): Draft on load without an approver, Approved on load with an approver, Withdrawn when Legal withdraws it (RWB-E1-034). The reference load status moves from loaded to refused or in force.

| RW-LEGAL, Legal counsel | Approves a template version; the approver named in the load (Documents A) |

| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Reads the catalog (Reference data R) |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Calls TemplateCatalog for the current version |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies.

### 12. Contract

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads** (exists, module P4)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file, table ("template" or "merge_field"), validFrom |
| Response | 201 ReferenceLoad: id, table, validFrom, status, rows |
| Errors | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 role lacks Reference data C (MSG-P4-002); 409 a load for the same table and file hash already exists (MSG-P1-002); 422 a row fails a check (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P6-006, MSG-P1-002); 503 store unavailable (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Reference data, right C |
| Idempotency | SHA-256 hash of the file per table; a repeat is refused (AC6) |

P4 owns the endpoint. This story adds two table handlers to it through the P4 published interface:

```java
public interface ReferenceLoadHandler {
    String table();                                   // "template" or "merge_field"
    LoadValidation validate(LoadFile file, LocalDate validFrom);
    LoadResult apply(LoadFile file, LocalDate validFrom, UUID loadedBy);
}
```

**Published interface TemplateCatalog** (P6, called by RWB-E1-052, RWB-E2-022, RWB-E2-026)

```java
public interface TemplateCatalog {
    TemplateVersion current(String templateCode, String language, LocalDate onDate)
        throws TemplateNotApprovedException, TemplateWithdrawnException;
    Optional<TemplateVersion> version(String templateCode, String language, int templateVersion);
    List<MergeField> mergeFields(String templateCode, String language, int templateVersion);
}
```

TemplateVersion carries id, templateCode, templateVersion, language, productGroup, channel, noticeType, signatureBasis, bodyRef, approvedBy, approvedAt, validFrom and the merge codes. No personal data.

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/comms/templates`, Java package `recovery.comms.templates`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TemplateEntity | Entity | Maps table template with the new columns |
| MergeFieldEntity | Entity | Maps table merge_field |
| TemplateRepository | Repository | Reads and writes template; finds the current version by code, language and date |
| MergeFieldRepository | Repository | Reads and writes merge_field by catalog version |
| TemplateLoadHandler | Service | ReferenceLoadHandler for table "template": parses rows, assigns versions, applies BR1 to BR6 |
| MergeFieldLoadHandler | Service | ReferenceLoadHandler for table "merge_field": checks field IDs against sys_fields |
| MergeCodeScanner | Service | Reads merge codes `{{CODE}}` from a DOCX body and compares them with the declared list |
| TemplateCatalogService | Published interface | Implements TemplateCatalog |

- Database: table template (Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql) gets the new columns approved_by uuid, approved_at timestamptz, valid_from date, channel varchar(15), notice_type varchar(25), signature_basis varchar(20), merge_codes jsonb. Constraint uk_template UNIQUE (template_code) is replaced by uk_template_version UNIQUE (template_code, language, template_version), because one code holds many versions. Check constraint: state in ('DRAFT','APPROVED','WITHDRAWN'); approved_by and approved_at both set when state = 'APPROVED'. New table merge_field with unique (merge_code, catalog_version). Flyway migration `V1_046__template_catalog.sql` creates merge_field and alters template.
- Configuration and reference data: LOV-LANG, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-NOTICE (loaded by RW-REFADM); the merge field catalog file (RW-REFADM, content agreed with Legal counsel, DL28); template files and their approvals (Legal counsel); new lists for channel (LETTER, SMS, LINE) and signature basis (E_SIGNATURE_ALLOWED, WET_INK_REQUIRED) recorded as additions.
- Build steps:
  1. Write the Flyway migration and the two entities; test the constraints with an in-memory PostgreSQL (Testcontainers).
  2. Build MergeFieldLoadHandler with the sys_fields check; test AC4.
  3. Build MergeCodeScanner over DOCX bodies; test that it finds every `{{CODE}}` and nothing else.
  4. Build TemplateLoadHandler: required fields, merge code check, version numbering, state from the approval columns; test AC1, AC3, AC5.
  5. Add the file hash check on repeat loads; test AC6.
  6. Build TemplateCatalogService with the BR2 selection and the withdrawn and Draft refusals; test AC2, AC7, AC8.
  7. Add both handlers to the P4 reference load service behind the feature flag.
- Feature flag: `rwb.comms.template-catalog`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass, and the migration runs clean on an empty schema and on the SIT schema.

| MSG-P6-006 | A template uses a merge code not in the catalog | {template} uses the merge field {field}, which is not in the merge field catalog. The load was refused. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The current version is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P1-002 | A catalog load fails a check, or repeats a load | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty in a load row | Enter {field}. |

No screen in this story. The reference data administrator loads files through the P4 load path and reads the result on the reference load record. SCR-40 Reference data (states Versions; load) shows the template and merge_field tables with their versions when it is built. The template screen SCR-33 comes in RWB-E1-034.

## RWB-E1-047 Feature flags for module release with a removal date

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-047 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P2 Integration |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-26 Control module release with dated feature flags |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-010 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.2; Business Requirements Program, section 5.7 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Should |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **a feature flag service with each flag held as data (key, owner, value per environment, removal date) and read by the service and the front end at run time**, so that **a feature can be released switched off and switched on without a deployment, and no flag stays after its removal date without its owner being told**.

### 2. Business rationale

Two squads release monthly from one repository, and one squad's unfinished change must not hold the other's release (ADR-008, DT11). A flag held as a data row lets the platform administrator switch a change off in SIT or UAT and let the release go ahead, with every change logged. A weekly report lists flags past their removal date so old code paths are removed. It meets REQ-DRI-010 (configuration changed without a code release).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 (recovery schema) is done.
- The person holds RW-PLATADM in the environment through the Entra ID group, for example RWB-UAT-RW-PLATADM.
- The ACE audit log service of the common module is available.
- The ACE front end loads the recovery module folder (ADR-006).
- Flag `rwb.casewf.case-list-queue-column` is created with default off and removal date 2027-01-31 for the tests.

### 4. Flow

1. Platform administrator: creates a flag with key, description, owner, default value and removal date.
2. System: validates the key pattern `rwb.<module>.<short-name>`, the removal date and the owner, and writes the flag row with every environment set to the default.
3. Service code: calls FeatureFlags.isOn(key) at each request; the value comes from a cache refreshed every 30 seconds (assumed; DL11).
4. Front end: reads GET /feature-flags at page load and hides or shows the component.
5. Platform administrator: switches the flag on for one environment with a reason.
6. System: checks the version, writes the new value and a feature_flag_change row with user, time, old and new value, and writes the ACE audit log entry.
7. Front end: after reload, shows the component; no deployment takes place.
8. Scheduler: the weekly flag report job runs every Monday 08:00 and lists every flag past its removal date with its owner.
9. System: sends the report to each owner and to the RW-PLATADM group by email and logs MSG-P2-003 per flag.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Removal date missing at creation | Refused; no flag is created | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | Removal date before today | Refused | MSG-GEN-003 | AC4 |
| X3 | Change without a reason | Refused | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X4 | Code asks for a key that does not exist | Returns off, the old code path runs, a warning is logged | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The flag store is unavailable | The last cached value is used; with no cached value the flag is off | None | AC7 |
| X6 | Two administrators change the same flag at once | The second change is refused | MSG-GEN-004 | AC8 |
| X7 | A change to a key that does not exist | Refused | MSG-P2-016 | AC9 |
| X8 | A role without the right changes a flag | Refused; nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-047-10 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the schema; every later story uses it |
| Negotiable | Flags, owners, values and dates are data rows; the cache interval is a property |
| Valuable | A failed change is switched off in SIT or UAT and the release goes ahead |
| Estimable | Two tables, one service with a cache, four endpoints, one weekly job, one React hook |
| Small | Within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Feature flags for module release with a removal date

  Background:
    Given flag "rwb.casewf.case-list-queue-column" exists with default off, owner team "P3 squad" and removal date 2027-01-31

  Scenario: AC1 Flag off by default
    Given the flag has no value set for UAT
    When the case list service starts in UAT
    Then FeatureFlags.isOn("rwb.casewf.case-list-queue-column") returns false
    Then the system hides the queue column on SCR-02 Case list

  Scenario: AC2 Flag switched on
    Given a platform administrator sets the flag to on in UAT with reason "UAT test of queue column" at 10:15
    When the case list page is reloaded at 10:16
    Then the queue column shows without a deployment
    Then a change row holds environment "UAT", old value off, new value on, the user and the time 10:15
    Then the ACE audit log holds the same change

  Scenario: AC3 Flag expiry
    Given flag "rwb.p5.ocr-intake" has removal date 2026-11-30 and owner team "P5 squad"
    Given today is Monday 2026-12-07
    When the weekly flag report runs at 08:00
    Then the system lists the flag for removal with its owner and 7 days past its removal date
    Then the report carries message MSG-P2-003 for the flag
    Then the system does not list flag "rwb.casewf.case-list-queue-column" with removal date 2027-01-31

  Scenario: AC4 Removal date checked at creation
    Given today is 2026-11-16
    When a platform administrator creates flag "rwb.p6.line-dispatch" with removal date 2026-11-10
    Then the system does not creat the flag
    Then the response is 422 with message MSG-GEN-003
    Then a creation with no removal date returns 422 with message MSG-GEN-001

  Scenario: AC5 Change without a reason refused
    When a platform administrator sets the flag to on in SIT with an empty reason
    Then the response is 422 with message MSG-GEN-001
    Then the flag stays off in SIT

  Scenario: AC6 Unknown key in code
    When code calls FeatureFlags.isOn("rwb.casewf.not-defined")
    Then the result is false
    Then a warning with the key and no user data is written to the application log

  Scenario: AC7 Flag store unavailable
    Given the flag is on in UAT and the cache holds the value from 10:20
    When the flag table cannot be read at 10:21
    Then FeatureFlags.isOn returns true from the cache
    Then after a restart with the table still unavailable it returns false

  Scenario: AC8 Two changes at once
    Given two platform administrators read the flag at version 4
    When both send a change with If-Match version 4
    Then the system saves one change with version 5
    Then the system refuses the other with 409 and message MSG-GEN-004

  Scenario: AC9 Change to a key that does not exist
    When a platform administrator sends a change for flag "rwb.p9.unknown"
    Then the response is 404 with message MSG-P2-016
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Unfinished work is behind a flag; a flag that is off returns the previous code path | DT11; ADR-008 |
| BR2 | Every flag has a key, an owner, a value per environment (DEV, SIT, UAT, PROD) and a removal date | Reference tables: Feature flags, Configuration |
| BR3 | A flag value changes without a code release, and each change is logged with user, time and reason | REQ-DRI-010; DT02 |
| BR4 | A flag past its removal date is reported to its owner every week until it is removed | ADR-008 consequences |
| BR5 | An unknown key or an unreadable store gives off, never on | DT11 |
| BR6 | Flag keys follow `rwb.<module>.<short-name>` | Story brief format, section 13 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the value of a flag per environment (off to on, on to off) and the flag's is_active column when a flag is retired.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Creates flags, changes values, retires flags (Platform administration, CRUD) |
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | Reads and changes flags (Platform administration, CRUDA) |
| RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY | Read flags and their change history (Platform administration, R) |
| RW-TRIBE, tribe lead and squad members | Receive the weekly report as flag owners; no change right |
| Every signed-in Workbench role | Reads the effective values through GET /feature-flags |

### 11. Data

| DF-OPS-209 | feature_flag | description | Write |

| Standard column | feature_flag_change | created_at | Write |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

All endpoints are new and recorded in the additions file.

| Method and path | Request | Response | Errors | Authorization | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /feature-flags | None | Map of flag key to boolean for the caller's environment | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001) | Any signed-in Workbench role (session check only) | Read only |
| GET /admin/feature-flags?overdue=true | Query: overdue, owner | Array of FeatureFlag: key, description, ownerTeam, values per environment, removalDate, daysOverdue, version | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002) | Platform administration, R | Read only |
| POST /admin/feature-flags | FeatureFlagRequest: key, description, ownerUserId, ownerTeam, defaultOn, removalDate | 201 FeatureFlag | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002); 409 key exists (MSG-GEN-004); 422 field missing or date in the past (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-003) | Platform administration, C | The key is unique; a repeat returns 409 |
| PATCH /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey} | FeatureFlagChange: environment, value, reason; header If-Match with the version | 200 FeatureFlag | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown key (MSG-P2-016); 409 version changed (MSG-GEN-004); 422 reason empty (MSG-GEN-001) | Platform administration, U | Setting the value it already has writes no change row |

**Job: weekly flag report (new, recorded in additions).** Trigger: Quartz, Monday 08:00 Asia/Bangkok. Input: feature_flag rows with is_active true and removal_date before today. Output: one email per owner and one to the RW-PLATADM group, one log line with MSG-P2-003 per flag. Events: none. Idempotency key: report date; a rerun on the same date sends nothing new. Restart: rerun from the start.

**Published interface (package recovery.integration.flags.api).**

```java
public interface FeatureFlags {
    boolean isOn(String flagKey); // false for an unknown key or an unreadable store with no cached value
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

- **Package.** folder `src/main/java/recovery/integration/flags`, Java package `recovery.integration.flags`; front end folder `src/modules/recovery/flags`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| FeatureFlagController | Controller | The four endpoints; validation; problem responses |
| FeatureFlagService | Service | Create, change and retire; version check; change row; ACE audit call |
| FeatureFlagsImpl | Published interface | isOn with a 30-second cache per key; environment from property `rwb.environment` |
| FeatureFlagRepository, FeatureFlagChangeRepository | Repository | The two flag tables only |
| FeatureFlag, FeatureFlagChange | Entity | JPA entities with the standard columns |
| FlagRemovalReportJob | Job | Weekly report |
| useFeatureFlag | React component | Hook that reads GET /feature-flags once per page load and returns the value for a key |
| FlagGate | React component | Renders its children only when the flag is on |

- **Database:** Flyway migration `V2026_11_47__p2_feature_flags.sql` creates feature_flag (primary key flag_key, check constraint on the key pattern `^rwb\.[a-z0-9]+\.[a-z0-9-]+$`, removal_date not null) and feature_flag_change (index on flag_key, changed_at).
- **Configuration and reference data:** property `rwb.environment` (DEV, SIT, UAT, PROD) per deployment; property `rwb.flags.cache-seconds` = 30 (assumed; DL11). Flag rows are created through the endpoints by RW-PLATADM.
- **Build steps:**
  1. Write the migration, entities and repositories with repository tests.
  2. Build FeatureFlagService with key, date and reason validation and the version check.
  3. Build FeatureFlagsImpl with the cache and the off-by-default rules for unknown keys and store failure.
  4. Build the four endpoints with the access check and the ACE audit write.
  5. Build useFeatureFlag and FlagGate with a component test that hides and shows a child.
  6. Build FlagRemovalReportJob with the email through the ACE notification path for staff.
  7. Put the case list queue column behind `rwb.casewf.case-list-queue-column` as the reference use.
- **Feature flag:** none. This story builds the flag service, which ships switched on.
- **Done when:** the tests in section 16 pass and the reference flag hides and shows the queue column in UAT without a deployment.

No screen in this story. The platform administrator uses the four endpoints through the ACE admin console API client; the flag list screen comes with SCR-44 in Epic 8. The business user sees the queue column on SCR-02 Case list appear or disappear after reload.

## RWB-E1-048 Rule change audit report

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-048 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-16 Report every rule change for audit |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-013, REQ-DRI-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3 and 4; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.7 |
| L3 process | 14 Set strategy, policy and decision rules |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Should |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-037, RWB-E1-011, RWB-E1-043 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the parameter change and rule change checklist (request, impact, test result, approver, load, verify, rollback plan) recorded on every change and reported for audit**, so that **a configuration change is as controlled as a code change**.

### 2. Business rationale

Audit found the collection procedure was not followed because rules lived in documents (CTL-08). When rules and limits are data, a wrong row changes every case it touches, so each change needs the same evidence as a code change: who asked, what it affects, the test result, who approved, when it took effect and how to undo it. This story makes the checklist fields required before a version can be approved and gives audit one report of every change. It meets REQ-CWC-013 and REQ-DRI-011. The measure is that every version in force has a complete checklist in the report.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-043 is done: every reference table version is a row in `reference_version` with author and approver.
- RWB-E1-037 is done: the permission matrix gives Rules and parameters R to RW-COE, RW-RISK and RW-AUDIT.
- RWB-E1-011 is done: the daily data quality report lists refused loads.
- Rule versions loaded through `POST /admin/rule-versions` (RWB-E1-029) are recorded in the same registry with table code `RULE_` and the route set, for example `RULE_UNIVERSAL_RULES`.
- The rule table test harness (RWB-TE-005) writes its result to the version for rule tables; the load checks of RWB-E1-043 write it for reference tables.

### 4. Flow

1. Center of excellence analyst: raises the change request in the bank's request tool and receives its reference, for example CR-2026-0042.
2. Reference data administrator: loads the new version through `POST /admin/reference-loads` (or `POST /admin/rule-versions`) with the request reference, the impact summary and the rollback plan as form fields.
3. Reference data service: stores the checklist fields on the version and records the test result from the load checks or the harness (PASSED or FAILED).
4. Approver: approves through `POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve`.
5. Reference data service: refuses the approval unless the request reference, impact summary, rollback plan and a PASSED test result are present and the approver is not the author.
6. Reference data administrator: after the valid from date, records the verification through `POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify`.
7. Internal audit or the center of excellence analyst: reads the report through `GET /admin/change-log` for a period and a table, as JSON or CSV.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A version reaches its valid from date with no approver | It is not served; the report shows it as not approved | None | AC2 |
| X2 | Approval with a checklist item missing | Refused; the version stays VALIDATED | MSG-P3-022 | AC3 |
| X3 | Approval of a version whose test result is FAILED | Refused | MSG-P3-022 | AC4 |
| X4 | The report period has no changes | An empty list is returned | None | AC6 |
| X5 | Verification recorded before the valid from date | Refused | MSG-GEN-003 | AC7 |
| X6 | The report period ends before it starts | Refused | MSG-GEN-003 | AC8 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Adds fields and one report to the registry of RWB-E1-043 |
| Negotiable | The checklist items are fixed by the Engineering Standards; the report columns can change |
| Valuable | Audit can test every configuration change without asking the team |
| Estimable | Six fields, one approval check, one verify call, one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is an API test on a PostgreSQL test container |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Rule change audit report

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-12-01
    Given SERVICE_LEVEL version 3 is in force with 10 working days for "MORTGAGE" status "IN_PROGRESS"
    Given user "U-REF-01" holds RW-REFADM, "U-RSK-01" holds the approve right and "U-AUD-01" holds RW-AUDIT

  Scenario: AC1 Change by checklist
    Given a request "CR-2026-0042" to change "MORTGAGE" status "IN_PROGRESS" to 8 working days from 2026-12-10
    Given "U-REF-01" loads SERVICE_LEVEL version 4 with impact summary "412 open Mortgage cases in IN_PROGRESS" and rollback plan "Reload version 3"
    Given the load checks pass
    Given "U-RSK-01" approves version 4 on 2026-12-02

    Then one entry shows table "SERVICE_LEVEL", version 4, request "CR-2026-0042", test result "PASSED", author "U-REF-01", approver "U-RSK-01", approved on 2026-12-02 and valid from 2026-12-10
    Then the entry shows 1 row changed, 0 added and 0 removed against version 3
    Then the approval time is before the valid from date

    Given SERVICE_LEVEL version 5 loaded by "U-REF-01" with valid from 2026-12-15 and never approved
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A version can be approved only when it carries a change request reference, an impact summary, a rollback plan and a test result of PASSED | CTL-08; refdata.txt Change process steps 1 to 4 |
| BR2 | The approver is not the author | roles.txt Separation of duty; CTL-08 |
| BR3 | A version that is not approved never takes effect | R-UNI-38; REQ-CWC-013 |
| BR4 | Verification is recorded on or after the valid from date | refdata.txt Change process step 6 |
| BR5 | The report lists every version of every reference and rule table whose load, approval, valid from or verification falls in the period | REQ-DRI-011 |
| BR6 | The effect of a version is the count of rows added, changed and removed against the version it replaces, and for rule tables the rule IDs changed | ADR-004 |
| BR7 | A rollback appears as its own entry naming the version it returns to | REQ-CWC-013; R-UNI-38 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It adds two conditions to the reference version statuses of RWB-E1-043: VALIDATED to APPROVED needs a complete checklist (BR1), and an APPROVED version gets a verification record after its valid from date.

### 12. Contract

**POST /admin/reference-loads** and **POST /admin/rule-versions** (P4 endpoints) take three more form fields: `changeRequestRef` (max 30), `impactSummary` (max 1000), `rollbackPlan` (max 1000). Missing fields do not refuse the load; they refuse the approval (BR1).

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve** (P4 endpoint): 409 with MSG-P3-022 naming the missing item when BR1 fails; otherwise as RWB-E1-043.

**POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify** (new, P3)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | `VerifyRequest`: `note` (max 1000, required) |
| Response | 200 `ReferenceLoad` with `verifiedBy`, `verifiedAt` |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Reference data U (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown load (MSG-P4-003); 422 empty note (MSG-GEN-001) or before valid from (MSG-GEN-003); 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right U |
| Idempotency | A second verification of the same version returns 200 with the first record and changes nothing |

**GET /admin/change-log** (new, P3)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query: `from` (date, required), `to` (date, required), `table` (optional), `format` (`json` default or `csv`), `page`, `size` (default 50, max 200) |
| Response | 200 `ChangeLogPage`: `items[]` of `ChangeLogEntry` (`table`, `version`, `status`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `changeRequestRef`, `impactSummary`, `testResult`, `authorUserId`, `loadedAt`, `approverUserId`, `approvedAt`, `verifiedBy`, `verifiedAt`, `rollbackPlan`, `rowsAdded`, `rowsChanged`, `rowsRemoved`, `rulesChanged[]`), `page`, `size`, `total`; or `text/csv` with the same columns |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Rules and parameters R (MSG-P4-002); 422 `to` before `from` (MSG-GEN-003); 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right R |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**Published interface** (added to `ReferenceVersionRegistry` of RWB-E1-043):

```java
ReferenceVersion verify(UUID loadId, UUID verifierUserId, String note, LocalDate businessDate);
Page<ChangeLogEntry> changeLog(LocalDate from, LocalDate to, Optional<String> tableCode, Pageable page);
```

No events are published.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery.casewf.refdata.audit` in the recovery module.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ChangeChecklistValidator | Service | The BR1 and BR2 checks called by `approve(...)` |
| ChangeEffectCalculator | Service | Compares the rows of a version with the version it replaces by `row_key` and `row_data`; lists changed rule IDs for `RULE_` tables |
| ChangeLogService | Service | Builds the report for a period and a table; paging; CSV writer |
| ChangeLogController | Controller | `GET /admin/change-log` and `POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify`; problem responses |
| ReferenceVersionRepository | Repository | Extended with the period query on loaded, approved, valid from and verified dates |

**Database.** Flyway migration `V<next>__rwb_e1_048_change_checklist.sql` adds to `reference_version`: `change_request_ref varchar(30)`, `impact_summary varchar(1000)`, `test_result varchar(10)` (PASSED, FAILED), `rollback_plan varchar(1000)`, `verified_by uuid`, `verified_at timestamptz`, `verify_note varchar(1000)`. Index on `(created_at)`, `(approved_at)` and `(valid_from)` for the period query.

**Configuration and reference data.** None beyond RWB-E1-043. The checklist items come from the Engineering Standards parameter and rule change checklists.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration and extend the entity.
2. Accept the three form fields in the P4 load handlers and pass them to `recordVersion(...)`; record the test result from the load checks or the harness.
3. Build `ChangeChecklistValidator` and call it from `approve(...)`; return MSG-P3-022 naming the first missing item.
4. Build `verify(...)` with the date check against the business date and the valid from.
5. Build `ChangeEffectCalculator` and test it on versions with added, changed and removed rows.
6. Build `ChangeLogService` and `ChangeLogController` with JSON and CSV output.
7. Write the tests in section 16.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.change-log`. Off: approval runs the RWB-E1-043 checks only and the report endpoint returns 404.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and the report for the SIT load period lists every version loaded in SIT with a complete checklist.

| MSG-GEN-001 | Verification with no note | Enter {field}. |

## RWB-E1-049 OCR pipeline on the Workbench document hub

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-049 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-07 Run the OCR pipeline on inbound documents |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-006, REQ-DCM-009 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-TE-012, RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-045 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **every inbound scan and upload read by the OCR service into text and layout in Thai and English, stored against the intake item and the document**, so that **classification and extraction can start and an unreadable page is sent back for rescan the same day**.

### 2. Business rationale

Scanned documents arrive as images; nothing in them can be classified, extracted or searched until the text is read (FSD P5 A2.7). This story builds the OCR step of the document intake: one intake record per file, the text and layout of every page, a quality check per page and a rescan request when a page cannot be read. It meets REQ-DCM-006 (fields extracted in Thai and English, which needs Thai and English text first) and REQ-DCM-009 (every path ends in the same intake). The measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.7.1).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-024 is done: documents are stored and DocumentStored (EV-16) is published.
- RWB-TE-012 is done: the intake and standard containers exist.
- RWB-E1-045 is done: product parameters are held as data.
- Document hub parameters loaded: OCR_MIN_QUALITY = 0.70, OCR_WORKERS = 4, OCR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120, OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3 (all assumed, DL11).
- The OCR service run by Autonomous Ops is reachable from SIT through the OcrClient adapter under the service identity SY-OCR.
- An intake item has scan_result CLEAN. The malware scan step is added in RWB-E1-041; until then test data is seeded CLEAN.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.ocr is on.

### 4. Flow

1. JOB-12 Document intake: starts every 15 minutes in business hours and runs the OCR step after the intake and scan steps.
2. DocumentStoredListener: for each DocumentStored event with source UPLOAD, creates an intake item with the case ID, the document ID and scan_result CLEAN (the upload was scanned before storage).
3. OcrStep: selects intake items with scan_result CLEAN and ocr_status PENDING, oldest first, locking each row so that no two workers take the same item; runs up to OCR_WORKERS items in parallel.
4. OcrClient: sends the file to the OCR service with the languages Thai and English and receives, per page, the lines, words, positions, language and word confidence.
5. OcrStep: computes the page quality as the mean word confidence of the page; stores the full output as JSON at ocr/{intakeId}.json in the standard container and sets ocr_ref.
6. OcrStep: writes one document_text row per page with the page text and quality, with the document ID where the item is already attached.
7. OcrStep: if every page has quality at or above OCR_MIN_QUALITY, sets ocr_status DONE; otherwise sets ocr_status RESCAN and rescan_pages to the page numbers below the threshold.
8. OcrStep: for an item in RESCAN with a known case, sends MSG-P5-018 to the case owner through the ACE notification path; for an item with no case, sets review_reason RESCAN so the item shows in the document review queue (SCR-31, RWB-E1-054).
9. OcrStep: records the run counts (read, done, rescan, failed) on the job record shown in the job monitor.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A page has quality below OCR_MIN_QUALITY | Item set RESCAN with the page numbers; case owner told, or the item goes to the review queue | MSG-P5-018 | AC3, AC4 |
| X2 | Page quality exactly at OCR_MIN_QUALITY | The page is accepted | None | AC5 |
| X3 | The OCR service does not answer within OCR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS or returns an error | ocr_attempts increases; the item stays PENDING for the next run; after two failed runs the job raises an alert to the platform administrator (JOB-12) | None | AC6 |
| X4 | The item fails OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS times or the file cannot be opened | ocr_status FAILED; review_reason UNREADABLE_FILE; item in the review queue | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The job runs again over items already DONE | Items are not read again; no second set of text rows | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Two workers start on the same item | The row lock lets one worker take it; the other skips it | None | AC9 |
| X7 | A user without the Documents right reads a document holding OCR text | Refused with 403; no text returned | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-049-10 (Access) |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store (RWB-E1-024) and the containers (RWB-TE-012); classification (RWB-E1-050) and extraction (RWB-E1-053) build on its output |
| Negotiable | Quality threshold, workers, timeout and attempts are parameters; the OCR service can change behind OcrClient |
| Valuable | Every scan becomes text that the later steps and the search read |
| Estimable | One table pair, one job step, one adapter, one listener |
| Small | Fits within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: OCR pipeline on the Workbench document hub

  Background:
    Given OCR_MIN_QUALITY is 0.70, OCR_WORKERS is 4 and OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS is 3
    Given the OCR service stub in SIT is replaced by the OCR service for AC1 and AC2

  Scenario: AC1 Sample processed
    Given the 180 synthetic sample documents, 30 of each of the six agreed types, in Thai and English, each as a CLEAN intake item
    When JOB-12 Document intake runs
    Then each of the 180 items has ocr_status "DONE" or "RESCAN" and an ocr_ref to its JSON output
    Then each page has a document_text row with the page text and its quality
    Then the text of the sample pages holds Thai and English words, and the languages recorded per item are "th" and "en" where both appear

  Scenario: AC2 Throughput
    Given 500 pages in 125 CLEAN intake items in SIT
    When they are processed by JOB-12 with 4 workers
    Then all 125 items reach "DONE" or "RESCAN" within 60 minutes of the first item starting

  Scenario: AC3 Unreadable page on a known case
    Given an uploaded court notice of 4 pages on case "RW-2026-000123" owned by user "TEST-CO-01"
    Given page 3 has quality 0.41 and the other pages are above 0.70
    When the OCR step runs
    Then the intake item has ocr_status "RESCAN" and rescan_pages "3"
    Then "TEST-CO-01" receives MSG-P5-018 naming page 3, the document and case "RW-2026-000123"

  Scenario: AC4 Unreadable page with no case yet
    Given a mailroom scan of 2 pages with no case and page 1 at quality 0.30
    When the OCR step runs
    Then the intake item has ocr_status "RESCAN", rescan_pages "1" and review_reason "RESCAN"
    Then the system sends no notification

  Scenario: AC5 Quality at the threshold
    Given a scan of 1 page with quality 0.70
    When the OCR step runs
    Then the item has ocr_status "DONE" and no rescan pages

  Scenario: AC6 OCR service unavailable
    Given the OCR service stub returns HTTP 503 for every call
    When JOB-12 runs twice
    Then each pending item has ocr_status "PENDING" and ocr_attempts 2
    Then the job monitor shows the OCR step failed in both runs and an alert is raised to the platform administrator
    Then when the service answers again the next run sets the items "DONE"

  Scenario: AC7 File that cannot be read
    Given a password-protected PDF as a CLEAN intake item
    When the OCR step runs
    Then the item has ocr_status "FAILED" and review_reason "UNREADABLE_FILE"
    Then no document_text row exists for it

  Scenario: AC8 Repeat run
    Given 10 intake items already "DONE" with 25 document_text rows
    When JOB-12 runs again
    Then the OCR service receives no call for those items
    Then they still have 25 document_text rows

  Scenario: AC9 Two workers on one item
    Given one CLEAN pending item and 4 workers starting at the same time
    When the OCR step runs
    Then the OCR service receives exactly one call for the item
    Then the item has one set of document_text rows
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every inbound file is read in Thai and English | REQ-DCM-006; FEAT-DCM-07 |
| BR2 | Scans, partner files, emails and uploads go through the same intake item and OCR step | REQ-DCM-009 |
| BR3 | A file is read only after its malware scan is CLEAN | REQ-DCM-010; FEAT-DCM-18 |
| BR4 | A page below OCR_MIN_QUALITY is sent for rescan; the threshold is inclusive | Document hub parameter OCR_MIN_QUALITY (New); DL11 |
| BR5 | A system that does not answer is retried on the next run and alerted after two failed runs | R-UNI-33; JOB-12 |
| BR6 | An item read once is not read again | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | Worker count, timeout and attempts are parameters | Principle 1; DT02 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the intake item OCR status: PENDING to DONE when every page passes; PENDING to RESCAN when a page is below the threshold; PENDING stays PENDING after a failed call below the attempt limit; PENDING to FAILED at the attempt limit or for a file that cannot be opened.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Reads intake files, writes OCR output and text rows (Documents CRU) |
| RW-CASEOWN | Receives the rescan notice for their case |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Sees the job counts and alerts in the job monitor; reruns JOB-12 |
| Roles with Documents R | Read the OCR text of documents in their scope through RWB-E1-033 |
